en: 1.01.001 *vṛddhi* is the substitution for *āT* and *aiC*.
1.01.002 *guṇa* is the substitution for *aT* and *eṄ*. 1.01.003 *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* are the substitutes for *iK*.

1.01.004 [The substitution of Guna and Vrddhi does not take place] when there is elision of a root-vowel (dhātu-lopa) before an ārdhadhātuka suffix. 1.01.005 [The substitution of Guna and Vrddhi does not take place] before a suffix marked with K or Ṅ as an IT. 1.01.006 [The substitution of Guna and Vrddhi does not take place] for the roots *dīdhī* and *vevī*, nor for the augment iṭ.

1.01.007 Consonants (*hal*) that follow immediately after one another constitute a *saṃyoga* (conjunct). 1.01.008 A sound articulated through both the mouth and the nose is *anunāsika* (nasalized). 1.01.009 Sounds produced with the same articulatory effort (*āsyaprayatna*) are *savarṇa* (homogeneous).

1.01.010 A vowel (*aC*) and a consonant (*haL*) [at the end of a word] are not [pragṛhya]. 1.01.011 A dual ending (*dvivacana*) that ends in *īT* or *ūT* is *pragṛhya*. 1.01.012 [The final vowel of] *adas-* [is *pragṛhya*] when it is followed by *mā*.
1.01.013 A particle [ending] in a single vowel, other than *aṅ*, [is called pragṛhya]. 1.01.014 An *oṭ* [vowel] [is called pragṛhya].

1.01.016: According to Śākalya, [the substitution of *o* occurs] for *u* and *ū* before a following vowel (*it*) in a *sambuddhi* (vocative singular), except in the case of Vedic (*ārṣa*) usage. 1.01.017: [The same applies] after *uÑ*.
1.01.019 And [the substitution of] *īT* and *ūT* occurs when they signify the locative case.
1.01.020 The roots *dā* and *dhā* are designated as *Ghu*, with the exception of *dāP*.
1.01.021 That which is single is treated like the beginning and the end.
1.01.022 The suffixes *taraP* and *tamaP* are designated as *GHa*.
1.01.023 The words *bahu*, *gaṇa*, and those ending in *vatU* and *Ḍati* are designated as *saṃkhyā* (numerals).
1.01.024 Words ending in *ṣ* and *ṇa* are designated as *ṣaṭ* (six).
1.01.025 And [the suffix] ḍati [is called pratyaya]. 1.01.026 The suffixes kta and ktavatū are termed niṣṭhā. 1.01.027 The words beginning with sarva are termed sarvanāman (pronouns).
1.01.028: Optionally [the elision of the case-ending] occurs in a Bahuvrīhi compound that is a directional (dik) compound.
1.01.029: [The elision of the case-ending] does not occur in a Bahuvrīhi [compound].
1.01.030: [The elision of the case-ending] occurs in a compound with an instrumental (tṛtīyā) [word].

1.01.031 And [the final vowel of the first member is optionally shortened] in a *dvandva* compound. 1.01.032 [The substitution of the short vowel *i* for the final vowel of the first member is] optional in the *jas* case-ending. 1.01.033 [The same optionality applies] to the words *prathama*, *carama*, *taya*, *alpa*, *ardha*, *katipaya*, and *nema*.

1.01.034 The words *pūrva*, *para*, *avara*, *dakṣiṇa*, *uttara*, *apara*, and *adhara* [are optionally termed *sarvanāman*] when used in their restricted senses (*vyavasthāyām*) and not as proper names (*asaṃjñāyām*). 1.01.035 The word *sva* [is optionally termed *sarvanāman*] when it does not denote a kinsman or wealth. 1.01.036 The word *antara* [is optionally termed *sarvanāman*] when it denotes being outside (*bahiryoga*) or an inner garment (*upasaṃvyāna*).

1.01.037 Indeclinables are the particles beginning with *svar*. 1.01.038 And [words ending in] secondary suffixes (*taddhita*) that do not take all case-endings [are also indeclinables]. 1.01.039 [Words] ending in a *kṛt* suffix and having *eC* as their final vowel [are also indeclinables].
1.01.040 The suffixes *ktvā*, *tosuN*, and *kasuN* [are called *kṛt*]. 1.01.041 And the *avyayībhāva* compound [is also called *avyaya*]. 1.01.042 The suffix *Śi* is a *sarvanāmasthāna*.
1.01.043 *sUṬ* [are applied] to that which is not neuter;
1.01.044 *na vā*—this is an optional rule (*vibhāṣā*); 1.01.045 *iK* and *yaṆ* undergo *samprasāraṇa*.
1.01.046: The markers *Ṭ* and *K* are placed at the beginning and the end [of an element].
1.01.047: A marker with *M* as its indicatory letter (*mit*) is placed after the final vowel (*ac*) [of the element].
1.01.048: When a short vowel is substituted for *eC*, the marker *iK* is placed [after the final vowel of the element].
1.01.049 The genitive case [is used] in the sense of "in place of.
1.01.050 In place [of something], that which is most similar [is substituted].
1.01.051 When followed by *r̥* or *r̥*, *u* [is substituted for *ṛ*].

1.01.052 *al* is substituted for the final [phoneme]. 1.01.053 Also when [an affix] marked with *ṅ* or *it* follows, [the substitution occurs]. 1.01.054 [The substitution] of the first [phoneme] of the subsequent [element].
1.1.55: An affix consisting of more than one phoneme (aL) that has an indicatory letter Ś (ŚIT) causes the entire original element to take its place.
1.1.56: A substitute (ādeśa) is treated like the original (sthānivat), except in the case of an operation prescribed for a non-vowel (aL-vidhau).

1.1.57: When an operation is prescribed for what precedes a vowel (aCaḥ), the substitute is treated like the original with respect to that preceding element, provided the cause of the operation remains after the substitution.

1.01.058 Not [applies] in the rules concerning the doubling of a word-final [consonant], the substitution of *vār*, elision (*lopa*), homogeneous vowels (*savarṇa*), the nasal *anusvāra*, lengthening (*dīrgha*), and the suffixes *jaŚ* and *caR*.
1.01.059 In the case of doubling, [the rule applies] when a vowel (*ac*) follows.
1.01.060 Non-appearance is termed *lopa* (elision).
1.01.061 The markers *luK*, *Ślu*, and *luP* are elided. 1.01.062 When an affix is elided, the grammatical operations conditioned by that affix still take place.
1.01.063 An operation conditioned by an affix does not take place when that affix is marked with *lu*.
1.01.064: The final vowel (*aC*) and the following consonant (*aT*) constitute the *ti* (the "base" for grammatical operations).
1.01.065: The letter immediately preceding the final letter (*aL*) is called the *upadhā* (penultimate).
1.01.066: When [an operation] is prescribed by means of the word *tasmin* ("in that"), it applies to what precedes that [which is specified].

1.01.067. After [the word] *tasmāt*, [the sixth case ending] belongs to what follows. 1.01.068. A word's own form (*svarūpam*) is [meant by its own name], except when it is a technical grammatical term (*saṃjñā*). 1.01.069. A vowel (*aṆ*) and a consonant with an indicatory letter *u* (*uT*) denote their own class (*savarṇa*), provided they are not themselves suffixes (*apratyayaḥ*).
1.01.070 That which has a long vowel (*ta*) following it [represents] its own duration.
1.01.071 An initial sound, together with a final *it* (indicatory letter), [denotes] the entire class of sounds beginning with it.
1.01.072 A grammatical operation (*vidhi*) is applied to that which ends in the same element by which the operation is prescribed.
1.01.073 That [word] whose initial vowel among its vowels is *vṛddhi* is called *vṛddha*.
1.01.074 And [the pronouns] beginning with *tyad* [are also *vṛddha*].
1.01.075 In the opinion of the Easterners, [a word] ending in *eṅ* [is *vṛddha*] when it denotes a region.

1.02.001 After the roots *gāṅ* (the substitute for *iṅ*) and those beginning with *kuṭ*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied before affixes marked with *Ñ* or *Ṇ* that have an indicatory letter *I*.
1.02.002 The augment *iṭ* is optionally applied after the root *vij*. 1.02.003 The augment *iṭ* is optionally applied after the root *ūrṇu*.
1.02.004 A sārvadhātuka suffix that does not have P or IT as an it-marker is ṅit.
1.02.005 After a root ending in a non-conjunct consonant, the *liṭ* suffix is *kit*.
1.02.006 And [the *liṭ* suffix is *kit*] after the roots *indh* and *bhū*.
1.02.007: After the roots *mṛḍ*, *mṛd*, *gudh*, *kuṣ*, *kliś*, *vad*, and *vas*, the suffix *Krvā* is applied.
1.02.008: After the roots *rud*, *vid*, *muṣ*, *grah*, *svap*, and *pracch*, both *saN* and *Krvā* are applied.
1.02.009: After a root ending in a single vowel (*iK*), the suffixes beginning with *jhaL* (consonants) are applied.
1.02.010 And [the augment *iṭ* is applied] after [a verbal root] ending in a consonant (*haL*).
1.02.011 [The augment *iṭ* is applied] before the suffixes *liṅ* and *sic* when they belong to the *ātmanepada*. 1.02.012 And [the augment *iṭ* is applied] before the suffix *us*.

1.02.013 The suffix *vā* is applied after the root *gam*. 1.02.014 The suffix *siC* is applied after the root *han*. 1.02.015 The suffix *siC* is applied after the root *yam* when it means "to scent."

1.02.016 The substitution [of *ya*] is optional (*vibhāṣā*) when the root means "to marry. 1.02.017 After the roots *sthā* and *ghu*, the augment *iṭ* is added [to the suffixes beginning with a consonant]. 1.02.018 The suffix *Ktvā* does not take the augment *sa-iṭ*.

1.02.019 The perfective participle suffix *niṣṭhā* is applied after the roots *śīṄ*, *svidi*, *midi*, *kṣvidi*, and *dhṛṣ*. 1.02.020 It is also applied after the root *mṛṣ* when it signifies endurance (*titikṣā*). 1.02.021 After a root having a penultimate vowel (*uT*), the suffix *niṣṭhā* is optionally applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) or an initial action (*ādikarman*).
1.02.022 After the root *pūñ*, the suffix *Ktvā* also takes the augment *iṭ*.
1.02.023 After a root ending in *th* or *ph* that does not have *n* as its penultimate letter (*an-upadha*), [the suffix *Ktvā*] optionally takes the augment *iṭ*.
1.02.024 [The suffix *Ktvā* takes the augment *iṭ*] after the roots *vañci*, *lunci*, and those ending in *ṛt*.

1.02.025 For the [roots] *tṛṣ*, *mṛṣ*, and *kṛś*, according to Kāśyapa. 1.02.026 After a root beginning with a consonant and having a penultimate *ṛ* or *lṛ*, there is optionally the suffix *saN*. 1.02.027 A vowel (*aC*) having the duration of *ū* is termed short (*hrasva*), long (*dīrgha*), or protracted (*pluta*).
1.02.028 And [a vowel] followed by *aC* [is called *svarita*]. 1.02.029 A high [pitch] is *udātta*. 1.02.030 A low [pitch] is *anudātta*.
1.02.031 A combination [of accents] is circumflex (svarita).
1.02.032 Of that [circumflex], the first half-mora is acute (udātta).
1.02.033 There is monotone (ekaśruti) when addressing someone from a distance.
1.02.034 In sacrificial rites, [the *vaṣaṭ* call is uttered] with a higher pitch than the *japa*, *ṛc*, *yajus*, and *sāman*.
1.02.035 Or rather, the *vaṣaṭ* call is uttered with a higher pitch. 1.02.036 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this is optional.
1.02.037 In the Subrahmaṇyā formula, however, a circumflex (svarita) vowel becomes acute (udātta).
1.02.038 In the words *deva* and *brahman*, [the circumflex] becomes grave (anudātta).
1.02.039 In continuous speech (saṃhitā), [the grave vowels] following a circumflex [vowel become udātta].
1.02.040 A vowel following an acute (udātta) or circumflex (svarita) accent is more depressed (sannatara).
1.02.041 An uncombined (apṛkta) suffix consisting of a single phoneme (eka=aL) is [called a pratyaya].
1.02.042 A Tatpuruṣa compound whose members have a common substratum (samāna-adhikaraṇa) is called a Karmadhāraya.

1.2.43: In a compound, that which is designated by the first case-ending is the *upasarjana*. 1.2.44: And [that which is designated by] a single case-ending is also [the *upasarjana*], provided it does not occur as a prior member (*pūrvanipāta*). 1.2.45: That which possesses meaning, is not a verbal root (*dhātu*), and is not an affix (*pratyaya*) is a nominal stem (*prātipadika*).

1.02.046 And [the terms] *kṛt*, *taddhita*, and compounds [are called *prātipadika*]. 1.02.047 A short vowel is substituted for the final vowel of a neuter *prātipadika*. 1.02.048 [A short vowel is substituted for the final vowel] of a feminine word ending in *go* or *strī* when they function as a subordinate member (*upasarjana*).
1.02.049 *luK* [is applied] when a *taddhita* suffix is elided (*luK*). 1.02.050 The feminine suffix *īT* is elided after the word *goṇī*.
1.02.051 When a *luP* elision occurs, the gender and number are like those of the original base (*yuktavat*).
1.02.052 And [the gender and number] of qualifiers [are not taught separately] when they do not denote a genus (ajāti).
1.02.053 That [teaching] need not be prescribed, because a name is authoritative [in itself]. 1.02.054 [The suffix is elided by] *lup* because the connection [of the meaning] is no longer perceived.
1.02.055 And in the case of the measure of application (*yoga-pramāṇa*), there would be non-perception in its absence.

1.02.056 The statement regarding the meaning of the primary and the secondary suffixes is unnecessary, because the meaning [of the compound] is established by other means of knowledge (*pramāṇa*). 1.02.057 And this is the same in the case of time (*kāla*) and the subordinate member (*upasarjana*).
1.02.058 When expressing a genus, the plural may optionally be used for a single entity. 1.02.059 The plural is optionally used for the word *asmad* ("we") when referring to two persons.
1.02.060 The plural is optionally used for the constellations *Phalgunī* and *Proṣṭhapadā*.
1.02.061 In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is the singular form for the two *punarvasū* constellations.
1.02.062 And likewise for the two *viśākhā* constellations.
1.02.063 In a copulative compound (*dvandva*) of constellations consisting of Tiṣya and Punarvasu, the dual number always takes the place of the plural.

1.2.64: Of words that have the same form, only one remains when they occur with the same case-ending. 1.2.65: An elder [male] is compounded with a youth, provided that the distinction between them is based solely on the characteristic [of age]. 1.2.66: The feminine form is treated like the masculine.
1.02.067 A masculine [noun] [is optionally used in the singular with a feminine noun].
1.02.068 The words *bhrātṛ* (brother) and *putra* (son) [are optionally used in the singular with] *svasṛ* (sister) and *duhitṛ* (daughter).
1.02.069 A neuter [noun] [is optionally used in the singular with a non-neuter noun as a single unit].
1.02.070 A father [is compounded] with a mother;
1.02.071 a father-in-law with a mother-in-law;
1.02.072 the pronouns beginning with *tyad* are always [compounded] with all [other words].
1.02.073: Among herds of domestic animals that are not young, a female [is the leader].
1.03.001: The roots (dhātu) begin with the root *bhū*.
1.03.002: In the grammatical instruction (upadeśa), a nasalized vowel (*anunāsika*) is called *it*.

1.03.003 A consonant (haL) is the final [element] of a nominal stem. 1.03.004 This does not apply to the case-endings *tu*, *si* (tU), and *mā* (tU-s-māḥ). 1.03.005 The markers ÑI, ṬU, and ḌU are placed at the beginning [of the suffixes they designate].
1.03.006. *ṣ* is the substitute for a suffix. 1.03.007. *c*, *ū*, and *ṭ* are markers (*it*).
1.03.008. *l*, *ś*, and *k* are markers (*it*) when not part of a *taddhita* suffix.

1.03.009 There is elision (lopa) of that [which has been taught]. 1.03.010 A subsequent designation of equal number [of elements] corresponds to their respective order. 1.03.011 An adhikāra (governing rule) is indicated by a circumflex accent (svarita).

1.03.012 The *ātmanepada* [endings] are used after a root that has an *anudātta* accent or an *ṅit* suffix. 1.03.013 [The *ātmanepada* endings are used] in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*).
1.03.014 [The *ātmanepada* endings are used] in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*) when there is a reciprocal action (*karmavyatihāra*).

1.03.015 [The suffix *kta* is not used after verbal roots meaning "motion" or "injury"]. 1.03.016 [Nor is it used] when *itaretara*, *anyonya*, or *upapada* [words] are present as co-occurring elements. 1.03.017 [Nor is it used] after the root *viś-* preceded by the prefix *ni*.
1.03.018 After *pari*, *vi*, and *ava*, [the suffix *ṣat* is applied] to the root *kṛ*.
1.03.019 After *vi* and *parā*, [the suffix *ṣat* is applied] to the root *ji*.
1.03.020 After *āṅ*, [the suffix *ṣat* is applied] to the root *dā*, except in the sense of opening the mouth.
1.03.021 The root *krīḍ* [takes the ātmanepada endings] after the prefixes *anu*, *sam*, and *pari*.
1.03.022 The root *sṭhā* [takes the ātmanepada endings] after the prefixes *sam*, *ava*, *pra*, and *vi*.
1.03.023 [The root *sṭhā* takes the ātmanepada endings] when meaning "to manifest" (*prakāśana*) or "to declare one's own position" (*stheyākhyā*).

1.03.024 After *ud*, [the suffix *ktvā* is used] except when the action involves rising upward. 1.03.025 After *upa*, [the suffix *ktvā* is used] when the mantra is the instrument of the action. 1.03.026 And [the suffix *ktvā* is used] after a verb that is intransitive (*akarmaka*).
1.03.027 The suffix *liṭ* takes the augment *ātmanepada* after the roots *tap* preceded by the prefixes *ud* and *vi*.
1.03.028 [The suffix *liṭ* takes the augment *ātmanepada*] after the roots *yam* and *han* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*.
1.03.029 [The suffix *liṭ* takes the augment *ātmanepada*] after the roots *gam*, *ṛcch*, *pracch*, *svar*, *ṛ*, *śru*, and *vid* when preceded by the prefix *sam*.

1.03.030 *ni*, *sam*, *upa*, and *vi* [are prefixes] for the root *hve*; 1.03.031 [the prefix] *āṅ* [is used] in the sense of rivalry; 1.03.032 [the prefix *āṅ* is used] with the root *kṛñ* in the senses of threatening, disparaging, serving, acting with rashness, effort, proclaiming, and employment.
1.03.033 [The suffix *lyap* is used] after the root *adhi* when it signifies "overpowering" (*prasahana*).
1.03.034 [The suffix *lyap* is used] after the root *vi* when it has sound as its object (*śabda-karman*).
1.03.035 And [the suffix *lyap* is used] after [the root *vi*] when it is intransitive (*akarmaka*).
1.03.036 The root *ni* is used with the accusative case in the senses of honoring, lifting up, making someone one's teacher, knowing, maintaining, counting, and spending.
1.03.037 And [it is used with the accusative] when the object is something other than the body, provided that the action resides in the agent.
1.03.038 The root *kram* is used with the accusative in the senses of livelihood, creation, and excessive indulgence.

1.03.039 [The suffix *ātmanepada* is used] after [the root *kram*] with the prefixes *upa* and *parā*. 1.03.040 [The suffix *ātmanepada* is used after the root *kram*] with the prefix *āṅ* when it means rising up. 1.03.041 [The suffix *ātmanepada* is used after the root *kram*] with the prefix *vi* when it means stepping out with the feet.
1.03.042 [The suffix *kha* is applied after the root *jñā*] when preceded by the prefixes *pra* or *upa*, provided they are semantically connected [to the action].
1.03.043 [The suffix *kha* is applied after the root *jñā*] optionally when no prefix is present. 1.03.044 [The suffix *kha* is applied after the root *jñā*] in the sense of concealment (*apahnava*).

1.03.045 And [the root *vad*] when intransitive (akarmaka). 1.03.046 [The roots *sam-vad* and *prati-vad*] with the preverbs *sam* and *prati*, except in the sense of thinking about (anādhyāne). 1.03.047 The root *vad* [is used in the Ātmanepada] in the senses of speaking, conversing, knowing, striving, disagreeing, and addressing.
1.03.048 [The affix *liṭ* is used] after [roots] whose speech is articulate, when there is a collective utterance [of the action].
1.03.049 [The affix *liṭ* is used] after [a root] preceded by *anu*, provided it is intransitive.
1.03.050 [The affix *liṭ* is used] optionally after [a root] meaning "to chatter," when preceded by *vi* or *pra*.
1.03.051 *ava* [is used] with *grah*; 1.03.052 *sam* [is used] in the sense of promising;
1.03.053 *ud* [is used] with *car* when it has an object.

1.03.054: [The sixth case ending is used for the word] *sama* when it is joined with a word in the third case. 1.03.055: [The sixth case ending is used for the word *sama*] after the root *dāṇ* (to give), provided that this [third-case word] has the sense of the fourth case. 1.03.056:
[The sixth case ending is used for the word *sama*] after the root *yama* (to restrain) in the sense of "making one's own."
1.03.057 After the roots *jñā*, *śru*, *smṛ*, and *dṛś*, the suffix *saN* [is applied when expressing the agent of the action performed by the object].
1.03.058 [The suffix *saN* is not applied] after the root *jñā* when preceded by *na*.
1.03.059 [The suffix *saN* is applied] after the root *śru* when preceded by *prati* or the prefix *āṄ*.
1.03.060 [The substitution of *s* for the root-final *ś*] occurs after the root *śad*, when it is marked with the indicatory letter *Ś*.
1.03.061 [The substitution of *s* for the root-final *ś*] also occurs after the root *mṛ*, in the *luṅ* (aorist) and *liṅ* (optative) tenses.
1.03.062 The same [substitution rules as those previously stated] apply to the suffix *saN*.
1.03.063 The suffix *ām* is optionally applied after the root *kṛ*, when it follows another verb used as an auxiliary (*anuprayoga*).
1.03.064 The suffix *ām* is optionally applied after the root *yuj* when preceded by *pra* or *upa*, provided that the action does not involve sacrificial vessels (*ayajñapātra*).
1.03.065 The suffix *ām* is optionally applied after the root *kṣṇu* when preceded by *sam*.
1.03.066 *bhuja* [is used] in the sense of protecting (*anavane*).

1.03.067 That which is the object (*karman*) of a root ending in *ṇiC*, provided it is not the agent (*kartṛ*) when that same root is without *ṇiC*, becomes the subject (*kartṛ*) in the *ṇiC*-form, except in the sense of remembering (*anādhyāne*).
1.03.068 [The roots] *bhī* and *smi* take the fifth case (*hetu*) when fear is caused by that [agent].
1.03.069 [The suffix *ṇic* is applied] after the roots *gṛdh* and *vañc* in the sense of deceiving; 1.03.070 [It is applied] after the root *lī* in the sense of honoring and making someone graceful;
1.03.071 [The suffix *ṇic* is applied] after the root *kṛ* when preceded by the prefix *mithyā* in the sense of repetition.
1.03.072: [The *ātmanepada* suffixes are used] after a root having a *svarita* accent or marked with the *ñ* or *it* indicatory letters, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent.

1.03.073: [The *ātmanepada* suffixes are used] after the root *vad* (to speak) preceded by the prefix *apa*. 1.03.074: [The *ātmanepada* suffixes are used] also after a root ending in the causative suffix *ṇic*.
1.03.075 The affix *a* is applied after the roots *am*, preceded by the prefixes *sam*, *ud*, and *āṅ*, provided they do not refer to a literary composition (*agranthe*).

1.03.076 The affix *a* is applied after the root *jñā*, when it is not preceded by any prefix (*anupasargāt*). 1.03.077 When the meaning [of the prefix] is understood from a co-occurring word (*upapadena pratīyamāne*), the application of the affix is optional (*vibhāṣā*).

1.03.078 The *parasmaipada* endings are used for the agent (*kartṛ*) after [a root] other than those [previously specified]. 1.03.079 [The *parasmaipada* endings are used] after the root *kṛñ* when preceded by the prefixes *anu-* and *parā-*.
1.03.080 [The *parasmaipada* endings are used] after the root *kṣip* when preceded by *abhi*, *prati*, and *ati*.

1.03.081 After *pra*, [the root] *vah* [is used with the ātmanepada endings]. 1.03.082 After *pari*, [the root] *mṛṣ* [is used with the ātmanepada endings]. 1.03.083 After *vi*, *āṅ*, and *pari*, [the root] *ram* [is used with the ātmanepada endings].
1.03.084 [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used after a root] beginning with the prefix *upa*. 1.03.085 [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used] optionally after an intransitive root.
1.03.086 [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used] after the roots *budh*, *yudh*, *naś*, *jan*, *iṅ*, *pru*, *dru*, and *sru*, when followed by the suffix *ṇi*.
1.03.087 [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used after roots] having the meaning of swallowing (*nigaraṇa*) or moving (*calana*).

1.03.088 [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used after a root] that is intransitive when not preceded by a prefix (*aṇau*), and whose agent (*kartṛ*) possesses consciousness (*cittavat*). 1.03.089 [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is not used after the following roots: *pā* (to drink), *dam* (to tame), *āṅ-yam* (to restrain), *āṅ-yas* (to exert), *pari-muh* (to be confused), *ruc* (to shine/please), *nṛt* (to dance), *vad* (to speak), and *vas* (to dwell).
1.03.090 Optionally [the suffix] Kyaṣ [is added after a root ending in a vowel].
1.03.091 [The substitution of] luṅ [occurs] after roots beginning with dyu.
1.03.092 [The substitution of luṅ occurs] after roots beginning with vṛ, except when followed by sya or san.

1.03.093: And [the substitution of *ya* for the root] *kḷp-* occurs before the suffix *luṭ*. 1.04.001: Up to the word *kaḍāra*, there is only one designation [for each grammatical element]. 1.04.002: In the case of a conflict between rules, the subsequent rule takes effect.
1.04.003 Feminine stems ending in *yū* are called *nadī*.
1.04.004 Those [stems] that do not end in a feminine gender and which take the place of *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* are not [called *nadī*].
1.04.005 Optionally so, when followed by the suffix *ām*.

1.04.006 A short vowel [is substituted] before an affix marked with Ṅ or Ṇ. 1.04.007 The remainder [of the words listed in 1.1.42], excluding *sakhi*, is designated as *ghi*. 1.04.008 The word *pati* is designated as *ghi* only when it occurs in a compound.
1.04.009 In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), [a word] joined with a genitive case ending [is optionally heavy].
1.04.010 A short vowel is light (*laghu*). 1.04.011 [A short vowel] is heavy (*guru*) when followed by a consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*).
1.04.012 And [the substitute] is long.

1.04.013 That from which the rule for an affix (*pratyaya*) is prescribed, beginning with that, is designated as "beginning with that" (*tadādi*) when an affix follows. 1.04.014 A word (*pada*) is that which ends in a nominal suffix (*sUP*) or a verbal suffix (*tiṄ*).

1.04.015 *naḥ* [is substituted for *as*] before *Kye*. 1.04.016 Also before a suffix beginning with *S-IT*. 1.04.017 Before *su* and the following [case endings], except when they are *sarvanāmasthāna*.
1.04.018 The [substitution of] *y* occurs before a vowel (*aC*) when followed by *BHA*.
1.04.019 The suffix *matUP* is applied after the words *tad* and *sad* in the sense of possession.
1.04.020 Words such as *ayasmaya* (made of iron) are formed according to the rules of the Vedic language (*chandas*).

1.04.021 The plural number is used for many things. 1.04.022 The dual and singular numbers are used for two and one thing, respectively. 1.04.023 [This applies] to the grammatical participant (kāraka).
1.4.24 That which remains fixed when there is a departure is the *apādāna* (ablative).
1.4.25 For verbs meaning "to fear" or "to protect," that which is the cause of fear is the *apādāna*. 1.4.26 For the verb *parā-ji* ("to defeat"), that which is not endured is the *apādāna*.
1.4.27: In the case of verbs meaning "to ward off," that which is desired [is called the *apādāna*].
1.4.28: In the sense of "concealment," that by means of whom one desires to be unseen [is called the *apādāna*].
1.4.29: In the case of the verb *ākhyā* ("to tell"), when used with *upayoga* ("instruction"), [the person from whom instruction is received is called the *apādāna*].
1.04.030 The source of the agent of birth is the *prakṛti* (material cause).
1.04.031 The origin of *bhū* (the earth) is its *prabhava* (source).
1.04.032 That which one approaches through an action is the *sampradāna* (recipient).
1.04.033 One who is being pleased is the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) of verbs meaning "to find pleasure in" (*ruci*).
1.04.034 One who is being informed is the recipient of the verbs *ślāgh* ("to praise"), *hnuṅ* ("to deny"), *sthā* ("to stand"), and *śap* ("to curse").
1.04.035 The creditor is the recipient of the verb *dhāri* ("to owe").
1.4.36: In connection with the verb *spṛh* ("to desire"), that which is desired [is called the object].

1.4.37: In connection with the verbs *krudh* ("to be angry"), *druh* ("to bear malice"), *īrṣy* ("to envy"), and *asūy* ("to find fault"), that which is expressed by the fourth case ending [is called the object].
1.4.38: When the verbs *krudh* and *druh* are compounded with a prefix, that which is expressed by the second case ending [is called the object].
1.04.039 In the case of the roots *rādh* and *īkṣ*, that person for whom the inquiry is made [is the agent].
1.04.040 In the case of the root *śru* preceded by *prati* or *āṅ*, the agent of the preceding action [is the agent]. 1.04.041 And also in the case of the root *gṛ* preceded by *anu* and *prati*.

1.4.42 The most effective means (*sādhakatama*) is called the instrument (*karaṇa*). 1.4.43 After the root *div*, [the word denoting the means] may also be designated as the object (*karman*). 1.4.44 In the sense of "bargaining" (*parikrayaṇa*), [the word denoting the means] is optionally designated as the recipient (*sampradāna*).

1.04.045 The locus (*ādhāra*) is the substratum (*adhikaraṇa*). 1.04.046 The object (*karma*) of the roots *adhi-śī* (to lie down), *adhi-sthā* (to stand), and *adhi-ās* (to sit) [is the locus]. 1.04.047 And [the object of] *abhi-ni-viś* (to enter/occupy) as well.
1.4.48 [The suffix *karmaṇi* is applied] after [the verbal root *ās*] preceded by *upa*, *anu*, *adhi*, and *ā*.
1.4.49 That which is most desired to be reached by the agent is the *karman*. 1.4.50 And that which is likewise connected [with the action], though not desired, [is also called *karman*].
1.4.51 And that which is not designated [as an object] (akathita).

1.4.52 The agent of roots meaning motion (gati), cognition (buddhi), consumption (pratyavasāna), those having sound as their object (śabdakarma), and those being intransitive (akarmaka), when followed by a causative suffix (ṇic), becomes the object (karman) in the causative (ṇau).
1.4.53 In the case of the roots *hṛ* (to carry) and *kṛ* (to do/make), it is optionally so.
1.4.54: The independent agent is called the *kartṛ*. 1.4.55: That which prompts him [the agent] is also called the *hetu* (cause). 1.4.56:
Words beginning with *īśvara* are *nipāta*s (irregularly formed words).
1.4.57: The particles beginning with *ca* are called *nipātas* when they do not denote a substance (*asattve*).
1.4.58: The particles beginning with *pra* are called *upasargas*.
1.4.59: These [beginning with *pra*] are called *upasargas* when they are in connection with a verbal action (*kriyā-yoge*).
1.04.060 And [the term] *gati*.
1.04.061 Also [the words] beginning with *ūrī* when followed by the suffixes *Cvi* and *ḌāC*.
1.04.062 Also an imitation (*anukaraṇa*) [of a sound], provided that it is not followed by the word *iti*.
1.04.063 *sat* and *asat* are used for respect and disrespect, respectively. 1.04.064 *alam* is used in the sense of ornamentation. 1.04.065 *antar* is used in the sense of non-inclusion.
1.04.066 *kaṇemanas* [is compounded] with *śraddhā* and *pratīghāta*;
1.04.067 *puras*, being an indeclinable, [is compounded]; 1.04.068 and *astaṃ* [is also compounded].
1.4.69: *accha* [is used] in the sense of movement toward (*gati*) and in Vedic expressions (*vadeṣu*).
1.4.70: *adaḥ* [is used] when there is no instruction (*an-upadeśe*).
1.4.71: *tiraḥ* [is used] in the sense of disappearance (*antardhau*).
1.04.072 Optionally [the accusative case is used] with the root *kṛ* (to do/make).
1.04.073 [The accusative case is used] with *upāja* and *anvāja*.
1.04.074 And [the accusative case is used] with *sākṣāt* and the following words.

1.04.075 In *anatyādhāna*, [the first vowel is pluta] when referring to the chest (*uras*) and the mind (*manas*). 1.04.076 Also in *madhye*, *pade*, and *nivacane*. 1.04.077 In *haste* and *pāṇau*, it is always [pluta] when referring to taking hold (*upayamana*).
1.04.078 *prādhvam* [is used] in the sense of binding; 1.04.079 *jīvikā* and *upaniṣad* [are used] in the sense of comparison; 1.04.080 those two [terms] occur before the verbal root (*dhātu*).

1.04.081 In the Vedic language (chandasi), [the particle *iti*] may also follow [its word]; 1.04.082 [the particle *iti*] may also be separated [from its word] by intervening words; 1.04.083 [these rules apply to] the karmapravacanīyas.
1.04.084 *anu* [is used] in the sense of a mark (*lakṣaṇa*).
1.04.085 [It is used] in the sense of the third case (*tṛtīyā-artha*).
1.04.086 [It is used] in the sense of inferiority (*hīna*).
1.4.87: *upa* [is used] in the sense of "inferiority" (*adhika*) and [in the sense of "nearness"].
1.4.88: *apa* and *pari* [are used] in the sense of exclusion (*varjana*). 1.4.89: *āṅ* [is used] in the sense of a limit (*maryādā*).

1.4.90: The particles *prati*, *pari*, and *anu* are used with a word denoting a characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*), a state of being (*itthambhūta*), a description (*ākhyāna*), a part (*bhāga*), or distributive repetition (*vīpsā*). 1.4.91: The particle *abhi* is used [with a word denoting a characteristic, etc. except when it signifies a share (*abhāga*). 1.4.92: The particle *prati* is used in the sense of a representative (*pratinidhi*) or an exchange (*pratidāna*).

1.04.093 *adhi* and *pari* [are prefixes] when they are meaningless (i.e., devoid of their own specific meaning). 1.04.094 *su-* [is a prefix] in the sense of praise (*pūjā*). 1.04.095 *ati-* [is a prefix] also in the sense of transgression (*atikramaṇa*).

1.4.96 The particle *api* is used [as a karmapravacanīya] in the senses of: (a) the meaning of a word (*padārtha*), (b) possibility (*sambhāvanā*), (c) permission (*anvavasarga*), (d) censure (*garhā*), and (e) conjunction (*samuccaya*).
1.4.97 The preposition *adhi* is used [as a karmapravacanīya] in the sense of lordship (*īśvara*). 1.4.98 [The rule 1.4.97 applies] optionally (*vibhāṣā*) when the verb *kṛñ* ("to do") follows.

1.4.99: *laḥ* [the suffixes] are called *parasmaipada*. 1.4.100: *taṅ* and *āna* [the suffixes] are called *ātmanepada*. 1.4.101: Of the *tiṅ* suffixes, there are three each for the first, middle, and last [persons].
1.04.102 Those [suffixes] are, respectively, the singular, dual, and plural. 1.04.103 They are called *sUP*.
1.04.104 And they are also called *vibhakti* (case endings).

1.04.105 When *yuṣmad* is the co-occurring word (*upapada*) and is in grammatical apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*), the second person (*madhyama*) is used, even if [the verb] is not present (*sthānin*).

1.04.106 And in cases of jesting (*prahāsa*), when *manya* is the co-occurring word, the first person (*uttama*) is used for the root *man*, and it is treated as a singular (*ekavat*). 1.04.107 When *asmad* is the co-occurring word, the first person (*uttama*) is used.
1.04.108 When [the first person] remains, the first [person ending] is used.
1.04.109 The closest proximity [of sounds] is *saṃhitā* (euphonic combination).
1.04.110 Cessation [of sound] is *avasāna* (pause).
2.01.001 A rule concerning words applies when they are semantically connected (*samartha*).
2.01.002 A word ending in a case-suffix (*sUP*) used as a vocative (*āmantrita*) is treated as if it were non-existent (*para-aṛgavat*) with respect to accent (*svara*).
2.01.003 From here up to the word *kaḍāra*, the section on compounds (*samāsa*) begins.
2.01.004 [A word ending in] *sUP* [is compounded] with [another word].
2.01.005 [The resulting compound is called] *avyayībhāva*.

2.01.006 An indeclinable (*avyaya*) [is compounded with another word to form an *avyayībhāva*] when it expresses: case-relation (*vibhakti*), proximity (*samīpa*), prosperity (*samṛddhi*), decline (*vyṛddhi*), the absence of meaning (*arthābhāva*), passing away (*atyaya*), the sense of "not now" (*asamprati*), the appearance of a sound (*śabdaprādurbhāva*), "after" (*paścāt*), "according to" (*yathā*), sequence (*ānupūrvya*), simultaneity (*yaugapadya*), similarity (*sādṛśya*), perfection (*sampatti*), entirety (*sākalya*), or the expression of a limit (*antavacana*).
2.01.007 *yathā* [is used] in the sense of "unlike" (asādṛśya);
2.01.008 *yāvat* [is used] in the sense of limitation (avadhāraṇa); 2.01.009 a nominal suffix (*sUP*) with *prati* [is used] in the sense of measure (*mātrā*).

2.01.010 The numbers [denoting] dice and counting-sticks are used with *pari* [in the sense of exclusion]. 2.01.011 [The use of the fifth case ending] is optional [when these words are used with *pari*].
2.01.012 The words *apa*, *pari*, *bahis*, and those ending in *añcu* [are used with the fifth case ending when expressing exclusion].
2.01.013 *āṅ* [is used] in the senses of limit (*maryādā*) and inclusion (*abhividhi*).
2.01.014 *abhi* and *prati* [are used] with a sign (*lakṣaṇa*) in the sense of being face-to-face (*ābhimukhya*).
2.01.015 *anu* [is used] in the sense of "along" (*yatsamayā*).
2.01.016 And [the word] *yasya* (of which) [is compounded with a word ending in a case-suffix].
2.01.017 And the group beginning with *tiṣṭhadgu*.
2.01.018 *Pāre* (on the far side of) and *madhye* (in the middle of) [are compounded] optionally with a word in the genitive case.

2.01.019 A numeral [is compounded] with a word denoting lineage. 2.01.020 Also with words denoting rivers. 2.01.021 And [a numeral is compounded] with another word to form a name when it denotes something other than its own meaning.
2.01.022 Tatpuruṣa; 2.01.023 and Dvigu;
2.01.024 [A word ending] in the second case is compounded with *śrita*, *atīta*, *patita*, *gata*, *atyasta*, *prāpta*, and *āpanna*.
2.01.025 [A word ending in] *svayam* [is compounded] with a word ending in a *kta*-suffix.
2.01.026 [The compound] *khaṭvā* [is used] in the sense of reproach (*kṣepa*).
2.01.027 [The compound] *sāmi*.
2.01.028 [The word] *kāla* [is used in the accusative case when expressing duration]; 2.01.029 [the same applies] when expressing continuous connection (*atyanta-saṃyoga*);

2.01.030 the third case ending (*tṛtīyā*) is used [after a word denoting time] when it is connected with a word expressing purpose (*artha*) caused by that [time], provided the latter is a quality-word (*guṇa-vacana*).
2.01.031 [The word *pūrva* is compounded] with words having the senses of "similar," "equal," "less," "dispute," "skillful," "mixed," and "smooth.
2.01.032 [A word ending in a *kṛt* suffix] is frequently compounded with the agent or the instrument when used with another *kṛt*-formed word.
2.01.033 [A word ending in a *kṛt* suffix] is compounded with a word ending in a *kṛtya* suffix to express the sense of "excessive" or "more than."

2.01.034 [The sixth case is used] with *anna* (food) when it means "an accompaniment"; 2.01.035 with *bhakṣya* (edible food) when it means "mixed with"; 2.01.036 the fourth case is used with words meaning "for the sake of that" (*tad-artha*), as well as with *artha*, *bali*, *hita*, *sukha*, and *rakṣita*.
2.01.037 The fifth case [is used] with a word expressing fear (*bhaya*).
2.01.038 [The fifth case is used] optionally with the words *apeta*, *apoḍha*, *mukta*, *patita*, and *apatrasta*.
2.01.039 The words *stoka*, *antika*, *dūra*, and those having the sense of *artha* and *kṛcchra* [are used in the fifth case] with a past passive participle (*Kta*).
2.01.040 [A word ending in] the seventh case [is compounded] with *śauṇḍa* and similar words; 2.01.041 [It is compounded] also with *siddha*, *śuṣka*, *pakva*, and *bandha*;
2.01.042 [It is compounded] with *dhvāṅkṣa* when used in a reproachful sense.
2.01.043 [A compound ending in] a *kṛtya* suffix is used in the sense of a debt (*ṛṇa*). 2.01.044 [A compound ending in a *kṛtya* suffix is used] as a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
2.01.045 [Compounds] with the past passive participle suffix *kta* denote parts of days and nights (*ahorātra*).
2.01.046. In that [context], 2.01.047. when there is censure (kṣepa), 2.01.048. the *pātresamitā* and others [are used].

2.01.049: The words *pūrvakāla* (prior in time), *eka* (one), *sarva* (all), *jarat* (worn out), *purāṇa* (ancient), *nava* (new), and *kevala* (exclusive) form a compound when joined with a word in grammatical apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*).
2.01.050: A cardinal number and a direction word form a compound when they denote a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
2.01.051: A compound is formed [with a word denoting] the meaning of a secondary derivative suffix (*taddhita*), a final member of a compound (*uttarapada*), or a collective (*samāhāra*).

2.01.052 A *dvigu* compound consists of a numeral as its first member. 2.01.053 A word denoting the censurable is compounded with words expressing censure. 2.01.054 The words *pāpa* and *aṇaka* are compounded with words expressing censure.
2.01.055 Words expressing a standard of comparison are compounded with words expressing the common quality [of comparison].
2.01.056 A word denoting that which is compared is compounded with words such as *vyāghra* ("tiger") and the like, provided that the common quality is not explicitly expressed.
2.01.057 An adjective is frequently compounded with the noun it qualifies.
2.01.058 The words *pūrva*, *apara*, *prathama*, *carama*, *jaghanya*, *samāna*, *madhya*, *madhyama*, and *vīra* [form a tatpuruṣa compound with a word ending in a case-affix].

2.01.059 The group of words beginning with *śreṇi* [form a tatpuruṣa compound] with words beginning with *kṛta*. 2.01.060 [The same applies] with a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix that is not distinguished by the negative particle *nañ*, provided it is not itself distinguished by *nañ*.
2.01.061 *sat*, *mahat*, *parama*, *uttama*, and *utkṛṣṭa* are used when something is being honored by those worthy of honor;
2.01.062 [the suffix *ka* is added] to *vṛndāraka*, *nāga*, and *kuñjara* when they are being honored;
2.01.063 *katara* and *katama* are used in questions regarding genus (*jāti*).
2.01.064 The particle *kim* [is compounded] with a word expressing censure.
2.01.065 A genus-word (*jāti*) is compounded with *poṭā*, *yuvati*, *stoka*, *katipaya*, *gṛṣṭi*, *dhenu*, *vaśā*, *vehat*, *baṣkayaṇī*, *pravaktṛ*, *śrotriya*, *adhyāpaka*, and *dhūrta*.
2.01.066 And [it is compounded] with words expressing praise.
2.01.067 A young man [is compounded] with a bald man, a grey-haired man, one with wrinkles, or an old woman.
2.01.068 A word denoting a specific action is compounded with another word denoting a similar action, provided they do not denote a genus (*jāti*).
2.01.069 A color-word is compounded with another color-word.
2.01.070 A *kumāra* (prince/youth) [is compounded] with *śramaṇā* (female ascetic) and so forth;
2.01.071 A four-footed animal [is compounded] with a pregnant female (*garbhiṇī*);
2.01.072 And *mayūravyaṃsaka* (peacock-deceiver) and other such compounds.
2.02.001 *Pūrva*, *apara*, *adhara*, and *uttara* [are compounded] with a word denoting a whole (*ekadeśin*) to form a *tatpuruṣa* compound when referring to a single substratum (*adhikaraṇe*).

2.02.002 When *ardha* is neuter, [the compound is a *tatpuruṣa*]. 2.02.003 *Dvitīya*, *tṛtīya*, *caturtha*, and *turya* [are optionally compounded] with a word denoting a whole to form a *tatpuruṣa* compound.
2.02.004 The words *prāpta* and *āpanna* are used with a word in the accusative case [to form a compound].
2.02.005 Words denoting time (*kāla*) are used with a word denoting that which is measured by it (*parimāṇin*).
2.02.006 The negative particle *naÑ*.

2.02.007 [The sixth case ending is used] with words meaning "slightly" (īṣat) and those ending in -akṛta; 2.02.008 [the sixth case ending is used] with the genitive; 2.02.009 [the sixth case ending is used] with *yājaka* and others.

2.02.010 Not [with a word] used in the sense of selection (*nirdhāraṇa*). 2.02.011 Not [with a word] that is a ordinal number (*pūraṇa*), a quality (*guṇa*), the word *suhita*, a verbal derivative (*SAD*) having the sense of "being," an indeclinable (*avyaya*), a gerundive (*tavya*), or a word in grammatical apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*). 2.02.012 Nor with a past passive participle (*Kta*) when it signifies honor (*pūjā*).
2.02.013 And [the genitive case ending is used] with a word expressing the locus (*adhikaraṇa*).
2.02.014 And [the genitive case ending is used] for the object (*karman*).
2.02.015 [The genitive case ending is used] for the agent (*kartṛ*) with words ending in *tṛC* and *aka*.
2.02.016 And [the compound is formed] when the agent is expressed. 2.02.017 It is obligatory when [the compound denotes] play or a livelihood.
2.02.018 *ku*, the *gati*s, and *pra* and so forth [form compounds with a following word].
2.02.019 An *upapada* that does not end in a verbal suffix (*atiṅ*) [is compounded with a verb].
2.02.020 An indeclinable (*avyaya*) is compounded only with [a word ending in] the accusative case marker (*am*).
2.02.021 Words beginning with the third case ending [are optionally compounded with a verb].
2.02.022 And [a word ending] in *ktvā* [is compounded with another].
2.02.023 The remainder [of compounds not otherwise specified] is the *bahuvrīhi*. 2.02.024 [A compound consisting of] more than one word [is formed] in the sense of another word.

2.02.025 Numerals, indeclinables (*avyaya*), words meaning "near" (*āsanna*), "not far" (*adūra*), and "more than" (*adhika*) [are compounded] with a numeral when the sense is that of a specific number (*saṃkhyeya*).
2.02.026 Words denoting directions (*diś-nāman*) [are compounded] when referring to the space between them.
2.02.027 [The compound] *tatra-tenedam* (e.g., *tatreyaṃ śālā*, "this hall is there") occurs when the two members are identical in form (*sarūpa*).
2.02.028 *tena saha* (with that) [is used] in the sense of equality;
2.02.029 *ca* (and) [is used] in the sense of conjunction;
2.02.030 the subordinate member (*upasarjana*) [of a compound] comes first.
2.02.031 In the case of *rājadanta* and similar compounds, the subsequent member [is the first].
2.02.032 In a *dvandva* compound, a word ending in a *ghī*-suffix [is the first].
2.02.033 [In a *dvandva*,] that which begins with a vowel (*aC*) and ends in short *a* (*aT*) [is the first].
2.02.034 The shorter of two [words] ending in a vowel (aC) [is placed first]. 2.02.035 In a Bahuvrīhi compound, when a word in the locative case or a qualifier [is present, it is placed first].
2.02.036 A past passive participle (niṣṭhā) [is placed first].
2.02.037 [The particle] *vā* [is used] in connection with *āhitāgni* and others.

2.02.038 Words beginning with *kaḍāra* [are optionally placed first] in a *karmadhāraya* compound. 2.03.001 [The sixth case ending is used] when [the relation] is not already expressed [by another word].
2.03.002 The second case ending is used for the object of an action.
2.03.003 And the third case ending is also used [for the object] in the Vedic language.
2.03.004 [The third case ending is used] when associated with *antarā* and *antareṇa*.
2.03.005 When there is continuous connection between time and distance, [the third case ending is used].
2.03.006 When completion [of an action] is indicated, the third case ending is used.
2.03.007 The seventh and fifth case endings are used to express that which lies between two factors of action.
2.03.008 The second case ending is used after a word joined with a *karmapravacanīya*.
2.03.009 The seventh case ending is used where there is the sense of "more than" (*adhika*) or where there is the expression of "lordship over" (*īśvara*).
2.03.010 The fifth case ending is used with the prepositions *apa*, *āṅ*, and *pari*.

2.03.011 And [the fourth case-affix is used] after a word denoting a substitute or an exchange. 2.03.012 After a verb meaning "to go," when physical motion is involved and the object is not a road, both the second and the fourth case-affixes are used. 2.03.013 The fourth case-affix is used in the sense of the recipient (*sampradāna*).

2.03.014 And [the sixth case ending is used] for the object of a word that has a verbal root meaning as its upapada, provided that the verbal root is not itself the *stānin* (the original form). 2.03.015 Also [the sixth case ending is used] after a word expressing an abstract action (*bhāva*) which has the sense of the suffix *-tum*.
2.03.016 Also [the sixth case ending is used] after the words *namas*, *svasti*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *alam*, *vaṣaṭ*, and *ogha*.
2.03.017 The sixth case-affix is optionally used for the object of the verb *man* (to think) when it expresses disregard, provided the object is not a living being.
2.03.018 The third case-affix is used for the agent and the instrument.
2.03.019 When joined with the word *saha* (with), the third case-affix is used for the subordinate element.
2.03.020 [The third case ending is used] for that by which a modification of a limb occurs.
2.03.021 [The third case ending is used] to denote a characteristic mark of a state of being.
2.03.022 The term *saṃjñā* optionally [takes the third case ending] when it denotes the object of the action.
2.03.023 [The third case suffix is used] in the sense of cause (hetu).
2.03.024 The fifth case suffix is used for that which is not the agent (akartṛ) when it signifies a debt (ṛṇa).
2.03.025 Optionally (vibhāṣā), when expressing a quality (guṇa) that is not feminine.
2.03.026 The sixth case-affix is used when a word expressing a cause (*hetu*) is employed.
2.03.027 When a pronoun (*sarvanāman*) is used [to express a cause], the third case-affix may also be used.
2.03.028 The fifth case-affix is used in the sense of the ablative (*apādāna*).

2.03.029 When words meaning "other than," "different from," or "except for"—namely *anya*, *ārat*, *itara*, *ṛte*, as well as the word *dik* (direction) and words ending in *añc*—are used as the final members of a compound, and when a feminine suffix (*āC*) or the suffix *āhi* follows, [the sixth case is used].
2.03.030 The sixth case is used before a suffix having the sense of the suffix *atas*.
2.03.031 The second case is used before the suffix *enaP*.
2.03.032 When the words *pṛthak*, *vinā*, *nānā*, or those ending in *-ūn* are used, the third case suffix is optionally employed [along with the sixth].

2.03.033 And when expressing the instrument (*karaṇa*), the third case suffix is optionally employed for the words *stoka*, *alpa*, *kṛcchra*, and *atipatha*, provided they do not denote a substance (*asattvavacana*).
2.03.034 With words having the sense of "far" (*dūra*) or "near" (*antika*), the sixth case suffix is optionally employed [along with the third].
2.03.035 The second case ending is also used after words expressing distance or proximity.
2.03.036 The seventh case ending is used in the sense of location (adhikaraṇa). 2.03.037 [The seventh case ending is also used] for that by whose action another action is characterized.
2.03.038 The sixth case ending is also used [with a word] when disregard is expressed;
2.03.039 and [it is used] with the words *svāmin*, *īśvara*, *adhipati*, *dāyāda*, *sākṣin*, *pratibhū*, and *prasūta*.
2.03.040 [The fifth case ending is used] after the words *āyukta* and *kuśala* when they signify service (*āsevā*).
2.03.041 [The fifth case ending is used] from that which there is selection (*nirdhāraṇa*).
2.03.042 [The fifth case ending is used] in the sense of separation (*vibhakta*).
2.03.043 When *sādhu* and *nipuṇa* are used in the sense of worship (*arcā*), the seventh case ending is employed, provided they are not preceded by *prati*.
2.03.044 With *prasita* and *utsuka*, the third case ending is also employed.
2.03.045 And when [the word] *nakṣatra* is used with the elision of the suffix (*luP*).

2.03.046 The first case ending (*prathamā*) is used in the sense of the nominal stem (*prātipadika*), gender, measure, and number alone. 2.03.047 And [the first case ending is used] in the sense of address (*sambodhana*).
2.03.048 That [first case form] is called *āmantrita* (vocative).
2.03.049 The singular number [of the second person pronoun] is used in the vocative case.
2.03.050 The genitive case is used for the remaining relations.
2.03.051 The instrumental case is used for the instrument of a verb meaning "to know" (*jñā*) when it does not mean "to recognize."
2.03.052 [The sixth case ending is used] for the object of roots meaning "to rule over" (*adhi-i*), "to pity" (*dayā*), and "to lord it over" (*īś*);
2.03.053 [It is also used] for the object of the root *kṛñ* when it signifies "effort toward improvement" (*pratiyatna*);
2.03.054 [And it is used] for the object of roots meaning "to afflict" (*ruj-arthānām*) that denote a state (*bhāva-vacanānām*), with the exception of *jvar* ("to fever").
2.03.055 The root *nāth* is used in the sense of benediction (*āśis*).
2.03.056 The roots *jās*, *ni*, *pra-han*, *nāṭ*, *krāth*, and *piṣ* are used in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*).
2.03.057 The roots *vy-ava-hṛ* and *paṇ* are used when they have a common meaning (*samarthayoḥ*).
2.03.058 [The sixth case ending is used] for the word *div* and its synonyms when they signify time.
2.03.059 [The sixth case ending is used] optionally when a preverb (*upasarga*) is present. 2.03.060 The second case ending is used [after a word signifying time] when it refers to a Brāhmaṇa.
2.03.061 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the roots *pra-iṣ* and *brū*, when the object is an oblation (*havis*) offered to a deity.
2.03.062 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *ghañ* is frequently used in the sense of the dative case.
2.03.063 And [the suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the root *yaj* in the sense of the instrumental case.

2.03.064 When used in connection with words having the sense of *kṛtvas* (times), the locative case is used for time as the locus. 2.03.065 With a *kṛt* suffix, the sixth case is used for both the agent and the object. 2.03.066 When there is the possibility of both [agent and object] being expressed, the sixth case is used for the object.

2.03.067 [The sixth case ending is used] after a word denoting the object when it occurs with a present participle. 2.03.068 [The sixth case ending is used] after a word expressing the locus (adhikaraṇa).

2.03.069 [The sixth case ending is not used] after words ending in *la*, *u*, *uka*, indeclinables (*avyaya*), past participles (*niṣṭhā*), *KHaL* suffixes, words having the sense of *artha*, or *tṚN*.

2.03.070 The sixth case ending is used for the agent or the object of a verb ending in *aka* or *in*, when it denotes the future or a debt. 2.03.071 The sixth case ending is optionally used for the agent of verbs formed with *kṛtya* suffixes.
2.03.072 When used with words having the sense of "equal," except for *tulā* and *upamā*, the third case ending is optionally used.
2.03.073 The dative case ending is also used to express a blessing when combined with the words *āyuṣya*, *madra*, *bhadra*, *kuśala*, *sukha*, *artha*, and *hita*.
2.04.001 A *dvigu* compound is singular in number.
2.04.002 And a *dvandva* compound consisting of names of living beings is also singular.

In the enumeration of musical instruments, armies, and Ṛgvedic hymns (2.04.003), and in the enumeration of Vedic schools (caraṇas) (2.04.004), the term *adhvaryu-kratu* (a sacrifice performed by an Adhvaryu priest) is not neuter.
2.04.005 For words whose designations are not separated by study [of the Veda],
2.04.006 the genus (*jāti*) of non-living things [is compounded], and 2.04.007 a river and a country distinguished by their specific names, provided they are not villages.
2.04.008 Small creatures;
2.04.009 those whose enmity is perpetual;
2.04.010 Śūdras who have not been exiled.
2.04.011 And [the compounds] beginning with *gavāśva* (cow-and-horse) [are neuter].
2.04.012 Optionally [the neuter gender applies] to compounds consisting of *vṛkṣa*, *mṛga*, *tṛṇa*, *dhānya*, *vyañjana*, *paśu*, *śakuni*, *aśva-vaḍava*, and *pūrvāpara-adharottara*.
2.04.013 And [optionally neuter] is that which expresses a contradiction (*vipratiṣiddha*), provided it does not denote a location (*an-adhikaraṇa-vāci*).
2.04.014 Not [the suffix *kan* is applied] after words such as *dadhi* (curd) and *payaḥ* (milk).
2.04.015 Also [not applied] when the sense is that of the limit of the locus (*adhikaraṇa*). 2.04.016 Optionally [the suffix *kan* is applied] when there is proximity.
2.04.017 That [compound] is neuter.
2.04.018 And the *avyayībhāva* [is neuter]. 2.04.019 A *tatpuruṣa* that does not contain the negative particle *naÑ* and is not a *karmadhāraya* [is neuter].

2.04.020 *kanthā* [is used] in the sense of a name when referring to the Uśīnaras. 2.04.021 *upajñā* and *upakrama* [are used] when there is a desire to express that as the beginning [of something]. 2.04.022 *chāyā* [is used] in the sense of abundance.

2.04.023 The word *sabhā* [is compounded with a word ending in] *rājan* when it does not have a non-human being as its prior member; 2.04.024 and [it is also so compounded] when it does not mean a hall.
2.04.025 The feminine suffix is optionally applied to *senā*, *surā*, *chāyā*, *sālā*, and *niśā*.

2.04.026 In a *dvandva* and a *tatpuruṣa* compound, the gender is like that of the final member (*paravat*). 2.04.027 In the case of *aśva-vaḍavau*, the gender is like that of the first member (*pūrvavat*).

2.04.028 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the words *hemanta* (winter) and *śiśira* (cool season), as well as *ahar* (day) and *rātri* (night), are optionally neuter. 2.04.029 The words *rātra*, *ahan*, and *aha* are masculine. 2.04.030 The word *apatha* (a bad path) is neuter.
2.04.031 The words *ardharca* and others [listed in the *gaṇapāṭha*] may optionally be masculine as well.
2.04.032 When *idam* is used in subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), the substitute *aś* is anudātta when it occurs at the beginning of the third case and following cases.
2.04.033 When *etad* is used in subsequent reference, the substitutes *tra* and *tas* are anudātta, and these forms *tra* and *tas* themselves are also anudātta.
2.04.034 *dvitīyā-tā-au-su-enah* (the second case ending, the suffix *tā*, the suffixes *au* and *su*, and the substitute *ena* [replace the final vowel and following consonant of a verbal root]).
2.04.035 *ārdhadhātuke* (in the context of an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix).
2.04.036 *ado jagdhir Lyap ti K-it-i* (the substitute *jagdhi* replaces the root *ad-* before the gerund suffix *Lyap* and before a suffix beginning with *K* that has an indicatory *i*).

2.04.037 *ghasḷ* is substituted for the roots *ad* and *jakṣ* before the suffixes *luṅ* and *san*. 2.04.038 It is also substituted for those roots before the suffixes *ghañ* and *ap*. 2.04.039 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this substitution occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
2.04.040 In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], [the substitution of *aṅ* for the root] is optional. 2.04.041 For the root *veñ*, there is the substitution of *vayi*.
2.04.042 For the root *han*, there is the substitution of *vadha* in the *liṅ* [optative mood].
2.04.043 And [the substitution of *gā* occurs] before the suffix *luṅ*.
2.04.044 Optionally, [the substitution of *gā* occurs] before the *ātmanepada* suffixes.
2.04.045 [The substitution of *gā* occurs] for the root *iṇ* before the suffix *luṅ*.

2.04.046: The root *gam* is substituted [for *iṇ*] before the causative suffix *ṇic*, except when it means "to understand. 2.04.047: [The substitution of *gam* for *iṇ* occurs] also before the desiderative suffix *saN*.
2.04.048: [The substitution of *gam* for *iṇ* occurs] also after the root *iṅ* ("to study").
2.04.049: The substitution of *gāṅ* occurs in place of the root *iṅ* before the *liṭ* suffix. 2.04.050: The substitution of *gāṅ* is optional (*vibhāṣā*) before the *luṅ* and *lṛṅ* suffixes.
2.04.051: The substitution of *gāṅ* also occurs before the causative suffix *ṇic* as well as before the *saṅ* and *caṅ* suffixes.
2.04.052 *aster bhūḥ* (the root *bhū* replaces *as*); 2.04.053 *bruvo vaciḥ* (the root *vac* replaces *brū*); 2.04.054 *cakṣiṄaḥ khyāÑ* (the root *khyā* replaces *cakṣiṄ*).
2.04.055 Or [the substitution of *vī* for *aj*] occurs before the *liṭ* suffix.
2.04.056 [The substitution of *vī* for *aj* occurs] except before *GHaÑ* and *aP*.
2.04.057 Optionally [the substitution of *vī* for *aj* occurs] before the suffix *y*.

2.04.058 The suffixes *Ṇya*, those following a *kṣatriya* name, those following an *ārṣa* name, and those ending in *Ñ* or *IT* are elided (*luK*) when forming a secondary derivative (*yūni*) denoting a grandson or later descendant, provided that the primary suffix *aṆ* or *iÑ* has been elided.
2.04.059 [The suffix *iÑ*] is also elided after the group beginning with *paila*.
2.04.060 [The suffix *iÑ*] is elided after a patronymic suffix (*iÑ*) belonging to the easterners (*prācām*).

2.04.061 Not from the descendants of Taulvali. 2.04.062 For a word denoting a tribal ruler (*tad-rāja*), when many [such rulers] are intended, the suffix *aṇ* is used by that very same rule, provided it does not refer to a feminine. 2.04.063 From the group beginning with Yaska, when denoting a lineage (*gotra*).
2.04.064. Also after [stems ending in] *yaÑ* and *aÑ*.
2.04.065. And after [the names of] Atri, Bhṛgu, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Gotama, and Aṅgiras.
2.04.066. After a [patronymic] formed with *iÑ* that has more than two syllables, when [the descendants] belong to the Easterners or the Bharatas.
2.04.067 Not [the suffix *cha*] after [words beginning with] *gopa-vana*.
2.04.068 [The suffix *cha*] does not occur after [words beginning with] *tika-kitava* when they form a *dvandva* compound.
2.04.069 After [words beginning with] *upaka*, [the suffix *cha*] may optionally [occur] when they do not form a *dvandva* compound.
2.04.070 For *Āgastya* and *Kauṇḍinya*, [the final syllable] becomes *agasti* and *kuṇḍinaC*.

2.04.071 [The substitution of *Śi* for the case endings] occurs in place of the *suP* [case endings] when they follow verbal roots (*dhātu*) and nominal stems (*prātipadika*). 2.04.072 After [verbal roots] beginning with *ad*, the suffix *ŚaP* [is added].

2.04.073 In the Vedic language (chandas), [the substitution of *śap* for *aṅ*] occurs diversely (*bahulam*). 2.04.074 [The substitution of *śap* for *aṅ* occurs] after the suffix *yaṅ* and before a vowel-initial affix (*aci*).
2.04.075 The elision (*ślau*) [of *aṅ*] occurs after the roots beginning with *juhoti*.
2.04.076. In the Vedic language (chandas), [the substitution of *iṭ*] occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
2.04.077. After the roots √gā, √sthā, those ending in GHU, √pā, and √bhū, the augment *iṭ* is not added to the *sIC* suffix when used in the parasmaipada.
2.04.078. Optionally (*vibhāṣā*), [the augment *iṭ* is not added to the *sIC* suffix] after the roots √ghrā, √dheṬ, √śā, √chā, and √sa.
2.04.079: After the roots *tan* and others, the suffixes *ta* and *thās* are replaced by *liṭ*.
2.04.080: In a mantra, the suffix *liṭ* is replaced by *luṅ* after the roots *ghas*, *hvar*, *naś*, *vṛ*, *dah*, *āp*, *vṛc*, *kṛ*, *gam*, and *jan*.
2.04.081: [The suffix *liṭ* is replaced by *luṅ*] after the root *ām*.
2.04.082 [The case endings] āP and sUP are elided after an indeclinable (avyaya).
2.04.083 After an indeclinable compound (avyayībhāva) ending in a short a, the case ending am is substituted for all case endings except the fifth (pañcamī).
2.04.084 After an indeclinable compound ending in a short a, the third and seventh case endings are diversely (bahulam) substituted by am.

2.04.085: For the first person of the *luṭ* [future tense], there are the substitutes *ḍā*, *rau*, and *ras*. 3.01.001: A suffix (*pratyaya*) [is placed after a verbal root]. 3.01.002: And it follows [the element that has been designated as the base].

3.01.003 And [the suffix] has its first syllable udātta. 3.01.004 The case endings (sUP) and the kṛt suffixes marked with P and IT are anudātta. 3.01.005 The desiderative suffix saN is added after roots ending in gup, after tij, and after those marked with K.
3.01.006: After the roots *mān*, *badh*, *dān*, and *śān*, the augment *iC* is added, and there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).
3.01.007: Optionally, when a desire for an action is expressed, the suffix *iC* is added after a verbal root that has the same agent as its object (*samānakartṛka*).
3.01.008: The suffix *KyaC* is added after a word ending in a case-suffix (*sUP*) that denotes the self (*ātman*).

3.01.009 And [the suffix *Kya*] is also used after a word expressing something desired (*kāmya*). 3.01.010 [The suffix *Kya*] is used after a word denoting a standard of comparison (*upamāna*) in the sense of behaving like that. 3.01.011 The suffix *Kyaṅ* is used after a word denoting the agent (*kartṛ*), and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the final syllable.

3.01.012 After the words *bhṛśa* and others, when used with the sense of becoming (*bhuvi*), there is the suffix *Kyaṅ*, and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the final consonant (*haL*) [of the stem], provided it is not the suffix *Cvi*. 3.01.013 After the words *lohita* and others, and after those ending in the suffix *ḌāC*, the suffix *Kyaṣ* is applied. 3.01.014 The suffix *Kyaṣ* is applied after the word *kaṣṭa* in the sense of making an effort toward it (*kramaṇe*).

3.01.015 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the word *karman*, when combined with *romantha* and *tapas*, provided that the meanings "subsisting" (*vartin*) and "practicing austerity" (*carin*) are respectively expressed.
3.01.016 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the words *bāṣpa* and *ūṣman*, when combined with the prefix *ud*, in the sense of "vomiting.
3.01.017 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the words *śabda*, *vaira*, *kalaha*, *abhra*, *kaṇva*, and *megha*, when combined with the prefix *ā*, in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇa*).
3.01.018 The affix *Kyaṅ* is applied after words beginning with *sukha*, when the agent experiences the feeling [expressed by the root].
3.01.019 The affix *KyaC* is applied after *namas*, *varivas*, and *citraṅ*.
3.01.020 The affix *ṆiṄ* is applied after *puccha*, *bhāṇḍa*, and *cīvara*.

3.01.021 The affix *ṆiC* is applied after the words *muṇḍa*, *miśra*, *ślakṣṇa*, *lavaṇa*, *vrata*, *vastra*, *hala*, *kala*, *kṛta*, and *tūsta*. 3.01.022 The affix *yaṄ* is applied after a verbal root that consists of a single vowel, begins with a consonant, and denotes the repetition of an action. 3.01.023 In the sense of crookedness of movement, *yaṄ* is applied invariably.
3.01.024 The affix *ghañ* is applied after the verbal roots *lup*, *sad*, *car*, *jap*, *jabh*, *dah*, *daś*, and *gṛ* when there is a censure (*garhā*) regarding the action itself.

3.01.025 The affix *ghañ* is applied after the following words [as the first members of a compound] to form a Bahuvrīhi: *satya*, *āpa*, *pāśa*, *rūpa*, *vīṇā*, *tūla*, *śloka*, *senā*, *loman*, *tvac*, and *varman*.
The suffix *ṆiC* is applied after [roots] such as *varṇa*, *cūrṇa*, and *cur* when a causal agent (*hetumat*) is expressed; likewise,
the suffix *yaK* is applied after [roots] such as *kaṇḍū*.

3.01.028 The suffix *āya* is added after the roots *gup*, *dhūp*, *vicch*, and the roots *paṇi* and *pani*. 3.01.029 The suffix *īyaṅ* is added after the root *ṛtīy*. 3.01.030 The suffix *ṇiṅ* is added after the root *kam*.
3.01.031 The [affixes] *āya* and so forth are optionally [treated as *ārdhadhātuka*] before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix.
3.01.032 Verbal roots (*dhātu*) ending with *saN* and so forth [are treated as roots].
3.01.033 The affixes *sya* and *tās* [are applied] before the suffixes of the future (*lṛṭ*) and the periphrastic future (*luṭ*).
3.01.034 The suffix *siP* is frequently applied after [a verbal root] in the *leṭ* mood.

3.01.035 After a verbal root ending in the suffix *kās*, the suffix *ām* is applied in the *liṭ* mood, except in mantras. 3.01.036 The suffix *ām* is also applied after a root beginning with a vowel (*iC*) that contains a heavy syllable (*gurumat*), provided it does not end in *ṛ* or *cch*.
3.01.037 After roots ending in *day*, *ay*, *ās*, and *aś*, [the suffix *liṭ* takes the augment *kvasu*].
3.01.038 After the roots *uṣ*, *vid*, and *jāgṛ*, [the suffix *kvasu* is optionally used for *liṭ*].
3.01.039 After the roots *bhī*, *hrī*, *bhṛ*, and *hu*, [the suffix *kvasu* is optionally used for *liṭ*,] and it behaves like *Ślu*.
3.01.040 The root *kṛ* is also employed with the suffix *liṭ*. 3.01.041 Optionally, [the form] *vidāṃkurvantu* is used.
3.01.042 In the Vedic language, [the following forms are used]: *abhyutsādayām*, *prajanayām*, *cikayām*, *ramayām*, *akam*, *pāvayām*, *kriyāt*, *vidām*, and *akran*.
3.01.043 *cli* is replaced by *luṅ*. 3.01.044 *siC* is substituted for *cli*.
3.01.045 *Ksa* is substituted for *śal* (the suffixes *liṭ*, *luṅ*, and *lṛṅ*) when it follows a verbal root that has *iK* as its penultimate (*upadha*) vowel and does not take the augment *iṬ*.
3.01.046 After the root *śliṣ*, [the augment *aṭ* is not applied] when it means embracing. 3.01.047 [The augment *aṭ* is not applied] after the root *dṛś*.
3.01.048 After the roots *ṇi*, *śri*, *dru*, and *sru*, [the augment *aṭ* is applied] before the *Caṅ* suffix when the agent (*kartṛ*) is expressed.

3.01.049 Optionally [the suffix *liṭ* takes the augment *ām*] after the roots *dheṭ* and *śvi*. 3.01.050 [The suffix *liṭ* takes the augment *ām*] after the root *gup* in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
3.01.051 [The suffix *liṭ* does not take the augment *ām*] after the roots *ūnayati*, *dhvanayati*, *elayati*, and *ardayati*.
3.01.052 The suffix *aṅ* is applied after the roots *as* (to throw), *vac* (to speak), and *khyā* (to tell).
3.01.053 The suffix *aṅ* is also applied after the roots *lip* (to smear), *sic* (to sprinkle), and *hve* (to call).
3.01.054 In the case of the *ātmanepada* endings, the application [of the suffix *aṅ*] is optional.
3.01.055 The roots beginning with *puṣ* and those beginning with *dyut* that have *ḷT* as an *it* [augment] take the *parasmaipada* endings.
3.01.056 Also after the roots *sṛ*, *tiṣṭhā* (*sthā*), *śās*, and *ṛ*.
3.01.057 After a root that has *IR* as an *it* [augment], the *parasmaipada* endings are optionally used.
3.01.058 [The suffix *aṅ* is applied] after the roots *jṝ*, *stanbhū*, *mruc*, *mluc*, *gruc*, *gluc*, *glunc*, *śvi*, and [the root *as*].
3.01.059 [The suffix *aṅ* is applied] after the roots *kṛ*, *mṛ*, *dṛ*, and *ruh* in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
3.01.060 The suffix *CiṆ* is applied to the root *pad* when it is used with the second person.
3.01.061 The suffix *hyat* is optionally used after the roots *dīp*, *jan*, *budh*, *pūr*, *tāy*, *pyāy*.
3.01.062 The suffix *hyat* is used [optionally] after a root ending in a vowel other than *a* when the agent is also the object (*karmakartṛ*). 3.01.063 And also after the root *duh*.
3.01.064 Not after the root *rudh*. 3.01.065 And [not] after *tap* when it means repentance. 3.01.066 The suffix *CiṆ* occurs in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*) or the object (*karman*).

3.01.067 *yak* is added after a verbal root before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix. 3.01.068 *ŚaP* is added [after a verbal root] when the agent (*kartṛ*) is expressed. 3.01.069 *ŚyaN* is added after roots belonging to the *div*-class and others.
3.01.070 The suffix *naṅ* is applied after the roots *bhrāś*, *bhlāś*, *bhram*, *kram*, *klam*, *tras*, *truṭ*, and *laṣ*.
3.01.071 The suffix *naṅ* is applied after the root *yas* when it is not preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*). 3.01.072 And [the suffix *naṅ* is applied] after *yas* even when preceded by *sam*.
3.01.073 The suffix *Śnu* is added after [roots] beginning with *su*.
3.01.074 For the root *śru*, there is the substitution of *śṛ* [before the suffix *Śnu*].
3.01.075 For the root *akṣ*, [the substitution of *śṛ* occurs] optionally.
3.01.076 The suffix *tak* is applied after the root *takṣ* in the sense of making thin.
3.01.077 The suffix *Śa* is applied after the roots beginning with *tud*.
3.01.078 The suffix *Śnam* is applied after the roots beginning with *rudh*.
3.01.079: After the roots beginning with *tan* and after *kṛñ*, the suffix *u* is added [to form the present stem].
3.01.080: After the roots *dhinv* and *kṛṇv*, the suffix *u* is added, and the final vowel of the root is replaced by *a*.
3.01.081: After the roots beginning with *krī*, the suffix *Śnā* is added [to form the present stem].

3.01.082 After the roots *stanbh*, *stunbh*, *skanbh*, *skunbh*, and *sku*, the suffix *Śnu* is also applied. 3.01.083 For a root ending in a consonant (*haL*), the suffix *Śānac* is substituted for *Śna* when the personal endings *hi* and *hu* follow. 3.01.084 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *Śāyac* is also applied [after a root ending in a consonant].
3.01.085 There is extensive transposition [of suffixes].

3.01.086 The *aṅ* suffix occurs after a verbal root when the *liṅ* (optative) is used in the sense of benediction (*āśis*). 3.01.087 An action whose operation is similar to that of the object is treated like the object (*karmavat*).
3.01.088: The suffix *tap* is applied only to the root *tap* when it has "austerity" (*tapas*) as its object.
3.01.089: The suffixes *yaK* and *CiṆ* are not applied after the roots *duh*, *snu*, and *nam*.
3.01.090: According to the Eastern grammarians, the suffix *ŚyaN* and the *parasmaipada* endings are applied after the roots *kuṣ* and *rañj*.
3.01.091 [A suffix] is applied after a verbal root (dhātu).
3.01.092 In that context, that which stands in the locative case is the *upapada*.
3.01.093 A *kṛt* suffix is applied when it is not a *tiṅ* suffix.
3.01.094 An affix not having the same form [as another] is optionally [used], except in the feminine gender.
3.01.095 The *kṛtya* affixes, as well as *prāc* and *ṇvul*, [are used after roots].
3.01.096 The affixes *tavyat*, *tavya*, and *anīyar* [are used after roots].
3.01.097 *yaT* [is added] after a word ending in *aC*.
3.01.098 [The suffix *yaT* is added] after a word ending in *pU*, provided that *aT* precedes it as a penultimate letter (*upadhā*).
3.01.099 [The suffix *yaT* is added] also after the roots *śaki* and *śah*.

3.01.100 *gadā-mada-cara-yamaḥ* [take the *ātmanepada*] when not preceded by a prefix (*anupasarga*). 3.01.101 *avadya-panya-varyāḥ* [take the *ātmanepada*] in the senses of "blameworthy" (*garhya*), "to be sold" (*paṇitavya*), and "not being obstructed" (*anirodha*) respectively. 3.01.102 *vahayaṃ karaṇam* [the word *vahyaṃ* takes the *ātmanepada*] when it denotes an instrument (*karaṇa*).
3.01.103 An *ārya* is the [term] for a master and a Vaiśya. 3.01.104 *Upasaryā* means "fit for breeding" (in the case of a cow). 3.01.105 *Ajaryam* means "enduring union."

3.01.106. After the root *vad*, when followed by a case-ending (*sUP*), the suffix *KyaP* is also applied. 3.01.107. After the root *bhū*, [the suffix *KyaP*] is applied in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*). 3.01.108. After the root *han*, the suffix *taC* is applied [in the sense of the abstract state].
3.01.109: The suffix *KyaP* is applied after the roots *i*, *stu*, *sās*, *vṛ*, *dṛ*, and *juṣ*.
3.01.110: The suffix *KyaP* is also applied after a root ending in *ṛ* as its penultimate letter (*ṛt-upadha*), except for the roots *kḷp* and *cṛt*.
3.01.111: And the vowel *ī* is substituted [for the final *a*] of the root *khan* when *KyaP* follows.

3.01.112 *bhṛÑ* [takes *kyap*] except when it denotes a name. 3.01.113 *mṛj* [takes *kyap*] optionally. 3.01.114 *rājasūya*, *sūrya*, *mṛṣodya*, *rucya*, *kupya*, *kṛṣṭapacya*, and *avyathya* [are formed with *kyap*].
3.01.115 *bhidya* and *uddhya* [are used] for a river;
3.01.116 *puṣya* and *sidhya* [are used] for a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*);
3.01.117 *vipūya*, *vinīya*, and *jitya* [are used] for *muñja* grass, *kalka* paste, and a plough, respectively.
3.01.118 The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *grah* when preceded by *prati* or *api*, in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
3.01.119 And [the suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the root *grah* when preceded by *pada*, *asvairin*, *bāhya*, and *pakṣya*.

3.01.120 The suffix *kvi* is optionally applied after the roots *kṛ* and *vṛṣ*. 3.01.121 And the suffix *yuc* is applied when the word refers to a leaf (*pattra*). 3.01.122 The form *amāvāsya* is optionally used [in place of *amāvāsyā*].

3.01.123 In the sense of Vedic meters (*chandas*), the following words are formed with the suffix *kyap*: *niṣṭarkya*, *devahūya*, *praṇīya*, *unnīya*, *ucchiṣya*, *marya*, *staryā*, *adhvaryu*, *khanya*, *khānya*, *devayajya*, *āpṛcchya*, *pratiṣīvya*, *brahmavādya*, *bhāvya*, *stāvya*, *upacāyya*, and *pṛḍā*.
3.01.124 The suffix *ṇyat* is applied after verbal roots ending in *ṛ* or a consonant (*haL*).
3.01.125 The suffix *ṇyat* is applied after a root ending in *o* when the sense is "necessity" (*āvaśyaka*).
3.01.126 The suffix *ya* is applied after the roots *āp*, *su*, *yu*, *vapi*, *rapi*, *lapi*, *trapi*, and *cam*.
3.01.127 *Ānāyya* is used when [the fire] is not permanent.
3.01.128 *Praṇāyya* is used when there is no respect [for the person].

3.01.129 The words *pāyya*, *sāṃnāyya*, *nikāyya*, and *dhāyyā* [are derived with the suffix -ya] in the senses of a measure, an oblation, a dwelling, and *sāmidhenī* verses, respectively. 3.01.130 In the sense of a sacrifice (*kratu*), the words *kuṇḍapāyya* and *saṃcāyya* [are formed].
3.01.131 In the sense of fire (*agni*), the words *paricāyya*, *upacāyya*, and *samūhya* [are formed].
3.01.132. And [the suffix *kyap*] is applied after the roots *cit* and *agnicit*. 3.01.133. The suffixes *ṇvul* and *tṛc* [are applied after verbal roots].
3.01.134. The suffixes *lyu*, *ṇini*, and *ac* are applied respectively after the group of roots beginning with *nand*, *grah*, and *pac*.
3.01.135: After verbal roots ending in *i*, *u*, or *ṛ* as penultimate vowels (*ik-upadha*), and after the roots *jñā*, *prī*, and *kṛ*, the suffix *Ka* is applied.
3.01.136: Also after a root ending in long *ā* (*āt*) when a prefix (*upasarga*) is present.
3.01.137: After the roots *pā*, *ghrā*, *dhmā*, *dheṭ*, and *dṛś*, the suffix *Śa* is applied.

3.01.138: After a verbal root that does not have a prefix (*anupasarga*), the suffix *ka* is applied to the roots *limpa*, *vinda*, *dhāri*, *pāri*, *vedi*, *udeji*, *ceti*, *sāti*, *sāhi*, and *hya*. 3.01.139: After the roots *dā* (to give) and *dhā* (to place), the suffix *ka* is optionally applied.
3.01.140: The suffix *ṇa* is applied after roots beginning with *jval* and after those ending in the suffix *kvasu*.

3.01.141 After the roots *śyai* (with the augment *ā*), *vyadh*, *ā-sru*, *saṃ-sru*, *ati-iṇ*, *ava-sā*, *ava-hṛ*, *lih*, *śliṣ*, and *śvas*, [the suffix *kta* is added in the sense of the agent]. 3.01.142 After the roots *du* and *nyo*, when no prefix (*upasarga*) precedes them, [the suffix *kta* is added in the sense of the agent]. 3.01.143 After the root *grah*, [the suffix *kta* is added in the sense of the agent] optionally.
3.01.144 *Kaḥ* [is added] after *geha*. 3.01.145 *ṢvuN* [is added] after [a word meaning] "artisan" (*śilpin*).
3.01.146 *thakaN* [is added] after *gas*.
3.01.147. And the suffix *ṇyuṭ*.
3.01.148. Also the suffix *ha*, when denoting *vrīhi* (rice) or *kāla* (time).
3.01.149. The suffix *vuṇ* is added after the roots *pru*, *sṛ*, and *lū* in the sense of repeated action (*samabhihāra*).
3.01.150 And [the suffix *aṅ* is used] in the sense of a blessing (*āśis*).
3.02.001 The suffix *aṆ* is used after a verbal root ending in a consonant when it denotes the object (*karman*).
3.02.002 Also after the roots *hve*, *vā*, and *ama*.
3.02.003 *Ka* is added after *ātaḥ* (a verbal root ending in long *ā*) when no prefix (*an-upasarga*) precedes it.
3.02.004 *Kha* is added after the root *sthā* when followed by a case-ending (*sUP*).
3.02.005 *Kha* is added after the roots *parimṛj* and *apanud* respectively when followed by the words *tunda* and *śoka*.
