3.02.006 [The suffix *ṇvi* is applied after roots ending in *dā* and *jñā*.
3.02.007 [The suffix *ṇvi* is applied after the root *khyā* when preceded by *sam-*.
3.02.008 [The suffix *ṭak* is applied after the roots *gā* and *pā*.]

3.02.009. The suffix *aC* is applied after the root *hṛ* when it does not mean "to undertake. 3.02.010. [The suffix *aC* is applied] also when it refers to age. 3.02.011. [The suffix *aC* is applied] after the prefix *āṄ* when it denotes habitual disposition (*tācchīlya*).
3.02.012 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a verbal root ending in] *arh*.
3.02.013 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the roots] *rami* and *japi* when combined with the prefixes *stamba-* and *karṇa-* respectively.
3.02.014 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after the root *śam* when used in the sense of a technical name (*saṃjñā*).

3.02.015 [The suffix *kha* is applied] after the root *śī* (to lie) when it occurs in a locative compound (*adhikaraṇe*). 3.02.016 [The suffix] *ṭa* is applied after the root *car* (to move). 3.02.017 [The suffix *ṭa* is applied] after the roots *bhikṣ* (to beg), *senā* (army), and *ā-dā* (to take) when they occur in a locative compound.

3.02.018 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the root *sṛ* when preceded by *puras*, *agratas*, or *agre*. 3.02.019 [The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *sṛ*] when preceded by *pūrva*, provided that the agent is indicated. 3.02.020 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the root *kṛ* when preceded by *pūrva*, in the sense of motive, habitual disposition, or compliance.

3.02.021 After *divā*, *vibhā*, *niśā*, *prabhā*, *bhās*, *kāra*, *anta*, *ananta*, *ādi*, *bahu*, *nāndī*, *kim*, *lipi*, *libi*, *bali*, *bhakti*, *kartṛ*, *citra*, *kṣetra*, *saṃkhyā*, *jaṛghā*, *bāhu*, *ahan*, *yad*, and *tad*,
[the suffix *ṭhañ*] is applied in the sense of "wages" (*bhṛtau*).
3.02.023 This does not apply after the words *śabda*, *śloka*, *kalaha*, *gāthā*, *vaira*, *cāṭu*, *sūtra*, *mantra*, and *pada*.
3.02.024 The suffix *iN* is applied after the roots [√sthā and √hṛ] when combined with the words *stamba-* and *śakṛt* respectively.
3.02.025 The suffix *iN* is applied after the root √hṛ when combined with the words *dṛti-* and *nātha*, provided the agent is an animal.
3.02.026 The forms *phale-grahi-* and *ātmambhari-* are irregularly formed.
3.02.027: After the verbal roots *van*, *san*, *rakṣ*, and *math*, the suffix *chandas* (the Vedic language) [is applied].
3.02.028: After the root *ej*, the suffix *KHaŚ* [is applied].
3.02.029: After the roots *dhmā* and *dheṭ*, the suffix *KHaŚ* is applied when combined with the words *nāsikā* and *stanau* respectively.
3.02.030 And [the suffix *ka* is applied] after the words *nāḍī* and *muṣṭi*.
3.02.031 After the prefix *ud-* followed by *kūla*, the suffix *ka* is applied when it means "disease" or "carrying away.
3.02.032 After the root *lih* preceded by *vaha* and *abhra*, the suffix *ka* is applied.
3.02.033 After the root *pac*, [the suffix *kha* is applied] when a measure word (*parimāṇa*) follows. 3.02.034 Also when *mita* and *nakha* follow.
3.02.035 After the root *tud*, [the suffix *kha* is applied] when *vidhu* or *aruṣ* follows.
3.02.036: After the words *asūrya* and *lalāṭa*, the suffix *KHa* is applied when combined with *dṛś* and *tapa* respectively.
3.02.037: The suffix *KHa* is applied after the roots *paś* (to see), *ir* (to go), *mad* (to be intoxicated), and *pāṇi* (hand), when preceded by *ugra*, *ira*, *mada*, and *pāṇi* respectively.
3.02.038: The suffix *KHaC* is applied after the root *vad* (to speak) when preceded by *priya* or *vaśa*.
3.02.039 After the words *dviṣat* and *para*, [the suffix *khaś* is applied] to the root *tap*.
3.02.040 After the word *vāc*, [the suffix *khaś* is applied to the root *yam*] when it denotes a religious observance (*vrata*).
3.02.041 After the words *pur* and *sarva*, [the suffix *khaś* is applied to the roots] *dṛ* and *sah* respectively.

3.02.042 After the root *kaṣ*, [the suffix *ghañ*] is applied when *sarva*, *kūla*, *abhra*, and *karīṣa* are the upapadas. 3.02.043 After the root *kṛ*, [the suffix *ghañ*] is applied when *megha*, *ṛti*, and *bhaya* are the upapadas. 3.02.044 When *kṣema*, *priya*, and *madra* are the upapadas, [the suffixes *ghañ*] and *aṇ* are also applied after the root *kṛ*.
3.02.045 The affix *kvip* is applied after the root *bhū* when combined with the prefix *āśit*, provided that the sense is either the instrument (*karaṇa*) or the abstract state (*bhāva*).
3.02.046 The affix *kvip* is applied after the roots *bhṛ*, *tṛ*, *vṛ*, *ji*, *dhṛ*, *śās*, *tap*, and *dam* when they form a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
3.02.047 The affix *kvip* is also applied after the root *gam*.
3.02.048: After the words *anta*, *atyanta*, *adhvan*, *dūra*, *pāra*, *sarva*, and *ananta*, the suffix *ḍa* is applied [to form a bahuvrīhi compound].
3.02.049: In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), the suffix *ḍa* is applied after the root *han*.
3.02.050 The suffix *ap* is added after the word *kleśa* when it is followed by *tamaḥ*. 3.02.051 The suffix *Ṇini* is added after the words *kumāra* and *śīrṣa*.
3.02.052 The suffix *ṬaK* is added after the words *jāyā* and *paty* when they denote a characteristic mark (*lakṣaṇa*).

3.02.053 And [the suffix *kvip* is applied] when the agent is not a human being. 3.02.054 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the words *hastin* and *kapāṭa* when they denote capability. 3.02.055 [The suffixes] *pāṇigha* and *tāḍagha* are formed [with *kvip*] when referring to an artisan.

3.02.056 The suffix *KHyuN* is applied after the root *kṛ*, with the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*), when the words *āḍhya*, *subhaga*, *sthūla*, *palita*, *nagna*, *andha*, and *priya* follow in the sense of the *Cvi*-suffix, provided that the *Cvi*-suffix itself is not present.
3.02.057 The suffixes *KHiṣṇuC* and *KHukaÑ* are applied after the root *bhū* in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*).
3.02.058 The suffix *KviN* is applied after the root *spṛś* when it does not mean "water" (*an-udake*).
3.02.059: [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the words *ṛtvij*, *dadhṛṣ*, *sraj*, *diś*, *uṣṇih*, and after verbs ending in *añc*, as well as after *yuj*, *kruñc*, and [verbs with penultimate *ṛ*].
3.02.060: After the pronouns beginning with *tyad* (i.e., *tyad*, *tad*, *yad*, etc.), the suffix *kañ* is applied to the root *dṛś* when it does not mean "seeing" (i.e., perceiving).
3.02.061: The suffix *kvip* is applied after the roots *sad*, *sū*, *dviṣ*, *druh*, *duh*, *yuj*, *vid*, *bhid*, *chid*, *ji*, *nī*, and *rāj*, even when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*).
3.02.062 The suffix *ṇvi* is applied after the root *bhaj*.
3.02.063 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), [the suffix *ṇvi*] is applied after the root *sah*.
3.02.064 And [the suffix *ṇvi* is applied] after the root *vah* as well.
3.02.065. The suffix *ñyuṭ* is applied after the verbal roots *kavi*, *purīṣa*, and *purīṣya*. 3.02.066.
The suffix *ñyuṭ* is applied after the root *havya*, provided it does not occur within the middle of a metrical foot (*pāda*).
3.02.067. The suffix *viṭ* is applied after the verbal roots *jan*, *san*, *khan*, *kram*, and *gam*.

3.02.068 The suffix *ad* is applied after the root *ad* when not meaning "food. 3.02.069 [The suffix *ad* is applied] also after [the root *ad*] when followed by *kravya*. 3.02.070 After the root *duh*, the suffixes *KaP* and *gha* are applied.
3.02.071 The suffix *ṆviN* is applied after the roots *śvit*, *vah*, *ukthaśaṃs*, and *puroḍāś* when used in a mantra.
3.02.072 The suffix *ṆviN* is applied after the root *yaj* with the prefix *ava*.
3.02.073 The suffix *viC* is applied after the root *yaj* with the prefix *upa* in Vedic literature (*chandas*).
3.02.074: [The suffixes] *maniN*, *kvaniP*, *vaniP*, and *aC* are applied after a verbal root ending in long *ā*.
3.02.075: These are also seen after other [verbal roots].
3.02.076: The suffix *kviP* is also applied.

3.02.077: After the root *sthā*, the suffix *Ka* is applied. 3.02.078: When a case-ending (*sUP*) follows, the suffix *Ṇini* is applied after a verbal root to express habitual action (*tācchilya*), provided it does not denote a genus (*ajāt-au*).
3.02.079: [The suffix *Ṇini* is applied] when the agent (*kartari*) is a standard of comparison (*upamāne*).
3.02.080 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after a verbal root in the sense of a religious observance (*vrata*).
3.02.081 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] diversely (*bahulam*) after a verbal root in the sense of repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*).
3.02.082 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the verbal root *man*.
3.02.083. Also [the suffix] Khaś is used after the root *mā* when it means "to measure oneself.
3.02.084. [The suffix *Khaś* is used] after a verbal root when it refers to the past.
3.02.085. [The suffix *Khaś* is used] after the root *yaj* when it refers to the instrument.
3.02.086: The suffix *KviP* is applied after the root *han* when it occurs in connection with an object (*karman*).
3.02.087: The suffix *KviP* is applied after the root *han* when *brahman*, *bhrūṇa*, or *vṛtra* are the objects.
3.02.088: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), [the application of this suffix] is diverse (*bahulam*).
3.02.089 The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *kṛ*, when followed by the words *sukarman*, *pāpamantra*, and *puṇya*.
3.02.090 The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *su*, when followed by the word *soma*.
3.02.091 The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *ci*, when followed by the word *agni*.

3.02.092 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after a verbal root denoting an action when it signifies the name of a fire (*agni*). 3.02.093 [The suffix] *ini* is applied after a verbal root signifying an action when it denotes the object (*karman*) of that action. 3.02.094 [The suffix] *KvaniP* is applied after the root *dṛś* ("to see").
3.02.095 After the root *kṛ* (to do/make) with the prefix *yudhi*, the suffix *rājan-i* [is applied].
3.02.096 And also after it with the prefix *saha*.
3.02.097 After the root *jan* (to be born), the suffix *Ḍa* is applied in the locative case (*saptamī*).
3.02.098 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after a verbal root] ending in the fifth case (ablative), provided that the action has not yet occurred (*ajātau*).

3.02.099 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after a verbal root] when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*), provided that the word formed is a technical name (*saṃjñā*). 3.02.100 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after a verbal root] when the prefix *anu* is present, provided that the action is directed toward an object (*karmaṇi*).
3.02.101 It is also seen in other cases.
3.02.102 The suffix *niṣṭhā* [is applied after verbal roots]. 3.02.103 The suffix *Ṅvanip* is applied after the roots *su* and *yaj*.
3.02.104 The suffix *atṛn* is added after the root *jṝ*. 3.02.105 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *liṭ* is applied. 3.02.106 After *liṭ*, the suffix *kānac* is optionally applied.
3.02.107 And [the suffix] KvasU [is used after verbal roots].
3.02.108 In common speech (bhāṣā), [the suffix KvasU is used] after the roots *sad*, *vas*, and *śru*.
3.02.109 And [the words] *upeyivān*, *anāśvān*, and *anūcānaḥ* [are formed with KvasU].
3.02.110 *luṅ* (the aorist suffix) 3.02.111 *laṅ* (the imperfect suffix) is used for times other than today (*an-adyatane*).
3.02.112 *lṛṭ* (the periphrastic future suffix) is used when there is a statement regarding recognition (*abhijñā-vacane*).
3.02.113 Not [is there elision] when *yat* follows; 3.02.114 optionally [there is elision] when there is expectancy (*sākāṅkṣa*); 3.02.115 the *liṭ* suffix is used for the remote past (*parokṣa*).
3.02.116 After the words *ha* and *śaśvat*, the suffix *lAṄ* (the imperfect tense marker) is also used [in addition to the perfect].
3.02.117 When a question is asked regarding a recent past time, the suffix *lAṄ* is also used. 3.02.118 In such cases, the suffix *lAṬ* (the present tense marker) is also used.
3.02.119 And [the particle *ca* is used] when there is no direct perception (*aparokṣa*).
3.02.120 [The particle *ca* is used] after *nanu* in a reply to a question. 3.02.121 [The particle *ca* is used] optionally after *na* and *nu*.
3.02.122: In the sense of the past (bhūta), the suffix *luṅ* is also used after a verbal root ending in *pur*.
3.02.123: In the sense of the present (vartamāna), the suffix *laṭ* is used.
3.02.124: From the suffix *laṭ*, the suffixes *śatṛ* and *śānac* are substituted, except when expressing the agent of the reflexive (ātmanepada) or when it is a denominative (*dhāraya*).
3.02.125 And [the particle *ca*] is used in the sense of addressing (*sam-bodhana*).

3.02.126 [The particle *ca* is also used] when indicating a characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*) or a cause (*hetu*) of an action (*kriyā*). 3.02.127 Those two [particles, *ca* and *hi*, in the aforementioned senses] are designated as *sat*.
3.02.128 The suffix *śānan* is applied after the roots *pūṅ* and *yaj*.
3.02.129 The suffix *cānaś* is applied [after a root] in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlya*), age (*vayaḥ*), or ability (*śakti*).
3.02.130 The suffixes *śatṛ* and *ṛcchri* are applied after the roots *iṅ* and *dhṛ*, respectively, when the agent is not a master (*ṛcchriṇi*).

3.02.131 After the root *dviṣ*, [the suffix *kvip* is applied] when the object is an enemy (*amitra*). 3.02.132 After the root *su*, [the suffix *kvip* is applied] when it is connected with a sacrifice (*yajña*). 3.02.133 After the root *arh*, [the suffix *kvip* is applied] in the sense of honoring (*pūjā*).
3.02.134 The suffix *ākv-i* is added after a verbal root to denote one who has that as his habit (*tacchīla*), that as his duty (*taddharma*), or who performs it well (*tatsādhukārī*).
3.02.135 The suffix *tṛn* is added after a verbal root to denote one who has that as his habit, that as his duty, or who performs it well.
3.02.136 The suffix *iṣṇuc* is added after the roots *alaṃkṛ*, *nirākṛ*, *prajan*, *utpac*, *utpat*, *unmad*, *ruc*, *apatrap*, *vṛt*, *vṛdh*, and *sah*.

3.02.137 The suffix *ṇa* is applied after the root *i* in the Vedic language; 3.02.138 and also after the root *bhū*; 3.02.139 and the suffix *Ksnū* is applied after the roots *glā*, *ji*, and *sthā*.
3.02.140: After the roots *tras*, *gṛdh*, *dhṛṣ*, and *kṣip*, the suffix *Knu* is applied.
3.02.141: After the eight roots beginning with *śam*, the suffix *GHinuṆ* is applied.

3.02.142: [The suffix *GHinuṆ* is applied] after *saṃ-pṛc*, *anu-rudh*, *āṅ-yam*, *āṅ-yas*, *pari-sṛ*, *saṃ-sṛj*, *pari-dev*, *saṃ-jvar*, *pari-kṣip*, *pari-vad*, *pari-dah*, *pari-muh*, *duṣ*, *dviṣ*, *druh*, *duh*, *yuj*, *ā-krīḍ*, *vi-vic*, *tyaj*, *raj*, *bhaj*, *ati-car*, *apa-car*, *ā-muṣ*, *abhy-ā-han*, and *aś*.
3.02.143 After the roots *kaṣ*, *laṣ*, *katth*, and *śrambh*, the suffix *vā* is added.
3.02.144 After the root *laṣ*, the suffix *ap* is also added.
3.02.145 After the roots *lap*, *sṛ*, *dru*, *math*, *vad*, and *vas*, preceded by *pra*, the suffix *ap* is added.

3.02.146 After the roots *nind* (to blame), *hiṃs* (to injure), *kliś* (to afflict), *khād* (to eat), *vi-nāś* (to destroy), *pari-kliś* (to torment), *pari-raṭ* (to shout around), *pari-vād* (to revile), *vyā-bhāṣ* (to speak excessively), and *asūy* (to envy), the suffix *vUÑ* is applied [to form a noun denoting the agent].
3.02.147 After the roots *dev* (to lament) and *kruś* (to cry out), when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*), the suffix *vUÑ* is applied [to form a noun denoting the agent].
3.02.148 After a root meaning "movement" or "sound," provided it is intransitive (*akarmaka*), the suffix *uC* is applied [to form a noun denoting the agent].
3.02.149: Also [the suffix *san*] follows a root that begins with a consonant and has an *anudātta* accent on its *it*.
3.02.150: [The suffix *san* follows the roots] *ju*, *car*, *kram*, *yad*, *dram*, *sṛ*, *gṛdh*, *jval*, *śuc*, *laṣ*, *pat*, and *pad*.
3.02.151: And [the suffix *san* follows roots] having the sense of anger (*krudh*) and pride (*maṇḍa*).
3.02.152 A suffix beginning with *y* is not applied [after a root ending in long *ā*]. 3.02.153 [The suffix *u* is applied] after the roots *sūd*, *dīp*, and *dīkṣ*.
3.02.154 The suffix *ukañ* is applied after the roots *laṣ*, *pat*, *pad*, *sthā*, *bhū*, *vṛṣ*, *han*, *kam*, *gam*, and *śṝ*.
3.02.155: After the verbal roots *jalp*, *bhikṣ*, *kuṭṭ*, *luṇṭh*, *vṛñ*, and *hrī*, the suffix *ṣākan* is applied.
3.02.156: After the root *pra-jan*, the suffix *ini* is applied.
3.02.157: The suffix *ini* is also applied after the roots *ji*, *dṛkṣi*, *vi-śri-iṇ*, *vam*, as well as after *avyathā*, *abhaḥ*, *amā*, *paribhū*, and *prasū*.
3.02.158 The suffix *āluC* is added after the roots *spṛh*, *gṛh*, *pat*, *day*, *ni-drā*, *tan-drā*, *śrad-dhā*.
3.02.159 The suffix *u* is added after the roots *dā* (with the augment *Ṭ*), *dhā*, *si*, *śada*, and *sad*.
3.02.160 The suffix *KmaraC* is added after the roots *sṛ*, *ghas*, and *ad*.
3.02.161 The suffix GHurac is added after the roots *bhañj*, *bhās*, and *mid*.
3.02.162 The suffix KuraC is added after the roots *vid*, *bhid*, and *chid*.
3.02.163 The suffix KvaraP is added after the roots *iṇ*, *naś*, *ji*, *sṛ*, and *ti*.
3.02.164 And [the suffix] *vara* follows the root *gā*.
3.02.165 [The suffix] *ūka* follows the root *jāgṛ*.
3.02.166 [The suffix] *ya* follows the roots *yaj*, *jap*, and *daś* when *yaṅ* has been elided.
3.02.167 After the roots *nam*, *kamp*, *smi*, *as*, *jas*, *kam*, *hiṃs*, and *dīp*, the suffix *ra* is applied.
3.02.168 After the roots *san*, *āśaṃs*, and *bhikṣ*, the suffix *u* is applied.
3.02.169 The forms *vinduḥ* and *icchuḥ* [are irregularly formed].
3.02.170. [The suffix *kyac* is applied] after a verbal root ending in a vowel, when a desired object (*chandasi*) is to be expressed.
3.02.171. The suffixes *āṭ*, *ki*, and *kin* are applied after the roots *ṛ*, *gam*, *han*, and *jan*, and [the suffixes] *liṭ* and *kyac* are also applied [after these roots].
3.02.172. The suffix *nañiṅ* is applied after the roots *svap* and *tṛṣ*.
3.02.173 After the roots *śṛ* ("to crush") and *vandi* ("to praise"), the suffix *āru* is added.
3.02.174 After the root *bhī* ("to fear"), the suffixes *Kru* and *KlukaN* are added.
3.02.175 After the roots *sthā*, *īś*, *bhās*, *pis*, and *kas*, the suffix *varaC* is added.
3.02.176 Also after [a root ending in] *y* when followed by *yaṅ*.
3.02.177 The suffix *Kvip* is applied after the roots *bhrāj*, *bhās*, *dhurvī*, *dyut*, *ūrj*, *pṝ*, *ju*, and *grāvastu*.
3.02.178 It is also seen after other [roots].
3.02.179: After the root *bhū*, [the suffix *ḍu*] is applied when it denotes a name (*saṃjñā*) or an interval (*antaram*).
3.02.180: After the prefixes *vi*, *pra*, and *sam*, [the suffix *ḍu*] is applied when it does not denote a name (*asaṃjñāyām*).
3.02.181: After the root *dhā*, the suffix *ṣṭran* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*).
3.02.182: After the roots √dāP, √nī, √śas, √yu, √yuj, √stu, √tud, √si, √sic, √mih, √pat, √daś, √nah, and √ah, the suffix *karaṇe* (the instrumental case marker) is applied.
3.02.183: After the root √pū, the suffix *karaṇe* is applied when it refers to a plough (*hala*) or a boar (*sūkara*).
3.02.184: After the roots √ṛ, √lū, √dhū, √sū, √khan, √śa, and √car, the suffix *itra* is applied.
3.02.185: After the root *pu*, [the suffix *Kti*] is used when forming a name (*saṃjñā*).
3.02.186: And [the suffix *Kti*] is used after [a root ending in *u*] when the agent (*kartṛ*) is a seer (*ṛṣi*) or a deity (*devatā*).
3.02.187: The suffix *Kta* occurs after roots marked with the indicatory letters *ÑI* or *IT*.
3.02.188: [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after words meaning "thought" (*mati*), "intellect" (*buddhi*), and "worship" (*pūjā*).
3.03.001: The *uṇ*-class suffixes are applied diversely.
3.03.002: They are seen even when denoting the past.
3.03.003 The suffixes *bhaviṣyat* (future), *gami* (the present participle suffix *śatṛ*), and others [are used for the future tense].
3.03.004 The suffix *laṭ* (present indicative) is used after a verb when the particles *yāvat* or *purā* are employed.
3.03.005 The suffix *laṭ* is optionally used after a verb when the particles *kadā* or *karhi* are employed.

3.03.006 [The genitive case is used] after a word ending in *kim* when there is a desire for something. 3.03.007 [The genitive case is used] also when the accomplishment of what is desired is indicated. 3.03.008 [The genitive case is used] also when the meaning of the imperative (*loṭ*) is indicated.
3.03.009 The suffix *liṅ* is used [after a verb] when another action occurs more than one *muhūrta* later.
3.03.010 The suffixes *tumun* and *ṇvul* are used after a verb when it denotes an action performed for the sake of another action.
3.03.011 And [the suffixes] expressing the abstract state (*bhāva*) are also used [in this sense].
3.03.012 The suffix *aṇ* is applied when the object (*karman*) is expressed.
3.03.013 The suffixes *lṛt* (the ten future participles) are applied when the remaining [kārakas] are expressed.
3.03.014 The suffixes *sat* (the ten participial suffixes beginning with *śatṛ*) may optionally take the place of *lṛt*.
3.03.015 The suffix *luṭ* is used after a verb when the sense is "not today" (*an-adya-tana*).
3.03.016 The suffix *Ghañ* is used after the roots *pad*, *ruj*, *viś*, and *spṛś*.
3.03.017 [The suffix *Ghañ* is also used] after the root *sṛ* when it conveys the sense of "firmness" (*sthira*).
3.03.018 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).
3.03.019 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] also when the agent (*kartṛ*) is not the agent of the action, provided it denotes a technical term (*saṃjñā*).
3.03.020 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after all [roots] when denoting a measure (*parimāṇa*).
3.03.021 And [the substitution of *ū* for the root vowel occurs] after a root ending in *iṅ*.
3.03.022 [The substitution of *ū* for the root vowel occurs] after a prefix (*upasarga*) before the root *ru*.
3.03.023 [The substitution of *ū* for the root vowel occurs] before the prefix *sam* in the case of the roots *yu*, *dru*, and *du*.
3.03.024 After the roots *śri*, *ṇī*, and *bhū*, [the suffix *ni*] may optionally [be substituted for *ṣṭran*].
3.03.025 After the roots *kṣu* and *sru*, [the suffix *ni*] is substituted for *ṣṭran* when preceded by *ava* or *ut*.
3.03.026 After the root *nī* preceded by *ava* or *ud*, [the suffix *ni* is substituted for *ṣṭran*].
3.03.027 [The suffix *kvanip* is applied after the roots] *dru*, *stu*, and *sru* when preceded by *pra*.
3.03.028 [The suffix *kvanip* is applied after the roots] *pū* and *lū* when preceded by *niṣ* and *abhi*, respectively.
3.03.029 [The suffix *kvanip* is applied after the root] *grā* when preceded by *ud* and *ni*.
3.03.030 *kṛ* [is used] with *dhānya*;
3.03.031 *sam-i stuv-ah* [is used] with *yajña*;
3.03.032 *pra-i str-ah* [is used] when not referring to a sacrifice (*ayajña*).
3.03.033 The suffix *va* is used after the root *prath* when it does not mean "sound. 3.03.034 It is also used [after *prath*] when it forms the name of a Vedic meter (*chandas*).
3.03.035 The suffix *va* is used after the root *grah* with the prefix *ud*.
3.03.036 The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *muh* when preceded by *sam*.

3.03.037 The suffix *kvip* is applied after the roots *nī* (in the form *ni*) and *iṇ* when preceded by *pari* and *ni*, respectively, in the senses of gambling and not deviating from the proper course.
3.03.038 The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *iṇ* when preceded by *pari* in the sense of "not passing over" or "not neglecting."
3.03.039 The suffix *kha* is applied after the root *śī* following the prefixes *vi-* and *upa-* when used in the sense of "turning" (*paryāya*).
3.03.040 It is also applied after the same roots when preceded by *hasta-* in the sense of "taking with the hand," provided it does not mean "stealing.

3.03.041 The suffix *ka* is applied after the root *ās* (to sit) following the prefix *ni-* in the sense of "dwelling," after *cit* in the sense of "heaping up," and after *dhā* in the sense of "placing upon the body. Furthermore, the initial *ā* of these roots is replaced by *i*.

3.03.042 The suffix *añ* is applied after the word *saṃgha* when it does not denote a hierarchical relationship. 3.03.043 The suffix *ṇac* is applied in the feminine gender after a verbal root when there is a mutual exchange of actions. 3.03.044 The suffix *inuṇ* is applied in the sense of an action (*bhāva*) when it denotes a pervasive quality (*abhividhi*).
3.03.045 The root *grah* is used with the prefixes *ā-* and *ava-* in the sense of reviling. 3.03.046 It is used with the prefix *pra-* in the sense of desire to obtain.
3.03.047 It is used with the prefix *pari-* in the context of a sacrifice.
3.03.048 The augment *n* is not applied after the root *vṛ* when followed by the suffix *na*, provided it does not refer to grain.
3.03.049 The augment *iṭ* is applied after the roots *śri*, *yā*, *pū*, *dru*, and *plu* when followed by the suffix *na*.
3.03.050 The augment *iṭ* is optionally applied after the roots *ru* and *plu* when followed by the prefix *āṅ*.

3.03.051 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the root *grah* (to seize) when there is an obstruction of rain; 3.03.052 [it is applied] after the root *pra-viṣ* (to enter) when referring to merchants; 3.03.053 and also after the root *viṣ* when preceded by *raśmi* (a rein).
3.03.054 The suffix *ni* is applied after the root *vṛ* in the sense of covering.
3.03.055 The suffix *ni* is applied after the root *bhū* preceded by *pari-* in the sense of contempt.
3.03.056 The suffix *ni* is applied after a root ending in *e*.
3.03.057. The suffix *aP* is applied after verbal roots ending in *ṛ*, *u*, or *o*.
3.03.058. The suffix *aP* is also applied after the roots *grah*, *vṛ*, *dṛ*, *ni-sci*, and *gam*.
3.03.059. When a prefix (*upasarga*) precedes it, the suffix *aP* is applied after the root *ad*.
3.03.060 *nau* and *ṇa* [are added after a verbal root ending in a vowel] when followed by the suffix *u*.
3.03.061 [The suffix *u* is added] after the roots *vyadh* and *jap* when no prefix (*upasarga*) precedes them.
3.03.062 [The suffix *u* is added] optionally after the roots *svan* and *has* when no prefix precedes them.
3.03.063 The suffix *ya* is applied after the roots *yam*, *sam*, *upa*, *ni*, and *vi*.
3.03.064 The suffix *na* is applied after the roots *gad*, *nad*, *paṭh*, and *svan*.
3.03.065 The suffix *na* is also applied after the root *kvaṇ* when it refers to the lute (*vīṇā*).

3.03.066 *paṇ* [is used] always in the sense of a measure (*parimāṇa*). 3.03.067 *mad* [is used] when no prefix (*upasarga*) precedes it. 3.03.068 *pramad* and *sammad* [are used] in the sense of joy (*harṣa*).
3.03.069 The suffix *a* is applied after the roots *aj* preceded by *sam-* and *ud-* when referring to animals.
3.03.070 The suffix *a* is applied after the root *glah* when referring to dice.
3.03.071 The suffix *a* is applied after the root *sar* when it means procreation.
3.03.072: After the verbal roots *ni*, *abhi*, *upa*, and *vi*, the vowel *hv-* undergoes *samprasāraṇa* (vocalization).
3.03.073: After the prefix *āṄ*, it is so when referring to a battle.
3.03.074: The term *āhāvaḥ* denotes a drinking place (*nipānam*).

3.03.075 The suffix *ghañ* is applied after a verbal root that does not have a prefix (*anupasarga*), provided it denotes an abstract state (*bhāva*). 3.03.076 The substitution of *vadh* for the root *han* also occurs [after such a prefixless root].
3.03.077 The substitution of *ghana* for the root *han* occurs when it denotes a solid mass or material object (*mūrti*).

3.03.078 The suffix *ghan* is applied after the prefix *antar-* when the word refers to a region (*deśa*). 3.03.079 When it refers to a part of a house (*agāra*), the forms *praghana* and *praghāṇa* are also [used]. 3.03.080 The form *udghana* denotes a place for storing firewood (*atyādhāna*).
3.03.081 The suffix *ghaṅ* is applied after the root *apa* [to form a feminine noun] when it does not refer to a limb (*aṅga*).
3.03.082 The suffix *ghaṅ* is applied after the roots *ay*, *vid*, and *ru* when they denote an instrument (*karaṇa*).
3.03.083 The suffix *ka* is also applied after the root *stambh* [in the same sense].
3.03.084 *parau ghaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.3.84): After the prefix *pari*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied [to form a noun].
3.03.085 *upaghna āśraye* (Pāṇini 3.3.85): *Upaghna* is formed with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of "a place of refuge" (*āśraya*).
3.03.086 *saṃghodghau gaṇapraśaṃsayoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.3.86): *Saṃgha* and *udgha* are formed with the suffix *ghañ* in the senses of "a multitude" (*gaṇa*) and "praise" (*praśaṃsā*) respectively.
3.03.087 The suffix *niGha* is applied after a root marked with the indicator *Ṇi*.
3.03.088 The suffix *Ktri* is applied after a root ending in *Ḍu* or having *IT* as an indicatory letter.
3.03.089 The suffix *athuC* is applied after a root ending in *Ṭu* or having *IT* as an indicatory letter.
3.03.090 The suffix naÑ is applied after the roots *yaj*, *yāc*, *yat*, *vicch*, *prach*, and *rakṣ*.
3.03.091 The suffix naÑ is applied after the root *svap*.
3.03.092 The suffix *ki* is applied after a root ending in *ghu* when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*).
3.03.093 [The suffix KtiN is applied] after verbal roots having the sense of an object (*karman*) or a locus (*adhikaraṇa*).
3.03.094 [The suffix KtiN is applied] in the feminine gender.
3.03.095 [The suffix KtiN is applied] after the roots *sthā*, *gā* (from *i*), *pā*, and *pac* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*).
3.03.096 In a mantra, the verbal roots √vṛṣ, √iṣ, √pac, √man, √vid, √bhū, and √vī, as well as the suffix -ra-, have an udātta accent.
3.03.097 Also, the words ending in -ūti, -yūti, -jūti, -sāti, -heti, and kīrti have an udātta accent.
3.03.098 The suffix KyaP is added after the roots √vraj and √yaj in the sense of abstract action (bhāva).

3.03.099: After the roots *sam-aj*, *ni-sad*, *ni-pat*, *man*, *vid*, *ṣo* (in the sense of purifying), *śī*, *bhṛ*, and *iṇ*, when used with the prefix *sam* in the sense of naming (*saṃjñāyām*), the suffix *kvip* is applied.
3.03.100: After the root *kṛ*, when used with the prefix *sam* in the sense of naming, the suffix *kvip* is applied, and the suffix *Śa* is also optionally applied.
3.03.101: The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *iccha* in the sense of naming.
3.03.102 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after a verbal root ending in a consonant that does not have a kṛt suffix marker (*apratyaya*).
3.03.103 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after a heavy (guru) verbal root ending in a consonant (*haL*).
3.03.104 [The suffix] *aṄ* is applied after the roots beginning with *bhid*.
3.03.105 The suffix *yuc* is applied after the roots *cint*, *pūj*, *kath*, *kumb*, and *carc*.
3.03.106 The suffix *yuc* is also applied after a root ending in long *ā* when a prefix (*upasarga*) precedes it.
3.03.107 The suffix *yuc* is applied after a root ending in *ṇi*, after roots ending in *ās*, and after the root *sranth*.
3.03.108 The suffix *ṆvuL* is applied diversely (*bahulam*) after a verbal root to form a word denoting a disease (*roga*). 3.03.109 [The suffix *ṆvuL* is applied] to form a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
3.03.110 In the sense of "narration" (*ākhyāna*) and "inquiry" (*paripraśna*), the suffixes *iN* and *ṆvuL* are optionally applied (*vibhāṣā*).
3.03.111 The suffix *ṆvuC* is applied after a verbal root in the senses of turn (*paryāya*), worthiness (*arha*), debt (*ṛṇa*), and production (*utpatti*).
3.03.112 In the sense of abuse (*ākrośa*), when the negative particle *naÑ* is present, the suffix *ani* is applied.
3.03.113 The *kṛtya* suffixes and *LyuṬ* are applied diversely (*bahulam*).
3.03.114 The suffix *Kta* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) when the word is neuter.
3.03.115 The suffix *LyuṬ* is also used [in the same sense].
3.03.116 The suffix *LyuṬ* is also used in the sense of the object (*karman*) when, through contact with it, there is physical pleasure for the agent (*kartṛ*).
3.03.117 And [the suffix GHaÑ] is applied after a verbal root when it denotes an instrument (karaṇa) or a locus (adhikaraṇa).

3.03.118 When the word is a masculine designation (saṃjñā), the suffix GHaÑ is generally applied. 3.03.119 Furthermore, the words *go-cara*, *saṃ-cara*, *vaha*, *vraja*, *vyaja*, *āpaṇa*, and *nigama* [are formed with GHaÑ].
3.03.120 The suffix GHaÑ is applied after verbal roots ending in *av*, *tṛ*, or *str*.
3.03.121 [The suffix GHaÑ is applied] also after verbal roots ending in a consonant (*haL*).
3.03.122 Furthermore, the forms *adhyāya*, *nyāya*, *udyāva*, *saṃhāra*, *ādhāra*, and *āvāya* are irregularly formed [with the suffix GHaÑ].
3.03.123 After the verbal roots *ud*, *ṛc*, and *arc*, the suffix *aC* is applied when not meaning "water.
3.03.124 The words *jāla* and *ānāya* are irregularly formed with this suffix.
3.03.125 After the root *khan*, the suffix *GHa* is also applied.
3.03.126 The suffix *KHaL* is applied after the words *īṣat*, *duḥ*, and *su* when they signify difficulty (*kṛcchra*) or ease (*akṛcchra*).
3.03.127 The suffix *KHaL* is also applied after the roots *bhū* and *kṛñ* when they have an agent (*kartṛ*) or an object (*karman*) as their upapada.
3.03.128 The suffix *yuC* is applied after a verbal root ending in long *ā*.
3.03.129 [The suffix *ktvā*] is used after verbal roots meaning "motion" when employed with a Vedic meter (*chandas*).
3.03.130 It is also observed after other [roots]. 3.03.131 When there is proximity to the present time, the suffixes of the present tense may optionally be used.
3.03.132 And [the suffixes expressing] the past tense may also be used when expressing a wish (āśaṃsā).
3.03.133 The suffix *lṛṭ* (the future tense) is used when expressing something that will happen quickly.
3.03.134 The suffix *liṅ* (the optative) is used when expressing a wish (āśaṃsā).
3.03.135 The present tense suffixes (*laṭ*) are not used for actions that are continuous or proximate to the present time.
3.03.136 The future tense suffixes (*lṛṭ*) are used when there is a limit (*maryādā*) in the future, provided it is subsequent to the current point in time.
3.03.137 And [the future tense suffixes are used] to denote a division of time, except in the case of days and nights.
3.03.138 Optionally [the conditional suffix *lṛṅ* is used] when the action is located in the future (*parasmin*).

3.03.139 The conditional suffix *lṛṅ* is used in place of the optative (*liṅ*) when there is a cause for it (i.e., the non-occurrence of the action) and when there is a failure of the action to take place.
3.03.140 And [the conditional suffix *lṛṅ* is used] when the action has occurred in the past.
3.03.141 *vā*, *ā*, *uta*, and *api* [are used with the present tense] when expressing possibility (*apy-arthe*).

3.03.142 When expressing censure (*garhā*), the present tense (*lAṬ*) is used with *api* and *jātu*. 3.03.143 Optionally, when *katham* is used, both the present tense and the optative (*liṄ*) are employed.

3.03.144 The optative (*liṅ*) and the periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*) are used after a word beginning with *kim* when it denotes a question. 3.03.145 When expressing impossibility or intolerance, these two suffixes are used even after words other than those beginning with *kim*. 3.03.146 The periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*) is used after *kim*, *kila*, and words having the sense of *asti*.
3.03.147 The *liṅ* [is used] after *jātu* and *yad*.
3.03.148 [The *liṅ* is used] also after *yat* and *yatra*. 3.03.149 [The *liṅ* is used] also when expressing censure (*garhā*).
3.03.150 And [the conditional *liṅ* is used] in the sense of expressing wonder (*citrīkaraṇa*).
3.03.151 In the remaining cases, the future tense suffix *lṛṭ* is used, except when followed by *yat*.
3.03.152 When *uta* and *api* are used in a sense of possibility (*samartha*), the potential mood suffix *liṅ* is used.
3.03.153 [The particle *iti* is used] after a verb expressing a desire, when the word *akaccit* follows.
3.03.154 [The particle *iti* is used] after a verb expressing capability, provided that the word *alam* is employed and the action is not already established.
3.03.155 [The particle *iti* is used] optionally after a verb expressing capability or praise, provided that the word *yadi* does not follow.
3.03.156 The suffix *liṅ* is used in the sense of cause and that which possesses the cause. 3.03.157 The suffixes *liṅ* and *loṭ* are used after verbs meaning "desire.
3.03.158 The suffix *tumun* is used when the agents of the two actions are the same.
3.03.159 The suffix *liṅ* [is used].
3.03.160 After roots expressing desire, *liṅ* is optionally used when the action is occurring at the present time (*vartamāne*).

3.03.161 *Liṅ* is used in the senses of injunction (*vidhi*), invitation (*nimantraṇa*), polite address (*āmantraṇa*), expression of preference (*adhīṣṭa*), inquiry (*saṃpraśna*), and entreaty (*prārthana*).
3.03.162 And the imperative (loṭ) [is used].
3.03.163 And the kṛtya suffixes are used for commanding, granting permission, and when the time has arrived. 3.03.164 And the optative (liṅ) is used when the time is after one muhūrta.

3.03.165 *smi* takes the suffix *loṭ* [in the sense of benediction]. 3.03.166 It also [takes *loṭ*] in the sense of entreaty (*adhīṣṭa*). 3.03.167 After [verbs] used with the words *kāla*, *samaya*, and *velā*, the suffix *tumun* is employed.
3.03.168 The suffix *liṅ* is used after a verbal root when the particle *yat* follows.
3.03.169 The *kṛtya* suffixes and *tṛc* are also used in the sense of fitness (*arha*).
3.03.170 The suffix *ṇini* is used in the sense of necessity (*āvaśyaka*) and debt (*ādhamarṇya*).

3.03.171 The suffixes used for the formation of *kṛtya* participles [are applied after a verbal root]. 3.03.172 The suffixes *śaki* and *liṅ* [are applied after a verbal root] when it expresses capability (*śakti*). 3.03.173 The suffixes *liṅ* and *loṭ* [are applied after a verbal root] in the sense of benediction (*āśis*).
3.03.174 The suffix *KtiC* is applied after a verbal root in the sense of a technical name (*saṃjñā*), as well as when followed by the suffixes *Kta* and *au*.
3.03.175 The suffix *luṅ* is applied after a verbal root when the word *māṅ* (the prohibitive particle *mā*) precedes it.
3.03.176 When the word *sma* precedes, both *laṅ* and *luṅ* are applied after a verbal root.
3.04.001 Suffixes [occur] when there is a connection with a verbal root (dhātu).

3.04.002 In the sense of the repetition of an action (kriyā-sam-abhi-hāra), the imperative suffix (loṭ) is used; and for the second person plural suffixes (ta and dhvam), hi and sva may optionally be substituted for them.
3.04.003 In a cumulative [construction], there is optionally [the use of the dual].
3.04.004 In the first case, there is application according to the rule.
3.04.005 In a cumulative [construction], there is [application] of the word expressing the general [notion].
3.04.006 In the Vedic language (chandas), the suffixes luṅ, laṅ, and liṭ [are used].
3.04.007 The suffix leṭ is used in the sense of the optative (liṅ).
3.04.008 And [it is also used] in the sense of mutual agreement (upa-saṃvāda) and expectation (āśaṅkā).

3.04.009 The suffixes *se*, *seN*, *ase*, *aseN*, *Kse*, *KaseN*, *adhyai*, *adhyaiN*, *kadhyai*, *kadhyaiN*, *śadhyai*, *śadhyaiN*, *tavai*, *taveN*, and *taveN* are used in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*).
3.04.010 [The suffixes *tavai*, *taveN*, and *taveN* are also used] after the roots *pra-i*, *ruha*, and *avyath*.
3.04.011 [The suffixes *tavai*, *taveN*, and *taveN* are also used] after the roots *dṛś* and *vi-khyā*.
3.04.012 The suffixes *ṇamul* and *kamul* are added after the root *śak*.
3.04.013 The suffixes *tosun* and *kasun* are added after the word *īśvara*.
3.04.014 The suffixes *tavai*, *ken*, *kenya*, and *tvan* are added in the sense of the *kṛtya* suffixes.
3.04.015 And [the suffix *tosun* is added] after the verb *ava-cakṣ*.
3.04.016 The suffix *tosun* is added after the verbs *sthā*, *iṇ*, *kṛ*, *vad*, *car*, *hu*, *tam*, and *jan*, when they denote an action that serves as a characteristic mark (*bhāva-lakṣaṇa*).
3.04.017 The suffix *KasuN* is added after the verbs *sṛp* and *tṛd*.
3.04.018: After the prohibitive particles *alam* and *khalu*, the suffix *Ktvā* is used according to the Eastern grammarians.
3.04.019: According to the Northern grammarians, the suffix *Ktvā* is used after the verb root *māṅ* (the prohibitive particle *mā*) when expressing reciprocity (*vyatīhāra*).
3.04.020: And [the suffix *Ktvā* is used] when there is a connection with "prior" (*para*) and "subsequent" (*apara*).
3.04.021: [The suffix *ktvā*] is applied after two verbal roots having the same agent when the action denoted by the first root precedes in time.
3.04.022: And [the suffix *ktvā*] as well as *Ṇamul* is applied when there is repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*).
3.04.023: This does not apply when the particle *yat* is used and the sentence is not expectant of further words (*an-ākāṅkṣa*).
3.04.024 The suffix *KHaL* is optionally applied after the root *kṛ*, when the words *agra*, *prathama*, and *pūrva* are used as upapadas.
3.04.025 The suffix *KHaMuÑ* is applied after the root *kṛ* when it has an object (*karman*) as its upapada, provided that the word expresses an insult (*ākrośa*).
3.04.026 The suffix *ṆamuL* is applied [after the root *kṛ*] when the word *svādu* is used as an upapada.
3.04.027 When *anyathā*, *evam*, *katham*, or *ittham* are used, the suffix *ām* is added [to the preceding word] provided that it is not connected with a verb (*asūyoge*).

3.04.028 When *yathā* and *tathā* are used in response to a statement expressing dissatisfaction (*asūyā-prativacana*), the suffix *ām* is added. 3.04.029 When the roots *dṛś* and *vid* take an object (*karmani*) and denote completeness (*sākalye*), the suffix *ām* is added.
3.04.030 The suffix *yat* is used after the words *vindu* and *jīva* [in the sense of "as much as"].
3.04.031 The suffix *pūra* is used after the words *carman* and *udara*.
3.04.032 When the measure is that of rainfall, the suffix *ūla* is optionally applied after these [words].

3.04.033 The root √ci (to gather) [takes the suffix *lyap*] when preceded by *kne*. 3.04.034 The root √kaṣ (to rub/to destroy) [takes the suffix *lyap*] when preceded by *ni-mūla* or *sa-mūla*. 3.04.035 The root √piṣ (to grind/to crush) [takes the suffix *lyap*] when preceded by *śuṣka*, *cūrṇa*, or *rūkṣa*.
3.04.036 The affix *kvip* is applied after the roots *han*, *kṛñ*, and *grah* when they are preceded by *samūla*, *akṛta*, and *jīva*.
3.04.037 The affix *kvip* is applied after the root *han* when it has an instrument (*karaṇa*) as its upapada.
3.04.038 The affix *kvip* is applied after the root *piṣ* when it has *sneha* (oil/fat) as its object (*karman*).
3.04.039 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *vṛt*] when preceded by *hasta*, and after *grah*.
3.04.040 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *puṣ*] when preceded by *sva*.
3.04.041 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *bandh*] when it denotes the locus (*adhikaraṇa*).
3.04.042 [The suffix *kha* is applied] after the verb *saṃjñā* when used in the sense of a name (*saṃjñāyām*).
3.04.043 [The suffix *kha* is applied] after the verbs *naś* and *vah* when the agent (*kartṛ*) is either a living being (*jīva*) or a person (*puruṣa*).
3.04.044 [The suffix *kha* is applied] after the verbs *śuṣ* and *pū* when preceded by the prefix *ūrdhva*.

3.04.045: [The suffix *lyap* is used] after a root ending in *kṛ*, when it has a word denoting comparison as its object. 3.04.046: In the case of roots beginning with *kaṣ*, the suffix *lyap* is applied according to the specific rules governing their usage. 3.04.047: The root *daṃś* (to bite) is used with the third case ending when accompanied by the prefix *upa*.

3.04.048: [The affix *lyap* is applied] after roots meaning "injury" (*hiṃsā*) when they have the same agent as the main verb. 3.04.049: [The affix *lyap* is applied] after the roots *upapīḍa*, *rudha*, and *karṣa* when the locative case (*saptamī*) is used. 3.04.050: [The affix *lyap* is applied] after the root *kṛṣ* in the sense of "placing together" (*samāsatti*).

3.04.051 Also after [a prefix] ending in *pra* when it denotes a measure; 3.04.052 After [a prefix] ending in *apa* or *ā* when there is a desire to take hold; 3.04.053 And also after [a prefix] ending in the second case.
3.04.054 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the roots *svṛ*, *aj*, and *dhru*, when they are in the present participle middle voice (*śānac*).
3.04.055 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] also after the root *kliś* when it is in the present participle middle voice (*śānac*).

3.04.056 [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the roots *viś*, *pati*, *pad*, and *skand*, respectively, when they are in the present participle middle voice (*śānac*) and the present participle passive (*karmakartari śānac*).
3.04.057 The suffix *Ktvā* is applied after the root *as* (to throw), *syati*, and *tṛṣ* when there is an interval of time between the action and another action.

3.04.058 The suffix *Ktvā* is applied after the roots *ā-diś* (to point out) and *grah* (to seize) when followed by a noun. 3.04.059 The suffixes *Ktvā* and *Ṇamul* are applied after the root *kṛ* (to do) when expressing an indeclinable used to describe something contrary to one's intention.

3.04.060 [The substitution of *tiraś* for *tiryañc* occurs] before a word ending in the suffix *ap*. 3.04.061 [The substitution of *sva* for *svar* occurs] before the suffix *tas*, when it follows the roots *kṛ* and *bhū*.
3.04.062 [The substitution of *sva* for *svar* occurs] before a suffix having the sense of *nāmadhātu*, when that suffix has the sense of the suffix *Cvi*.
3.04.063 The suffix *tumun* is applied after verbal roots meaning "to be" (*bhū*) when used with the word *tūṣṇīm*.
3.04.064 The suffix *tumun* is applied after verbal roots meaning "to go" (*anv-aj*) when used with the word *ānulomye* (in the sense of compliance).
3.04.065 The suffix *tumun* is applied after the verbal roots *śak*, *dhṛṣ*, *jñā*, *glā*, *ghaṭ*, *rabh*, *labh*, *kram*, *sah*, *arh*, and those having the sense of *asti* ("to exist").
3.04.066 [The sixth case ending is used] after words expressing "sufficiency" (*paryāpti*) when they have the sense of "adequate for" (*alam*).
3.04.067 A *kṛt* suffix occurs in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*).
3.04.068 The forms *bhavya*, *geya*, *pravacanīya*, *upasthānīya*, *janya*, *āplāvya*, and *āpātya* are optionally [used as *kṛt* formations].

3.04.069: The affix *la* occurs after verbal roots that take an object (*sakarmaka*) in the sense of the object (*karman*), and after those that do not take an object (*akarmaka*) in the sense of the action itself (*bhāva*).
3.04.070: The *kṛtya* affixes, as well as *Kta* and *KHal*, have the same meanings as those [affixes mentioned in 3.04.069].
3.04.071: The affix *Kta* occurs after a root in the sense of the beginning of an action (*ādikarman*), and also in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*).

3.04.072 [The affix *kta* is applied after roots meaning "to go," after intransitive roots, and after the roots *śliṣ*, *śīṅ*, *sthā*, *ās*, *vas*, *jan*, *ruh*, *jṝ*, and *yati*. 3.04.073 [The affixes *dāś* and *goghn* are applied in the sense of the recipient (*sampradāna*).
3.04.075 [In cases other than those two, the *uṇ*-ādī affixes are applied.]

3.04.076 The suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the locus (*adhikaraṇa*), as well as in the senses of remaining fixed (*dhrauvya*), motion (*gati*), and cessation (*pratyavasāna*). 3.04.077 [The following are the substitutes] for *la*.
3.04.078 *tiP*, *tas*, *jhi*; *siP*, *thas*, *tha*; *miP*, *vas*, *mas*; *ta*, *ātām*, *jha*; *thās*, *āthām*, *dhvam*; *iṭ*, *vahi*, *mahiṄ*.

3.04.079 For the substitutes of *ṭe* belonging to the *ātmanepada*, the substitute *e* is applied after those [suffixes] that have *ṭ* as their *it*. 3.04.080 For the substitute of *thās*, the substitute *se* is applied.
3.04.081 For the suffixes *ta* and *jha* of the *liṭ* [perfect], the substitutes *eś* and *irec* are applied respectively.
3.04.082 For the *parasmaipada* [terminations], *ṇal*, *atus*, *us*, *thal*, *athus*, *a*, *ṇal*, *va*, and *māḥ* [are substituted].
3.04.083 After the root *vid*, the substitutes for the *laṭ* [tense] are optionally [the same as those for the *liṭ* tense].
3.04.084 For the five [terminations] beginning with the first person, *āha* is substituted for the root *brū*, and it retains the form *brū*.
3.04.085 The substitutes for the imperative (loṭ) endings are like those of the imperfect (laṅ).
3.04.086 For the [imperative] ending *e*, the substitute is *u*.
3.04.087 For the [imperative] ending *se*, the substitute is *hi*, and it is also designated as having an indicatory letter *p* (apit).
3.04.088 Optionally in Vedic;
3.04.089 *niḥ* replaces *me*;
3.04.090 *ām* replaces *eT*.
3.04.091 After the [prefixes] *sa-* and *va-*, [the case endings] *vas* and *am* are substituted by *au*.
3.04.092 The first person ending (*uttama-puruṣa*) is replaced by *āṬ*, and it is also treated as having an indicatory letter *P*.
3.04.093 [The substitute] *ai* is applied in place of *eT*.
3.04.094 The suffixes leṭ and laṅ take the augment aṭ.
3.04.095 After a verbal root ending in long ā, the substitution of ai takes place for the personal endings of leṭ.
3.04.096 In other cases, the substitution of e optionally takes place after a verbal root ending in long ā.

3.04.097 There is also elision of the augment *iṭ* before the *parasmaipada* endings. 3.04.098 [The substitution of] *s* occurs for the final letter of the first person (*uttama*) ending. 3.04.099 This substitution is obligatory when the ending is marked with the indicatory letter *ṅ*.
3.04.100 *iṭ* is also [substituted for *jha*].
3.04.101 For *tas*, *thas*, *tha*, and *miP*, there are respectively *tām*, *tam*, *ta*, and *am*.
3.04.102 *sīyuṬ* is substituted for the *liṅ* [affixes].
3.04.103 The affix *yāsuṬ* is acute (*udātta*) in the parasmaipada endings and is marked with the indicatory letter *Ṅ*.
3.04.104 An affix marked with the indicatory letter *K* is acute in the benedictive (*āśis*).
3.04.105 For the ending *jha*, *raṇ* is substituted.
3.04.106 The substitute *aT* replaces the *iṬ* augment. 3.04.107 The augment *suṬ* is added before the *tiP* and *thas* endings. 3.04.108 The substitute *Jus* replaces the *jhi* ending.
3.04.109: The affix *sīC* is applied after reduplicated roots (*abhyasta*) and the root *vid*. 3.04.110: [The substitution of] *āT* occurs [in place of the final vowel of the root]. 3.04.111:
According to Śākaṭāyana alone, [the substitution of *āT* occurs] after the *lAṄ* (aorist) suffix.
3.04.112 And [a suffix] beginning with *dvis* [is termed *ārdhadhātuka*].
3.04.113 A suffix beginning with a *tiṅ* or a *śit* [is termed *sārvadhātuka*].
3.04.114 The remainder [of suffixes] is termed *ārdhadhātuka*.
3.04.115 The *liṭ* [affixes] also [are used after verbal roots].
3.04.116 The *liṅ* [affixes] are used in the sense of benediction (*āśis*).
4.01.001 [The suffixes *Nī*, *ĀP*, and those following] a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) [are added to form feminine bases].

4.01.002 *sU-au-Jas-am-auṬ-Śas-Ṭā-bhyām-bhis-Ṅe-bhyām-bhyas-ṄasI-bhyām-bhyas-Ṅas-os-ām-Ṅi-os-suP* 4.01.003 *striyām* (in the feminine) 4.01.004 *aja-ādi-aTaḥ-ṬāP* (the suffix *ṬāP* is applied after [stems] beginning with *aja-* and those ending in short *a*)
4.01.005 The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after [stems ending in] *ṛt* (the vowels *ṛ*, *ṝ*, and *ḷ*).
4.01.006 The suffix *ṅīp* is also applied after [stems whose final vowel is] marked with the *it* designation *u*.
4.01.007 The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after the stem *van*, and [the final *n* of *van*] is replaced by *r*.

4.01.008 The suffix *pād-* [is applied] optionally. 4.01.009 The suffix *ṬāP* [is applied after a stem ending in *ṛ*] when it denotes a *ṛc* (verse). 4.01.010 [The suffix *ṬāP*] is not applied after the six [numerals] nor after *svasṛ* and so forth.
4.01.011 *man-* [is substituted for the final vowel of a Bahuvrīhi compound ending in *an*].
4.01.012 *an-* [is substituted for the final vowel of a Bahuvrīhi compound ending in *an*].
4.01.013 The suffix *ḌāP* may optionally be applied after both [of these, i.e., after a Bahuvrīhi ending in *man* or *an*].
4.01.014 After a word that is not a secondary member (*an-upasarjana*).

4.01.015 The suffixes *ṭhaÑ*, *aṆ*, *aÑ*, *dvayasaC*, *daghnaC*, *mātraC*, *tayaP*, *ṭhaÑ*, *kaÑ*, and *KvaraP* [are added after a word ending in a consonant]. 4.01.016 The suffix *yaÑ* is also added after a word ending in *as*.

4.01.017 The suffix *ṣpha* is applied [after a word denoting a descendant] of the Easterners, forming a secondary derivative (*taddhita*). 4.01.018 This [suffix *ṣpha*] is applied in all cases after words beginning with *lohita* and ending with *kata*. 4.01.019 It is also applied after the words *kauravya* and *māṇḍūka*.
4.01.020 [The feminine suffix ṅīp is applied] after a word denoting age in the first instance.
4.01.021 [The feminine suffix ṅīp is applied] after a *dvigu* compound.

4.01.022 [The feminine suffix ṅīp is applied] after a *dvigu* compound that does not end in a word for measure (*apari-māṇa*), nor in *bista*, *ācita*, or *kambalya*, provided there is no elision (*luK*) of a secondary suffix (*taddhita*).

4.01.023 After [a word ending in] *kāṇḍa*, when *kṣetra* follows, [the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied]. 4.01.024 After [a word ending in] *puruṣa*, when it denotes a measure, [the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied optionally]. 4.01.025 After the word *ūdhas* at the end of a *bahuvrīhi* compound, [the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied].
4.01.026 The suffix *ṄīP* is applied after a feminine stem ending in *ā* that begins with a numeral or an indeclinable (*avyaya*).
4.01.027 [The suffix *ṄīP* is applied] also after a feminine stem ending in *dāman* or *hāyana*.
4.01.028 [The suffix *ṄīP* is applied] after a feminine stem ending in *an*, provided that the penultimate (*upadhā*) vowel is long (*ūpin*) and the word does not end in *ni*, *ara*, or *yām*.
4.01.029 The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is always applied after [a stem ending in] a name (*saṃjñā*) or a Vedic verse (*chandas*).
4.01.030 [The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied] also after *kevala*, *māmaka*, *bhāgadheya*, *pāpa*, *apara*, *samāna*, *āryakṛta*, *sumaṅgala*, and *bheṣaja*.
4.01.031 [The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied] also after *rātri*, except when the suffixes *jas* or *au* follow.

4.01.032 The augment *nuK* is added after the words *antarvat* and *pativat*. 4.01.033 The substitute *na-* is applied to the word *pati-* when it is connected with a sacrifice. 4.01.034 This substitution is optional when [the word *pati-*] is preceded by another word.
4.01.035 The word *nityam* is always [substituted] for *sapalī* and so forth.
4.01.036 For *pūtakratu*, the vowel *ai* is substituted [for the final vowel].
4.01.037 In *vṛṣākapi*, *agni*, *kusīda*, and *kusīda*, the [first] vowel is acute-accented (*udātta*).
4.01.038: After the word *manu*, [the suffix *taddhita* *aṇ*] is optionally replaced by *u*.
4.01.039: After a word ending in a non-anudātta vowel, provided that *t* is its penultimate letter, the [suffix *taddhita* *aṇ*] is replaced by *na*.
4.01.040: In other cases, [the suffix *taddhita* *aṇ*] is replaced by *Ṅīṣ*.
4.01.041 The suffix *ṣit* [is applied] after the words beginning with *gaura*.

4.01.042 [The suffix *ṣyaṅ* is applied] after *jānapada*, *kuṇḍa*, *goṇa*, *sthala*, *bhāja*, *nāga*, *kāla*, *nīla*, *kuśa*, *kāmuka*, and *kabara*, [respectively] when the senses of livelihood (*vṛtti*), vessel (*amatra*), sowing (*āvapana*), non-artificial (*akṛtrima*), porridge (*āśrāṇā*), stoutness (*sthaulya*), color (*varṇa*), non-garment (*anācchādana*), iron-product (*ayovikāra*), sexual union (*maithuna*), desire (*icchā*), hair (*keśa*), and arrangement (*veśa*) are intended.
4.01.043 [The suffix *ṣyaṅ* is applied] after *śoṇa* when [the feminine] ends in long *ā*.

4.01.044 After a word expressing a quality (*guṇavacana*) ending in *vā* or *uT*, [the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied]. 4.01.045 Also after words beginning with *bahu*. 4.01.046 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this [application] is obligatory (*nityam*).
4.01.047 And [the suffix ṅīṣ is applied] after the word *bhū*.
4.01.048 [The suffix ṅīṣ is applied] when a woman is designated by her connection with a male [relative].

4.01.049 After the words *indra*, *varuṇa*, *bhava*, *śarva*, *rudra*, *mṛḍa*, *hima*, *araṇya*, *yava*, *yavana*, *mātula*, and *ācārya*, the suffix *ānuk* is applied [before the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*].
4.01.050 [The suffix *ṣyañ* is applied] after a word ending in *krī*, provided it is preceded by an instrument (karaṇa).
4.01.051 [The suffix *ṣyañ* is applied] after a word ending in *Kta*, when it denotes something small (*alpa*).
4.01.052 [The suffix *ṣyañ* is applied] also after a *bahuvrīhi* compound that has an acute accent (*udātta*) on its final syllable.
4.01.053 Optionally [the suffix -ī] is applied after a compound whose prior member is *asvāṅga* (not denoting a limb of one's own body).
4.01.054 [The suffix -ī is applied] also after a secondary derivative (*upasarjana*) ending in *svāṅga* that does not have *y* as its penultimate letter.
4.01.055 [The suffix -ī is applied] also after [secondary derivatives ending in] *nāsikā*, *udara*, *oṣṭha*, *janghā*, *danta*, *karṇa*, and *śṛṅga*.

4.01.056 Not [after a word] beginning with *kroḍa* etc., nor after one having many vowels (*bahv-aC*). 4.01.057 Not [after a word] preceded by *saha*, *naÑ*, *vid*, *yam*, or *māna*. 4.01.058 Not [after a word] ending in *nakha* or *mukha* when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
4.01.059 *dīrghajihvī* [is formed] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
4.01.060 The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after a word ending in *vāh* when it has a cardinal direction as its prior member.
4.01.061 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *vāh*.
4.01.062 The term *sakhī* (female friend) and *aśiśvī* (one who does not have a child) [are used] in common parlance (*bhāṣā*).
4.01.063 The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after a genus name (*jāti*) that does not denote a female, provided it has the letter *y* as its penultimate (*upadhā*) vowel.
4.01.064 [The suffix *ṅīp* is also applied] after a genus name ending in the words *pāka*, *karṇa*, *parṇa*, *puṣpa*, *phala*, *mūla*, or *vāla*.

4.01.065 [The suffix] *īN* is applied after a word ending in *i* or *a* that denotes a human species. 4.01.066 [The suffix] *ūN* is applied after a word ending in a vowel (*uT*) that denotes a human species.
4.01.067 [The suffix *ūN* is applied] after a word ending in *bāhu* when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
4.01.068 And [the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied] after *paṅga*.

4.01.069 [The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied] after a word ending in *ūru* when it occurs as the final member of a compound expressing a comparison (*aupamya*). 4.01.070 [The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied] also after words beginning with *saṃhita*, *śapha*, *lakṣaṇa*, and *vāma*.
4.01.071 After the words *kadru* and *kamaṇḍalu*, the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied when referring to a Vedic meter (*chandas*).
4.01.072 [The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied] when forming a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
4.01.073 After the class of words beginning with *śāṛṅgarava* and after a word ending in the feminine suffix *aṆ*, the suffix *ṅīṅ* is applied.
4.01.074 The suffix yaṄ is designated as CāP.
4.01.075 [The suffixes beginning with] āvaṭya are also [designated as CāP].
4.01.076 These are called taddhita suffixes.
4.01.077 *ti* is substituted for the [genitive] ending of *yuvan*.

4.01.078 *Ṣyaṅ* is substituted for the [genitive] ending of a *gotra* [patronymic] formed by *aṇ* or *iñ*, provided that the [base] consists of more than two syllables and is not a Vedic (*ārṣa*) name.
4.01.079 [The substitution of *Ṣyaṅ* occurs] after a [patronymic] that is a constituent part of a *gotra*.
4.01.080 And [the suffix *cha*] is applied after [patronymic stems] beginning with *krauḍi*.
4.01.081 After [the patronymic stems] *daivayajñi*, *śauci*, *vṛkṣi*, *sātyamugri*, and *kāṇṭheviddhi*, the suffix *nya* is optionally applied.
4.01.082 From among words that are semantically connected, the suffix is optionally applied after the first word.
4.01.083 Before the suffix *divyat*, [the suffix] *aṇ* [is applied].

4.01.084 And [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after [words beginning with] *aśvapati*. 4.01.085 After [words ending in] *diti*, *aditi*, *āditya*, or *pati* as the final member [of a compound], the suffix *ṇya* [is applied].
4.01.086 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after [words] beginning with *utsa*.
4.01.087 The suffixes *naÑ* and *snaÑ* are respectively applied after the words *strī* and *puṃs*, when they denote a location (*bhavana*).
4.01.088 The elision (*luK*) of the suffix occurs after a *dvigu* compound, except when it denotes offspring (*apatya*).
4.01.089 There is elision (*luK*) of the *gotra* [secondary suffix] before a vowel-initial [patronymic suffix].
4.01.090 There is elision (*luK*) of the *yuvan* [suffix] before a vowel-initial [patronymic suffix].
4.01.091 There is optionally the elision (*luK*) of the suffixes *phaK* and *phiÑ*.

4.01.092 [The suffix *yañ* is applied after a word ending in *taddhita* *aṇ*] to denote his offspring; 4.01.093 [the suffix *iñ* is applied] when there is only one [lineage] in a *gotra*; 4.01.094 [the suffix *phak* is applied] after a *gotra* name to denote a younger descendant (*yuvan*), except in the case of the feminine gender.
4.01.095 *iÑ* is substituted for [the final vowel] of a stem ending in short *a*.
4.01.096 *iÑ* is also substituted [for the final vowel] after stems beginning with *bāhu*.
4.01.097 After *sudhātṛ*, *akaṄ* is also [substituted].
4.01.098 The suffix *CphaÑ* is applied after [names of] lineages (*gotra*) beginning with *kuñja*.
4.01.099 The suffix *phaK* is applied after [names of] lineages beginning with *naḍa*.
4.01.100 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after [names of] lineages beginning with *harita*.
4.01.101 [The suffix] *yaÑ* is applied after [stems ending in] *iÑ*.
4.01.102 [The suffix *yaÑ* is applied] after *śaradvat*, *śunaka*, and *darbha*, when [the patronymic refers respectively to] *bhṛgu*, *vatsa*, and *āgrāyaṇa*.
4.01.103 [The suffix] *nya* is applied after *droṇa*, *parvata*, and *jīvant*. 4.01.104 [The suffix *nya* is applied] after [stems ending in] *ara* and *yā*.
4.01.104 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after [patronymic stems] beginning with *Bida*, provided they are not names of *ṛṣis* and there is no immediate succession [of generations].
4.01.105 The suffix *yaÑ* is applied after [patronymic stems] beginning with *Garga*.
4.01.106 The suffix *yaÑ* is applied after the words *madhu* and *babhru* when [the resulting patronymics refer respectively to] the *Brāhmaṇas* and the *Kauśikas*.
4.01.107 [The suffix *yañ* is applied] after *kapi* and *bodha* when *Āṅgirasa* follows.
4.01.108 [The suffix *yañ* is also applied] after *vataṇḍa*.
4.01.109 [In the feminine gender, there is] elision (*luk*).
4.01.110 The suffix *phaK* is added after [the group of words] beginning with *aśva*.
4.01.111 The suffix *traigarta* is added after *bharga*.
4.01.112 The suffix *aṆ* is added after [the group of words] beginning with *śiva*.

4.01.113 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after feminine stems] denoting rivers or human females that do not have a penultimate vowel subject to *vṛddhi* strengthening and do not end in the name of a mother.
4.01.114 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] also after [stems ending in] the names of seers (*ṛṣi*), as well as those of the Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis, and Kurus.

4.01.115 [The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied after the word] *mātṛ* when it follows a numeral, the word *sam*, or the word *bhadra*. (In these cases, the final syllable of *mātṛ* undergoes *uT* substitution.)

4.01.116 For *kanyā*, [the substitute] *kanīna* is also used. 4.01.117 After *vikarṇa*, *śuṅga*, and *chagala*, [the patronymic suffixes] are applied when [the progenitors are] Vatsa, Bharadvāja, and Atri respectively.
4.01.118 For *pīlā*, [the suffix] is optionally applied.

4.01.119 And [the suffix] ḍhaK [is applied] after the word *maṇḍūka*. 4.01.120 [The suffix] ḍhaK [is applied] after feminine [stems]. 4.01.121 [The suffix ḍhaK is applied] after a stem consisting of two vowels (*dvyaC*).
4.01.122 Also after *it*, and [after a stem] ending in *as* that does not end in *iÑ*.
4.01.123 And also after [stems] beginning with *śubhra*.
4.01.124 After *vikarṇa* and *kuśītaka* when [the patronymic] *kāśyapa* follows.
4.01.125 *vuK* is also [the substitute] for *bhruv-*.
4.01.126 For words beginning with *kalyāṇī*, *inaṄ* [is the substitute].
4.01.127 For *kulaṭā*, it is optionally [so].
4.01.128 From *caṭakā*, the suffix *airaK* [is applied].
4.01.129 From *godhā*, the suffix *ḍhraK* [is applied].
4.01.130 According to the Northern grammarians, the suffix *āraK* [is applied].
4.01.131 Optionally after *kṣudrā*.
4.01.132 After *pitṛṣvasṛ*, the suffix *chaṆ* is added.
4.01.133 There is elision [of the final vowel] before the suffix *ḍhak*.
4.01.134 And [the suffix ḍhak is applied] after *mātṛṣvasṛ* (mother’s sister).
4.01.135 [The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after [words denoting] quadrupeds (*catuṣpād*).
4.01.136 And [the suffix *ḍhañ* is applied] after [the group of words beginning with] *gṛṣṭi*.
4.01.137 The suffix *yaT* is added after *rājan* and *śvaśura*.
4.01.138 The suffix *gha* is added after *kṣatra*. 4.01.139 The suffix *kha* is added after *kula*.

4.01.140 After a word that does not have *apūrva* as its prior member, the suffixes *yat* or *ḍhakañ* may optionally be applied [to form a patronymic]. 4.01.141 After the word *mahā-kula*, the suffixes *aṇ* or *khañ* are applied.
4.01.142 After the word *duṣ-kula*, the suffix *ḍhak* is applied.
4.01.143 *svasuḥ* [the suffix] *cha* [is applied]. 4.01.144 *bhrātuḥ* [the suffix] *vyaṭ* [is applied], and [the suffix] *cha*.
4.01.145 *vyaṅ* [is applied] in the sense of "co-wife" (*sapatna*).
4.01.146 The suffix *ṭhak* is added after [patronymic stems] beginning with *revatī*.
4.01.147 The suffix *ṇa* is also added [after a patronymic stem] denoting a female when contempt is expressed.
4.01.148 The suffix *ṭhak* is frequently added after a [patronymic] stem containing a *vṛddhi* vowel when referring to the Sauvíras.
4.01.149: After the words *pheṇa* and *śca*, [the suffix *cha* is applied].
4.01.150: After the words *phāṇṭāhṛti* and *mimata*, the suffixes *Ṇa* and *phiñ* [are applied respectively].
4.01.151: After the group of words beginning with *kuru*, the suffix *Ṇya* [is applied].
4.01.152 [The suffix *cha*] is also applied after words ending in *senā*, as well as after words characterized by a final *lakṣaṇa* and after *kārin*.
4.01.153 According to the Northern Grammarians (*udīcām*), the suffix *iÑ* is applied [after the aforementioned bases].
4.01.154 The suffix *phiÑ* is applied after the group of words beginning with *tika*.
4.01.155 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *kausalya* and *kārmārya*.
4.01.156 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in the suffix *aṇ*, provided it consists of more than two syllables.
4.01.157 According to the Northern grammarians, [the suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in the suffix *vṛddhi*, provided it is not a *gotra* name.

4.01.158: After words beginning with *vākin*, the suffix *kuK* is added [to form the feminine]. 4.01.159: After a word ending in *putra*, the suffix *kuK* is optionally added. 4.01.160: According to the Eastern grammarians, the suffix *phiN* is frequently applied after a non-*vṛddhi* [word] to form the feminine.
4.01.161: After the word *manu*, when the suffixes *aṇ* or *yañ* follow, there is the augment *ṣuk*.
4.01.162: Descendants beginning with the grandson are called *gotra*. 4.01.163: However, while a member of the lineage is still living, [the descendant] is called *yuvan* (the younger).
4.01.164 And [the suffix *kan* is added] when an elder brother is alive; 4.01.165 or when another sapinda who is more senior is alive;
4.01.166 and [it is added] in the sense of honoring an elder.

4.01.167 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after *yuvan* when contempt is expressed. 4.01.168 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after a word denoting a *kṣatriya* that is a name of a people (*janapada*). 4.01.169 And [the suffix *aÑ* is applied] after *sālveya* and *gāndhāri*.
4.01.170: After [a word] ending in two vowels, and after *Magadha*, *Kaliṅga*, and *Sūramasa*, the suffix *aṆ* is applied.
4.01.171: After a word with a *vṛddhi* vowel in the first syllable, after a word ending in the augment *iT*, and after *Kośala* and *Ajāda*, the suffix *ÑyaṄ* is applied.
4.01.172: After the words *Kuru* and those beginning with *Na*, the suffix *Ṇya* is applied.
4.01.173: After *sālva*, *avayava*, *pratyagratha*, *kalakūṭa*, and *aśmaka*, the suffix *iÑ* is applied [to form patronymics].
4.01.174: Those [patronymics] denote the king of that [territory].
4.01.175: After *kamboja*, there is elision (*luK*) [of the patronymic suffix].
4.01.176. [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after the words *avanti*, *kunti*, and *kuru* when they denote a feminine.
4.01.177. [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after a word ending in short *a*.
4.01.178. [The suffix *ṅīp* is not applied] to words denoting Easterners (*prācya*), nor to the group beginning with *bharga*, nor to the group beginning with *yaudheya*.
4.02.001 That by which something is colored (rakta) is called *rāga*.
4.02.002 The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after the words *lākṣā*, *rocanā*, (*śakala*, *kardama*) in the sense of "colored by.
4.02.003 Time conjoined with a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) [is denoted by the suffix *aṇ*].

4.02.004 *luP* [is applied] when there is no distinction [between the meanings of the members]. 4.02.005 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after *śravaṇā* and *aśvattha* when they form a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
4.02.006 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a *dvaṃdva* compound.
4.02.007 The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the word *dṛṣṭa* [to form a name for a Sāman].
4.02.008 The suffix *ḍhak* is applied after the word *kali*.
4.02.009 The suffixes *ḍyaṭ* and *ḍya* are applied after the word *vāmadeva*.
4.02.010 The suffix *cha* (*īya*) is applied after the word *parivṛta* when it follows *ratha*.
4.02.011 The suffix *ini* is applied after the word *pāṇḍukambala*.
4.02.012 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after the words *dvaipa* and *vaiyāghra*.

4.02.013 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *kaumāra*, when it does not denote something previously experienced. 4.02.014 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after that [word], when it means "taken out from vessels. 4.02.015 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *sthaṇḍila*, when it refers to one who observes a vow of sleeping on the bare ground.
4.02.016 The suffix *cha* (ya) is applied after the word *saṃskṛta* when it means "prepared as food.
4.02.017 The suffix *tyaP* is applied after the compound *śūlokhā*.
4.02.018 The suffix *ṭhaK* is applied after the word *dadhi*.
4.02.019 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] optionally after *udaśvit*.
4.02.020 [The suffix] *ḍhaÑ* is applied after *kṣīra*.
4.02.021 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word ending in the genitive case] in the sense of "that full moon day (*paurṇamāsī*) occurs in this [month]," provided it is a name (*saṃjñā*).
4.02.022 The suffix *ṭhaK* is added after *āgrahāyaṇī* and *aśvattha*.
4.02.023 The suffix [ṭhaK] is optionally added after *phālgunī*, *śrāvaṇā*, *kārttikī*, and *caitrī*.
4.02.024 That [deity] is his deity (*sā asya devatā*).
4.02.025 The suffix *iṭ* is added after *ka*.
4.02.026 The suffix *ghaÑ* is added after *śukra*.
4.02.027 The suffix *gha* is added after *aponaptṛ* and *apāṃnaptṛ*.

4.02.028: [The suffix] *cha* and *ca* [are applied after the word *mahendra*]. 4.02.029: [The suffixes] *gha* and *aṇ* are also [applied after the word *mahendra*]. 4.02.030: [The suffix] *ṭyaṇ* [is applied] after the word *soma*.
4.02.031 The suffix *yaT* is applied after *vāyu*, *ṛtu*, *pitṛ*, and *uṣas*.
4.02.032 The suffix *yaT* is also applied after *dyāvāpṛthivī*, *śunāsīra*, *marutvat*, *agnīṣoma*, *vāstoṣpati*, and *gṛhamedha*.
4.02.033 The suffix *ḍhaK* is applied after *agni*.
4.02.034 [The suffix *cha*] is applied after words denoting time, just as it is applied after words denoting origin (*bhava*).
4.02.035 The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the words *mahārāja* and *proṣṭhapada*.
4.02.036 The forms *pitṛvya*, *mātula*, *mātāmaha*, and *pitāmaha* are irregularly formed [by the substitution of specific suffixes].

4.02.037 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word ending in] *tad*, [to form a word meaning] "a collection thereof. 4.02.038 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after [the group of words beginning with] *bhikṣā*. 4.02.039 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after] *gotra* and *ukṣan*.
The suffix *vuÑ* is applied after *uṣṭra*, *urabhra*, *rājan*, *rājanya*, *rājaputra*, *vatsa*, *manuṣya*, and *aja*.
(Pāṇini 4.2.40) The suffix *yaÑ* is also applied after *kedāra*. (Pāṇini 4.2.41) The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is applied after *kavacin*. (Pāṇini 4.2.42)
4.02.042 *yañ* is added after *brāhmaṇa*, *māṇava*, and *vāḍaba*.
4.02.043 *tal* is added after *grāma*, *jana*, *bandhu*, and *sahāya*.
4.02.044 *añ* is added after words beginning with an anudātta vowel.
4.02.045 And [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after [the group of words] beginning with *khaṇḍika*.
4.02.046 After [words denoting] Vedic schools (*caraṇa*), [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] as in the case of *dharma*.
4.02.047 The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after [words ending in] *acitta*, *hastin*, and *dhenu*.
4.02.048 The suffix *yañ* or *cha* may optionally be applied after the words *keśa* and *aśva*.
4.02.049 The suffix *ya* is applied after the group of words beginning with *pāśa*.
4.02.050 [The suffix *ya* is applied] after the words *khala*, *go*, and *ratha*.
4.02.051 The suffixes *ini*, *tra*, *kaṭyac*, and *as* [are applied after a word denoting the object of a desire].
4.02.052 [The same suffixes] are applied when the object is a place (*deśa*).
4.02.053 The suffix *vuñ* is applied after words such as *rājanya* and others [when the object is a place].
4.02.054 The suffixes *vidhal* and *bhakta* are added after the groups beginning with *bhauriki* and *aiṣukāri*.
4.02.055 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *sa-* is added [to a word] when it means "this is the beginning of that," provided it occurs in *pragātha* verses.
4.02.056 The suffix *sa-* is added after words denoting a battle, its purpose, or the combatant therein.
4.02.057 The suffix *Ṇa* is applied [to a word denoting an instrument] in the sense of "striking with that" when referring to a sport (*krīḍā*).

4.02.058 The suffix *Ña* is applied [to a word denoting an action] in the sense of "this is the activity performed with that. 4.02.059 The suffix *Ṇa* is applied [to a word denoting a subject matter] in the senses of "one studies that" or "one knows that."
4.02.060 The suffix *ṭhak* is added after words such as *kratu*, *uktha*, and those ending in *sūtra*.
4.02.061 The suffix *vuñ* is added after words such as *krama*.
4.02.062 The suffix *inī* is added after the word *anubrāhmaṇa*.
4.02.063 The suffix *ṭhak* is added after [words beginning with] *vasanta*.
4.02.064 There is elision (*luk*) of the suffix when it is prescribed by the word *prokta*.
4.02.065 And [the suffix *ṭhak* is added] after the word *sūtra*, provided it has *ka* as its penultimate letter (*upadha*).
4.02.066 The suffix *cha* (forming the word *chāndasa*) is applied to the name of a *brāhmaṇa* when it refers to that [Vedic] subject matter.
4.02.067 The suffix *aṇ* is applied in the sense of "this exists in this" to form the name of a region.
4.02.068 The suffix *aṇ* is applied in the sense of "produced by means of that."
4.02.069: [The suffix *cha* is applied after a word] meaning "his dwelling.
4.02.070: [The suffix *cha* is applied] also after a word meaning "situated not far from that.
4.02.071: [In these cases, the substitute] *aÑ* is used in place of the suffix *oR*.

4.02.072 The suffix *mat* is also [added] after a word ending in *aṅga* that has more than two syllables. 4.02.073 [The suffix *mat* is added] after a word with more than two syllables when referring to wells (*kūpa*).
4.02.074 And [the suffix *mat* is added] after the word *vipāś* when preceded by *udaka*.
4.02.075 And [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after *saṃkala* and others.
4.02.076 Among women, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after [names of] Sauvīra and Sālva in the Eastern region.
4.02.077 After *suvāstu* and others, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied].
4.02.078 *roṇī* 4.02.079 Also after a stem having *kā* as its penultimate (*upadha*).

4.02.080 The suffixes *vuñ*, *chaṇ*, *ka*, *ṭhac*, *ilac*, *sa*, *ini*, *ra*, *ḍhañ*, *ṇya*, *ya*, *phak*, *phiñ*, *iñ*, *ṇyakaṅ*, *ṭhak* [are applied] after the words *arīhaṇa*, *kṛśāśva*, *ṛśya*, *kumuda*, *kāśa*, *tṛṇa*, *prekṣā*, and *aśman*.

The suffix *luP* is applied [to denote a country] after the words *sakhi*, *saṃkāśa*, *bala*, *pakṣa*, *karṇa*, *sutaṅgama*, *pragadin*, *varāha*, *kumuda*, and so forth; as well as after the group beginning with *varaṇā*. 4.2.81–82.
4.02.083. Or [the suffix] śarkarāyaḥ. 4.02.084. And [the suffixes] ṭhak and cha.
4.02.085. [The suffix] matUP is used after a word denoting a river.
4.02.086 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after *madhu* and others.
4.02.087 The suffix *ḍmatup* is applied after *kumuda*, *naḍa*, and *vetasa*.
4.02.088 The suffix *ḍvalac* is applied after *naḍa* and *śāda*.
4.02.089 *śikhā-yāḥ* = *valaC* 4.02.090 From *utkara* and so forth, *cha-* [is added]. 4.02.091 For *naḍa* and so forth, *kuK* [is added] as well.
4.02.092 [The suffix *śas* is applied] after the word *śeṣa*.
4.02.093 [The suffixes] *gha* and *kha* are applied after the compound *rāṣṭrāvārapāra*.
4.02.094 [The suffixes] *ya* and *khañ* are applied after the word *grāma*.
4.02.095 The suffix *ḍhakañ* is added after [words ending in] *katṛ* and others.
4.02.096 The suffix *śvan* is added after *kula*, *kukṣi*, and *grīvā* when followed by *asi*, *alaṃ*, or *āre*.
4.02.097 The suffix *ḍhak* is applied after words such as *nadī*. 4.02.098 The suffix *tyak* is applied after *dakṣiṇā*, *paścāt*, and *puras*. 4.02.099 The suffix *ṣphak* is applied after *kāpiśī*.
4.02.100 The suffix *aṇ* is added after *raṅku*, provided it does not refer to a human being.
4.02.101 The suffix *yaT* is added after *dyu*, *prāc*, *apāc*, *udac*, and *pratīc*.
4.02.102 The suffix *ṭhaK* is added after *kaṇṭhā*.
4.02.103 The suffix *vuK* is applied after a vowel.
4.02.104 The suffix *tyaP* is applied after an indeclinable (*avyaya*).
4.02.105 The suffix *nyaT* is applied after the words *aiṣamas*, *hyas*, and *śvas*.

4.02.106 The suffixes *aÑ* and *Ña* are applied after a compound whose final member is *tīra* or *rūpya*. 4.02.107 The suffix *Ña* is applied after a compound whose first member is a cardinal direction (*dik*), provided it is not a proper name (*asaṃjñā*). 4.02.108 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after the word *madra*.
4.02.109: [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a village name from the North that has more than two vowels (*bahu-aC*) and ends with an acute-accented vowel.
4.02.110: [The suffix *aṆ* is applied] after a word ending in *prastha*, after a word having *paladī* as its first member, and after a word having *ka* as its penultimate letter.
4.02.111: [The suffix *aṆ* is applied] after the group beginning with *Kaṇva* to denote a gotra (lineage).
4.02.112 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in *iṅ*.
