4.02.113 Not so, however, after a word with two vowels (*dvyaC*) among those belonging to the Easterners or to the Bharatas.
4.02.114 After a word containing a *vṛddhi* vowel in its first syllable, the suffix *cha* is applied.
4.02.115 The suffixes *thaK* and *chaS* are added after the word *bhavat*.
4.02.116 The suffixes *thaÑ* and *ñiṬh* are added after the group of words beginning with *kāśi*.
4.02.117 [The same suffixes] are also added after the names of villages belonging to the Vāhīkas.
4.02.118 The suffix *cha* is optionally applied [after a word denoting a country] among the Uśīnaras.
4.02.119 The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a country name beginning with *o*.
4.02.120 The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a country name containing a *vṛddhi*-vowel according to the Eastern grammarians.
4.02.121: The suffix *vuñ* is added [to form a patronymic] after a word ending in *dhanvan*, provided that the penultimate letter is *ya*.
4.02.122: [The suffix *vuñ* is added] also after words ending in *prastha*, *pura*, or those ending in a vowel.
4.02.123: According to the Eastern grammarians (*prācām*), the suffix *vuñ* is added after words whose penultimate letter is *ra* or which end in the long vowel *ī*.

4.02.124 [The suffix *cha* is applied after a word denoting a country or its boundary. 4.02.125 [The suffix *cha* is applied] even after a word that is not a *vṛddhi*-stem, provided it refers to a plural number. 4.02.126 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a compound whose final member is *kaccha*, *agni*, *vaktra*, or *varta*.

4.02.127 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after *dhūma* and so forth. 4.02.128 After *nagara*, [the suffix *cha* is applied] in the sense of contempt or skillfulness. 4.02.129 After *araṇya*, [the suffix *cha* is applied] in the sense of a human being.
4.02.130 The suffix *aṇ* is optionally applied after the words *kuru* and *yugandhara*.
4.02.131 The suffix *kaN* is applied after the words *madra* and *vṛji*.
4.02.132 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after a word that has *ka* as its penultimate (*upadhā*) letter.
4.02.133 And [the suffix *vuñ* is added] after *kaccha* and others.
4.02.134 The suffix *vuñ* is added after a word denoting a human being or something residing therein.
4.02.135 After the word *sālva*, [the suffix *vuñ* is added], except when it means "foot-soldier."
4.02.136 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *go* and *yavāgū*.
4.02.137 Also [the suffix *cha* is applied] after a word that has *garta* as its final member.
4.02.138 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after the group of words beginning with *gaha*.

4.02.139 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after words beginning with *kaṭa* when they denote eastern [localities]. 4.02.140 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after *rājan*, and [the final *n*] is replaced by *k*.
4.02.141 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word denoting a place that has a long vowel (*vṛddhi*) as its penultimate letter, provided it ends in *aka* or *ika*.
4.02.142 [The suffix *cha* (i.e., *īya*) is applied] after words ending in *kaṇṭha*, *palada*, *nagara*, *grāma*, and *hrada* when they form the final member of a compound;
4.02.143 and also after *parvata*; 4.02.144 optionally (*vibhāṣā*), provided that the referent is not a human being.

4.02.145: After *kṛkaṇa* and *parṇa*, [the suffix *cha*] is applied when *bharadvāja* follows. 4.03.001: After the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the suffix *khañ* is optionally applied. 4.03.002: And when that [suffix] is *aṇ*, the substitutes *yuṣmāka-* and *asmāka-* are applied [to *yuṣmad* and *asmad*].
4.03.003 The suffix *ya* is applied after the words *tavaka* and *mamaka* when used in the singular; 4.03.004 [The suffix *yaT* is applied] after the word *ardha*;
4.03.005 [The suffix *yaT* is applied] also after words preceded by *para*, *avara*, *adhama*, and *uttama*.
4.03.006 The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is also [added] after a word beginning with *dik-* (direction) as its first member.
4.03.007 The suffixes *aÑ* and *ṭhaÑ* are added after a word denoting a part of a village or a district (*grāma-janapada*).
4.03.008 The suffix *ma-* is added after the word *madhya-* (middle).
4.03.009 [The suffix *ka* is applied after a word ending in *sāman* when it means "opposite to" (*prati*)].
4.03.010 [The suffix *yañ* is applied after a word meaning "continent" (*dvīpa*) when it signifies "extending along the ocean" (*anu-samudram*)].
4.03.011 [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word meaning "time" (*kāla*)].

4.03.012 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *śarad*] in the sense of "fit for a *śrāddha*. 4.03.013 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the words *śarad*, *roga*, and *ātapa*] optionally. 4.03.014 [The suffix *cha* is applied] also after the words *niśā* and *pradoṣa*.
4.03.015 After the word *śvas*, [the suffix] *tuṬ* is also [added].
4.03.016 After *saṃdhi*, *velā*, and so forth, as well as *ṛtu*, *nakṣatra*, and *hyaḥ*, the suffix *aṆ* is added.
4.03.017 After *prāvṛṣ*, the suffix *eṇya* is added.
4.03.018 The suffix *ṭhak* is added after the word *varṣā*.
4.03.019 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *ṭhañ* is added.
4.03.020 And [the suffix *ṭhañ* is added] after the word *vasanta*.
4.03.021 After *hemanta*, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied]. 4.03.022 In all cases, *aṇ* is applied [after *hemanta*], and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the *t*.
4.03.023 After the indeclinables *sāyam*, *ciram*, *prāhṇe*, *prage*, and *hyas*, the suffixes *ṭyu* and *ṭyuL* are applied, and *tuṭ* is inserted [before them].

4.03.024 The suffixes [ṭhaÑ and ṭhaL] are optionally applied after the words *pūrvāhṇa* and *aparāhṇa*. 4.03.025 The suffix *cha* (ya) is applied after a word ending in the locative case when it means "born there. 4.03.026 The suffix *ṭhaP* is applied after the word *prāvṛṣ*.

4.03.027 *vuÑ* is added after *śarad* in the sense of a name (*saṃjñā*). 4.03.028 *vuÑ* is added after *pūrvāhṇa*, *aparāhṇa*, *ārdrā*, *mūla*, *pradoṣa*, and *avaskara*. 4.03.029 After *pathin*, *pantha* is substituted [for *pathin*] and *vuÑ* is added.
4.03.030 [The suffix *kaN* is applied] after *amāvāsyā*, optionally;
4.03.031 [the suffix *kaN* is applied] after [a word ending in] *a*; 4.03.032 [the suffix *kaN* is applied] after *sindhu* and *apakara*.
4.03.033. And [the suffix] *aṆ* is replaced by *aÑ*.
4.03.034. [The suffix] *luK* is applied after the names of the asterisms *śraviṣṭhā*, *phalgunī*, *anurādhā*, *svāti*, *tiṣya*, *punarvasu*, *hasta*, *viśākhā*, *aṣāḍhā*, and *bahulā*.
4.03.035. [The suffix *luK* is also applied] after words ending in *sthāna*, as well as after *go*, *śāla*, *khara*, and *śālā*.
4.03.036 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the words] *vatsa-śālā*, *abhijit*, *aśva-yuj*, and *śata-hiṣaj*, optionally.
4.03.037 [The suffix *cha* is applied] diversely (*bahulam*) after the names of lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
4.03.038 [The suffix *cha* is applied after a word ending in the locative case when it means] "made," "obtained," "bought," or "skilled" (*kṛta-labdha-krīta-kuśala*).
4.03.039 *prāya-bhava-* (the suffix *cha* is applied after these words in the sense of "mostly occurring there");
4.03.040 *upa-jānu*, *upa-karṇa*, *upa-nīvi*—the suffix *ṭhaK* [is applied after these in the sense of "mostly occurring there"];
4.03.041 *saṃ-bhū-te* (the suffix *cha* is applied after these words in the sense of "originating from that").
4.03.042 The suffix *ḍhaÑ* is applied after the word *kośa*.
4.03.043 The suffix *ḍhaÑ* is applied after the word *kāla* when it signifies "good for," "flowering at," or "ripening at" [a particular time].
4.03.044 And [the suffix *ḍhaÑ* is applied] after the word *upta* (sown) in the same senses.
4.03.045 The suffix *vuÑ* is added after *āśvayujī*.
4.03.046 The suffix *vuÑ* is optionally added after *grīṣma* and *vasanta*.
4.03.047 The suffix *vuÑ* is added after [a word ending in] *deya* when it means "a debt."
4.03.048 The suffix *uṆ* is applied after *kalāpin*, *aśvattha*, and *yavabus*.
4.03.049 The suffix *vuÑ* is applied after *grīṣma* and *avarasama*.
4.03.050 The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is also applied after *saṃvatsara* and *āgrahāyaṇī*.
4.03.051 A deer utters [a cry].
4.03.052 That has been endured by him. 4.03.053 That which exists therein.
4.03.054 The suffix *yaT* is applied after [words] such as *diś* (direction).
4.03.055 And [the suffix *yaT* is applied] after a word denoting a limb of the body.
4.03.056 The suffix *ḍhaÑ* is applied after *dṛti*, *kukṣi*, *kalaśi*, *vasti*, *asti*, and *ahi*.
4.03.057 The suffix *aṇ* is also applied after [the word] *grīvā*.
4.03.058 The suffix *ñya* is applied after [the word] *gambhīra*. 4.03.059 And [the suffix *ñya* is applied] after an *avyayībhāva* compound.
4.03.060 The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a compound whose prior member ends in *anta*.
4.03.061 The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *grāma* when preceded by *pari* or *anu*.
4.03.062 The suffix *cha* is applied after the words *jihvāmūla* and *aṅguli*.
4.03.063 [The suffix *ka*] is also applied after a word ending in *varga*.
4.03.064 After a word ending in *a*, the suffixes *yaT* or *kh* are optionally applied when the word *śabda* does not follow.
4.03.065 The suffix *kaN* is applied after *karṇa* and *lalāṭa* when referring to an ornament.
4.03.066 And [the suffix *cha*] occurs after [a word ending in] *vyākhyāna*, provided that the *vyākhyā* (explanation) is not a Vedic text (*avyāmnāta*).
4.03.067 The suffix *ṭhaÑ* occurs after a Bahuvrīhi compound ending in a vowel other than *aC*, which has an udātta accent on its final syllable.
4.03.068 [The suffix *ṭhaÑ*] also occurs after words denoting *kratu* (sacrificial sessions) and *yajña* (sacrifices).
4.03.069 [The suffix *ya*] is applied after the names of Ṛṣis only when they occur in the *adhyāyas*.
4.03.070 [The suffix] *ṣṭhan* is applied after the words *pauroḍāśa* and *puroḍāśa*. 4.03.071 [The suffixes] *yaT* and *aṆ* are applied after the word *chandas*.

4.03.072 The suffix *ṭhak* is added after a word ending in two vowels (*dvy-aC*), after the words *ṛt*, *brāhmaṇa*, *ṛc*, *prathama*, *adhvara*, *puruṣa*, *caraṇa*, a proper name (*nāman*), and a verb (*ākhyāta*).
4.03.073 The suffix *aṇ* is added after the words *ṛg-ayana* and others.
4.03.074 The suffix *aṇ* is added in the sense of "come from that" (*tata āgataḥ*).
4.03.075 The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words meaning "place of residence.
4.03.076 The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the group of words beginning with *śuṇḍika*.
4.03.077 The suffix *vuñ* is applied after words denoting a relationship through learning or by birth.
4.03.078 The suffix *thañ* is applied after the word *ṛta*.
4.03.079 The suffix *yaT* is also applied after the word *pitṛ*.
4.03.080 After a word denoting a *gotra*, the suffixes are applied as in the case of *ṛk*.
4.03.081 The suffix *rūpya* optionally occurs after words meaning "cause" (*hetu*) and "human being" (*manuṣya*).
4.03.082 The suffix *mayaṬ* also [occurs in these senses].
4.03.083 [The suffix *mayaṬ* occurs] in the sense of "originates from" (*prabhavati*).
4.03.084 The suffix Ñya is applied [to a word denoting a distance] in the sense of "from that distance.

4.03.085 The suffix Ñya is applied [to a word denoting a distance] in the sense of "a path leading to that" or "a messenger going to that. 4.03.086 The suffix Ñya is applied [to a word denoting a distance] in the sense of "a door leading out from that."
4.03.087 The suffix *cha* (ya) is added [to a word] when it has been composed as a treatise concerning that [subject].
4.03.088 The suffix *cha* (ya) is also added after the words *śiśukranda*, *yamasabha*, *dvandva*, *indrajana*, and so forth.
4.03.089 The suffix *sa* (aṇ) is added [after a word] to form a derivative meaning "this is his dwelling."
4.03.090 And [the suffix] *añ* is applied after [words denoting] one's lineage (*abhi-jana*).
4.03.091 And [the suffix] *cha* is applied after [words denoting] those who live by weapons (*āyudha-jīvin*) when [the word] *parvata* follows.
4.03.092 [The suffix] *ñya* is applied after [words belonging to the class beginning with] *śaṇḍika*.
4.03.093: After [place names] such as Sindhu and Takṣaśilā, the suffixes aṆ and aÑ [are applied].
4.03.094: After Tūdī, Śalātura, Varmatī, and Kūcavāra, the suffixes ḍhaK, chaṆ, ḍhaÑ, and yaK [are applied respectively].
4.03.095: The suffix bhakTi is applied [to denote devotion].
4.03.096. The suffix *ṭhaK* is applied after [words] other than those meaning "mind" (*acitta*) when they do not denote a place or a time.
4.03.097. The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is applied after the word *mahārāja*.
4.03.098. The suffix *vuN* is applied after the words *vāsudeva* and *arjuna*.

4.03.099: After names of *gotras* and *kṣatriyas*, the suffix *vuñ* is generally applied [to form patronymics]. 4.03.100: For those [names] ending in *-pada* that denote a country (*janapada*), everything [the rules for country names] applies as for a country name, provided they have the same form as the country name when used in the plural. 4.03.101: [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] to form the name of a work proclaimed by someone.
4.03.102 After *tittiri*, *vara*, *tantu*, *khaṇḍika*, and *ukha*, the suffix *cha* (forming *īya*) is applied.
4.03.103 After the names of the sages *kāśyapa* and *kauśika*, the suffix *ṇini* is applied.
4.03.104 After *kalāpin*, and after those ending in *vaiśampāyana*, as well as after those ending in *antevāsin*, the suffix *ṇini* is applied.
4.03.105 [The suffix *prokta* is applied] after the word *purāṇa* and after names of small Brāhmaṇas.
4.03.106 [The suffix *prokta* is applied] after *śaunaka* and others when referring to Vedic meters (*chandas*).
4.03.107 After *kaṭha* and *caraka*, there is elision (*luK*) [of the suffix *prokta*].
4.03.108 After *kalāpin*, the suffix *aṆ* [is applied].

4.03.109 After *chagalin*, the suffix *ḍhinuK* [is applied]. 4.03.110 After *pārāśarya* and *śilālin*, [the suffixes *aṆ* and *ṇini* respectively are applied] in the sense of "mendicant" (*bhikṣu*) and "actor" (*naṭa*) according to their respective *sūtras*.

4.03.111 The suffix *ini* is added after *karmanda* and *kṛśāśva*. 4.03.112 [The suffix *ini* is added] after a word denoting direction when it means "in the same direction as that. 4.03.113 The suffix *tasi* is also [added in this sense].
4.03.114 The suffix *yaT* is also [added] after *uras*.
4.03.115 [The suffix *yaT* is added] after *upa-jñā* when it means "invented by.
4.03.116 [The suffix *yaT* is added] after *kṛta* when it refers to a literary work (*grantha*).
4.03.117 [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after a word denoting a personal name (*saṃjñā*).
4.03.118 The suffix *vuñ* is applied after words such as *kulāla* (potter) and others.
4.03.119 The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the words *kṣudra*, *bhramara*, *vaṭara*, and *pādapa*.
4.03.120: The suffix *cha* (forming *-īya*) is applied after [a word ending in] *tasya idam* ("belonging to this").
4.03.121: The suffix *yaT* is applied after [a word meaning] "chariot" (*ratha*).
4.03.122: The suffix *aÑ* is applied after [a word] preceded by *pattra*.
4.03.123 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the words] *pattra*, *adhvaryu*, and *pariṣad*.
4.03.124 [The suffix] *ṭhak* is applied after *hala* and *sīra*.
4.03.125 [The suffix] *vuñ* is applied after a *dvandva* compound when it denotes enmity (*vaira*) or a matrimonial alliance (*maithunika*).
4.03.126: The suffix *vuñ* is added after a word denoting a *gotra* (lineage) or a *caraṇa* (Vedic school).
4.03.127: The suffix *aṇ* replaces the suffixes *aṅ*, *yaṅ*, and *iṅ* when they denote a *saṃgha* (an assembly), a *ṛk* (a verse), or a *lakṣaṇa* (a characteristic mark).
4.03.128: After the word *śākala*, the suffix *aṇ* is optionally applied.

4.03.129 The suffix *Ñya* is applied after the words *chandoga*, *aukthika*, *yājñika*, *bahvṛca*, and *naṭ*. 4.03.130 This [suffix] is not applied after the words *daṇḍamāṇava* and *antevāsin*. 4.03.131 The suffix *Cha* is applied after the group of words beginning with *raivatika*.
4.03.132: After *kaupīñjala* and *hāstipada*, the suffix *aṆ* is applied. 4.03.133: For *ātharvaṇika*, there is also the elision of the suffix *ika*.
4.03.134: [The suffix *aṆ* is applied] to denote "a modification thereof" (*tasya vikāraḥ*).

4.03.136 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after [words] beginning with *bilva*. 4.03.137 And [the suffix *aṆ* is applied] after [words] having *ka* as their penultimate letter (*upadhā*). 4.03.138 The augment *ṣuK* is applied after *trapu* and *jatu*.
4.03.139 *o-r aÑ* 4.03.140 *an-udātta-ādeś-ca* 4.03.141 *palāśa-ādi-bhyaḥ vā*
4.03.142: After the word *śamyā*, the suffix *ṬlaÑ* [is applied].
4.03.143: In common usage (*bhāṣā*), the suffix *mayaṬ* is optionally applied after these two [suffixes], except when the resulting word denotes food or clothing.
4.03.144: The suffix *mayaṬ* is invariably applied after words ending in *vṛddhi* vowels and after the group beginning with *śara*.
4.03.145 The suffix *kaN* is applied after the word *go-* when it means "cow-dung.
4.03.146 [The suffix *kaN* is applied] also after the word *piṣṭa-* (meaning "flour").
4.03.147 The suffix *kaN* is applied [after a word ending in *a*] to form a proper name (*saṃjñā*).

4.03.148 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *vrīhi* when *puroḍāśa* follows. 4.03.149 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after *tila* and *yava*, provided they do not form a technical name (*asaṃjñāyām*). 4.03.150 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a stem ending in two vowels (*dvyac*) in the Vedic language (*chandasi*).
4.03.151 Not [the suffix *cha*] after words ending in *u*, nor after *vadhra* and *bilva*. 4.03.152 The suffix *aṆ* after [words beginning with] *tāla*.
4.03.153 [The suffix *aṆ*] after words denoting gold (*jātarūpa*) when expressing a measure.
4.03.155 And [the suffix *cha*] is added after a word ending in *ñit*, provided that it is a secondary derivative (*pratyaya*).
4.03.156 The suffix *cha* is added after a word denoting a measure, as if it were a word ending in the suffix *krīta*.
4.03.157 The suffix *vuñ* is added after the word *uṣṭra*.
4.03.158 The suffix *ya* is optionally applied after the words *umā* and *ūrṇā*.
4.03.159 The suffix *ḍhañ* is applied after the word *eṇī*. 4.03.160 The suffix *yat* is applied after the words *go* and *payas*.

5.01.079 [The suffix *kṛt*] is applied after a verbal root to denote that which has been accomplished by means of that [action].
5.01.080 [The suffix *kṛt*] is applied after a verbal root to denote one who has been requested for that [action], or one who has been hired for it, or one who has been summoned for it.
5.01.081 The suffixes *yaT* and *kh* are applied after the word *māsa* to denote age.

5.01.082 The suffix *yaP* is applied after a *dvigu* compound. 5.01.083 After the word *ṣaṇmāsa*, the suffix *ṆyaT* is also applied. 5.01.084 When not referring to age, the suffix *ṭhaN* is also applied.
5.01.085: After the word *samā*, the suffix *kha* [is applied].
5.01.086: After a *dvigu* compound, [the suffix *kha*] is optionally [applied].
5.01.088: After the word *varṣa*, there is also elision (*luk*) [of the suffix].
5.01.089 [The suffix *matup*] is always [elided] before a word ending in *cittavat*.

5.01.090 [The suffix *kan* is added after] words meaning "sixty" when they signify "cooked in sixty nights. 5.01.091 [The suffix *cha* is added after a word ending in *vatsara*,] and [the suffix *sa* is added] in the Vedic language (*chandasi*).
5.01.092 The suffix *kha* (īna) is also applied after [the prefix] *sam*, *pari*, and *ūrv-* [when combined with a root].
5.01.093 The suffix *kha* is applied after [a word ending in the third case] to form adjectives meaning "conquerable by that," "obtainable by that," or "to be done by that.
5.01.094 That [period of time] constitutes his *brahmacarya* (student life).
5.01.095 And [the suffix *cha*] is applied after words meaning "sacrifice" (*yajña*) when followed by *dakṣiṇā*.
5.01.096 And in that case, the word *kārya* is used as the substitute for *bhava*.
5.01.097 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after words beginning with *vyuṣṭa*.
5.01.098 The suffixes *Ṇa* and *yaT* are applied after [the words] *tad*, *anaya-thā-kathā-ca*, *hasta*, and *ahya*.
5.01.099 [The suffix *Ṇa* is applied] after [words ending in the seventh case] when the meaning is "one who accomplishes.
5.01.101 [The suffix *Ṇa* is applied] after words such as *saṃtāpa* in the sense of "that which is capable of producing" that [which ends in the fifth case].
5.01.102 The suffix *yaT* is applied [after a word denoting a cause] due to connection (*yogāt*).
5.01.103 The suffix *ukaÑ* is applied after a word denoting an object (*karmaṇaḥ*).
5.01.104 The suffix *yat* is applied [after a word denoting time] in the sense of "that has been obtained by him" (*tad asya prāptam*).
5.01.105 The suffix aṆ is applied after the word *ṛtu*.
5.01.106 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix ghaS is applied.
5.01.107 The suffix yaT is applied after words denoting time (*kāla*).

5.01.108 The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is applied [after a word ending in the locative case] in the sense of "drawn out" (*pra-kṛṣ-ṭa*). 5.01.109 [The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is applied after a word ending in the locative case] in the sense of "the purpose" (*prayojana*). 5.01.110 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after the words *viśākhā* and *aṣāḍhā* [in the locative case], when the meaning is "a churning-stick" (*manthadaṇḍa*).

5.01.111 The suffix *cha* is applied after [compounds] beginning with *anupravacana*. 5.01.112 The suffix *cha* is applied after *samāpanna*, provided it is preceded by another word. 5.01.113 The suffix *aikāgārika* is applied in the sense of "thief."

5.01.114 The suffix *kālika* is added after *ā* in the sense of "lasting until that time. 5.01.115 If the action is equal [to another], the suffix *vati* is added after a word ending in the third case (*tena*). 5.01.116 The suffix *vati* is also added after a word ending in the seventh case (*tatra*) or the sixth case (*tasya*) in the sense of "like that" (*iva*).
5.01.117 That [suffix] is used in the sense of "deserving" (arha).
5.01.118 In the Vedic language, [the suffix *ghañ*] is used after a prefix (*upasarga*) in the sense of the verbal root's meaning.
5.01.119 The abstract state (*bhāva*) of that [thing] is expressed by the suffixes *tva* and *tal*.
5.01.120 [The suffix *ka* is applied] up to and including [the rule ending in] *tv*.

5.01.121 [The suffix *ka* is not applied] after a *tatpuruṣa* compound beginning with the negative particle *naÑ*, except for the words *acatura*, *saṃgata*, *lavaṇa*, *vaṭa*, *yudha*, *kata*, *rasa*, and *lasa*.
5.01.122 [The suffix] *maniC* is applied after [words beginning with] *pṛthu* and others.
5.01.123: After words beginning with *varṇadṛḍha*, the suffix *ṣyañ* is added [to form a feminine noun].
5.01.124: After words expressing qualities (*guṇavacana*) and those beginning with *brāhmaṇa*, the suffix *ṣyañ* is added in the sense of an action (*karman*).
5.01.125: After the word *stena*, the suffix *yaT* is added, and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the nasal *n*.

5.01.126 *sakhyuḥ* [the suffix] *yaḥ* [is applied after the word *sakhi*]. 5.01.127 After the words *kapi* and *jñāti*, the suffix *ḍhaK* [is applied]. 5.01.128 After words ending in *pati*, and after the group beginning with *purohita*, the suffix *aK* [is applied].

5.01.129: The suffix *aÑ* is applied after words denoting species (*jāti*), age (*vayas*), or speech (*vacana*), as well as after *udgātṛ* and similar terms, when followed by the patronymic suffix *hya*.
5.01.131: The suffix *uÑ* is also applied after a word ending in an *iK* vowel (i, u, ṛ, ḷ) that has a light (*laghu*) penultimate syllable.
5.01.132: The suffix *uÑ* is applied after a word whose penultimate letter is *ya*, provided it has a heavy (*guru*) penultimate syllable and ends in a labial (*pu*).
5.01.133 The suffix *hyaṅ* is applied after a *dvandva* compound and words such as *manojña*, etc., in the sense of "equal to.
5.01.134 The suffix *hyaṅ* is applied after a *gotra* name and a *caraṇa* name when expressing praise, reproach, or the state of being that [name].
5.01.135 The suffix *cha* is applied after the names of *hotṛ* priests.
5.01.136 *brahmaṇas tvaḥ* (The suffix *tva* is added after the word *brahman*).
5.02.001 *dhānyānāṃ bhavane kṣetre khañ* (The suffix *khañ* is added after words denoting grains when [the compound] means "a field for the production of" those grains).
5.02.002 *vrīhiśālyor ḍhak* (The suffix *ḍhak* is added after the words *vrīhi* and *śāli* [in the same sense]).
5.02.003 The suffix *aT* is applied after *yava*, *yavaka*, and *ṣaṣṭi*.
5.02.004 The suffix *aT* is optionally applied after *tila*, *māṣa*, *umā*, *bhṛṅga*, *aṇu*, and *hya*.
5.02.005 The suffixes *kha* and *khaÑ* are applied after *sarvacarman* when it means "made from" (*kṛta*).
5.02.006 [The suffix *kha* is applied after a verbal root] when preceded by *yathāmukha* and *saṃmukha*, provided that the face (*mukha*) is visible.
5.02.008 [The suffix *kha* is applied after a verbal root] when preceded by *āprapada*.

5.02.009 [The suffix *kha* is applied after a verbal root] when preceded by *anupada*, *sarvānna*, *āyāna*, or *anaya*, in the sense of "binding," "eating," "leading away," and "being led," respectively.
5.02.010 He experiences the succession of sons and grandsons, one after another, from father to son.
5.02.011 He goes to the earth, reaching its near shore, its far shore, its limit, and its very end.
5.02.012 He is born year after year.
5.02.013 [The suffix *in* is applied after the words *adya* and *śvas* when they are compounded with *ava-ṣṭabdha*.
5.02.014 [The word *āgavīnaḥ* is derived [from *go* with the suffix *kha* and the replacement of the final vowel with *ī*].
5.02.015 [The suffix *ini* is applied after the words *anu-gu* and *alaṃ-gu* when they are followed by *gāmī*.]
5.02.016 The suffixes *yaT* and *kha* are added after the word *adhvan*.
5.02.017 The suffixes *yaT*, *kha*, and *cha* are also added after the word *abhyamitra*.
5.02.018 The suffix *khaÑ* is added after the word *goṣṭha* when it signifies "having previously existed there."
5.02.019 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *aśva*] in the sense of "one who can travel in a single day.
5.02.020 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the words *śālīna* and *kaupīna*] in the senses of "not being ashamed" and "not being noble," respectively.
5.02.021 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *vrāta*] in the sense of "one who lives by means of a troop."
5.02.022 The word *sāptapadīnam* denotes friendship.
5.02.023 The word *haiyaṅgavīnam* is used as a technical term (*saṃjñā*) for fresh butter.

5.02.024 The suffixes *kuṇap* and *jāhac* are applied after the words *pīlu* and others, and *karṇa* and others, respectively, when the sense is "its fruit" (*tasya pākaḥ*) or "its root" (*tasya mūlam*).
5.02.025 *ti* is added after *pakṣa*.
5.02.026 The suffixes *cuñcup* and *caṇap* are added after [a word] in the instrumental case in the sense of "skilled therein.
5.02.027 The suffixes *nā* and *nān* are added after *vi-* and *nañ-* respectively, with the meaning "not together" (*asaha*).
5.02.028 After the prefix *vi-*, the suffixes *śālac* and *śarakaṭac* [are applied].
5.02.029 After the prefixes *sam-*, *pra-*, *ut-*, and *ad-*, the suffix *kaṭac* [is applied].
5.02.030 After the prefix *ava-*, the suffix *kuṭārac* [is also applied].
5.02.031 The suffixes *ṭīṭac*, *nāṭac*, and *bhrāṭac* are added after the word *nāsikā* when it is not part of a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
5.02.032 The suffixes *biḍac* and *birīṣac* are added after the word *ni*.
5.02.033 The suffixes *inaṅ*, *piṭac*, *cik*, and *ci* are also added [after *ni*].
5.02.034 The suffix *tyakan* is added after the roots *upa* and *adhi* when they are followed by the words *āsanna* (near) and *ūḍha* (carried).
5.02.035 The suffix *aṭhac* is added to the root *ghaṭ* when the object (*karman*) is present.
5.02.036 The suffix *itaC* is added to words such as *tārakā* etc., when the sense is "that has arisen in him" (*tad asya sañjātam*).
5.02.037: After a word denoting measure, the suffixes *dvayasaC*, *daghnaC*, and *mātraC* are added [to form a bahuvrīhi].
5.02.038: After the words *puruṣa* and *hastin*, the suffix *aṆ* is also added [along with the aforementioned suffixes].
5.02.039: The suffix *vatUP* is added after *yat*, *tat*, *etad*, and *hyas* when expressing a measurement of circumference (*parimāṇa*).
5.02.040: After the words *kim* and *idam*, the suffix *gha* (which becomes *v* before vowels) is applied.
5.02.041: After *kim*, when expressing a number or a measure, the suffix *ḍati* is also applied. 5.02.042: The suffix *tayaP* is applied after a numeral to express a constituent part.
5.02.043 After the words *dvi* and *tri*, the suffixes *tayaP* and *yaC* are optionally [added].
5.02.044 After the word *ubha*, the suffix *tayaP* is always [added] with an acute accent (*udātta*) on its first syllable.
5.02.045 The suffix *Ḍa* is added after a word ending in *daśan* in the sense of "that is more than this."
5.02.046 The suffix *tamaP* is applied after the words *śata* and *viṃśati*.
5.02.047 The suffix *mayaṬ* is applied after a numeral when it denotes the measure of a quality.
5.02.048 The suffix *ḌaṬ* is applied in the sense of "completing that [number]."

5.02.049 The suffix *maṬ* is added after a word ending in *an*, provided it does not begin with a numeral. 5.02.050 And in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *thaṬ* is also added [after such words]. 5.02.051 The suffix *thuK* is added after the words *ṣaṣ*, *kati*, *katipaya*, and *catur*.
5.02.052 For *bahu*, *pūga*, *gaṇa*, and *saṃgha*, [the suffix] *tithuk* is applied.
5.02.054 After *dvi*, the suffix *tīya* is applied.
5.02.055 After *tri*, there is vowel-protraction (*samprasāraṇa*).
5.02.056 The suffix *tamaṬ* may optionally be added after words beginning with *viṃśati*.
5.02.057 The suffix *tamaṬ* is necessarily added after words beginning with *śata*, as well as after *māsa*, *ardhamāsa*, and *saṃvatsara*.
5.02.058 [The suffix *tamaṬ* is also added] after words beginning with *ṣaṣṭi*, provided they do not begin with a numeral (*saṃkhyā*).
5.02.059 The suffix *cha* is applied after the words *sūkta* and *sāman* when they denote a collection (*mata*).
5.02.060 The suffix *luK* (elision) is applied after the same words when they denote a chapter (*adhyāya*) or a section (*anuvāka*).
5.02.061 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after the group of words beginning with *vimukta*.
5.02.062 The suffix *vuÑ* is applied after [the group of words] beginning with *goṣad*.
5.02.063 The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *pathin* when it means "skilled in that.
5.02.064 The suffix *kaN* is applied after [the group of words] beginning with *ākārṣa*.
5.02.065 The suffix *kan* is added after the words *dhana* and *hiraṇya* when desire is expressed.
5.02.066 The suffix *kan* is added after words ending in *sva* and *arga* when a loan is indicated.
5.02.067 The suffix *ṭhak* is added after the word *udara* when it refers to one who does not gamble.
5.02.068 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *sasya* when it means "grown around";
5.02.069 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *aṃśa* when it means "one who takes a share";
5.02.070 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *tantra* when it means "recently removed from the loom."]

5.02.071 The suffix *ka* is applied after *brāhmaṇa* when it denotes a name; [the suffix] *ām* [is applied after *brāhmaṇa*] when it does not denote a name. 5.02.072 The suffix *in* is applied after *śīta* and *uṣṇa* when they signify the agent of the action.
5.02.073 The suffix *ika* is applied after *adhika*.
5.02.074 The suffix *kan* is applied after the words *anu*, *abhi*, and *abhī* when they signify "desire" (*kāmi*).
5.02.075 The suffix *kan* is applied after the word *pārśva* when it signifies "seeking along the side" (*anvicchati*).
5.02.076 The suffixes *ṭhak* and *ṭhañ* are applied after the words *ayaḥśūla*, *daṇḍa*, and *jin* [respectively].
5.02.077 The suffix *tāvatitha* is optionally elided (*luk*) when it denotes "grasping" (*grahaṇa*).
5.02.078 The suffix *ṭhak* is applied [after a word denoting a number] to form a name meaning "he is their leader" (*grāmaṇī*).
5.02.079 The word *śṛṅkhala* is used [with the suffix *ṭhak*] to mean "that which binds this [camel]" (*bandhana*) when referring to a young camel (*karabha*).

5.02.080 *utka-* and *unmanas-* [are formed with the suffix *kan*]. 5.02.081 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after a word denoting time, when it signifies the purpose for which [the action] is undertaken. 5.02.082 [The suffix *kan* is applied] to that [word], in the sense of "this is the usual food therein," provided it forms a conventional designation (*saṃjñā*).
5.02.083 The suffix *aÑ* is applied after *kulmāṣa*.
5.02.084 The suffix *śrotriyaN* is applied to one who studies the *Chandas* (Veda).
5.02.085 The suffixes *ini* and *ṭhaN* are applied to one by whom a *śrāddha* has been eaten.
5.02.086 The suffix *ini* is added after [the word] *pūrva*.
5.02.087 And [it is added] also after [a word] preceded by *sa-* (*sapūrva*).
5.02.088 And [the suffix *ini* is added] after [the group of words] beginning with *iṣṭa*.

5.02.090 The suffix *an* is added after the root *pad* with the prefix *anu* in the sense of "one who seeks. 5.02.091 The suffix *an* is added after the root *dṛś* with the prefix *sākṣāt* in the sense of a "witness" (*saṃjñā*).
5.02.092 The suffix *kṣetriyac* is added [after the root *cikits*] in the sense of "curable in another's body" (*para-kṣetre cikitsyaḥ*).

5.02.093 [The suffix *matUP* is applied after a word ending in *indra*, provided that it means] "belonging to Indra," "having the characteristics of Indra," "seen by Indra," "created by Indra," "touched by Indra," or "eaten by Indra.
5.02.094 The suffix *matUP* is applied [after a word] in the sense of "he has this" (*tad asyāsti*) or "this is in him" (*tad asmin*).
5.02.095 [The suffix *matUP* is applied] also after words beginning with *rasa*.
5.02.096. After a word ending in a vowel denoting a living being, the suffix *laC* is optionally applied [to form a possessive derivative].
5.02.097. And [the suffix *laC* is applied] after the group of words beginning with *sidhma*.
5.02.098. The suffixes *kāma* and *bala* are applied respectively after the words *vatsa* and *aṃsa*.
5.02.099: After *phena*, the suffix *ilaC* is also [added].
5.02.101: After *prajñā*, *śraddhā*, *arcā*, *vṛtti*, and *hrī*, the suffix *Ṇa* is added. 5.02.102: After *tapas* and *sahasra*, the suffixes *vini* and *ini* are added.
5.02.103 And [the suffix] aṆ.
5.02.104 After the words *sikatā* and *śarkarā*, [the suffix] a [is applied].
5.02.105 When denoting a region (*deśa*), [the suffixes] *luP*, *ilac*, and *aU* [are applied].
5.02.106 The suffix *uraC* is applied after [a stem ending in] *danta* when it has the vowel *u* elided (*un-na-ta*).
5.02.107 The suffix *raC* is applied after *ūṣan*, *suṣi*, *muṣka*, and *madhu*.
5.02.108 The suffix *maC* is applied after *dyu* and *dru*.

5.02.109. After *keśa*, the suffix *va* is optionally applied [to form a possessive compound]. 5.02.110. After *gāṇḍī* and *ajaga*, [the suffix *va* is applied] when forming a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
5.02.111. After *kāṇḍa* and *āṇḍa*, the suffixes *īraṇ* and *īrac* are respectively applied [to form a possessive compound].
5.02.112 The suffix *valac* is applied after the words *rajas*, *kṛṣi*, *ā-uti*, and *pariṣad*.
5.02.113 The suffix *valac* is applied after *danta* and *śikha* when they form a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
5.02.114 The forms *jyotsnā*, *tamisrā*, *śṛṅgaṇa*, *ūrjasin*, *ūrjala*, *gomin*, *malina*, and *malīmasa* [are formed with the suffix *valac*].
5.02.115 After a word ending in short *a*, the suffixes *ini* and *ṭhan* are added [to form a matup meaning].
5.02.116 And [the suffixes *ini* and *ṭhan* are added] after words beginning with *vrīhi*.
5.02.117 And the suffix *ilac* is also added after words beginning with *tuṇḍa*.
5.02.118 The suffix *ṭhaÑ* is invariably applied after a word ending in *eka*, *go*, or *pūrva*.
5.02.119 The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word ending in *śata*, *sahasra*, or *niṣka*.
5.02.120 The suffix *aP* is applied after the word *rūpa* when it denotes that which has been purchased (*āhṛta*) or when it expresses praise (*praśaṃsā*).
5.02.121 The suffix *ini* is added after [stems ending in] *as*, *māyā*, *medhā*, and *sraj*. 5.02.122 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
5.02.123 The suffix *yuS* is added after the word *ūrṇā*.
5.02.124 The suffix *gmini* is added after the word *vāc* [to denote one who speaks].
5.02.125 The suffixes *ālac* and *āṭac* are added [after a nominal stem] to denote one who laughs excessively.
5.02.126 The suffix *svāmin* is added [after a nominal stem] to denote lordship or ownership.
5.02.127 The suffix *aC* is applied after [words beginning with] *arśas* (hemorrhoids) and others.
5.02.128 The suffix *ini* is applied after a *dvandva* compound, after words meaning "affliction," and after words denoting a censurable bodily part.
5.02.129 After the words *vāta* (wind) and *atisāra* (diarrhea), the augment *kuK* is also added [before the suffix *ini*].
5.02.130 [The suffix *matup* is applied] after a word ending in *vayas* when it denotes age.
5.02.131 [The suffix *matup* is applied] also after words beginning with *sukha*.
5.02.132 [The suffix *matup* is applied] after a word ending in *dharma*, *śīla*, or *varṇa*.
5.02.133 [The suffix *cha* is applied after a word ending in] *hasta* when [the derivative denotes] a person born [from it].
5.02.134 [The suffix *cha* is applied after a word ending in] *varṇa* when [the derivative denotes] a *brahmacārin*.
5.02.135 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after [words beginning with] *puṣkara* when [the derivative denotes] a region (*deśa*).
5.02.136 The suffix *matup* occurs after [words beginning with] *bala*, etc., provided that the suffixes *nya*, *ara*, or *ya* do not follow.
5.02.137 The suffixes *man* and *māh* occur when a name (*saṃjñā*) is being formed.
5.02.138 The suffixes *kam*, *śam*, *hyām*, *ba*, *bha*, *yuS*, *ti*, *tu*, *ta*, and *yaS* occur [after a word ending in the seventh case].
5.02.139: After *tuṇḍi*, *vali*, and *vaṭi*, the suffix *bha* [is applied].
5.02.140: After the words *aham* and *śubham*, the suffix *yuṣ* [is applied].
5.03.001: From here up to the word *diś* [in 5.3.27], the term *vibhakti* [is understood].

5.03.003 *idam* [replaces *idam*] before the suffix *aḥ*, and *iŚ* is substituted [for the final vowel]. 5.03.004 *eta* and *it* [are substituted for *etad*] before the suffixes *ra* and *tha*. 5.03.005 *etad* [is replaced by *an*] before the suffix *aḥ*.
5.03.006 The suffix *sa* is optionally used for the word *sarva* before the locative case ending *i*.
5.03.007 The suffix *tasiL* is used after a word in the fifth (ablative) case. 5.03.008 And [the suffix *tasiL* is also used] after a word ending in *tasa*.

5.03.009 [The suffix *at* is applied] after the prepositions *pari* and *abhi*, when followed by a word ending in the seventh case. 5.03.010 [The suffix *at* is applied] after a word ending in the seventh case.
5.03.011 [The suffix *ha* is applied] after the pronoun *idam*.

5.03.012 The suffix *aT* is applied after the word *kim*. 5.03.013 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the particle *ha* may optionally [be used] as well. 5.03.014 [Particles] are also seen [used] after other words besides these.
5.03.015 After the words *sarva*, *eka*, *anya*, *kim*, *yad*, *tad*, and *adaḥ*, the suffix *dā* is added in the sense of time (*kāle*).
5.03.016 After the word *idam*, the suffix *rhiL* is added in the sense of time. 5.03.017 [The form] *adhunā* [is derived from *idam* with the suffix *dhunāN*].
5.03.018 *dānīm* is substituted for *tad-*; 5.03.019 *dā* is also substituted for *tad-*;
5.03.020 in the Vedic language, the suffixes *dā* and *rhiL* are also substituted for those two (*tad-* and *idam*).
5.03.021: After a word ending in *at*, the suffix *rhiL* is optionally used when the sense is "not today" (*an-adya-tane*).

5.03.022: The following are the forms [ending in *taddhita* suffixes] expressing specific points of time: *sadyas* (today), *parut* (last year), *parāri* (the year before last), *aiṣamas* (this year), *paredyavi* (the day after tomorrow), *adya* (today), *pūrvedyus* (the day before yesterday), *anyedyus* (another day), *anyataredyus* (one of two days), *itaredyus* (the other day), *aparedyus* (the following day), *adharedyus* (the day below/previous day), *ubhayedyus* (both days), and *uttaredyus* (the next day).
5.03.023: The suffix *thāL* is used to express the meaning of "in what manner" (*prakāra*).

5.03.024 *idam* [replaces the first member of a compound] with the suffix *-asthamu-*; 5.03.025 and also with *kim* when followed by *asthamu-*; 5.03.026 and in the Vedic language, *thā* is substituted for it when used in the sense of cause (*hetu*).
5.03.027 The suffix *astāti* is applied after words denoting direction (*dik*), provided they signify direction, place, or time, to form the seventh, fifth, and first case endings.
5.03.028 The suffix *atasuC* is applied after the words *dakṣiṇa* and *uttara*.
5.03.029 The suffix *atasuC* is optionally applied after the words *para* and *avara*.
5.03.030 The suffix *luK* is applied after the root *añc*.
5.03.031 [The forms] *upari* and *upariṣṭāt* [are derived from *upa*].
5.03.032 [The form] *paścāt* [is derived from *paśca*].
5.03.033 *paśca* and *paścāt* [are formed] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
5.03.034 After *uttara*, *adhara*, and *dakṣiṇa*, the suffix *āti* [is added].
5.03.035 Optionally, when not meaning "not far" (*adūra*) and not used as an adverb (*aanamyā*), the suffix *enaP* [is added].
5.03.036 The suffix *āC* is applied after *dakṣiṇa*.
5.03.037 And [the suffix] *āhi* is applied [after *dakṣiṇa*] when it denotes distance.
5.03.038 And [the suffix *āhi* is applied] after *uttara*.

5.03.039 For *pūrva*, *adhara*, and *avara*, [the final vowel and consonant] are substituted by *pur*, *ad*, and *av* respectively; and for these [three], [the same substitution applies] before the suffix *astāt*.
5.03.040 And [the substitution applies] before the suffix *astāt*. 5.03.041 For *avara*, the substitution is optional.
5.03.042 The suffix *dhā* is added after a numeral in the sense of "fold" (*vidhā*). 5.03.043 It is also added [after a numeral] in the sense of "changing the location" (*adhikaraṇa-vicāla*).
5.03.044 After a numeral beginning with the sound *e*, the suffix *dhyamuÑ* is added in the sense of "not being in a straight line" (*nyāra*).
5.03.045 The suffix *dhamuÑ* is applied after words ending in *dvi*, *tri*, and *oṣ*.
5.03.046 The suffix *edhāC* is also applied [after those same words].
5.03.047 The suffix *pāśap* is applied when expressing a prohibition (*yāpye*).
5.03.048: After a word ending in *tīya* that denotes a part (*bhāga*), the suffix *aṆ* is added [to form a feminine ordinal].
5.03.049: Before the number eleven (*ekādaśan*), [the suffix *aṆ* is added] in non-Vedic usage.
5.03.050: After the words *ṣaṣṭha* and *aṣṭa*, the suffix *Ña* is also [added].
5.03.051 The suffix *kaN* is applied after words meaning "measure" (*māna*), "livestock" (*paśu*), "verse" (*ṛc*), and "day" (*aha*), and there is also elision (*luK*) [of the suffix].
5.03.052 The suffix *ākiniC* is applied after the word *eka* when it means "without a companion," and there is also elision [of the suffix].
5.03.053 The suffix *caraṬ* is applied in the sense of "having occurred previously."
5.03.054 The suffix *rūpya* is also applied after a word ending in the sixth case (genitive).
5.03.055 The suffixes *tamaP* and *iṣṭhaN* are applied in the sense of excellence (*atiśāyana*).
5.03.056 [The suffixes *tamaP* and *iṣṭhaN*] are also applied after a verbal suffix (*tiṅ*).
5.03.057: The suffixes *taraP* and *īyasuN* are applied after a word that has two syllables and whose final member is divisible [into two parts].

5.03.058: These suffixes are applied only after a quality-word (*guṇavacana*) beginning with a vowel (*ac*). 5.03.059: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), however, they are applied even after a word ending in *tu*.
5.03.060 *praśasya* becomes *śra*.
5.03.061 And [it becomes] *jya*. 5.03.062 And [it becomes so] for *vṛddha* as well.
5.03.063: The suffixes *nedas* and *sādhu* are substituted for *antika* and *bāḍha* respectively.
5.03.065: The elision (*luk*) of the suffixes *vin* and *matup* occurs [in the neuter].
5.03.066: The suffix *rūpap* is applied in the sense of praise.

5.03.067 The suffixes *kalpaP*, *deśya*, and *deśīyaR* are used in the sense of "not quite complete" (*īṣadasamāpti*). 5.03.068 Optionally, when a polysyllabic nominal stem (*bahuC*) follows a case-ending (*sUP*), these suffixes may appear before it.
5.03.069 The suffix *jātīyaR* is used in the sense of expressing a kind or variety (*prakāravacana*).
5.03.070: Before the suffix *iva*, [the word-final vowel] becomes *ka*.
5.03.071: For indeclinables and pronouns, the augment *akaC* is inserted before the suffix *ṭe*. 5.03.072: And for the [suffix] *ka*, [the final consonant] becomes *da*.

5.03.073 The suffix *ka* is applied after a verbal root ending in *a* when the sense is "not knowing" (ajñāte). 5.03.074 It is applied when the sense is "contempt" (kutsite). 5.03.075 The suffix *kaṅ* is applied when the sense is the formation of a name (*saṃjñāyām*).
5.03.076 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word expressing compassion (*anukampā*).
5.03.077 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word joined with that [compassion], when it signifies policy (*nīti*).
5.03.078 After a human name consisting of more than two syllables (*bahvac*), the suffix *ṭhac* is optionally applied.
5.03.079 The suffixes *ghaÑ* and *ilac* [are applied after verbal roots].
5.03.080 According to the Eastern grammarians, the suffixes *aḍac* and *vuC* [are applied] after a prefix (*upa*) beginning with a vowel.
5.03.081 The suffix *kaN* is applied to a word denoting a genus (*jāti*) when it is used as a name (*nāman*).
5.03.082 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *ajina*, when it ends in the locative case (*ante*), and when preceded by the words *uttara*, *adhas*, and *upa*.
5.03.083 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in *ṭha*, a vowel (*aC*), or the word *ūrdhvam*, provided that it is followed by a second member beginning with a vowel (*aC*).
5.03.084 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the third member of the compounds beginning with *śevala*, *supari*, *viśāla*, *varuṇa*, and *aryaman*.

5.03.085 [The suffix *ka* is applied] after a word denoting a small quantity; 5.03.086 [The suffix *ka* is applied] after a short vowel; 5.03.087 [The suffix] *kaN* is applied when forming a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
5.03.088: After *kuṭī*, *śamī*, and *śuṇḍā*, the suffix *ra* is applied.
5.03.089: After *kutū*, the suffix *ḍupac* is applied. 5.03.090: After *kāsū* and *goṇī*, the suffix *ṣṭarac* is applied.

5.03.092: After *kim*, *yad*, and *tad*, when used for selection (*nirhāraṇa*) between two things, the suffix *ḍatarac* is applied. 5.03.093: When used for selection among many in a question concerning a genus (*jāti*), the suffix *ḍatamac* is applied. 5.03.094:
And [the suffix *ḍatarac*] is applied after [the word] *eka* according to the Eastern grammarians.

5.03.095 The suffix *kaN* is applied in the sense of "throwing down" (*avakṣepaṇa*). 5.03.096 [The suffix *kaN* is applied] in the sense of a "counterfeit" (*pratikṛti*) when followed by the word *iva*. 5.03.097 [The suffix *kaN* is applied] also when forming a name (*saṃjñā*).
5.03.098 [The suffix *taddhita*] is elided (*lup*) when referring to a human being.
5.03.099 [The suffix is elided] also when the meaning is "means of livelihood," provided it is not a commodity for sale.
5.03.100 [The suffix is elided] after the group of words beginning with *devapatha*.
5.03.101 The suffix *ḍhaÑ* is added after the root *vaste-* (to wear).
5.03.102 The suffix *ḍha* is added after the word *śilā* (stone/slate).
5.03.103 The suffix *yaT* is added after the group of words beginning with *śākhā* (branch).
5.03.104 And [the suffix *cha*] occurs after a word denoting a substance when it refers to something that is likely to become that.
5.03.105 [The suffix *cha* occurs] after *kuśāgra*. 5.03.106 And [the suffix *cha* occurs] after a compound whose scope is limited to that [same category].
5.03.107 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after [words beginning with] *śarkarā*.
5.03.108 The suffix *ṭhaK* is applied after [words beginning with] *aṅguli*.
5.03.109 The suffix *ṭhaC* is optionally applied after *ekaśālā*.
5.03.110 The suffix *īkaK* is added after *karka* and *lohit*.
5.03.111 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *thāL* is added after *pratna*, *pūrva*, *viśva*, and words ending in *im*.
5.03.112 The suffix *Ñya* is added after a name of a group (*pūga*) that does not have *grāmaṇī* as its first member.
5.03.113 The suffixes *CphaÑ* and *ra* are applied after the word *vrāta*, provided it does not denote a feminine.
5.03.114 The suffix *ÑyaṬ* is applied after a collective noun denoting a group of people who live by arms, provided they are non-Brahmins and non-Kṣatriyas, when referring to the Āhīkas.
5.03.115 The suffix *ṬeṇyaṆ* is applied after the word *vṛka*.
5.03.116: After [stems] beginning with *dāman* and ending with the sixth [stem] *tri-garta*, the suffix *ha* is applied [to form patronymics].
5.03.117: After [stems] beginning with *parśu* and those beginning with *yaudheya*, the suffixes *aṆ* and *aÑ* are applied respectively [to form patronymics].
5.03.118: After [stems] ending in the suffix *aṆ* derived from *abhi-jit*, *vidabhṛt*, *śālāvat*, *śikhāvat*, *śamīvat*, *ūrṇāvat*, and *śrumat*, the suffix *yaÑ* is applied [to form patronymics].
5.03.119: The suffixes beginning with *ñya* (i.e., *ñya*, *ña*, and *ñin*) are called *tad-rāja*.

5.04.001: The suffix *vuÑ* is added after a numeral beginning with *pāda* or *śata* when expressing distributive repetition (*vīpsā*), and there is elision (*lopa*) of the final vowel and its following consonant.
5.04.002: The suffix *vuÑ* is also added after such words in the sense of "inflicting punishment" (*daṇḍa*) and "bestowing" (*vyavasarga*).

5.04.003: The suffix *kaN* is added after words such as *sthūla* when expressing a particular kind or degree. 5.04.004: The suffix *Kta* is added [after a word] when it does not express a state of absolute completion. 5.04.005: [The suffix *Kta* is not added] after a word expressing "half" (*sāmi*).
5.04.006 The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *bṛhatī* when it means "covering.
5.04.007 The suffix *kha* is applied after a compound whose final member is *aṣaḍakṣa*, *āśitaṅgu*, *alaṃkarman*, *alapuruṣa*, or one beginning with *adhi*.
5.04.008 The suffix *cha* is optionally applied after the root *añc* when it does not denote a direction or a feminine noun.

5.04.009: [The suffix *bandhun*] is also applied after a word ending in a genus-term (*jāti*). 5.04.010: Optionally, [the suffix *bandhun*] is applied after a word ending in a term for a place (*sthāna*), provided that it is co-referential with the place itself (*sa-sthānena*). 5.04.011:

[The substitution of *ām* occurs] after a word ending in *eC*, a verbal suffix (*tiṅ*), an indeclinable (*avyaya*), or a word ending in *ghu*, except in the case of the Vedic language (*arvācīna-arṣe*).
5.04.012 The suffix *amu* is applied after [the verbal root] *chand* in the sense of Vedic meters.
5.04.013 The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after [the nominal stem] *anugādin*.
5.04.014 In the feminine gender, the suffix *aÑ* is applied after [a nominal stem ending in] *ṆaC*.
5.04.015 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after [a verbal root] ending in *inu* or *uṆ*.
5.04.016 The suffix *aṆ* is applied after the root *sṛ* when preceded by *vi*, provided the word refers to a fish (*matsya*).
5.04.017 The suffix *kṛtvasuC* is applied after a numeral when expressing the repetition of an action (*kriyābhyāvṛtti*) or its counting (*gaṇana*).
5.04.018 The suffix *suC* is added after the words *dvi*, *tri*, and *catur*.
5.04.019 And [the suffix *suC* is added] after the word *eka*, and [the word *sakṛt* is substituted for it].
5.04.020 After the word *bahu*, the suffixes *dhā*, *vi*, *pra*, *ṛṣ*, and *taK* are optionally [added], provided that time (*kāla*) is not the meaning.

5.04.021 The suffix *mayaṭ* is added [to a word] when expressing "made from that" (*tat-prakṛta*). 5.04.022 And [the suffix *mayaṭ*] is also used in the sense of a "collection" (*samūha*) when referring to many [individuals].
5.04.023 The suffix *ñya* is added after the words *ananta*, *āvasatha*, *itihāsa*, and *bheṣaja*.
5.04.024 The suffix *yaT* is added after a word ending in *devatā* when the sense is "intended for that.
5.04.025 [The suffix *yaT* is added] also after *pāda* and *argha*. 5.04.026 The suffix *Ñya* is added after *atithi*.
5.04.027 The suffix *taL* is applied after the word *deva*.
5.04.028 The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *ava*.
5.04.029 The suffix *kaN* is applied after words beginning with *yāva*.

5.04.030 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after the word *lohita* when the meaning is "a gem. 5.04.031 [The suffix *kan* is applied] also when the meaning is a color that is not permanent. 5.04.032 [The suffix *kan* is applied] in the sense of "dyed."

5.04.033 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word denoting time (*kāla*). 5.04.034 The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words such as *vinaya*. 5.04.035 [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after the word *vāc*, when it signifies that which has been spoken.
5.04.036 The suffix *aṆ* is added after a verbal root (*karman*) joined with that [instrumental word].
5.04.037 The suffix *aṆ* is added after the word *oṣadhi*, except when it denotes a genus (*jāti*).
5.04.038 The suffix *aṆ* is also added after words beginning with *prajña*.
5.04.039 The suffix *tikaN* is added after the word *mṛd*.
5.04.040 The suffixes *sa* and *sn* are added after a word denoting excellence.
5.04.041 In Vedic literature, the suffixes *tiL* and *tātiL* are also added after the words *vṛka* and *jyeṣṭha*.
5.04.042 The suffix *śas* is added after a word signifying "much" or "little," provided it functions as a *kāraka* (participant in an action) and does not end in the word *ara*.
5.04.043 The suffix *śas* is added after a numeral used in the singular number when expressing distributive repetition (*vīpsā*).
5.04.044 The suffix *tasi* is added to a word ending in the fifth case (*pañcamī*) in the sense of "in relation to" (*pratiyoga*).
5.04.045 And [the suffix *kha*] is applied after the roots *hī* and *ruh* when used with the prefix *apa-* in the sense of taking away (*apādāna*).

5.04.046 [The suffix *kha*] is applied after a word ending in the third case (*tṛtīyā*) in the senses of surpassing (*atigraha*), not causing pain (*avyathana*), and censuring (*kṣepa*), provided it does not denote the agent (*akartari*).
5.04.047 And [the suffix *kha* is applied] also after a word joined with that which is being censured (*hīyamāna*) or with the word *pāpa*.
5.04.048 The suffix *Cvi* is applied after a word ending in the sixth case when it denotes a change of basis (*vyāśraya*).
5.04.049 The suffix *Cvi* is also applied after a word denoting a disease (*roga*) when it signifies the removal thereof (*apanayana*).
5.04.050 The suffix *Cvi* is applied after the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, and *as* when they are joined with a word signifying the agent of accomplishment (*sam-padyamāna*).
5.04.051: There is elision (*lopa*) of the final vowel of *arus*, *manas*, *cakṣus*, *cetas*, *rahas*, and *rajas*.
5.04.052: Optionally (*vibhāṣā*), the suffix *sāti* is applied after a verbal root ending in *kārt* when the suffix *sn* follows.
5.04.053: The suffix *sam-pat* is also applied in the sense of "attainment" (*abhi-vidhi*).
5.04.054 The suffix *kha* is used after a word denoting dependence on something.

5.04.055 When that which is to be given (*deya*) is the object, the suffixes *tra* and *kha* are also used. 5.04.056 After the words *deva*, *manuṣya*, *puruṣa*, *puru*, and *martya*, the suffix *hyaṅ* is frequently used when the second case ending is elided.

5.04.057: After an unexpressed imitation (avyaktānukaraṇa) ending in a vowel other than *iC*, provided it consists of more than one syllable and ends in a consonant, the suffix *ḌāC* is added when the particle *iti* does not follow.
5.04.058: The suffix *ḌāC* is added after the verb *kṛñ* ("to do") when preceded by the words *dvitīya*, *tṛtīya*, *śamba*, or *bīja*, provided the action refers to ploughing.
5.04.059: The suffix *ḌāC* is added after a numeral followed by the word *guṇa*.
5.04.060 And [the suffix *kyaṅ*] is used after [a word ending in] *samaya* in the sense of "passing time.
5.04.061 [The suffix *kyaṅ*] is used after [a word ending in] *sapattra* and *niṣpattra* in the sense of "acting accordingly.
5.04.062 [The suffix *kyaṅ*] is used after [a word ending in] *niṣkula* in the sense of "exterminating."
5.04.063 [The suffix *ya* is added after the word *sukha*] when it means "favorable to"; 5.04.064 [The suffix *ya* is added after the word *duḥkha*] when it means "adverse to";
5.04.065 [The suffix *ya* is added after the word *śūla*] when it means "cooking."
5.04.066 [The suffix *kvin* is applied after the root *sat-*] when it does not refer to an oath (*aśapatha*).
5.04.067 [The suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *mad-*] when it refers to the act of shaving (*parivāpana*).
5.04.068 [The following rules concern] the finals of compounds (*samāsānta*).
5.04.069 Not after the root *pūj*. 5.04.070 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after *kim* when used in the sense of censure. 5.04.071 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after a *naÑ*-tatpuruṣa compound.
5.04.072 The suffix *pathin* is optionally [replaced by *path*].
5.04.073 In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, when a numeral is the thing to be counted (*saṃkhyeya*), the suffix *ḍac* is applied, except after the words *bahu* and *gaṇa*.
5.04.074 For the words *ṛc*, *pur*, *ap*, *dhur*, and *path*, [the final vowel is elided] before a word beginning with a vowel, provided it does not mean "an axle" (*anakṣe*).
5.04.076 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *akṣan*, provided that it does not denote the eye.

5.04.077 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *acatura*, *avicatura*, *sucatura*, *strī*, *uṃsa*, *dhenu*, *naḍuha*, *ṛk*, *ām*, *vār*, *anas*, *akṣibhruva*, *dāragava*, *ūṣṭhīva*, *padāṣṭhīva*, *naktaṃdiva*, *iva*, *rātriṃdiva*, *ahardiva*, *sarajas*, *niḥśreyasa*, *puruṣāyusa*, *dvyāyusa*, *tryāyusa*, *ṛgajuṣa*, *jātokṣa*, *mahokṣa*, *vṛddhokṣa*, *upaśuna*, *goṣṭhaśva*.
5.04.079 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *avasamandha*, *hyas*, and *tamas*.
5.04.080 After *śvas*, [the suffix *taraP* is applied] to express "better" (*vasīyaḥ*) or "more excellent" (*śreyaḥ*).
5.04.081 After *rahas* following *anu* or *ava*, [the suffix *taraP* is applied] to express "heated" (*tapta*).
5.04.082 After *uras* following *prati*, provided it ends in the seventh case, [the suffix *taraP* is applied].
5.04.083 [The suffix *am* is added after *anu* when it is compounded with *gava-* in the sense of "extent.
5.04.084 The sacrificial altar (*vedi*) is called *dvi-stāvā* or *tri-stāvā*.
5.04.085 [The suffix *am* is added after *adhvan-* when it follows a prefix (*upasarga*).]

5.04.086: In a *tatpuruṣa* compound, [the substitution of] *ṛc* for *ṛc* occurs after a numeral or an indeclinable as the first member. 5.04.087: [The substitution of] *ahan* for *ahar* occurs after *sarva*, a word denoting a part (*ekadeśa*), a numeral, *tad*, or *puṇya*, when followed by *rātri*. 5.04.088:
[The substitution of] *ahn* for *ahar* occurs after these [words mentioned in 5.04.087].
5.04.089 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after a numeral and so forth, when forming a collective compound (*samāhāra*).
5.04.090 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after the words *uttama* and *eka*.
5.04.092 [The suffix *aC* is applied] after the word *go*, provided it is not followed by a *taddhita* suffix that undergoes elision (*luK*).
5.04.093: [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after the word *uras-* when it signifies "foremost" (*agra-ākhyā*).
5.04.095: [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after the word *takṣan-* when it follows *grāma-* or *kauṭa-*.
5.04.096: [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after the word *śvan-* following the prefix *ati-*.
5.04.097 [The suffix ṅīp is applied] after a word ending in the feminine suffix *mān*, when it does not refer to a living being.
5.04.098 [The suffix ṅīp is applied] after the word *sakthi* when it follows *uttara* or *mṛgīrva*.
5.04.099 [The suffix ṅīp is applied] after the word *nau* when it occurs at the end of a *dvigu* compound.
5.04.100 [The suffix *kan* is applied after a word ending in] *ardha*.
5.04.101 [The suffix *kan* is applied after the word] *khārī* according to the Eastern grammarians.
5.04.102 [The suffix *kan* is applied after the word] *añjali* when preceded by *dvi*, *tri*, or *dvi-tri*.
5.04.103 After a neuter stem ending in *an* or *as*, [the suffix *ṅi* becomes *ī*] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
5.04.104 [The suffix *ṅi* becomes *ī* after the word *brahman*] when it denotes the name of a country (*jānapada*).
5.04.105 [The suffix *ṅi* becomes *ī*] after the words *ku-* and *mahat*, provided that the following vowel is not *a-ra* (i.e., not *a*, *ṛ*, or *lṛ*).
5.04.106 After a *dvandva* compound ending in a vowel other than *u*, in *d*, *ṣ*, or *h*, the suffix *samāsānta* [is applied] when it is a feminine (*samā*) or a neuter (*āra*).
5.04.107 In an *avyayībhāva* compound, [the suffix is applied] after words beginning with *śarat*. 5.04.108 And [it is applied] after a word ending in *an*.
5.04.109 After a neuter [stem], [the suffix *ṅasi*] optionally [becomes *ṅas*].

5.04.110 [The suffix *ṅasi* becomes *ṅas* after stems ending in] *nadī*, *paurṇamāsī*, *āgrahāyaṇī*, and *hyas*. 5.04.111 [The suffix *ṅasi* becomes *ṅas*] after [stems ending in] a consonant (*jhaY*).
5.04.112 Also after *giri*, according to Senaka.
5.04.113 In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the suffix *ṣac* is added after *sakthi* and *akṣi* when preceded by *su* or *ṛc*.
5.04.114 [The suffix *ṣac* is added] after *arati* when *dāru* follows.

5.04.115 After *dvi* and *tri*, [the suffix] *ṣa* is substituted for *mūrdhan*. 5.04.116 The [suffix] *ap* is substituted [for *mūrdhan*] when it occurs in a ordinal number (*pūraṇī*) or in the sense of a measure (*pramāṇa*). 5.04.117 [The suffix *ap* is also substituted for *mūrdhan*] after *antar* and *bahis* when followed by *loman*.

5.04.118: For *nāsikā*, when it forms a name (*saṃjñā*), the substitute *nas* is applied, provided it does not mean "thick" (*asthūla*). 5.04.119: [The substitution of *nas* for *nāsikā* also occurs] after a preverb (*upasarga*).
5.04.120: The forms *suprāta*, *suśva*, *sudin*, *śārikukṣa*, *caturaśra*, *eṇīpada*, *ajapada*, and *proṣṭhapada* are [irregularly formed compounds].
5.04.121 The suffix *asiC* is applied after *naÑ*, *dus*, *su*, and verbal roots ending in *hy*, before a consonant (*hal*) and the words *sakthi* (thigh), provided that another word follows.
5.04.122 The suffix *asiC* is applied invariably after the words *prajā* (offspring) and *medhā* (intelligence).
5.04.123 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the form *bahuprajāḥ* is used.
5.04.124 The suffix *aniC* is applied after the word *dharma* when it stands alone (without a prefix).
5.04.125 The suffix *aniC* is applied after the words *jambha*, *su*, *harita*, *tṛṇa*, *soma*, and *ahni*.
5.04.126 The form *dakṣiṇermā* is used in connection with a hunter (*lubdha*).
5.04.127 The suffix *iC* is applied [to a verbal root] when there is a reciprocal action (*karma-vyatihāra*). 5.04.128 [The suffix *iC* is also applied] after [compounds] such as *dvidaṇḍi*.
5.04.129 After the prefixes *pra-* and *sam-*, the word *jānu-* is replaced by *jñu-* [when forming a bahuvrīhi compound].

5.04.130 Optionally [the substitution of *ū* for *au* occurs] after [a stem ending in] *ūrdhva*. 5.04.131 The substitute *anaṅ* [replaces the final phoneme] of *ūdhas*. 5.04.132 And also [the substitute *anaṅ* replaces the final phoneme] of *dhanus*.
5.04.133 Or [the substitution of *iK* for the final vowel of the first member] occurs when a feminine noun (*saṃjñā*) follows.
5.04.134 The suffix *niṄ* is applied after the word *jāyā*.
5.04.135 The substitution of *iT* for the final vowel of *gandha* occurs when it follows *ud*, *pūti*, or *su-surabhi*.

5.04.136 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after a word denoting a small quantity; 5.04.137 [it is applied] also after a word expressing a standard of comparison; 5.04.139 [the suffix *kan* is applied] in the case of words such as *kumbhapadī*.

5.04.140 [The final *n* of] a word preceded by a numeral or the word *su* [is changed to *ṇ*]. 5.04.141 [The final *n* of] the word *danta* [is changed to *ṛ*] when expressing age. 5.04.142 [This also applies] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
5.04.143 [The suffix *kan* is applied after a word ending in *i*] when it is a feminine proper name.
5.04.144 [The suffix *kan* is applied] optionally after the words *śyāva* and *aroka*.
5.04.145 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after the words *agra*, *anta*, *śuddha*, *śubhra*, *vṛṣa*, *varāha*, and *ahya*.
5.04.146 There is elision of *kakuda* when it denotes a state of being. 5.04.147 [The elision of *kakuda* occurs] in *trikakuda* when it refers to a mountain.
5.04.148 [The elision of *kakuda* occurs] after *ut* and *vi*.
5.04.149 After *pūrṇa*, [the suffix *ka*] is optionally [added].
5.04.150 *Suhṛd* and *durhṛd* are used in the senses of "friend" and "enemy" respectively.
5.04.151 After words beginning with *uras*, the suffix *kaP* is added.
5.04.152 The suffix *in* [is applied] in the feminine; 5.04.153 and also after a stem ending in *nadī* or *ṛt*; 5.04.154 optionally, from the remainder.
5.04.155 Not [after a word] used as a name. 5.04.156 And not after [a word ending in] *īyas*.
5.04.157 [The suffix *ṣyaṅ* is applied] to the word *bhrātṛ* when it means "one who pays homage."
5.04.158 After *ṛt*, [the suffix *ṅīp* is applied] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
5.04.159 [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *nāḍī* and *tantrī* when followed by a word beginning with *sva* or *ar*.
5.04.160 And [the suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *niṣpra* and *vāṇi*.
6.01.001 For a single vowel (*aC*), the first [of the two] is doubled.
6.01.002 For a consonant beginning with a vowel (*aC-ādi*), the second [consonant] is doubled.
6.01.003 *n*, *r*, and *ṣ* (denoted by *na-n-d-r-āḥ*) do not undergo doubling when they are the first members of a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*).
6.01.004 The preceding [element] is reduplicated.
6.01.005 Both [the preceding and following elements] are reduplicated.
6.01.006 The six beginning with *jakṣ* are [reduplicated].
6.01.007: For the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) of roots beginning with *tuj*, there is lengthening.

6.01.008: In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, for a root that is not reduplicated (*anabhyāsa*), [there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel]. 6.01.009: [There is lengthening] before the suffixes *saN* and *yaṄ*.
6.01.010 Ślu (the elision of the suffix liṭ) [is applied];
6.01.011 Caṅ (the aorist marker) [is applied];
6.01.012 And [the forms] dāśvān, sāhvān, and mīḍhvān [are derived].
6.01.013 There is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the *ṣyaṅ* [suffix] when followed by *putra* or *pati* in a *tatpuruṣa* compound.
6.01.014 There is vocalization of the *ṣyaṅ* [suffix] when followed by *bandhu* in a *bahuvrīhi* compound.
6.01.015 There is vocalization of the roots *vac*, *svap*, and those beginning with *yaj* before an affix marked with *K*.

6.01.016: [The substitution of *samprasāraṇa* occurs] for the roots *grah*, *jyā*, *vay*, *vyadh*, *vaṣ*, *ṭi*, *vic*, *at*, *vṛśc*, *pṛcch*, and *bhṛjj*, both when followed by an affix marked with *ṅ* or *it* and when in the *liṭ* tense.
6.01.017: In the *liṭ* tense, the substitution of *samprasāraṇa* occurs for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) of both groups [of roots].
6.01.018: [The substitution of *samprasāraṇa* occurs] also for the root *svap* when followed by the *caṅ* (the aorist marker).
6.01.019: [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel] of the roots *svap*, *syami*, and *vyeÑ* occurs before the suffix *yaṅ*.
6.01.020: [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel] does not occur for the root *vaś* before the suffix *yaṅ*.
6.01.021: For the root *cāy*, [the substitution of *ī* for the final vowel] is replaced by *kī* before the suffix *yaṅ*.
6.01.022 The substitution of *sphī* for *sphāy* occurs before the suffix of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*).
6.01.023 The substitution of *styai* occurs for *pra-styai*.
6.01.024 The substitution of *śyai* occurs for *śyai* when meaning "flowing" or "solid form," and when meaning "touch."
6.01.025 *prateś ca* (the augment *iṭ* is optionally added after the root *śrī* when preceded by *pra*).
6.01.026 *vibhāṣā abhy-ava-pūrvasya* (the augment *iṭ* is optionally added after the root *śrī* when preceded by both *abhi* and *ava*).
6.01.027 *śṛtam pāke* (the word *śṛta* is used in the sense of cooking).
6.01.028 The root *pyāy* is replaced by *pī*. 6.01.029 This replacement also occurs before the *liṭ* and *yaṅ* suffixes. 6.01.030 For the root *śvi*, this replacement is optional.
6.01.031 [The substitution of *i* for *y* occurs] before the affix *ṆaU*, as well as before *saN* and *CaṄ*.
6.01.032 There is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the root *hve*. 6.01.033 And there is vocalization of the reduplicated syllable (*abhy-asta*).
6.01.034 *bahulam chandasi* (In the Vedic language, [the substitution of *yaṇ* for *vṛddhi*] occurs diversely).
6.01.035 *cāyaḥ kī* (For the root *cāy*, the substitute *kī* is applied).

6.01.036 *apa-spṛdhe-thām-ān-ṛcus-ān-ṛhus-cicyuṣe-tityāja-śrātāḥ-śritam-āśīrtaḥ* (The forms *apaspṛdhe*, *thām*, *ānṛcuḥ*, *ānṛhuḥ*, *cicyuṣe*, *tityāja*, *śrātāḥ*, *śritam*, and *āśīrtaḥ* are established as correct).
6.01.037 When a *samprasāraṇa* [vowel] occurs, the preceding *samprasāraṇa* [vowel] does not take place.
6.01.038 Before the suffix *liṭ*, the *y* of *vay* [is replaced by its *samprasāraṇa*].
6.01.039 Optionally, before a *kit* suffix, the *v* of this [root *vay*] is also [replaced by its *samprasāraṇa*].
6.01.040 After the verbal root *veñ*, [the suffix *LyaP* is applied].
6.01.041 And also before the suffix *LyaP*.
6.01.042 And also after the suffix *jy*.
6.01.043 The substitution of *i* for the final vowel of a verbal root ending in *as* occurs before the affix *kvi*.
6.01.044 Optionally, the substitution of *i* for the final vowel of a verbal root ending in *as* occurs before the affix *pare*.
6.01.045 The substitution of *ā* for the final vowel of a verbal root ending in *eC* (any vowel except *a*) occurs when it is taught with an initial consonant (*aŚIT*) as an upadeśa.

6.01.046 There is no substitution [of *vṛddhi*] for the vowel of the root *vyā* before the *liṭ* suffix. 6.01.047 There is no substitution [of *vṛddhi*] for the vowels of the roots *sphurati* and *sphulati* before the *ghañ* suffix. 6.01.048 There is no substitution [of *vṛddhi*] for the vowels of the roots *krī*, *iṅ*, and *jī* before the *ṇi* suffix.
6.01.049 The substitution of *s* for the root *sidh* occurs when it does not refer to the attainment of the other world (*apāralaukika*).
6.01.050 The substitution of *s* for the roots *mī*, *mi*, and *dīṄ* occurs before the suffix *LyaP*.
6.01.051 The substitution of *s* for the root *lī* is optional before *LyaP*.
6.01.052 [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of] *khid* occurs before an affix marked with *ṅ* when used in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
6.01.053 [The substitution of *ū* for the final vowel of] *apagur* occurs before the affix *Ṇamul*.
6.01.054 [The substitution of *ū* for the final vowel of] *ci* and *sphur* occurs before the affix *Ṇa*.
6.01.055 [The suffix *lyap* is used] after the root *vī* when it means "to procreate.
6.01.056 [The suffix *lyap* is used] after the root *bhī* when the cause of fear is expressed.
6.01.057 [The suffix *lyap* is used] invariably after the root *smi*.

6.01.058: For the roots *sṛj* and *dṛś*, when followed by a suffix beginning with a consonant (jhaL) that has no indicatory letter *k* (aK), [the penultimate vowel] becomes short (*am*). 6.01.059: And for a root having *ṛ* as its penultimate letter, when it is unaccented (*anudātta*), [the penultimate vowel] optionally becomes short (*am*) under the same conditions. 6.01.060: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the word *śīrṣan* [is substituted for *śiras*].
6.01.061 Also before a *taddhita* suffix beginning with *y*.
6.01.062 Before a suffix beginning with a vowel (*aC*), the word *śiras-* becomes *śīrṣa-*.

6.01.063 In the strong cases (*Śas*-prabhṛti) beginning with the nominative plural, the forms *pad*, *dat*, *nas*, *mās*, *hṛd*, *niś*, *asan*, *yūṣan*, *doṣan*, *yakan*, *śakan*, *udan*, and *āsan* [are substituted for their respective bases].
6.01.064: The *ṣ* at the beginning of a verbal root (*dhātu*) becomes *s*.
6.01.065: The *ṇ* [at the beginning of a verbal root] becomes *n*.
6.01.066: There is elision (*lopa*) of *v* and *y* before a *vaL* (a consonant other than *y*).
6.01.067: [The substitution of] *y* occurs for the *r* of a suffix that is not a single phoneme (*apṛkta*).

6.01.068: After a long vowel that is either a consonant (*haL*), the feminine suffix *Ṅī*, or the feminine suffix *ĀP*, the *sU*, *ti*, and *si* that are not single phonemes (*apṛkta*) are elided, provided they end in a consonant (*haL*).
6.01.069: In the vocative singular (*saṃbuddhi*), after *eṄ* (e, o) or a short vowel, [the *sU* suffix] is elided.
6.01.070: *śe* is diversely applied in Vedic meter.
6.01.071: *tuK* is inserted after a short vowel before a suffix marked with *p* when it is a *kṛt* suffix. 6.01.072: This occurs in *saṃhitā*.
6.01.073 [The substitution of *e* occurs] for *cha*.
6.01.074 [The substitution of *e* occurs] for *āṅ* and *māṅ*.
6.01.075 [The substitution of *e* occurs] after a long vowel.
6.01.076 Optionally [the substitution occurs] after a word-final [vowel].
6.01.077 A *yaṇ* is substituted for an *iK* vowel before a non-homogeneous vowel (*aC*).
6.01.078 *Ay*, *av*, *āy*, and *āv* are substituted for *eC*.
6.01.079 Before an affix beginning with *y*, [the substitution of *iK* for the final vowel of a stem] occurs when the stem ends in *va*.
6.01.080 That [substitution] occurs only when the cause of the affix is present in the verbal root (*dhātu*).
6.01.081 The suffixes *kṣayya* and *jayya* are used in the sense of "capable of" (*śakya*).
6.01.082 The suffix *krayya* is used in the sense of "to be purchased for that.
6.01.083 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the forms *bhayya* and *pravayya* also [occur].
6.01.084 A single [substitute] replaces both the preceding and the following [sounds].
6.01.085 And [the substitution] is as if it were the final element and the initial element [of the preceding and following elements].
6.01.086 The substitution of *ṣ* and *tuK* is not considered non-existent (*asiddha*).
6.01.087 There is the *guṇa* substitution for *ā*.
6.01.088 Vṛddhi is substituted [for the final vowel of the first member] before a vowel beginning with eC (e, o, ai, au).
6.01.089 [Vṛddhi is substituted for the final vowel of the first member] before the verbal roots iN (to go), edh (to prosper), and the augment ūṬH.
6.01.090 [Vṛddhi is also substituted for the final vowel of the first member] after the augment āṬ.

6.01.091: [The substitution of *u* for the vowel of] a verbal root beginning with *ṛ* occurs after a prefix. 6.01.092: According to Āpiśali, this substitution is optional when a case-ending (*sUP*) follows. 6.01.093: [The substitution of *ū* for the final *ā* of a stem ending in] *ā* occurs before the accusative singular and dual endings (*am* and *śas*).

6.01.094 Before *eṅ*, the single substitute is the subsequent form (*pararūpa*). 6.01.095 Also before *om* and *āṅ*. 6.01.096 Before *us*, [the single substitute is the subsequent form], except when it follows the end of a word (*apadānta*).
6.01.097 Before a single substitute (*guṇa*), [the final *a* or *ā* of a stem is elided].
6.01.098 In the case of an unexpressed imitation of sound (*avyaktānukaraṇa*), [the *at* of the second syllable is replaced by] *it* when followed by *iti*.
6.01.099 However, this does not apply to the final syllable of a reduplicated word (*āmreḍita*), where the substitution is optional.
6.01.100 When a suffix beginning with a vowel follows a reduplicated stem, [the single substitute for both is] always the long vowel.
6.01.101 When a homogeneous vowel follows a short vowel (aK), the long vowel is the single substitute for both.
6.01.102 In the case of the first two cases (nominative and accusative), the single substitute is the vowel homogeneous with the preceding one.
6.01.103. From that [stem], *śas* becomes *naḥ* in the masculine.
6.01.104. [The substitution of *naḥ* for *śas* does not occur] after a long vowel before a vowel-initial suffix (*iC*). 6.01.105. [Nor does it occur] before *jas* following a long vowel.
6.01.106 Or [the substitution of *u* for *v*] occurs in the Vedic language (*chandas*). 6.01.107 Before the ending *-am*, the preceding [vowel] is substituted [for the following vowel].
6.01.108 And [the substitution of the single vowel occurs] after a *samprasāraṇa*.

6.01.109: *eṅaḥ* [is substituted] for [the final phoneme of] a word ending in *eṅ*, before a vowel (*aT*). 6.01.110: [The substitution of *o* occurs] also before the case-endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas*. 6.01.111: [The substitution of *u* occurs] for the final phoneme of a word ending in *ṛT*.
6.01.112: [The substitution of] *ru* occurs in place of the vowel following a word ending in *khy*, *ti*, or *āt*.
6.01.113: [The substitution of] *ru* occurs in place of the vowel *a* that follows a non-prolated (*apluta*) vowel, provided it is not itself prolated (*apluta*).
6.01.114: [The substitution of *ru* also occurs] before a consonant of the *haś* class.
6.01.115 [The word *pra*] retains its original form (*prakṛtyā*) within a *pāda*, except when followed by *a* or *va*.
6.01.116 [The word *pra* retains its original form] before *avyāt*, *avadyāt*, *avakramuḥ*, *avrata*, *ayam*, *avantu*, and *avas-yuṣu*.
6.01.117 In the *Yajurveda*, [the word *pra* retains its original form] before *uraḥ*.
6.01.118: [The substitution of *e* for *a* occurs] in *āpaḥ*, *juṣāṇaḥ*, *vṛṣṇaḥ*, *varṣiṣṭhe*, *ambe*, *ambāle*, and *ambike*, when followed by a word beginning with *pūrve*.

6.01.119: [The substitution of *e* for *a* occurs] also when followed by a word beginning with *ṛk*. 6.01.120: [The substitution of *e* for *a* occurs] also when followed by an unaccented (*anudātta*) *ku* or *dha*.
6.01.121 And [the substitution of *avaṅ* for *go* occurs] before the suffix *a*, as well as before the suffix *thās*. 6.01.122 Everywhere, the substitution of *go* is optional.
6.01.123 According to Sphoṭāyana, the substitution of *avaṅ* [for *go* occurs] before the suffix *a*.

6.01.124 [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] invariably before the word *indra*. 6.01.125 [The substitution of *anusvāra* occurs] invariably before a vowel (*aC*) following a *pluta* vowel or a *pragṛhya* vowel. 6.01.126 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the *āṅ* [substitution] is nasalized.
6.01.127 Before a vowel that is not homogeneous (*asa-varṇa*), the *iK* vowels may optionally take their short form according to Śākalya.
