6.01.128 [The substitution of a long vowel occurs] when a vowel follows an *ṛT* sound.
6.01.129 This applies when the preceding word is not protracted (*apluta*) and is contiguous (*upasthita*).
6.01.130 The substitution of *ī* occurs for the final vowel of *cākravarmaṇa*.
6.01.131 The substitution of *ū* occurs for the final vowel of *div*.

6.01.132 The elision (*lopa*) of the case-ending *sU* occurs after *etad* and *tad* when followed by a consonant (*haL*), provided that it is not part of a negative compound (*naÑ-samāsa*) and the following suffix is not *ak*.
6.01.133: In Vedic literature, the substitution of *sya* for *sa* occurs diversely.
6.01.134: When *sa* is followed by a vowel (*aC*), its elision (*lopa*) may optionally take place, provided that the completion of the metrical foot (*pāda-pūraṇa*) is thereby achieved.
6.01.135: The augment *suṬ* is placed before the verbal root when it begins with a consonant (*k*).
6.01.136 The augment *aṬ* is inserted before a verbal root even when there is an intervening *abhyāsa* (reduplication) or *vy-ava* (the syllables *vi* and *ava*).
6.01.137 The augment *aṬ* is inserted before the root *kṛ* when preceded by the prefixes *sam*, *pari*, or *upa*, provided that the sense is "adornment.
6.01.138 And [the augment *aṬ* is inserted] when the sense is "coming together" (*samavāya*).

6.01.139 [The suffix *ṇamul* is used after a verb] following the prefix *upa*, in the sense of counteracting (*pratiyatna*), modification (*vaikṛta*), supplying an ellipsis (*vākyādhyāhāra*), and so forth.
6.01.140 [The suffix *ṇamul* is used after the root *kṛ*] following the prefix *ava*, in the sense of cutting (*lavana*).
6.01.141 [The suffix *ṇamul* is used after the root *kṛ*] following the prefix *pra*, and also [after the root *kṛ*] following the prefix *prati*, in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*).
6.01.142 *apāt* [forms a compound] with a word having four syllables when referring to birds, provided it does not denote a drawing (*ālekha*).
6.01.143 *kustumburuṇi* [is neuter] when it denotes a genus (*jāti*).
6.01.144 *aparaspārāḥ* [is used] in the sense of uninterrupted continuity of action (*kriyāsātatyam*).
6.01.145 *goṣpada* [is used] in the sense of the measure of that which has been frequented or not frequented by cattle;
6.01.146 *āspada* [is used] in the sense of a foundation or support;
6.01.147 *āścarya* [is used] in the sense of what is not constant (the marvelous).
6.01.148 *avaskaraḥ* [means] excrement;
6.01.149 *apaskaraḥ* [means] a part of a chariot;
6.01.150 *viṣkiraḥ* [means] a bird, or [something that scatters].
6.01.151 In a mantra, [the word] *candra* following a short vowel [is optionally acute]. 6.01.152 Also, *pratiṣkaśaḥ* is [acute on the first syllable] when derived from the root *kaś*.
6.01.153 *Praskaṇva*, *Hariscandra*, and [names of] sages [are acute on the first syllable].
6.01.154 *maskara* and *maskarin* [are used] in the sense of "bamboo" and "wandering mendicant" respectively.
6.01.155 *kāstīra*, *ajastunda*, and *nagara*.
6.01.156 *kāraska* and *karīra* [denote] a type of tree.
6.01.157 And compounds beginning with *pāraskara* are [neuter] when they are proper names.
6.01.158 A word has one syllable that is not acute (anudātta), with the exception of one [which is acute].
6.01.159 A word ending in the suffix *GHaÑ*, provided it ends in the root *karṣ* or a long vowel (*ĀT*), has its final syllable acute.
6.01.160 And [the substitution of *u* for *i* occurs] in the case of *uñcha* and so forth.

6.01.161 And [the substitution of *u* for *i* occurs] for a non-udātta vowel where there is the elision of an udātta vowel. 6.01.162 [The substitution of *u* for *i* occurs] in the case of a verbal root (*dhātu*).
6.01.163 [The substitution of] *a* occurs in place of a *k-it* suffix.
6.01.164 [The substitution of *a* occurs] in place of a *taddhita* suffix.
6.01.165 [The substitution of *a* occurs] in place of a *k-it* suffix.
6.01.166 [The substitution of *au* occurs] for the case-ending *Jas* after the word *tisṛ*.
6.01.167 [The substitution of *Śī* occurs] for the case-ending *Śas* after the word *catur*.
6.01.168 The third case-ending and those following it are called *vibhakti* when they follow a stem consisting of a single vowel (*eka-aC*).

6.01.169: After a word ending in *it* (the vowel *i*) which has its final syllable as an *anta* (end), the suffix *nya* is optionally applied when followed by another word, provided it does not end in the locative plural (*ām*).
6.01.170: In Vedic literature (*chandas*), after the word *añc*, the suffix *ūṭh* is applied before any case-ending other than the nominative singular (*sarvanāmasthāna*).
6.01.171: The suffix *ūṭh* is applied after the words *idam*, *pad*, *ap*, *pum*, *rai*, and *dyu* when they stand at the beginning of a word.

6.1.172: [The substitution of] *au* for *aṣṭan-* occurs after a long vowel. 6.1.173: [The designation] *nadī* applies to the suffix *śatṛ* when it does not have the augment *anuṃ*, provided it ends in a vowel (*ac*) that is high-pitched (*udātta*) and preceded by a consonant (*haL*). 6.1.174: [The designation *nadī* applies to the suffix *śatṛ*] when it has the augment *yaṅ* and is preceded by a consonant (*haL*).
6.01.175 Not [after a word ending in] ūṄ or after a verbal root (dhātu). 6.01.176 The suffix matUP [is added] after [a word ending in] a short vowel or the augment nuṬ.
6.01.177 After [a word ending in] n, [matUP is added] optionally.
6.01.178 The suffix *ṅī* is frequently applied in the Vedic language (*chandas*).

6.01.179 After the words *ṣaṣ*, *tri*, and *catur*, the suffix beginning with a consonant (*hal*) [is applied]. 6.01.180 When a suffix beginning with a non-nasal consonant (*jhal*) follows, the penultimate vowel [is acute].
6.01.181 Optionally [the substitution of *au* for *as* occurs] when speech (*bhāṣā*) is intended.
6.01.182 The substitution of *au* for *as* does not occur after *go*, *śvan*, a word ending in *a* or *ā*, *rājan*, *ṛk*, *kruk*, or a word ending in *kṛt*.
6.01.183 After the word *div*, [the suffix *jhal* is substituted for *as*].
6.01.184: Optionally, [the augment *nṛc* is added] after the word *nṛ*.
6.01.185: A suffix marked with *T* or *IT* is acute (*svarita*).

6.01.186: A *l*-sārvadhātuka suffix following a root that has an *anudātta* *IT*, or one marked with *Ṅ* or *IT*, or one taught with a final short *a*, is *anudātta*, except for the roots *hnu* and *iṅ*.
6.01.187. The augment *āṭ* optionally precedes the *sic* suffix.
6.01.188. The augment *āṭ* precedes the roots *svap* and others, as well as *hiṃs*, when followed by a vowel-initial suffix that does not have the augment *iṭ*.
6.01.189. The augment *āṭ* precedes reduplicated roots ending in *n*.

6.01.190 And [the substitution of *sarvanāmasthāna* occurs] after [a stem ending in] a non-udātta vowel. 6.01.191 [The substitution of *sarvanāmasthāna* occurs] for the whole [stem] when followed by a case-ending (*sUP*).
6.01.192 [The substitution of *sarvanāmasthāna* occurs] before a *p-it* affix after the verbal roots *bhī*, *hrī*, *bhṛ*, *hu*, *mad*, *jan*, *dhan*, *daridrā*, and *jāgṛ*.

The initial [augment] *iṭ* is optionally applied before the suffix *ṇamul*. 6.01.194. [The initial *iṭ* is optionally applied] before *ṇamul*. 6.01.195. [The initial *iṭ* is applied] after a vowel (*ac*) before the suffix *yak* when it denotes the agent.
6.01.196 A *thaL* affix following a verbal root ending in *sa-iṬ* (the augment *iṬ* with *s*) is optionally treated as having an indicatory *iṬ*.

6.01.197 An affix marked with *Ñ* or *Ṅ* as its *it* always causes the initial vowel of the preceding element to be accented acute. 6.01.198 And the same applies to that which follows a vocative (*āmantrita*).

6.01.199: [The substitution of *an* occurs] for the final phoneme of *pathin* and *mathin* before a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix. 6.01.200: And [the substitution of *an* occurs] for the final phoneme of *antaḥ* before the suffix *tavai*, both simultaneously.
6.01.201: [The substitution of *an* occurs] for the final phoneme of *kṣaya-* when it means "dwelling."
6.01.202 The suffix *karaṇa* [is applied after a word ending in the genitive case] to express "victory.
6.01.203 [The suffix *karaṇa* is also applied] after words such as *vṛṣa*.
6.01.204 [The suffix *karaṇa* is applied] to a word expressing a standard of comparison (*upamāna*) when it forms a name (*saṃjñā*).
6.01.205 The suffix *niṣṭhā* (the past passive participle suffixes *kta* and *ktavatu*) is *anudātta* when it follows a stem ending in two vowels (*dvy-aC*) that do not begin with *ā*.
6.01.206 The words *śuṣka-* and *dhṛṣṭa-* are irregularly derived as *niṣṭhā* forms.
6.01.207 The word *āśita-* denotes the agent (*kartṛ*).

6.01.208 Optionally [the substitution of *e* for *as* occurs] before the locative ending *-i*. 6.01.209 And [the substitution of *e* for *as* occurs] before *juṣṭe* and *arpite* in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
6.01.210 In the Mantras, [the substitution of *e* for *as* occurs] invariably.

6.01.211. [The substitution of *yuṣmāka* and *asmāka* occurs] for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* before the [genitive] ending *ṅasi*. 6.01.212. [The same substitution occurs] also before the [genitive] ending *ṅi*.
6.01.213. [The substitution of *yuṣmāka* and *asmāka* occurs] for a *yaṭ*-ending stem that does not end in *-an*.
6.01.214 The [suffix] ṆyaT is applied after the verbal roots √īḍ, √vand, √vṛ, √śaṃs, and √duh.
6.01.215 The [suffix] ṆyaT is optionally applied after the words veṇu and indhana.
6.01.216 [The suffix ṆyaT is applied] after tyāga, rāga, hāsa, kuha, śvaṭha, kratha, and āna.
6.01.217: Before a suffix beginning with *r* (ṛt), the penultimate vowel becomes long.
6.01.218: Before the *caṅ* (the *aṅ* of the third person plural imperfect), the penultimate vowel optionally becomes long.
6.01.219: In the feminine gender, when a technical name (*saṃjñā*) is formed, the letter *ā* is substituted for the vowel preceding the suffix *matup*.
6.01.220 [The suffix] *anta* is applied after a word ending in *avatī*. 6.01.221 [The suffix] *īvat* is applied after a word ending in *avatī*.
6.01.222 [The suffixes] *cau* [are applied].
6.01.223 [The elision of the final *s*] of a compound [is optional].
6.02.001 In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the first member retains its original form (*prakṛti*).

6.02.002 In a *tatpuruṣa* compound, the first member retains its original form when it has the sense of "equal to," or when it is a word ending in a third-case suffix, a seventh-case suffix, a word used as a standard of comparison (*upamāna*), an indeclinable (*avyaya*), a second-case suffix, or a gerundive (*kṛtya*).

6.02.003 The word *varṇa* [is compounded] with words meaning "caste" (*varṇa*) when it does not mean "entered. 6.02.004 The words *gādha* and *lavaṇa* [are compounded] with the word *pramāṇa* when it means "measure. 6.02.005 The word *dāyādya* [is compounded] with the word *dāyāda*.
6.02.006 [The suffix *ka* is added] after the root *prati-bandh-* in the sense of "delay" (*cira*) and "difficulty" (*kṛcchra*).
6.02.007 [The suffix *ka* is added] after the root *pad-* in the sense of "pretext" (*apadeśa*).
6.02.008 [The suffix *ka* is added] after the root *ni-vāt-* in the sense of "protection from wind" (*vātatrāṇa*).
6.02.009 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *śarad*] in the sense of "not belonging to the season" (*an-ārtava*).
6.02.010 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *adhvaryu* and *kaṣāya* in the sense of "originating from" (*jātau*).
6.02.011 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *sadṛśa* and *pratirūpa* in the sense of "resemblance" (*sādṛśye*).
6.02.012 [The final member of] a *dvigu* compound [retains its original accent] when it denotes a measure (*pramāṇa*).

6.02.013 [The final member of a *dvigu* compound retains its original accent] when it means "to be traveled" (*gantavya*) or "merchandise" (*paṇya*), provided the compound refers to a merchant (*vāṇija*).
6.02.014 [A word ending in the third case retains its original accent] when it occurs before *mātra*, *upajñā*, *upakrama*, or *chāyā*, provided the resulting neuter compound is a bahuvrīhi.
6.02.015 [The genitive case is used] for *sukha* (happiness) and *priya* (dear) when they signify welfare (*hita*).
6.02.016 [The genitive case is used] also when they signify affection (*prīti*).
6.02.017 [The word] *sva* takes the genitive case when it means "one's own master" (*svāmin*).
6.02.018 [The suffix *yañ* is applied after the word *pati* when *aiśvarya* (lordship) is expressed.
6.02.019 [The suffix *yañ* is not applied after the words *bhū*, *vāk*, *cit*, or *didhiṣu*.
6.02.020 [Alternatively, the suffix *aṇ* is applied after the word *bhuvana*.]
6.02.021 [The suffix *samāsānta* *aC* is applied after a compound ending in] *ā-śarkara*, *ā-bādha*, or *nedīyas*, when expressing "possibility" (*sambhāvanā*).
6.02.022 [The suffix *aC* is applied after a compound ending in] *pūrva*, when expressing "having previously been so" (*bhūtapūrva*).
6.02.023 [The suffix *aC* is applied after a compound ending in] *sa-vidha*, *sa-nīḍa*, *sa-maryāda*, *sa-veśa*, or *sa-deśa*, when expressing "proximity" (*sāmīpya*).

6.02.024 The words *vi*, *spaṣṭa*, and so forth [are compounded] with words expressing qualities (*guṇavacana*). 6.02.025 [The words *śreṣṭha*, *jyeṣṭha*, *avama*, *kan*, and *pāpa* are compounded] with a word expressing a state (*bhāva*) in a *karmadhāraya* compound. 6.02.026 [The word] *kumāra* [is also compounded] in this manner.

6.02.027 The word *ādi* [is compounded] with a word expressing an offense (*praty-enas*). 6.02.028 [The word *ādi* is compounded] with words denoting a multitude (*pūga*), optionally. 6.02.029 In a *dvigu* compound, [the first member retains its original accent] when it ends in an *ik* vowel, or when it denotes time, or when it is *kapāla*, *bhagāla*, or *śarāva*.
6.02.030 *bahu-anya-tarasyām* (The suffix *bahuc* is optionally substituted for *bahu* when followed by a feminine affix).
6.02.031 *diṣṭi-vitas-tyoś-ca* (The same substitution occurs after *diṣṭi* and *vitas*).
6.02.032 *saptamī-siddha-śuṣka-pakva-bandheṣu-akālāt* (The seventh case-affix is compounded with words ending in *siddha*, *śuṣka*, *pakva*, and *bandha*, provided they do not denote time).

6.02.033 When *pari*, *prati*, *upa*, *apa*, and *ā* are excluded, [the suffix -ṭac is applied] to words denoting days and nights, and to words denoting age. 6.02.034 In a dvandva compound consisting of a plural form of the word *rājanya*, when referring to the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, [the suffix -aṇ is applied].
6.02.035 [The suffix -aṇ is applied] after a numeral [to denote a collection].
6.02.036 And [the word] *antevāsī* [is formed with the suffix *ṇini*] when preceded by *ācārya* or *upasarjana*.
6.02.037 [The following are] *kṛta-kauñjapādayaḥ* (compounds ending in *ka* or *kañ*).
6.02.038 [The suffix *kan* is added after the word *mahat*] before *vrīhi*, *aparāhṇa*, *gṛṣṭi*, *iṣvāsa*, *jābāla*, *bhāra*, *bhārata*, *hailihila*, *raurava*, and *pravṛddha*.

6.02.039 A *kṣullaka* [is used] in the sense of *vaiśvadeva*. 6.02.040 An *uṣṭra* [is used] in the sense of a rider of either a horse or a female camel. 6.02.041 A *go* [is used] in the sense of a rider, a non-rider, or a charioteer.

6.02.042 [The fourth case ending is used] after *kuru*, *gārhapatya*, *riktaguru*, *asūtajaratī*, *aślīladṛḍharūpa*, *apārevaḍabā*, *taitila*, *kadrū*, *paṇyāmbaḷa*, *āsībhāra*, and [words ending in] *-an*.
6.02.043 The fourth case ending is used in the sense of "for the sake of that" (*tadartha*).
6.02.044 [The fourth case ending is used] in the sense of "purpose" (*artha*).

6.02.045: [The substitution of] *ktvā* for *ktvā-lyap* occurs when followed by a word beginning with *e*. 6.02.046: In a *karmadhāraya* compound, [the substitution of *ktvā* for *ktvā-lyap* occurs], except when the following member is a past passive participle (*aniṣṭhā*). 6.02.047: [The substitution of *ktvā* for *ktvā-lyap* occurs] after a word ending in the second case (*dvitīyā*), provided that the following member is not *ahīna*.

6.02.048 The third case ending is used for the object (*karman*). 6.02.049 A *gati* [particle] that is immediately followed by a verbal root is compounded with it. 6.02.050 And when a *kṛt* suffix beginning with *ta-* or *na-* (and having an indicatory letter *ṇ*) follows, provided it does not end in *-at*.

6.02.051 The suffixes *taviṣ* and *ant* occur simultaneously [with the verbal root]. 6.02.052 A verbal root ending in a vowel other than *iK*, as well as the roots *añc* and *at*, take the suffix *va* when the suffix *ati* follows.
6.02.053 The prefixes *ni* and *adhi* [are compounded with a following word].
6.02.054 The suffix *īṣat* [is optionally a *karmapravacanīya*] when used with another word.
6.02.055 A measure of gold is [a *karmapravacanīya*] when it refers to wealth (*dhana*).
6.02.056 The word *prathama-* [is a *karmapravacanīya*] when followed by *acira-* and the suffixes *-ap* and *-am*.

6.02.057 The forms *katara-* and *katama-* [are compounded] in a *karmadhāraya* compound. 6.02.058 The word *ārya-* [is compounded] with *brāhmaṇa-* and *kumāra-*. 6.02.059 And [the word] *rājā-* [is compounded with *brāhmaṇa-* and *kumāra-*].

6.02.060 The sixth case ending is used [for the agent] when the word *prati* is combined with a word denoting an offense (*enas*). 6.02.061 The sixth case ending is used [for the agent] after a word ending in the suffix *Kta* when it has the sense of necessity (*nitya*).
6.02.062 The word *grāma-* takes the sixth case ending when combined with a word denoting an artisan (*śilpin*).
6.02.063 In the sense of praise, the word *rājan* [is optionally acute on the first syllable]. 6.02.064 The initial [syllable] is acute.
6.02.065 In a compound denoting "righteous" (*dharmya*) but not "taking away" (*aharaṇa*), the locative case ending and the word *hārin* [are optionally acute on the first syllable].

6.02.066 And [the suffix *kvip* is applied] after a word ending in *yuk*. 6.02.067 Optionally [the suffix *kvip* is applied] after the word *adhyakṣa*. 6.02.068 And [the suffix *kvip* is applied] after the word *pāpa* when it refers to a craftsman (*śilpin*).
6.02.069 [The suffix *cha* (*eya*) is applied] after the words *gotra*, *antevāsin*, *māṇava*, and *brāhmaṇa* when expressing the sense of "scorning.
6.02.070 [The suffix *cha* (*eya*) is applied] after the word *maira* to express the sense of "not being a Ṛg-verse."

6.02.071 The term *bhakta* (food) [is used] in the sense of "that for the sake of which" (*tad-artha*). 6.02.072 [The term *bhakta* is used] as a comparison (*upamāna*) with respect to a cow, a cat, a lion, and *saindhava* (salt). 6.02.073 [The term *bhakta* is used] with the suffix *-aka* in the sense of a means of livelihood (*jīvikā*).

6.02.074 [The suffix *khañ* is applied] after words ending in *prāc*, in the sense of a sport; 6.02.075 [The suffix *khañ* is applied] after a word ending in *aṇ*, when it denotes one who is appointed [to that activity]; 6.02.076 And [the suffix *khañ* is applied] after a word ending in *aṇ*, in the sense of an artisan, provided it does not end in the root *kṛ*.

6.02.077 And [the suffix *ka* is applied] after a word ending in a nominal stem (*saṃjñā*) [to form a patronymic]. 6.02.078 [The suffix *ka* is applied] after *go*, *tantri*, and *yava* when followed by *pāla*. 6.02.079 [The suffix *ka* is applied] when followed by the agentive suffix *ṇini*.
6.02.080 The word *upamāna* is [an optional substitute] when it is the base (*prakṛti*) for the meaning of a word.
6.02.081 The words *yuktārohin* and so forth are also [formed with the suffix *ṇini*].
6.02.082 [The substitution of *ai* for *e* occurs] after *dīrgha*, *kāśa*, *tuṣa*, *bhrāṣṭra*, and *vaṭa* before the suffix *jya*.
6.02.083: [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in *ant*, preceded by more than one vowel (*bahvac*), [provided it does not denote a village].
6.02.084: [The suffix *cha* is applied] after words denoting non-residents of a village (*grāma*).
6.02.085: [The suffix *cha* is applied] after words beginning with *ghoṣa*.
6.02.086 [The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *chattri* and others when meaning "a hall.
6.02.087 [The suffix *ka* is applied after words ending in *prastha*, provided they do not have a *vṛddhi* vowel in the first syllable, except for *karkī* and others.
6.02.088 [The suffix *ka* is also applied] after *mālā* and others.

6.02.089 The word *nava* (new) does not undergo elision [of its final vowel] when preceded by *amahat* (not large), provided it refers to a city (*nagara*), except in the opinion of the Northern grammarians.
6.02.090 Furthermore, in the case of *arma*, a word consisting of two or three vowels (*dvyac* / *tryac*) ending in a vowel other than *a* (*avarṇa*) does not undergo elision [of its final vowel].
6.02.091 [The words] *bhūta*, *adhika*, *saṃjīva*, *madra*, *aśman*, and *kajjala* do not undergo elision [of their final vowel] when preceded by *amahat*.

6.02.092 *anta-* [is compounded with a word ending in *guṇa*] when expressing excellence; 6.02.093 *sarva-* [is compounded with a word ending in *guṇa*] when expressing totality; 6.02.094 [the same applies to *sarva-*] when forming a name, provided it refers to a mountain (*giri*) or a multitude (*nikāya*).
6.02.095 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after the word *kumārī* when expressing age.
6.02.096 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after the word *udaka* when it does not denote something complete (*akevala*).
6.02.097 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after a *dvigu* compound denoting a sacrifice (*kratu*).
6.02.098 [The suffix *cha* (i.e., *īya*) is applied] after the word *sabhā*, when it denotes a neuter [place].
6.02.099 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *pur*, according to the Eastern grammarians.
6.02.100 [The suffix *cha* is applied] also after words preceded by *ariṣṭa* and *gauḍa*.
6.02.101 Not [the suffix *cha*] after *hastin*, *phalaka*, and *mārdeya*.
6.02.102 [The suffix *cha*] is applied in the sense of "inside" (*bila*) after *kusūla*, *kūpa*, *kumbha*, and *śāla*.
6.02.103 Words denoting directions (*dik-śabda*) [take the suffix *cha*] when referring to villages (*grāma*), inhabited tracts (*jana-pada*), or the name of a non-Aryan king (*cānarāṭ*).
6.02.104 And [the word] *ācārya* becomes *ācārya-upasarjana* when it occurs at the end of a compound.
6.02.105 When there is *vṛddhi* of the final member of a compound, the whole [word *ācārya*] becomes *ācārya-upasarjana*.
6.02.106 In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, [the word] *viśva* becomes *ācārya-upasarjana* when it forms a name (*saṃjñā*).
6.02.107 [The suffix *kan* is applied after *udara*, *aśva*, and *iṣu*] when expressing the sense of "throwing.
6.02.108 [The suffix *kan* is applied] when expressing the sense of "throwing.
6.02.109 [The suffix *kan* is applied after *nadī*] when expressing the sense of "kinsman" (*bandhu*).
6.02.110 The suffix *niṣṭhā* preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*) [is optionally acute on its first syllable]. 6.02.111 The initial syllable of the second member [of a compound] [is acute].
6.02.112 [The word] *karṇa-* [is acute on the first syllable when it follows a word denoting] a color or a characteristic mark.
6.02.113 And [the final vowel of the first member] is also elided before a name or a word expressing a comparison.
6.02.114 And [the final vowel of the first member] is elided before *kaṇṭha*, *pṛṣṭha*, *grīvā*, and *jaṅghā*.
6.02.115 And [the final vowel of the first member] is elided before *śṛṅga* when it denotes a state or condition.
6.02.116 After the negative particle *naÑ*, [the final vowel of] *jara*, *mara*, *mitra*, *mṛta*, and *ā* [is replaced by the corresponding semivowel].
6.02.117 After the same [particle], [the final vowels of] *manas*, *aloman*, and *uṣas* [are replaced by the corresponding semivowels].
6.02.118 [The words] *kratu* and others [are included in this rule].
6.02.119 In the Vedic language, a word consisting of two vowels (dvy-aC) has its first syllable acute (ādy-udātta). 6.02.120 [The same applies to] the words *vīra* and *vīrya*.
6.02.121 In an avyayībhāva compound, the words *kūla*, *tīra*, *tūla*, *mūla*, *śālā*, *akṣa*, and *sama* have their first syllable acute.

6.02.122 [The final vowel of] *kaṃsa*, *mantha*, *śūrpa*, *pāyya*, and *kāṇḍa* [is shortened] when followed by a numeral compound (*dvigu*). 6.02.123 In a *tatpuruṣa* compound ending in *śālā*, [the final vowel is shortened] provided it is not neuter.
6.02.124 And [the same applies to] *kanthā*.

6.02.125 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the class of words beginning with *cihaṇa*] to express contempt. 6.02.126 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the group of words] *cela*, *kheṭa*, *kaṭuka*, and *kāṇḍa* to express contempt.
6.02.127 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the word] *cīra* when it is used as a standard of comparison.
6.02.128 [The suffix *a* is applied after the words *palala*, *sūpa*, and *śāka* when they are compounded with a word ending in the locative case.
6.02.129 [The suffix *a* is applied after the words *kūla*, *sūda*, *sthala*, and *karṣa* when they form a proper name (*saṃjñā*).
6.02.130 [The suffix *a* is applied after the word *rājya* in a compound that is not a *karmadhāraya*.]
6.02.131 And [the suffixes] *vargya* and so forth [are applied]. 6.02.132 [The suffix *yañ* is applied after a word ending in] *putra*, provided it is masculine.
6.02.133 Not [after the words] *ācārya* and *rājan*.
In the case of a name associated with a sacrificial priest (*ṛtvij*), [the suffix *cha* is applied] after a word denoting a relative (*jñāti*) [ending in the sixth case].

(Pāṇini 4.1.94) [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *cūrṇa* and others when they do not denote a living being, provided they are in the sixth case. (Pāṇini 4.2.80) And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after the six words beginning with *kāṇḍa*. (Pāṇini 4.2.81)

6.02.136 *kuṇḍam* [is neuter] when it denotes a forest. 6.02.137 *bhagālam* [is neuter] by its very nature (*prakṛtyā*). 6.02.138 After the root *śī*, [the suffix] *na* is always applied in a Bahuvrīhi compound that does not end in *-ah* and is not a *bha*-stem.

6.02.139 A *kṛt* suffix [is applied] after a verbal root (*gati*), a case-factor (*kāraka*), or an upapada. 6.02.140 In the case of compounds beginning with *vanaspati*, both [the *pūrvapada* accent and the *uttarapada* accent] apply simultaneously. 6.02.141 And also in the case of a *devatā-dvandva* (compound of dual deities).

6.02.142 [The acute accent] does not occur on the penultimate syllable of a word ending in a long vowel when it is followed by a compound-final member beginning with an unaccented vowel, except for *pṛthivī*, *rudra*, *pūṣan*, and *manthin*.

6.02.143 [The acute accent occurs] on the final syllable of a word ending in *tha*, *atha*, *GHaÑ*, *Kta*, a suffix beginning with a vowel (*aC*), the feminine suffix *aP*, or the suffixes *itRa* and *KāN*.

6.02.144 [The acute accent occurs] on the final syllable of a word ending in *tha*, *atha*, *GHaÑ*, *Kta*, a suffix beginning with a vowel (*aC*), the feminine suffix *aP*, or the suffixes *itRa* and *KāN*.
6.02.145 The suffix *kta* [is optionally elided] after a word ending in *su-upamāna*.
6.02.146 [The suffix *kta* is optionally elided] in the sense of a name (*saṃjñā*), provided it does not begin with *an* or *acit*.
6.02.147 [The suffix *kta* is optionally elided] also after words beginning with *pravṛddha*.

6.02.148 [The suffix *lyap* is applied] after a word ending in a *kāraka* case, provided that the words *datta* or *śruta* follow, and the sense is one of benediction (*āśis*). 6.02.149 [The suffix *lyap* is applied] also when the sense is "done by one who is thus situated" (*itthambhūtena kṛtam*).
6.02.150 [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after a verbal root ending in *an*, provided it expresses a state (*bhāva*) or an action (*karman*).

6.02.151 The suffix *k*ti*N* occurs after a verbal root in the sense of "explanation" (*vyākhyāna*), "lying down" (*śayana*), "sitting" (*āsana*), "standing" (*sthāna*), "one who sacrifices" (*yājaka*), and so forth, as well as after the root *krī* ("to buy").
6.02.152 The seventh case ending is used with words having the sense of "meritorious" (*puṇya*).
6.02.153 The third case ending is used with words having the sense of "deficient" (*ūna*) and with the word *kalaha* ("quarrel").
6.02.154: And [the word] *miśra* [is treated as a *pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara* when it is] without a prefix (*anupasarga*) and not in a compound (*asaṃdhi*).

6.02.155: After the negative particle *nañ*, [the words] *sampādī*, *arha*, *hita*, and those having the sense of *alam* are [treated as *pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*] when they are *taddhita* suffixes used in the sense of negating a quality (*guṇapratiṣedha*).

6.02.156: [The substitution of *ya* and *yaT* occurs] for the [final vowel and consonant of a nominal stem], provided that the suffix does not express that meaning. 6.02.157: [The substitution of *ya* and *yaT* occurs] for a vowel (*aC*) before the suffixes *K* and *au*, provided that the agent is incapable [of the action]. 6.02.158: [The same substitution occurs] also in the sense of reviling.
6.02.159 [The suffix *ka* is applied] when a name (*saṃjñā*) is to be expressed.
6.02.160 [The suffix *ka* is applied] after words ending in a *kṛt* suffix, after words ending in *uka*, after words ending in *iṣṇuc*, and after the group beginning with *cāru*.
6.02.161 [The suffix *ka* is applied] optionally after the word *tṛn*, and after the words *anna*, *tīkṣṇa*, and *śuci*.

6.02.162 In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the words *idam*, *etad*, *tad*, *hyaḥ*, and the first ordinal numbers [ending in the nominative] are substituted when counting actions. 6.02.163 The word *stana* is substituted for a numeral [in a *bahuvrīhi*].
6.02.164 In the Vedic language, this substitution is optional.

6.02.165 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the words *mitra* and *ajina*] when they form a proper name (*saṃjñā*). 6.02.166 [The suffix *ka* is applied after a word ending in *i*, *u*, or *ṛ*,] provided that there is an intervening element (*antara*) consisting of *vi*, *ava*, or *in*.
6.02.167 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *mukha*] when it refers to one's own limb (*sva-aṅga*).
6.02.168 [The suffix *kta* is not used after] indeclinables, words denoting direction (*dik-śabda*), the words *go*, *mahat*, *sthūla*, *muṣṭi*, *pṛthu*, and *vatsa*.
6.02.169 [The suffix *kta* is optionally used] after a word ending in a past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) when it follows a word used as a standard of comparison (*upamāna*).

6.02.170 [The suffix *kta* is used] after words denoting genus (*jāti*), time, and *sukha* etc., provided they do not denote clothing (*an-ācchādana*), and [the resulting words] are not *kṛta*, *mita*, or *pratipanna*.

6.02.171 Or [the augment *ṭi*] is applied after [a stem ending in] *jāt*; 6.02.172 [The augment *ṭi* is applied] after [stems ending in] *naÑ* and *su*; 6.02.173 [The augment *ṭi* is applied] before [the suffix] *kaP*.

6.02.174: When a short vowel stands at the end [of a bahuvrīhi compound], the penultimate syllable [is acute]. 6.02.175: In a bahuvrīhi compound beginning with *nañ*, the accentuation is like that of the suffix *tara* when it occurs in the sense of *hūmni*. 6.02.176: The *guṇa* vowels and so forth are not considered constituent parts [for the purposes of this rule].
6.02.177 After a prefix (*upasarga*), the word *svargam* [retains its original accent], provided it does not mean "one's own path" and is not followed by *parśu*.
6.02.178 In a compound (*samāsa*), the word *vanam* [retains its original accent].
6.02.179 The word *antaḥ* [retains its original accent in a compound].
6.02.180 And [the suffix *ka* is added] after [the root *ant*].

6.02.181 [The suffix *ka* is not added] after [the roots *ni* and *vi*. 6.02.182 [The suffix *ka* is added] after [the root *pari* when it expresses] being on both sides (*abhito-bhāvin*) or a circle (*maṇḍala*).
6.02.183 *pra* and *āt* [are compounded] with *asva-aṅga* (non-limb of a horse) in the sense of a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
6.02.184 *nirudaka* and so forth [are also compounds].
6.02.185 *mukha* [is compounded] with *abhi*.
6.02.186 Also after *ap*.
6.02.187 After *sphig*, *pū*, *ta*, *vīṇā*, *añjas*, *adhvan*, *kukṣi*, *sīra*, and a name, [the suffix -ka is applied]. And [this applies] when it is a name.

6.02.188 [The word *adhi* is a governing term (*adhikāra*) for what follows. 6.02.189 [The word *upari-stham* is a governing term for what follows. 6.02.189 [The word *anoḥ* is a governing term for what follows, except when it refers to the subordinate (*apradhāna*) or the comparative suffix *kanīyas*.
6.02.190 [The word *puruṣaḥ* is also a governing term for what follows, provided it is not designated as a subsequent rule (*anvādiṣṭa*).]
6.02.191 The augment *at* is applied after the prefix *ati* before a word that does not end in a case-ending (*apada*).
6.02.192 The augment *at* is applied after the prefix *ni* before a word other than *nidhāna*.
6.02.193 The words beginning with *aṃśu* take the augment *at* after the prefix *prati* when they form a *tatpuruṣa* compound.

6.02.194. After the prefix *upa*, the suffix *a* (in the sense of an instrument) is applied to a word ending in two vowels, provided it does not mean "antelope skin" (*ajina*) or belong to the *gaura*-class.
6.02.195. The suffix *a* is applied after the root *sū* in the sense of "throwing away.
6.02.196. The suffix *a* is optionally applied after the root *pucch* with the prefix *ud*.
6.02.197. In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the word-final *-pād-* and *-mūrdhan-* are substituted for *dvi-* and *tri-* respectively, when followed by *pada*, *dat*, or *mūrdhan*.

6.02.198. The word *sakthi* is also [substituted] [for *dvi-* and *tri-*], provided it does not end in the suffix *kṛt* *aṅ*. 6.02.199. In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the substitution of the subsequent [vowel] or the initial [vowel] occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
6.03.001 The suffix *luK* is elided when [a word ending in] *ojas*, *sahas*, *ambhas*, or *tamas* is followed by a word whose final syllable is udātta (*udātta-uttara-pada*).
6.03.002 The suffix *luK* is elided after the ablative case (*pañcamī*) when it follows words beginning with *stoka*.
6.03.003 The suffix *luK* is elided after the instrumental case (*tṛtīyā*) when it follows *ojas*, *sahas*, *ambhas*, or *tamas*.
6.03.004 [The suffix *kha* is applied after *manas*] when it denotes a name (*saṃjñā*). 6.03.005 [The suffix *kha* is applied after *manas*] also when followed by the suffix *ājin*.
6.03.006 [The suffix *kha* is applied after *ātman*] also when it denotes a ordinal number (*pūraṇa*).
6.03.007: In place of the dative case-ending, when it follows a word denoting a grammatical term (vaiyākaraṇa-ākhyā), provided that the word ends in the letter *i*.
6.03.008: And [the substitution of *ai* occurs] in place of the dative ending of the following [word as well].
6.03.009: In place of the locative case-ending, when it follows a word ending in a consonant (*haL*) or the vowel *aT*, provided that the word is a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
6.03.010 And [the suffix *cha* is applied] after a word denoting a maker (*kāra*) when it occurs before a consonant-initial [patronymic suffix], according to the Eastern grammarians.
6.03.011 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word that has a heavy syllable (*guru*) as its middle member.
6.03.012 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word other than *mūrdhan* and *mastaka*, provided it ends in *sva* or *ṛc*, except when desire (*kāma*) is intended.
6.03.013 In *bandha*, [the elision of the case-ending] is optional. 6.03.014 In a *tatpuruṣa* compound ending in a *kṛt*-suffix, [the elision of the case-ending] occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
6.03.015 In the case of *prāvṛṣ*, *śarad*, *kāla*, and *div*, [the elision of the case-ending] occurs before the suffix *j*.
6.03.016 The suffix *vibhāṣā* (optionally) [is applied after a word ending in] *varṣa*, *kṣara*, *śara*, or *vara*.
6.03.017 The suffix *GHaÑ* is applied after a word denoting time when it is used as the first member in a compound with words meaning "time" (*kāla*) or "continuity" (*tana*).
6.03.018 The suffix *KHaL* is applied after a word that is not a word for time when it occurs before the words *śaya*, *vāsa*, or *vāsin*.

6.03.019 Not [substitution] occurs for the genitive case-ending in the words *asiddha*, *badhna*, and *ati*. 6.03.020 And [not] in the word *stha* when used in common speech (*bhāṣā*). 6.03.021 [Not] in the genitive case-ending when used in an abusive expression (*ākrośa*).

6.03.022 The suffix *putra* is optionally [added] after [a word ending in the sixth case] when it signifies "the son of another. 6.03.023 The suffix *hyas* is added after [a word ending in the sixth case] denoting a relationship through learning or birth. 6.03.024 The suffix *hyas* is optionally added after [a word ending in the sixth case] signifying "sister" (*svasṛ*) or "husband" (*pati*).

6.03.025 The suffix ānaṄ is substituted for the final vowel of a word ending in ṛT when it occurs in a Dvandva compound. 6.03.026 [The same substitution applies] also in a Dvandva compound of deities.
6.03.027 The long vowel īT is substituted for the final vowel of the word agni when it follows soma or varuṇa in a Dvandva compound.
6.03.028 *i* and *u* are substituted for [the final vowel of a word ending in] *vṛdh* when followed by a suffix beginning with a vowel (*vṛddhi*).
6.03.029 *divaḥ* becomes *dyāvā*. 6.03.030 *divas-* also [becomes *dyāvā*] before *pṛthivī*.
6.03.031 *uṣāsā* for *uṣasaḥ*; 6.03.032 *mātara-pitarau* for the northern grammarians; 6.03.033 *pitarā-mātarā* [also] in the Vedic language.

6.03.034 When a feminine word follows a masculine word of the same referent (samānādhikaraṇa) that has already expressed its masculinity, the feminine form is treated like the masculine, provided it does not end in the suffix ūṄ and is not a word denoting a ordinal number, nor one belonging to the class beginning with *priyā*.

6.03.035 This [masculine treatment] applies from the suffixes beginning with *tasil* up to, but excluding, *kṛtvasuC*. 6.03.036 It also applies when the denominative suffix *KyaṄ* or the suffix *mānin* follows.

6.03.037 Not [the substitution of vṛddhi] occurs for a vowel that has *k* or *u* as its penultimate (*upadhā*). 6.03.038 Nor does it occur for a feminine name (*saṃjñā*) or a ordinal number (*pūraṇī*).
6.03.039 Nor does it occur for a *taddhita* suffix that is the cause of *vṛddhi*, provided it does not denote a coloring (*rakta*) or a transformation (*vikāra*).
6.03.040: [The feminine suffix] īT is elided after a word ending in a vowel other than a short *a*, provided it does not denote a measure (māna) or possess a suffix denoting possession (matUP).
6.03.041: [The feminine suffix īT is also elided] after a word denoting a genus (jāti).
6.03.042: In a *karmadhāraya* compound, as well as in words ending in the suffixes *jātīya* and *deśīya*, [the first member] is treated like the masculine (*puṃvat*).

6.03.043: After a stem ending in more than one vowel (an-ek-aC), the suffix *Ṅya* is applied in the sense of "having the form of" (*gha*), "resembling" (*kalpa*), "clothed in" (*celaṬ*), "calling oneself" (*bruva*), "belonging to the lineage of" (*gotra*), "approved by" (*mata*), or "struck by" (*hata*); furthermore, the preceding vowel is shortened. 6.03.044: In the case of a feminine stem ending in *nadī*, the substitution of the *Ṅya*-suffix for the remaining [genitive] case endings is optional.
6.03.045: And [the substitution of *Ṅya* occurs] after a stem that has the augment *uk* or is marked with the indicatory letter *it*.
6.03.046 The substitute *āt* is applied to the final vowel of *mahat* when followed by a word in the same grammatical case (*samānādhikaraṇa*) or by the suffix *jātīya*.
6.03.047 The substitute *dvi* is applied to *dvi* and *aṣṭan* when used in enumeration (*saṃkhyā*), except in a *bahuvrīhi* compound or before the word *aśīti*.
6.03.048 The substitute *traya* is applied to *tri*.
6.03.049 Optionally, when followed by "forty" (*catvāriṃśat*) and the subsequent numbers, [the substitution] applies to all [the stems mentioned].
6.03.050 For *hṛdaya*, the substitution of *hṛd* occurs before the suffix *laK*, the suffix *yaT*, and in the word *hlāsa*.
6.03.051 Optionally, [the substitution of *hṛd* for *hṛdaya* occurs] before the suffix *Śoka*, the suffix *ŚyaÑ*, and in the word *roga*.
6.03.052 [The substitution of *pada* for *pāda* occurs] before *aji*, *āti*, *ga*, *upa*, *ha*, and *te*.
6.03.053 [The substitution of *pada* for *pāda* occurs] before a *yaT* suffix that does not express its own meaning (*atadartha*).
6.03.054 [The substitution of *pada* for *pāda* occurs] also before *himakāṣin* and *hata*.
6.03.055 [The substitution of *ṛc* for *ṛcaḥ* occurs] before the suffix *śas*.
6.03.056 [The substitution of *ṛc* for *ṛcaḥ*] optionally occurs in words that denote a mixture of sounds.
6.03.057 [The substitution of *uda* for *udaka* occurs] in a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
6.03.058 [The suffix *kvin* is applied after a verbal root] before the words *peṣam*, *vās*, *vah*, *anaduh*, and *dhi*.

6.03.059 [The suffix *kvin* is applied after a verbal root] ending in a single consonant when it is to be connected with a word beginning with a vowel (*pūrayitavye*) and not preceded by the negative particle *na*.
6.03.060 [The suffix *kvin* is applied after a verbal root] also before the words *mantha*, *odana*, *saktu*, *bindu*, *vajra*, *bhārahāra*, *vīvadhaga*, and *gāha*.

6.03.061 According to Gālava, a short vowel replaces the *iK* of a word ending in a suffix other than *aṄ*. 6.03.062 A short vowel replaces the final vowel of a stem before a single *taddhita* suffix.
6.03.063 In names and in Vedic literature, the substitution of a short vowel for the feminine suffixes *Ṅī* and *ĀP* occurs frequently.
6.03.064 Also before the suffix *tva*.
6.03.065 [The final vowel and consonant of] *iṣṭakā*, *iṣīkā*, and *mālā* are elided when followed by *cita*, *tūla*, and *bhārin* respectively.
6.03.066 [The final vowel and consonant of] a word ending in a *khiṭ*-suffix are elided, provided it is not an indeclinable (*avyaya*).
6.03.067: The augment *muṭ* is added after the word *aruṣ*, as well as after a word ending in a vowel other than *a*, when followed by a word beginning with *dviṣat*.
6.03.068: The augment *m* is added after a monosyllabic word ending in a vowel other than *a*, when followed by a suffix beginning with a vowel.
6.03.069: The forms *vācaṃyama* and *puraṃdara* are irregularly formed.
6.03.070 The suffix *ka* is applied after the word *satyāgada*.
6.03.071 The suffix *ñi* is applied after *śyena* and *tila* when followed by the word *pāta*.
6.03.072 After the word *rātri*, the suffix *ka* is optionally applied when followed by a word ending in the suffix *kṛt*.

6.03.073 The elision (*lopa*) of the *n* of the negative particle *nañ* [occurs before a following vowel]. 6.03.074 After that [elided *n*], the augment *nuṭ* is inserted before a vowel. 6.03.075 The words *na*, *bhrāj*, *pāt*, *vedas*, *satya*, *muci*, *kula*, *kha*, *puṃsaka*, *kṣatra*, *kra*, and *aka* remain in their original form (*prakṛtyā*) when preceded by *na*.

6.03.076 *Eka* and so forth [are substituted] for the word *eka*, and the augment *aduk* is added after it. 6.03.077 *Na* is substituted for *ga* in words denoting non-living beings, except when followed by *ny* or *ara*. 6.03.078 *Sa* is substituted for *saha* when it forms a technical term (*saṃjñā*).

6.03.079 Also [the suffix *ṭac* is applied] after a word ending in *grantha*, when it means "more than. 6.03.080 And [the suffix *ṭac* is applied] in the accusative case, provided that it does not mean "beyond" (*an-atyaya*). 6.03.081 And [the suffix *ṭac* is applied] in an *avyayībhāva* compound, provided that it does not denote time (*akāla*).
6.03.082 The [substitute] *vā* is substituted for the final vowel of an upasarjana.
6.03.083 In a benediction (*āśis*), the original form (*prakṛti*) is retained before the words *go*, *vatsa*, and *hala*.
6.03.084 In Vedic literature (*chandas*), the original form of *samāna* is retained except when it occurs in the word *mūrdhan*.
In the sense of "beginning with" (*prabhṛti*) and "ending with" (*udarka*),

[the first member of a compound retains its original accent] when followed by words denoting light, a country, night, a navel, a name, a lineage, form, place, color, age, speech, or kinship. (Pāṇini 6.2.85)

6.03.086 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *caraṇa* when it means a Vedic school (*brahmacārin*). 6.03.087 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the word *tīrtha* when it means a teacher (*yājaka*). 6.03.088 [The suffix *cha* is applied] optionally (*vibhāṣā*) after the word *udara*.

6.03.089 [The suffix] vatU is applied after the words *dṛś* and *dṛśa*. 6.03.090 The substitutes *īŚ* and *kī* are applied respectively after the words *idam* and *kim*. 6.03.091 The substitute *ā* is applied for the final vowel of a pronominal (*sarvanāman*).
6.03.092: The word *viṣvañc* (and *devaṃyañc*) undergoes the substitution of *adri-añc* when followed by the suffix *ṭa* and the suffix *va*.
6.03.093: The substitution of *sam* for *sam* occurs [before a following vowel].
6.03.094: The substitution of *tiri* for *tiras* occurs when there is no elision (*alopa*).
6.03.095 *saha* becomes *sadhr-* [before a vowel]. 6.03.096 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), [the word] *sadhá* [is substituted for *saha*] before *māda* and *stha*.
6.03.097 After a preposition (*upasarga*) containing two vowels, the long vowel *ī* is substituted for the *i* of the root *ap*.

6.03.098: *ūt* is substituted for the final vowel of a word ending in *an*, when followed by a word denoting a location (*deśa*). 6.03.099: The augment *duK* is applied after the verbal roots *āśā*, *āsthā*, *āsthitā*, *utsuka*, *ūti*, *kāraka*, *rāga*, and *cheṣa*, provided they are not in the genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) nor in the third case (*tṛtīyā*). 6.03.100: When the word *artha* follows, the augment *duK* is optionally applied.

6.03.101 *kat* is substituted for *koḥ* in a *tatpuruṣa* compound when followed by a vowel-initial suffix (*aC*). 6.03.102 [The substitution of *kat* for *koḥ* occurs] also before *ratha* and *vada*. 6.03.103 [The substitution of *kat* for *koḥ* occurs] also before *tṛṇa*, when it denotes a genus (*jāti*).

6.03.104 [The word] *pathin* [takes the suffix *ka*] when followed by *akṣaya*. 6.03.105 [The suffix *ka* is applied] in the sense of "slight" (*īṣadartha*). 6.03.106 [The application of the suffix *ka*] is optional (*vibhāṣā*) when followed by *puruṣa*.
6.03.107 *kava* is substituted for *kim* before the locative suffix *-uṣṇe*.
6.03.108 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), it is also substituted before *pathi*.
6.03.109 Words such as *pṛṣodara* are formed according to their traditional instruction.
6.03.110: For the word *ahan* (day), when it follows a numeral, *vi*, *sāya*, or *ūrdhva*, the substitution of *ahan* for *ahar* optionally takes place in the locative singular (*Ṅ-i*).

6.03.111: When *ḍha* or *ra* is elided, the long vowel (*dīrgha*) is substituted for the preceding vowel that is not *Ṇ* (i.e., not *ṛ*). 6.03.112: In the roots *sah* and *vah*, the substitute *oT* is applied in place of the vowel *a*.

6.03.113 [The substitution of] *sāḍhyai*, *sāḍhvā*, and *sāḍha* occurs in the Vedic usage (*nigama*). 6.03.114 [The substitution of *sa* for *sam*] occurs before a word beginning with a vowel in a *saṃhitā*. 6.03.115 [The substitution of *sa* for *sam* occurs] before a mark (*lakṣaṇa*) on the ear that is not *viṣṭa* or *aṣṭan*.
The suffix *Kv* occurs after the roots *man*, *bhid*, *chid*, *chidra*, *srū*,
*svasti*, *kṛ*, *nah*, *vṛt*, *vṛṣ*, *vyadh*, *ruc*, *sah*, and *tan*, when followed by the affix *au*. (Pāṇini 3.2.176)
6.03.117 In the sense of a name, the final vowel of *koṭara*, *kiṃśulaka*, and so forth, is elided when followed by the words *vana* or *giri*. 6.03.118 [The same applies] before the suffix *vala*.
6.03.119 Before the suffixes *mat* and *au*, the final vowel of a word consisting of more than two syllables (*bahvac*) is elided, except for *ajira* and other such words.
6.03.120 And [the final vowel] of *śara* and so forth [is lengthened before a suffix beginning with *n*].
6.03.121 [The final vowel of a word ending in] a short *iK* vowel is lengthened before the root *vah*, except when it means "a cart" (*pīla*).
6.03.122 The [final vowel] of a preposition (*upasarga*) is diversely lengthened before the suffix *GHaÑ*, provided it does not refer to a human being.
6.03.123: After a stem ending in *i* or *u*, the long vowel is substituted before the feminine suffix *kāś*.
6.03.124: The long vowel is substituted for the final letter of a word ending in *d* when followed by *ti*.
6.03.125: The substitution of *aṣṭā-* for *aṣṭan-* occurs when it forms part of a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
6.03.126 And [the substitution of *vasu* for *viśva* occurs] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
6.03.127 [The substitution of *vasu* for *viśva* occurs] before the suffix *kaP*, when it follows *cit*.
6.03.128 [The substitution of *vasu* for *viśva* occurs] before *vasu* and *rāj*.
6.03.129 [The suffix *matUP* is applied after a word ending in *a*] when it denotes a person (*nar-*) as the object of recognition (*saṃjñā-ay-ām*).
6.03.130 [The suffix *matUP* is applied after a word ending in *a*] also when it means *mitra-* (a friend) who is a seer (*ṛṣ-au*).

6.03.131 [The suffix *matUP* is applied after a word ending in *a*] in the sense of a mantra (*mantr-e*), provided that the words *soma*, *aśva*, *indriya*, or *viśva* precede the word ending in *a*. The suffixes *mat* and *au* [are also used].
6.03.132 *oṣadhi* and [the word ending in] a vowel take the augment *t* before a case-ending other than the nominative singular (*prathamā*) and the locative plural (*ām*).
6.03.133 In a *ṛc* (Vedic verse), the words *tu*, *nu*, *gha*, *makṣu*, *taṅ*, *kutra*, *uruṣyā*, and [words ending in] *an* take the augment *t*.
6.03.134 A word ending in an *iK* vowel takes the augment *suṆ* before the vocative singular suffix *su*.
6.03.135 The final vowel of a finite verb ending (tiṅ) that consists of two vowels and ends in a short *a* is elided [before a following vowel].
6.03.136 And [the final vowel] of an indeclinable (nipāta) [is elided before a following vowel].
6.03.137 This [elision] is also observed in other cases.
6.03.138 *cau* 6.03.139 *sam-pra-sār-aṇasya* 6.04.001 *aṛgasya*
6.04.002 After a consonant [ending in a pratyāhāra beginning with *ha* and ending with *l*], [the substitution of *n* for the final letter occurs].
6.04.003 Before a case-ending (*nām*) [beginning with a vowel], [the substitution of *n* for the final letter occurs].
6.04.004 Not so, however, in the case of *tisṛ* and *catasṛ*.
6.04.005 In Vedic (chandas), both ways [the augment *it* is applied].
6.04.006 Also after the word *nṛ*.
6.04.007 Not after a stem-final vowel (*upadhā*) that is long.
6.04.008 And [the substitution of *na* for *m* occurs] in all case-endings (*sarvanāmasthāna*), except in the vocative singular.
6.04.009 Optionally [the substitution of *na* for *m* occurs] in the Vedic language (*nigama*) when preceded by *ṣ*.
6.04.010 [The substitution of *na* for *m* occurs] after a *sa*-ending or the word *mahat*, when followed by a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*).

6.04.011 [The long vowel *ā* is substituted for the final vowel of] the stems ending in *aptṛ*, *tṛN*, *tṛC*, *svasṛ*, *napṭṛ*, *neṣṭṛ*, *tvaṣṭṛ*, *kṣattṛ*, *hotṛ*, *potṛ*, and *praśāstṛ* [before the nominative singular ending *su*].
6.04.012 [The long vowel *ā* is substituted for the final vowel of] the stems *in*, *han*, *pūṣan*, and *aryaman* [before the nominative singular ending *su*].
6.04.013 Also after [a verbal root] ending in /s/ followed by /au/.
6.04.014 And also after [a verbal root] ending in /atU/, provided it does not end in the suffix /as/ and is not a verbal root (*adhātu*).

6.04.015 [The substitution of /an/ for the final phoneme] of a nasalized vowel (*anunāsika*) occurs before the suffix *Kvi* and before consonant-initial suffixes (*jhaL*) that have the markers *K* or *Ṅ*.
6.04.016 The substitution of *aC* occurs for the roots *han*, *gam*, and [others] before the suffix *saN*.
6.04.017 The substitution of *aC* for the root *tan* before the suffix *te* is optional.
6.04.018 The substitution of *aC* also occurs for the root *kram* before the suffix *Ktvā*.
6.04.019: The substitution of *ś* and *ūṭh* occurs respectively for *c* and *ch*, and for *v* and *o*, when followed by a nasal (*anunāsika*).
6.04.020: The substitution of *ūṭh* occurs for the vowel following the *upadhā* (penultimate) of the roots *jvar*, *tvar*, *sriv*, *av*, and *mav*.
6.04.021: There is elision (*lopa*) of the vowel following an *r*.
6.04.022 The suffix *as* is treated like *siddha* (already accomplished) from here up to [the end of] the sixth chapter.
6.04.023 There is the elision (*lopa*) of the *n* following the root *śn*.

6.04.024 When a suffix beginning with a consonant (*hal*) and marked with *K* or *Ṅ* as an *it* follows, there is the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) of roots ending in a consonant that have no *it* marker.
6.04.025 The substitution of *na* for the final consonant occurs after the roots *daṃś*, *sañj*, and *svañj* when followed by the affix *Śap*.
6.04.026 And it also occurs after the root *rañj* [when followed by *Śap*].
6.04.027 And it occurs [with the substitution of *na*] also before the affix *GHaÑ* when it denotes either an abstract action (*bhāva*) or an instrument (*karaṇa*).
6.04.028 *syada-* [is substituted for *sṛ*] in the sense of speed; 6.04.029 *avoda*, *edha*,
*odman*, *praśratha*, and *himaśratha*.

6.04.030 The substitution of *na* for *an* occurs before the suffix *ya* when it denotes worship (*pūjā*). 6.04.031 The substitution of *na* for *an* occurs before the suffix *Ktvā* after the roots *skand* and *syand*. 6.04.032 The substitution of *na* for *an* is optional after roots ending in *j* and after the root *naś*.
6.04.033 And [the substitution of] *bhañj* occurs before the affix *Ciṇ*.
6.04.034 An *iṭ* augment is added to the root *śās* before an affix beginning with a vowel other than *aṅ*.
6.04.035 [The substitution of] *śā* occurs for *śās* before the affix *ha*.
6.04.036: For the root *han*, [the substitute] *ja* is applied [in place of the final consonant].

6.04.037: For roots taught with an anudātta indicatory vowel (*upadeśa*), for the root *van*, and for those beginning with *tan*, the penultimate nasal is elided before an affix beginning with a *jhaL* (any consonant except a semivowel or *y*) that has an indicatory *K* or *Ṅ*.
6.04.038: This elision is optional when the affix is *lyap*.

6.04.039 There is no lengthening [of the vowel] before the suffix *KtiC*. 6.04.040 [There is no lengthening] of the root *gam-* before the suffix *Kvau*. 6.04.041 Before the suffixes *viṭ* and *van*, there is lengthening of a nasalized vowel (*anunāsika*) that ends in *āT*.

6.04.042: The substitution of *na* for the final consonant of the roots *jan*, *san*, and *khan* occurs before the suffix *saN* and before a *jhaL* (consonant) beginning affix. 6.04.043: This substitution is optional (*vibhāṣā*) before the suffix *ya*.
6.04.044: The substitution of *na* for the final consonant of the root *tan* occurs before the suffix *yaK*.
6.04.045: Before the suffix *KtiC*, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the vowel of the root *san*, provided that the following syllable begins with *ny*, *ar*, or *ay*.
6.04.046: In the domain of *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes, [the substitution of *guṇa* applies].

6.04.047: For the root *bhrasj*, when followed by an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with *ny*, *ar*, or *ay*, the substitute *raM* (i.e., *r*) replaces both the penultimate vowel and the consonant *j*.

6.04.048 There is elision (lopa) of the *a* following [the final element of] a verbal root ending in *at*. 6.04.049 There is elision of the *y* of the suffix *kyac* when it follows a consonant (*hal*). 6.04.050 The elision of the *y* of the suffix *kyac* is optional.
6.04.051 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel of a verbal root occurs] before the affix *ṇa*, provided that no augment *iṭ* is inserted.
6.04.052 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel of a verbal root occurs] before the past passive participle suffix (*niṣṭhā*) when it bears the augment *seṭ*.
6.04.053 [In the Vedic language (*mantra*),] the form *janitā* is used [for *janayitā*].
6.04.054 The suffix *śamitṛ* is applied after the root *yaj* in the sense of a sacrifice (*yajña*).
6.04.055 The suffixes *ay*, *ām*, *anta*, *ālu*, *āyya*, *itnu*, *iṣṇu*, and *u* are applied [after a verbal root] when preceded by a light vowel.
6.04.056 The suffix *LyaP* is applied [after a verbal root] when it is preceded by a light vowel.

6.04.057 The long vowel is optionally substituted for the final *ā* of verbal roots ending in *ā*. 6.04.058 In Vedic literature, the long vowel is substituted for the final vowels of the roots *yū* and *plu*. 6.04.059 [The long vowel is substituted for the final vowel] of the root *kṣi*.

6.04.060: In the case of a *niṣṭhā* suffix, when it does not have the sense of *ṇyad*. 6.04.061: Optionally, in the case of verbal abuse or dejection. 6.04.062: Before the affixes *sya*, *sic*, *sīyuṭ*, and *tāsi*, when expressing the sense of becoming (*bhāva*) or an object (*karman*), [the augment *iṭ* is applied] as in the case of *ciṇ*, provided that the root begins with a vowel (*ac*) and is not *han* or *grah* or *dṛś* in its original form (*upadeśe*). And [the augment *iṭ* is applied] after these roots.
6.04.063: After the root *dīṄ*, the suffix *yuṬ* is inserted before an affix beginning with a vowel that has an indicatory *K* or *Ṅ*.
6.04.064: The elision (*lopa*) of the long vowel *Ā* occurs before the augment *iṬ* and before an affix beginning with a vowel that has an indicatory *K* or *Ṅ*.
6.04.065: The substitution of *īT* occurs in place of the long vowel *Ā* before the affix *yaT*.
6.04.066: For the roots √ghu, √mā, √sthā, √gā, √pā, √jā, √hā, and √ti, [the substitution of iK for the final vowel occurs] before a consonant (haL).
6.04.067: In the potential (liṅ), [the substitution of iK for the final vowel of √ghu, etc.,] occurs [only] when followed by the augment iṭ.
6.04.068: In other cases, [the substitution of iK for the final vowel] optionally occurs for those roots beginning with a conjunct consonant (saṃyoga) that have a single vowel.
6.04.069 [The substitution of *iṭ*] does not occur before an affix having the designation *LyaP*.
6.04.070 The augment *iṭ* optionally occurs after the root *mā* (to measure) before the affix *te*.
6.04.071 In the place of the affixes *luṅ*, *liṅ*, and *lṛṅ*, the augment *aṭ* is added, and it is udātta-accented.
6.04.072 The substitution of *āṬ* occurs for vowels beginning with *aC*.
6.04.073 This is also observed in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
6.04.074 It does not occur when there is a connection with the pronoun *māṅ*.
6.04.075 In Vedic (chandas), [the substitution of *u* for *ū*] occurs frequently even when not joined with a *māṅ* [prohibitive particle].
6.04.076 For the root *ir*, [the substitute *īr* is replaced by] *re*.
6.04.077 Before a vowel (*aC*), the *y* and *v* of the suffix *Śnu*, verbal roots, and the word *bhru* are replaced respectively by *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*.
6.04.078 [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of] a reduplicated syllable [is applied] before a vowel that is not homogeneous (*asa-varṇa*).

6.04.079 [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of] the word *strī* [is applied] before a vowel that is not homogeneous. 6.04.080 [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of *strī*] is optional (*vā*) before the case-endings *am* and *Śas*.
6.04.081 *iṇ* is replaced by *yaṇ*.
6.04.082 *e* is replaced by *yaṇ* when it consists of more than one vowel (*anekāc*) and is not followed by a conjunct consonant (*asaṃyoga*) or the word *ūrvī*.
6.04.083 *o* is replaced by *yaṇ* before case endings (*sUP*).
6.04.084 Also after *varṣā* and *bhū*.
6.04.085 Not after *bhū*, *su*, and *dhī*. 6.04.086 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), it is both ways.
6.04.087: The augment *śnu* is added after the roots *hu* and *bhū* when followed by a *sārvadhātuka* affix.
6.04.088: The augment *vuK* is added after the root *bhū* when followed by the *luṅ* or *liṭ* affixes.
6.04.089: The augment *ūT* is added to the penultimate vowel of the root *guh*.
6.04.090 The substitution of *doṣ* occurs before the affix *ṇu*.
6.04.091 Optionally, when there is a change of consciousness or loss of passion (*virāga*).
6.04.092 The short vowel is substituted for those [roots] that have *m* as an *it*.

6.04.093: The long vowel [is substituted] for the root-final of roots ending in *ciṇ* before the suffixes *ṇamul* and [the kṛt-suffix] *kta*, optionally. 6.04.094: A short vowel [is substituted] for the root-final before the suffix *KhaC*.
6.04.095: [The substitution of a short vowel occurs] for the root *hlād* before a *niṣṭhā* suffix.
6.04.096: The substitution of *GHa* occurs for the root *chad* when it is not preceded by two prefixes.
6.04.097: The substitution of *GHa* also occurs for the root *chad* before the affixes *i*, *mantraN*, and *kvip*.
6.04.098: There is elision (*lopa*) of the final letter of the roots *gam*, *han*, *jan*, *khan*, and *ghas* before an affix marked with *K* or *Ṅ* that does not have the augment *aṄ*.
6.04.099 In the Vedic language, the substitution of *t* occurs for the final consonant of the suffixes *tan* and *pati*.
6.04.100 In the Vedic language, the substitution of *t* occurs for the final consonant of the roots *ghas* and *bhās* before a consonant.
6.04.101 After the root *hu* and after consonants, the substitution of *dhi* occurs for the imperative suffix *hi*.
6.04.102 In the Vedic language (chandas), [the suffixes] after the roots *śru*, *śṛ*, *ṇu*, *pṝ*, *kṛ*, and *vṛ* [take the augment *iṭ*].
6.04.103 And [the suffixes] that do not have *ṅ* as an *it* [take the augment *iṭ*].
6.04.104 There is elision (*luK*) of the *CiṆ* suffix.
6.04.105: *he-* [is substituted] for *at-ah* [the final vowel of a word ending in short *a*].
6.04.106: [The substitution of *he-*] also [occurs] after a suffix beginning with *uT* (any vowel except *r*) that does not end in a conjunct consonant (*asaṃyogapūrva*).
6.04.107: And there is optionally (*anyatarasyām*) the elision (*lopa*) of this [suffix] before the case-endings *m* and *voḥ*.

6.04.108 After the root *kṛ*, [the augment *iṭ*] is always [added before an affix beginning with a consonant]. 6.04.109 And [it is added] before an affix beginning with *y*. 6.04.110 Before an *ārdhadhātuka* affix beginning with a vowel, *uṭ* is substituted for the final short *a* of a verbal root.

6.04.111: There is elision (*lopa*) of the *a* following the suffixes *śna* and *as*. 6.04.112: There is substitution of long *ā* (*āt*) for the vowel of the root in the case of the suffix *śnā* and in reduplication (*abhyāsa*).
6.04.113: Long *ī* is substituted [for the final vowel] before a consonant beginning with *hal*, except when the root belongs to the *aghu* class.
6.04.114 *iṭ* [is optionally added] after *daridra*.
6.04.115 [The augment *iṭ* is optionally added] after *bhī*.
6.04.116 [The augment *iṭ* is also optionally added] after *jahāti*.
6.04.117 The augment *āṭ* is applied before *ha*.
6.04.118 There is elision (*lopa*) of the *y* [of the suffix *yaṅ*] when followed by a suffix beginning with *i*.
6.04.119 After a root ending in *ghu*, the vowel *eT* is substituted for the *ha* of the imperative suffix, and there is also elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*).

6.04.120: A short *a* [is substituted] for a long *ā* that occurs between two single consonants, provided it is not a substitute [of a preceding element], when followed by a suffix marked with *liṭ*. 6.04.121: And [the same substitution occurs] before the suffix *thal*, provided it is accompanied by the augment *iṭ*. 6.04.122: Also for the roots *tṛ*, *phal*, *bhaj*, and *trap*.
6.04.123 *rādha* in the sense of injury;
6.04.124 optionally for *jṛ*, *bhram*, and *tras*; 6.04.125 and for the seven beginning with *phaṇ*.
6.04.126 The [substitution of] guṇa for the vowels of śas, dadā, and so forth, and for the suffix ṇ, does not take place.
6.04.127 For the word *arvan*, the substitution of *tṛ* occurs before the nominative singular ending *asau*, provided it is not preceded by the negative particle *nañ*.
6.04.128 The form *maghavan* is used diversely.
6.04.129 For *bha*, [the substitution of *u* for *v* occurs].
6.04.130 *pāda-* becomes *pad-*.
6.04.131 There is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the vowel of the suffix *vasu*.
6.04.132 The suffix *ūṬH* is applied after the word *vāha*.
6.04.133 The suffix *ūṬH* is applied after the words *śvan*, *yuvan*, and *maghavan* when a non-taddhita suffix follows.
6.04.134 A vowel beginning with *a* is substituted for the final *an* of a stem when the elision (*lup*) of a suffix occurs.
6.04.135: [The substitution of *u* for the final vowel of the roots] *han*, *dhṛ*, and *rājan* occurs before the suffix *aṇ* when preceded by the letter *ṣ*.

6.04.136: This substitution is optional (*vibhāṣā*) before the locative singular ending *ṅi* and the nominative/accusative dual ending *śi*. 6.04.137: The substitution does not occur after a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*) that ends in *v* or *m*.
6.04.138 Before [a suffix] beginning with a vowel, [the final *i* or *u* of a verbal root ending in] *ac* [is replaced by *ī*].
6.04.139 After the prefix *ud*, [the final *i* or *u* of a verbal root ending in] *ac* [is replaced by *ī*].
6.04.140 [The final *i* or *u* of] a verbal root ending in long *ā* [is replaced by *ī* before a suffix beginning with a vowel].
6.04.141: In mantras, the substitution of *āṅ* for the initial vowel of *ātman* occurs [before a case ending beginning with a vowel].
6.04.142: The substitution of *ti* for the final phoneme of *viṃśati* occurs before an affix marked with the *ḍit* designation.
6.04.144: The substitution of *n* for the final phoneme of a word ending in *an* occurs before a *taddhita* affix.

6.04.145. [The substitution of *u* for the final vowel of] *ahan-* occurs only before the suffixes *ṭa* and *kha*. 6.04.146. [In the case of *ahan-*,] *o* is substituted [for the final vowel] when a *guṇa*-strengthening is required. 6.04.147. [The final vowel of *ahan-*] is elided before the suffix *ḍha*, except in the case of *akadrūḥ*.
6.04.148: [The substitution of *iK* occurs] for the *y* of the suffix *yat*, when a vowel (*īT*) follows.
6.04.149: [The substitution of *iK* occurs] for the *y* that stands as a penultimate letter (*upadhā*) in the words *sūrya*, *tiṣya*, *agastya*, and *matsya*.
6.04.150: [The substitution of *iK* occurs] for the *y* of a *taddhita* suffix beginning with a consonant (*haL*).

6.04.151: And [the elision of *ya*] occurs for the *apatya* (descendant) suffix when followed by a *taddhita* suffix that does not begin with *ā*. 6.04.152: [The elision of *ya*] also occurs for the *ya* of the *kyac* and *cvi* suffixes.
6.04.153: The *luk* elision of the suffix *cha* occurs after words beginning with *bilvaka*.
6.04.154: Before the suffixes *iṣṭhan*, *iman*, and *īyas*, the augment *tu* is added after the word *tṛ*.

6.04.156: In the case of *sthūla*, *dūra*, *yuvan*, *hrasva*, *kṣipra*, and *kṣudra*, the semivowel (*yaṇ*) and following portion are replaced by their corresponding vowels, and there is *guṇa* substitution for the preceding vowel.

6.04.157 For *priya*, *sthira*, *sphira*, *uru*, *bahu*, *guru*, *vṛddha*, *tṛpra*, *dīrgha*, and *vṛndāraka*, there are substituted [respectively] *pra*, *stha*, *spha*, *baṃhi*, *gar*, *varṣi*, *trap*, *drāghi*, and *vṛnd*.
6.04.158 There is elision (*lopa*) of the final syllable of *bahu*, and *bahu* is replaced by *bhū*.
6.04.159 The suffix *iṣṭhan* is replaced by *iy*.
6.04.160 The substitution of *ī* occurs for the vowel *a* following a *jhal*-ending [affix] after a root ending in *īyas*.
6.04.161 The substitution of *r* occurs for the light *ṛ* of a root beginning with a consonant (*hal*) when followed by a *jhal*-ending [affix].
6.04.162 In the Vedic language, the substitution of *r* for the *ṛ* of the root *ṛj* is optional.
6.04.163 A single-vowel [stem] by its very nature [is called *gati* when it precedes a verb].
6.04.164 [A word ending in *in*] before the suffix *aṇ*, provided it does not denote offspring. 6.04.165 [The words] *gāthin* and *vidathin*.
The suffixes -in,
gaṇin, and paṇin, as well as those beginning with a conjunct consonant, [are added after a word ending in a vowel] 6.04.166.
6.04.167 [The substitution of *an* occurs] before the suffixes *ya* and *kha*.
6.04.168 [The substitution of *an* occurs] before the suffix *ya* when it does not denote a state (*bhāva*) or an object (*karman*).
6.04.169 [The substitution of *ātman* occurs] for *ātman* before the suffix *kha*, and [the substitution of *adhyān* occurs] for *adhvan* before the same suffix.

6.04.170. A word preceded by *ma* does not take the suffix *aṇ* in the sense of offspring, except for the word *avarmaṇ*. 6.04.171. The suffix *brāhma* is used in the sense of "belonging to" (*tasyedam*), but not when it denotes a genus (*jāti*). 6.04.172. The suffix *kārm* is used in the sense of "having that as one's habitual practice" (*tācchīlya*).
6.04.173 *aukṣam* [is used] in the sense of *anaptye*.

6.04.174 The forms *dāṇḍināyana*, *hāstināyana*, *ātharvaṇika*, *jaihmāśineya*, *vāsineya*, *bhrauṇahatya*, *dhāivatya*, *sārava*, *aikṣvāka*, *maitreya*, and *hiraṇmaya* [are used as masculine stems].
6.04.175 In the Veda (*chandas*), the forms *ṛtvya*, *vāstvyá*, *vāstva*, *mādhvī*, and *hiraṇyaya* [are used].
7.01.001 *yu* and *vu* are replaced by *ana* and *aka*, respectively, when followed by a suffix beginning with a consonant other than *y*.
7.01.002 The substitutes *āyan*, *ey*, *īn*, *īy*, and *iy* take the place of the suffix-initial *pha*, *ḍha*, *kha*, *cha*, and *gha*.
7.01.003 A suffix beginning with a *jh* sound is replaced by *anta*.
7.01.004 [The augment *iṭ* is applied] after the root *as* when followed by the suffixes beginning with *at*.
7.01.005 [The augment *iṭ* is applied] after roots ending in a vowel other than *a* when the *ātmanepada* suffixes follow.
7.01.006 [The augment *ruṭ* is applied] after the root *śīṅ*.
7.01.007 The substitution of *ai* for the case-ending *bhis* after the verbal root *vid* is optional. 7.01.008 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this substitution occurs diversely.
7.01.009 The substitution of *ais* for the case-ending *bhis* occurs after a stem ending in a short vowel other than *a*.
7.01.010 In the Vedic language, the plural ending *bahu-lam* is optionally substituted [for the nominative plural].

7.01.011 The substitution of *ina* for the genitive singular ending *ṭā*, and of *āt* for the genitive singular (*ṅasi*) and ablative singular (*ṅas*), does not occur after the pronouns *idam* and *adas* when they do not end in *ak*.
7.01.012 For the endings *ṭā*, *ṅasi*, and *ṅas*, the substitutes *ina*, *āt*, and *syāḥ* respectively are applied.
7.01.013 *ṅe* becomes *ya*.
7.01.014 For a pronoun (*sarvanāman*), *smai* is substituted [for *ṅe*].
7.01.015 For *ṅasi* and *ṅi*, *smāt* and *smin* are substituted [respectively].

7.01.016 From [the group of words] beginning with *pūrva* up to *nava*, the substitution of *Śī* occurs in place of the case-ending *Jas*. 7.01.017 The substitution of *Śī* occurs in place of the case-ending *Jas*. 7.01.018 The substitution of *āP* occurs in place of the case-ending *auṅ*.
7.01.019 Also after a neuter [stem ending in] /a/.
7.01.020 For the [case endings] Jas and Śas, there is Śi.
7.01.021 After [the forms of] aṣṭan ending in auŚ.
7.01.022 *luK* [is substituted] for the six [case endings].
7.01.023 [The substitution of *su* and *am* by *luK* does not occur] after a neuter stem ending in a vowel other than *a*.
7.01.024 *am* [is substituted] for [the nominative singular case ending] after a neuter stem ending in *a*.

7.01.025 The suffix *adḍ* is substituted [for the nominative singular ending] after the five beginning with *itará*. 7.01.026 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), it is not [substituted] after *itara*. 7.01.027 After *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the substitution of *aŚ* occurs for the ending *Ṅas*.
7.01.028 *ṅe* and the first case [singular] endings take *am*.
7.01.029 The [genitive plural] ending *śas* takes *na*.
7.01.030 The [ablative plural] ending *bhyas* takes *bhyam*.
7.01.031 For the fifth case [ending], *āt* is substituted.
7.01.032 And for the singular number [of the fifth case], *āt* is substituted.
7.01.033 For the word *sām*, *ākam* is substituted [in the fifth case].
7.01.034 For a long vowel *ā* [ending in a verbal root], *au* is substituted before the *ṇal* suffix.
7.01.035 In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), *tāt* is substituted for the suffixes *tu*, *hi*, and *os* when they follow a root ending in *ni* or *ar*.
7.01.036 After the root *vid*, the suffix *vasu* is substituted for the suffix *śatṛ*.

7.01.037 In a compound (samāsa) where the preceding member is not *nañ*, the suffix *Ktvā* is replaced by *LyaP*. 7.01.038 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *Ktvā* may also [be replaced by *LyaP*]. 7.01.039 For the case endings (*sUP*), there are the following substitutes: *su*, *luk*, *pūrvasavarṇa*, *āT*, *śi*, *ya*, *ḍā*, *ḍyā*, *yāC*, and *āL*.
7.01.040: *am* is substituted for *aḥ* before *maṅ*.
7.01.041: There is elision (*lopa*) of *taḥ* in the *ātmanepada* [terminations]. 7.01.042: *dhvāt* is substituted for *dhvam-aḥ*.

7.01.043 And [the suffix *śas* is applied] after the verb *yaj*, with the form *yaja-dhvam*. 7.01.044 For that [suffix], the substitute *tāt* is applied. 7.01.045 And [the substitutes] *taP*, *tanap*, *tan*, *thaN*, and *ā* [are applied].
7.01.046 The suffix *mas* has the augment *iT* at its end.
7.01.047 The suffix *yaK* is applied after [the verbal root] *kṛtvaḥ*.
7.01.048 And [the suffixes] *iṣṭhā*, *īyasun*, and *imanic* [are applied].

7.01.049 The suffix *iṣṇu* is applied after [roots] beginning with *snā*. 7.01.050 The augment *asuK* is applied after the root *ās* when followed by the suffix *jasi*. 7.01.051 The suffix *KyaC* is applied after the words *aśva*, *kṣīra*, *vṛṣa*, and *lavaṇa* when expressing one's own pleasure (*ātmaprītau*).
7.01.052 *suṬ* is added after a pronoun ending in *ām*.
7.01.053 *trayaḥ* is substituted for *treḥ*.
7.01.054 *nuṬ* is added after a short vowel, a feminine noun ending in *nadī*, or the feminine suffix *āP*.
7.01.055 [The substitution of *u* for *o* occurs] after [the words ending in] *ṣaṣ* and *catur*.
7.01.056 [The substitution of *u* for *o* occurs] after the words *śrī*, *grāmaṇī*, and *chandasi* (in the Vedic language).
7.01.057 [The substitution of *u* for *o* occurs] for the word *go* at the end of a metrical foot (*pāda*).
7.01.058 The augment *nuṭ* is added to a verbal root ending in *iṭ*.
7.01.059 The augment *nuṭ* is added after the roots *muc-* and others before the suffix *śa*.
7.01.060 The augment *nuṭ* is added after the roots *masj-* and *naś-* before a consonant (*jhaL*).

7.01.061: [The substitution of] *radh* for *jabh* occurs before an *aC* vowel. 7.01.062: The substitution of *radh* for *jabh* does not occur before the augment *iṭ*, except in the *liṭ* tense. 7.01.063: The substitution of *rabh* for *jabh* occurs except before the suffix *śap* and in the *liṭ* tense.

7.01.064 [The suffix *iC* is applied after the root *labh* when followed by the prefix *āṅ*. 7.01.065 [The suffix *iC* is applied after the root *labh* when preceded by *āṅ* and followed by the letter *y*.
7.01.066 [The suffix *iC* is applied after the root *labh* when preceded by *upa* in the sense of praise.]

7.01.067 [The substitution of *ī* for the vowel of a verbal root] occurs after a prefix (*upasarga*) before the suffixes *KHaL* and *GHaÑ*. 7.01.068 This substitution does not occur when the prefixes *su-* or *dur-* stand alone (without another prefix).
7.01.069 In the case of the suffixes *CiṆ* and *Ṇamul*, the substitution is optional.
7.01.070: For [stems ending in] uK, IT, and ā, [the substitution of Guna occurs] in the place of a nominal suffix (sarvanāmasthāna), provided it is not a verbal root.
7.01.071: [The substitution of Guna occurs] for the root *yuj* when it is not in a compound.
7.01.072: [The substitution of Guna occurs] for neuter [stems] ending in a consonant (jhaL) or a vowel (aC) [in the place of a nominal suffix].
7.01.073 Before a case-ending beginning with a vowel, [the final *i* or *u*] of a word ending in *ik* is replaced by *a*.
7.01.074 In the third case-ending and those following, a neuter word that has the masculine form expressed [in its stem] behaves like the masculine, except for its accent.
7.01.075 For the words *asthi*, *dadhi*, *sakthi*, and *akṣi*, the substitute *anaṅ* is applied [before a case-ending beginning with a vowel], and it is acute-accented.
7.01.076 This [substitution] is also seen in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
7.01.077 And the substitution of *ī* occurs in the dual number.
7.01.078 [The substitution of *ī* does not occur] after a reduplicated stem (*abhyasta*) followed by the suffix *śatṛ*.
7.01.079 Or [the augment *nuṭ* is inserted after a stem ending in a vowel] before a neuter [case-ending].
7.01.080 The augment *num* is inserted after [a stem ending in a vowel] before the feminine suffixes *āP* and *Śī*, and before a *nadi* [vowel].
7.01.081 The augment *num* is always inserted before the affixes *ŚaP* and *ŚyaN*.
7.01.082 The substitution of *s-au* occurs for *anaḍuh*.
7.01.083 In Vedic literature, the substitution of *s-au* occurs for *dṛś*, *svavas*, and *svatavas*.
7.01.084 The substitution of *auT* occurs for *div*.
7.01.085 The forms *pathin*, *mathin*, and *ṛbhukṣan* [take the augment *āt*].

7.01.086 In the case of [stems ending in] *it*, [the final vowel is replaced by] *at* in the strong cases (*sarvanāmasthāna*). 7.01.087 [The *th* of the suffixes *jas* and *śas* is replaced by] *nth*.
7.01.088 There is elision of the suffix *ṭi* after [the word ending in] *bha*. 7.01.089 The suffix *asuṅ* is applied after the word *puṃs*. 7.01.090 The suffix *ṇit* is applied after the word *go*.
7.01.091 The suffix *ṆaL* is optionally [the substitute] for the first person singular (*uttama*).
7.01.092 [The substitution of] *sakhī* occurs for *sakhi* except in the vocative case.
7.01.093 *anaṄ* is the substitute [for the final phoneme] before the ending *s-au*.
7.01.094 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after *ṛt*, *uśanas*, *puru-daṃśas*, and words ending in *anehas*.
7.01.095 [The suffix *kan* is applied] after *kroṣṭu* as if it were [a word ending in] *tṛc*.
7.01.096 [The suffix *kan* is applied after *kroṣṭu*] also in the feminine.

7.01.097. Optionally [the substitution of *ām* occurs] before case endings beginning with the third case-ending (*tṛtīyā*) when followed by a vowel (*aC*). 7.01.098. For the words *catur* and *anaḍuh*, the substitution of *ām* is acute-accented (*udātta*). 7.01.099.
The substitution of *am* occurs in the vocative singular (*saṃbuddhau*).
