7.01.100: *i* is substituted for the final *ṛ* of a verbal root (*dhātu*). 7.01.101: *i* is also substituted for a penultimate (*upadhā*) *ṛ*. 7.01.102: *u* is substituted for a penultimate *ṛ* that is preceded by a labial (*oṣṭhya*).
7.01.103: In the Vedic language, [the substitution of a long vowel] occurs diversely.
7.02.001: Before the *siC* suffix, when followed by *parasmaipada* endings, there is *vṛddhi* [substitution] for the final vowel of the root.
7.02.002: [The same applies] to a root ending in *r* or *l*, provided that it ends in a short vowel (*aT*).

7.02.003: [The substitution of *ū* for *o* occurs] after the roots *vad*, *vraj*, and those ending in a consonant (*haL*), when followed by a vowel (*aC*) [beginning with an affix]. 7.02.004: This does not occur when the augment *iṬ* follows.

7.02.005: [The substitution of *ū* for *o* occurs] after roots ending in *h*, *m*, or *y*, as well as after *kṣaṇ*, *śvas*, *jāgṛ*, the root *Ṇi*, and roots having *eT* or *iT* as their indicatory letters (*IT*).
7.02.006 The substitution [of *u* for *o*] after the root *ūrṇu* is optional.
7.02.007 [The substitution of *u* for *o* occurs] after a light vowel beginning with a consonant that ends in a short *a*.
7.02.008 The augment *iṭ* is not applied before a *kṛt* suffix beginning with *vaś*.

7.02.009: [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] before the suffixes *ti*, *tu*, *tra*, *ta*, *tha*, *si*, *su*, a vowel (*sara*), *ka*, and *se*. 7.02.010: [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] for a single vowel (*aC*) that is not acute (*anudātta*) in its original enunciation (*upadeśe*). 7.02.011: [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] for the root *śri* when followed by a *k-it* suffix.
7.02.012 The augment iṭ is not applied after the roots *grah* and *guh* when followed by the suffix *saN*.
7.02.013 The augment iṭ is not applied after the roots *kṛ*, *sṛ*, *bhṛ*, *vṛ*, *stu*, *dru*, *sru*, and *śru* when followed by the suffix *liṬ*.
7.02.014 The augment iṭ is not applied after the root *śvi* or after a root ending in a short vowel (*īT*) or the letter *I* (denoted as *IT*) when followed by the suffix *niṣṭhā*.
7.02.015 For that [root] for which there is an option;

7.02.016 And also for those [roots] whose initial vowel is long (āT) or which have an indicatory letter i (IT); 7.02.017 There is an option regarding the formation of the abstract action (bhāva), and so forth, and the object (karman).

7.02.018 The words *kṣubdha*, *svānta*, *dhvānta*, *lagna*, *mliṣṭa*, *viribdha*, *phāṇṭa*, and *bāḍha* are used respectively in the senses of churning, mind, darkness, clinging, indistinct speech, sound, unstrained decoction, and intense.
7.02.019 The words *dhṛṣita* and *śasta* are used in the sense of fearlessness (*vaiyāt-ya*).
7.02.020 The word *dṛḍha* is used in the senses of thick (*sthūla*) and strong (*bala*).

7.02.021 *parivṛḍhaḥ* [is formed] with *pra* and *bhu*. 7.02.022 *kaṣaḥ* [takes *ṇamul*] in the sense of difficulty (*kṛcchra*) and entering a thicket (*gahana*). 7.02.023 *ghuṣ* [takes *ṇamul*] except when it means making a sound (*aviśabdane*).
7.02.024 The suffix *ardha* is added after the prefixes *sam*, *ni*, and *vi*.
7.02.025 It is also added after *abhi* when not meaning "nearby" (*avidūrya*).
7.02.026 The suffix *ṇa* (forming *vṛtta*) is added after a root ending in *ṇi* when it means "studied."
7.02.027 The suffixes *kta* (having the markers *dā*, *śā*, *pūrṇa*, *das*, *spaṣṭa*, *channa*, *jña*, and *ptā*) [are used in the sense of the past tense].
7.02.028 [The same applies] after the roots *ruṣ*, *am*, *tvar*, *saṃghuṣ*, and *āsvan*.
7.02.029 After the root *hṛṣ*, [the suffix *kta* is used] in the sense of "hair" (*loman*).
7.02.030 And [the word] *apacita*.
7.02.031 [The substitution of] *hru* for *hvare* occurs in the Veda.
7.02.032 And [the word] *aparihvr̥ta*.
7.02.033 After [the verbal roots] *som*, *hvṛ*, and *ita*.

7.02.034 Also after *grasita*, *skabhita*, *stabhitā*, *uttabhita*, *catta*, *vikasta*, *viśastṛ*, *śaṃstṛ*, *śāstṛ*, *tarutṛ*, *tarūtṛ*, *varutṛ*, *varūtṛ*, *varutrī*, and after [roots ending in] *ujjvaliti*, *kṣariti*, *kṣamiti*, *vamiti*, and *amiti*.
7.02.035 The augment *iṭ* is added to an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*vaL*).

7.02.036: The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of the roots *snu* and *kram* occurs when they are followed by an affix that causes the *ātmanepada* endings, provided it is not the *niṣṭhā* affix.

7.02.037: In the case of the root *grah*, a long vowel is substituted [for the penultimate short vowel] before an affix beginning with a consonant other than *y*, provided it is not the *liṭ* (perfect) tense.
7.02.038: In the case of the root *vṛ* and those ending in *ṝ*, the substitution of a long vowel is optional under the same conditions as 7.02.037.
7.02.039 Not before the suffix *liṅ*. 7.02.040 Nor before *sic* when followed by parasmaipada endings.
7.02.041 The augment *iṭ* is optionally applied before *saṇ*.
7.02.042: [The substitution of] *iṭ* occurs before the *liṅ* and *sic* suffixes when they belong to the *ātmanepada*.
7.02.043: [The substitution of *iṭ* occurs] also after a root ending in *ṛ*, provided that the root begins with a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*).
7.02.044: [The substitution of *iṭ*] is optional after roots containing the vowel *svarati*, *sūti*, *sūyati*, *dhūñ*, or a root having *ū* as its *it*.
7.02.045 [The augment *iṭ* is applied] after the roots beginning with *radh*.
7.02.046 [The augment *iṭ* is applied] after the root *kuṣ* when preceded by the prefix *niḥ*.
7.02.047 [The augment *iṭ* is applied] before the *niṣṭhā* suffixes (*kta* and *ktavatu*).
7.02.048 [The substitution of *iK* for the final vowel of a root occurs] before the suffixes *saN*, *iṣ*, *saha*, *lubh*, *ruṣ*, *riṣ*, and *aC*.

7.02.049 [The substitution of *iK* for the final vowel of a root occurs] before the suffix *saN* when the roots end in *iK*, or contain *ṛ*, or are *ṛdh*, *bhrasj*, *danbH*, *śri*, *svṛ*, *yu*, *ūrṇu*, *bhara*, *jñapi*, *san*, or *ām*.
7.02.050 [The substitution of *iK* for the final vowel of the root] *kliś* occurs before the suffixes *Ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*.
7.02.051 After the root *pūṅ*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied [before the third-person singular ending *ta*].
7.02.052 The augment *iṭ* is applied after the roots *vas* and *kṣudh* [before the third-person singular ending *ta*].
7.02.053 The augment *iṭ* is applied after the root *añc* when it signifies worship (*pūjā*).
7.02.054 The suffix *Kta* is optionally added after the root *lubh* when it means "to release.
7.02.055 The suffix *Ktvā* is added after the roots *jṛ* and *vraśc*.
7.02.056 When the root ends in a vowel (*uT*) or the letter *i*, the suffix *Ktvā* is optionally added.
7.02.057 The augment *iṭ* is applied after the roots *kṛt*, *cṛt*, *chṛd*, *tṛd*, and *nṛt* when followed by an affix beginning with *a* that does not have the marker *siC*.
7.02.058 The augment *iṭ* is applied after the root *gam* when followed by an affix beginning with *a* that has the marker *parasmaipada*.
7.02.059 The augment *iṭ* is not applied after the four roots beginning with *vṛt* when followed by an affix beginning with *a* that has the marker *parasmaipada*.
7.02.060 And [the substitution of] those *kḷp* suffixes [is like that of the Aorist].
7.02.061 When *thaL* follows, the [substitution] of the non-*iṭ* [Aorist] suffix is always like that of the [Aorist] suffix following a vowel (*aC*).
7.02.062 In the original grammatical instruction (*upa-deśa*), [the substitution] is like that of a short vowel (*aT*).

7.02.063 According to Bhāradvāja, [the substitution of *ṛ* for the root vowel occurs] after roots ending in *ṛ*. 7.02.064 In the Vedic usage (*nigama*), the forms *babhūtha*, *ātata*, *tatantha*, *jagrbhma*, *vavarta*, and *vavṛdhe* [are found]. 7.02.065 Optionally, [the substitution of *ṛ* for the root vowel occurs] after the roots *sṛj* and *dṛś*.
7.02.066 The suffix *iṭ* is added after [roots ending in] *at*, *ti*, *ar*, *vyaya*, and those ending in *n*.
7.02.067 The suffix *vasu* is added after [roots ending in] *ekāc*, *āT*, and *ghas*.
7.02.068 The suffix *vasu* is optionally added after the roots *gam*, *han*, *vid*, and *viś*.
7.02.069 The augment *iṭ* is added after the roots *san*, *sa*, and *san*, when followed by the suffixes *vāṃs* and *am*.
7.02.070 The augment *iṭ* is added after the roots ending in long *ṝ* and the root *han*, when followed by the suffix *sy*.
7.02.071 The augment *iṭ* is added after the root *añj*, when followed by the suffix *siC*.
7.02.072: After the roots *stu*, *su*, and *dhūñ*, the augment *iṭ* is added before the *parasmaipada* suffixes.
7.02.073: After the roots *yam*, *ram*, *nam*, and those ending in long *ā*, the augment *saK* is added [before the *parasmaipada* suffixes].
7.02.074: The augment *saN* is applied after the roots *smi*, *pūñ*, *ṛ*, *añjū*, and *aś*.
7.02.075 Also after the five roots ending in *kir*.
7.02.076 [The augment *iṭ* is added] after the roots beginning with *rud* before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix.
7.02.077 [The augment *iṭ* is added] after the root *īś* before the suffix *si*.

7.02.078 The substitution of *ī* occurs for the final vowel of the roots *īḍ* and *jan* before the suffix *dhve*. 7.02.079 The *s* of the *liṅ* (optative) suffix is elided when it is not the penultimate letter.
7.02.080 The substitution of *yā* for *i* occurs after a short vowel (*aT*) before the *liṅ* suffix.
7.02.081 After [a verbal root ending in] long Ā (āT), when followed by an affix marked with the indicatory letter Ṅ or Ṭ, [the augment iṭ is inserted].
7.02.082 Before the case-ending āN, [the augment] muK is inserted [after a verbal root ending in long Ā].
7.02.083 [The augment iṭ is inserted] after the verbal root ās (to sit) when it ends in short ī (īT).
7.02.084: *aṣṭan-* [takes *nūṭ*] before a case-ending (*vibhakti*).
7.02.085: [The substitution of *ai* for the final vowel of] *rāyaḥ* [occurs] before a consonant (*hal*).
7.02.086: [The substitution of *au* for the final vowel of] *yuṣmad-* and *asmad-* [occurs] when there is no substitute (*an-ādeśe*).
7.02.087 [The substitution of *au* occurs] for the second case-ending (*dvitīyā*) as well.
7.02.088 [The substitution of *au* occurs] for the first case-ending (*prathamā*) in the dual number in the spoken language (*bhāṣā*).
7.02.089 [The substitution of *au* occurs] for the vowel *ya* when followed by a vowel (*aC*).

7.02.090 There is elision of the remainder [of the suffix]. 7.02.091 [The elision applies] to that which ends in *m*. 7.02.092 In the dual number, *yu* and *au* are substituted for [the dual endings of the nominative and accusative].
7.02.093 *yu* and *vay* are substituted for *yūyam* before the case-ending *Jas*.
7.02.094 *tv* and *ah* are substituted for *tvam* before the case-endings *Su* and *Au*.
7.02.095 *tubhyam* and *mahyam* are substituted for *tvā* and *mā* before the case-ending *Ṅi*.

7.02.096: *tavad* and *mavad* are substituted for *tvad* and *mad* respectively before the [genitive] case-ending *ṅasi*. 7.02.097: *tvam* and *aham* are substituted for *tvad* and *mad* respectively in the singular number. 7.02.098: [The substitution of *tvam* and *aham* occurs] also before a suffix and a subsequent word (*uttarapada*).
7.02.099 For *tri* and *catur*, when used in the feminine, [the substitutes] *tisṛ* and *catasṛ* [are applied].
7.02.100 Before a vowel (*aC*), *ra* is substituted for the final *ṛT*.
7.02.101 For *jarā*, *jaras* is optionally substituted.

7.02.102 For *tyad* and the other [demonstrative pronouns], *a* [is substituted for the final vowel and consonant]. 7.02.103 For *kim*, *ka* [is substituted]. 7.02.104 Before *ti* and *ha*, *ku* [is substituted for *kim*].

7.02.105: [The substitution of *e* occurs] for the vowel *a* when followed by a non-*at* sound. 7.02.106: For the final sounds of *tad* and *doṣ*, the substitution of *sa-* occurs before the dual endings *au* and *s-au*.
7.02.107: For the word *adas*, the substitution of *au* occurs, and there is also the elision (*lopa*) of the nominative singular ending *su*.
7.02.108 For *idam*, [the substitute] *ma* [is applied].
7.02.109 And for *adasa*, [the substitute *ma* is applied].
7.02.110 For *ya*, [the substitutes] *sau* [are applied].
7.02.111. *id* becomes *ay* before a masculine [suffix].
7.02.112. *an* becomes *ak* when followed by a suffix beginning with *āP*.
7.02.113. There is elision (*lopa*) of the final consonant (*haL*) [of the stem] before a [suffix beginning with] *haL*.
7.02.114 There is *vṛddhi* for the root *mṛj*.
7.02.115 [There is *vṛddhi*] for a vowel other than *aC* (i.e., for *a*) before an affix marked with *Ñ* or *Ṇ* that has an *iT* augment.
7.02.116 [There is *vṛddhi*] for the penultimate (*upadhā*) vowel *aT* (i.e., *a*).

7.02.117: In the context of *taddhita* suffixes, [the long vowel] replaces the first vowel among the vowels [of the base]. 7.02.118: [The long vowel replaces the first vowel] also before a suffix marked with *K* or *IT*.
7.03.001: The augment *āT* is added after [the final vowel of] *devikā*, *śiṃśapā*, *aditya*, *vāh*, *dīrghasattra*, and *śreyas*.
7.03.002 For the words *kekaya*, *mitrayu*, and those ending in *pralaya*, the vowel *i* is substituted for the initial *ya*.
7.03.003 Not so when [the suffix] follows a word ending in *y* or *v*; however, in such cases, *aiC* (the vowels *ai*, *au*, or *e*) is substituted for both of those [suffixes].
7.03.004 And this also applies to the words beginning with *dvāra*.
7.03.005 And [the suffix *ka* is applied] after the word *nyagrodha* when it stands alone;
7.03.006 not when there is a mutual exchange of actions;
7.03.007 and also after words such as *svāgata*.
7.03.008 [The substitution of *śvan* for *śvan* occurs] before a suffix beginning with *iṅ*.

7.03.009 [The substitution of *śvan* for *śvan* occurs] optionally when it is at the end of a word (*padānta*). 7.03.010 [The substitution of *śvan* for *śvan* occurs] when it is the final member of a compound (*uttarapada*).
7.03.011 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word ending in *ava-yava*, provided it ends in *ṛtu*.
7.03.012 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word denoting a *janapada* (region) that begins with *su*, *sarva*, or *ardha*.
7.03.013 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word denoting a direction (*diś*), except for those beginning with *madra*.

7.03.014 [The elision of the case-ending] occurs after words denoting eastern villages and cities. 7.03.015 [The elision of the case-ending] occurs after a numeral and after a word denoting a number of years (*saṃvatsara*).
7.03.016 [The elision of the case-ending] occurs after the word *varṣa* when it refers to the future.
7.03.017 The [final vowel] of a word ending in a measure [term], except for *saṃjñā* and *śāṇa*, [is replaced by the long vowel].
7.03.018 In the case of the word *proṣṭhapadāḥ*, [the final vowel is replaced by the long vowel] before the suffix *j*.
7.03.019 When the words *hṛd*, *bhaga*, or *sindhu* occur at the end [of a compound], the first member [also takes the long vowel substitute] as well.

7.03.020 And [the final vowel] of *anuśatika* and similar compounds [is lengthened]. 7.03.021 And [the final vowel] of the first member in a copulative compound (*dvandva*) of deities [is lengthened].
7.03.022 But not [is the final vowel lengthened] of *indra* when it follows another [deity].
7.03.023 Also after a long vowel, [the final *s* of] *varuṇa* [is changed to *ṇ*].
7.03.024 According to the Eastern grammarians, [the final *s* of *varuṇa* is changed to *ṇ*] when it occurs at the end of a city name.
7.03.025 For a word ending in *jaragala*, *dhenu*, *vala*, or *ja*, the subsequent [vowel sandhi rule] is optional.

7.03.026: When the first member of a compound denoting a measure ends in *ardha*, the substitution [of *vṛddhi*] optionally takes place. 7.03.027: This does not occur when the subsequent member begins with a vowel (*aT*).
7.03.028: In the case of *pravāhaṇa*, the substitution [of *vṛddhi*] occurs before the suffix *ḍha*.
7.03.029 And [the substitution of *na* for *nañ* occurs] before a word ending in the suffix *-pratyaya*.
7.03.030 [The substitution of *na* for *nañ* occurs] before the words *śuci*, *īśvara*, *kṣetrajña*, *kuśala*, and *nipuṇa*.
7.03.031 [The substitution of *na* for *nañ* occurs] before *yathātatha* and *yathāpura* when used in the sense of "alternately" (*paryāye*).
7.03.032: After the root *han*, [the substitution of] *ta* occurs in place of *Ciṇ* and *ṆaL*.
7.03.033: The augment *yuK* is added after a long vowel (*āT*) before *Ciṇ* and a *kṛt* suffix.
7.03.034: The augment *naT* is not applied to a root taught with an udātta accent that ends in *m*, except for the root *ām*.
7.03.035 The augment *nuṭ* is added after the roots *jan* and *vadh*.
7.03.036 The augment *puK* is added before the suffixes *aṅ* and *ṇi* after the roots *ṛ*, *hrī*, *vlī*, *rī*, *knūyī*, *ksmāyī*, and those ending in long *ā*.
7.03.037 The augment *yuK* is added before the suffix *aṅ* after the roots *śā*, *chā*, *sā*, *hvā*, *vyā*, *ve*, and *pā*.
7.03.038: After the verbal roots *vā* and *vah*, the augment *juK* is added when the sense is "shaking off.

7.03.039: After the roots *lī* and *līṅ*, the augments *nuK* and *luK* respectively are added when the suffixes *nya* and *ara* follow, provided the meaning is the falling away of oiliness (adhesion).
7.03.040: After the root *bhī*, the augment *ṣuK* is added when the cause of fear is expressed.
7.03.041 For the root *sphāy*, [the suffix] *va* [is substituted for *na*].
7.03.042 For the root *śad*, when not meaning "to go," *ta* [is substituted for *na*].
7.03.043 For the root *ruh*, *pa* [is optionally substituted for *na*].

7.03.044: After a *k* that occurs before an affix beginning with a vowel, the substitution of *iT* takes the place of the preceding *t*, provided that the following vowel is not a case-ending (*asup*). 7.03.045: This substitution does not take place after the roots *yā* and *sā*.
7.03.046: According to the Northern Grammarians (*udīcām*), the substitution of *āT* takes the place of the final vowel of a feminine stem ending in *ā*, provided it is preceded by *yak*.
7.03.047 The feminine suffix *āP* is applied after the words *bhastrā*, *eṣā*, *ajā*, *jñā*, *dvā*, *svā*, as well as after [stems ending in] *naÑ*, *ūR*, and *ṇ*.
7.03.048 And [the feminine suffix *āP* is applied] after a word that does not express the masculine gender [but whose corresponding masculine form exists].
7.03.049 According to the teachers, [the feminine suffix *āP* is applied] after a word ending in long *Ā*.

7.03.050: *ika* is substituted for *ṭha*. 7.03.051: The suffix *ka* is applied after a word ending in *is*, *us*, or *uK*. 7.03.052: A *kU* substitute is applied in place of *ca* and *ja* before a *GHIT* affix or the suffix *ṆyaT*.
7.03.053 And [the substitution of *iK* for the final vowel] occurs in place of the penultimate vowel of roots beginning with *ny-ṛc*.
7.03.054 In place of the *ha* of the root *han*, [the substitution of *jhaL* occurs] before suffixes marked with the indicatory letters *Ñ* or *Ṇ* that have an *IT* augment, as well as before *ne*.
7.03.055 And [the substitution of *jhaL* occurs] in place of the penultimate vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) before those same suffixes.
7.03.056: After the root *hrī*, [the substitution of] *aC* occurs before the suffixes *Caṅ* and [others].
7.03.057: Before the suffixes *saN* and *liṭ*, [the substitution of] *je* occurs [after the root *hrī*]. 7.03.058: Before the suffix *ciṇ*, [the substitution of *je* after *hrī*] is optional.
7.03.059 Not for [a root] beginning with *kū*. 7.03.060 And not for *aj* and *vṛj*.
7.03.061 *Bhuj* and *ubj* [are used] in the senses of "hand" and "afflicting," respectively.
7.03.062 The words *prayāja* and *anuyāja* [are derived from the root *yaj*] in the sense of a sacrifice. 7.03.063 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the root *vañc*] in the sense of "going.
7.03.064 [The suffix *ka* is applied after the roots *vas* and *uc*] in the sense of "home" (*okaḥ*).
7.03.065: [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel of the root] occurs before an affix beginning with *ṇ*, when necessity (*āvaśyaka*) is expressed.
7.03.066: [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel of the root] occurs before an affix beginning with *ṇ* after the roots *yaj*, *yāc*, *ruc*, *pravac*, and *ṛc*.

7.03.067: [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel of the root] occurs before an affix beginning with *ṇ* after the root *vac*, provided it does not form a technical grammatical term (*śabdasaṃjñā*).
7.03.068 The suffixes *niyojya* and *prayojya* are used in the sense of "capable" (*śakyārthe*).
7.03.069 The suffix *bhojya* is used in the sense of "that which is to be eaten" (*bhakṣye*).
7.03.070 There is optionally the elision (*lopa*) of the *ghu*-class roots before the *leṭ* suffix.
7.03.071: The substitution of *o* for the final vowel of a root ending in *a* occurs before the suffix *ŚyaN*.
7.03.072: The substitution of *aC* (any vowel) for the final vowel of a root ending in *KS* occurs before a suffix beginning with a vowel.

7.03.073: The suffix *luK* (elision) optionally applies to the roots *duH*, *diH*, *liH*, and *guh* when followed by an affix marked with *eT* that begins with a dental consonant, provided the action is reflexive (*ātmanepada*).
7.03.074 The long vowel is substituted for the final vowel of the roots *śam* and the eight roots beginning with *ām* before the affix *Śyan*.
7.03.075 The long vowel is substituted for the final vowel of the roots *ṣṭhiv*, *klam*, and *cam* before an affix marked with the mute letter *Ś*.
7.03.076 The long vowel is substituted for the final vowel of the root *kram* before Parasmaipada affixes.
7.03.077 For the roots *iṣ*, *gam*, and *yam*, *cha* is substituted [for the suffix *ap*].

7.03.078 For the roots *pā*, *ghrā*, *dhmā*, *sthā*, *mnā*, *dāṇ*, *dṛśi*, *ṛ*, *sṛ*, *śad*, and *sad*, the forms *piba*, *jighra*, *dhama*, *tiṣṭha*, *mana*, *yaccha*, *paśya*, *ṛccha*, *dhau*, *śīya*, and *sīda* are substituted [respectively for the root-final consonant and the following *ap*].
7.03.079 For the roots *jñā* and *jan*, *jā* is substituted [for the root-final consonant and the following *ap*].

7.03.080 The short vowel is substituted for the roots beginning with *pū*. 7.03.081 In the *Nigama*, the short vowel is substituted for the root *mī* when it ends in *nā*. 7.03.082 Guṇa is substituted for the root *mid*.
7.03.083 *jus* is substituted for *caṅ*.
7.03.084 [The substitution of *jus* applies] to all verbal suffixes (*sārvadhātuka*) and to those beginning with a vowel that are not marked with *ṅ* (i.e., *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes).
7.03.085 [The substitution of *jus* for *śnā* occurs] after the root *jāgṛ*, except when followed by the suffix *viCiṇ*, *ṆaL*, or a suffix marked with *Ṅ* or *IT*.

7.03.086 And [guṇa is substituted] for a root ending in *pu* or having a light penultimate vowel. 7.03.087 [Guṇa is not substituted] for a reduplicated root before a sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a vowel that has *P* as its *it*. 7.03.088 [Guṇa is not substituted] for the roots *bhū* and *su* before a *tiṅ* affix.
7.03.089 Vṛddhi is substituted for *u* and *ū* before a consonant when a suffix beginning with a consonant and marked with *luK* follows.
7.03.090 For the root *ūrṇu*, vṛddhi is optionally substituted under the same conditions.
7.03.091 Guṇa is substituted [for the penultimate vowel] before a suffix consisting of a single phoneme (*apṛkta*).
7.03.092 After the root *tṛh*, the suffix *iṭ* is inserted before the third person singular ending *aṭ*.
7.03.093 After the root *brū*, the suffix *īṭ* is inserted before the third person singular ending *aṭ*.
7.03.094 After a reduplicated stem (*yaṅ*), the suffix *īṭ* is optionally inserted before the third person singular ending *aṭ*.

7.03.095: The augment *iṭ* is applied after the roots *tu*, *ru*, *stu*, and *śam*, before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix that begins with a vowel. 7.03.096: The augment *iṭ* is applied after the root *as* and after a *siC* affix, before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix that consists of a single phoneme (*apṛkta*). 7.03.097: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this [application of the augment] occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
7.03.098. And [the augment *aṭ* is added] after the root *rud-* and after the five [roots beginning with *bru*].
7.03.099. According to Gārgya and Gālava, the augment *aṭ* is added [after the root *bru*] in all cases.
7.03.100. According to all [grammarians], the augment *aṭ* is added after the root *ad*.

7.03.101 A long vowel is substituted for a short *a* before the suffix *yañ*. 7.03.102 [A long vowel is substituted for a short *a*] also before case-endings (*sup*). 7.03.103 [A long vowel is substituted for a short *e*] before a consonant-initial plural ending (*jhal*).
7.03.104 And [the substitution of *ś* for *s* occurs] before the suffix *osi*.
7.03.105 And [the substitution of *ś* for *s* occurs] before the suffix *āṅ* (i.e., *ām*), provided it is not the feminine suffix *āP*.
7.03.106 And [the substitution of *ś* for *s* occurs] in the vocative singular (*saṃbuddhi*).
7.03.107 Before [the suffixes] *ambā*, *artha*, and *nadī*, [the final vowel of the preceding word] becomes short.
7.03.108 A short vowel is replaced by its corresponding *guṇa* [vowel]. 7.03.109 And also before the case-ending *Jas*.
7.03.110: After a stem ending in /ṛ/, [the substitution of] /ā/ occurs before the case endings *ṅi* and the *sarvanāmasthāna* endings.
7.03.111: After a stem ending in the suffix *gha*, [the substitution of] /ā/ occurs before an ending marked with the *ṅit* designation.
7.03.112: After a feminine stem ending in *nadī*, [the substitution of] *āṬ* occurs before an ending marked with the *ṅit* designation.
7.03.113 The suffix *yāṬ* is applied after a feminine stem ending in *āP*.
7.03.114 After a pronominal (*sarvanāman*) ending in *āP*, the suffix *syāṬ* is applied, and the short vowel *a* is substituted for the final vowel.
7.03.115 The application of these two suffixes is optional when the second or third case endings follow.
7.03.116 After [stems ending in] *nadī*, *āP*, and *nī*, the suffix *ṅe* is replaced by *ām*.
7.03.117 After [stems ending in] vowels other than *i* (*iT*) and *u* (*uT*), [the suffix *ṅasi* is replaced by *āt*]. 7.03.118 After [stems ending in] *auT*, [the suffix *ṅasi* is replaced by *āt*].

7.03.119: After a word ending in *at*, the suffix *GHe* becomes *aT*. 7.03.120: After a word ending in *āṅ*, the suffix *nā* is substituted, except in the feminine gender. 7.04.001: Before the suffix *ṆaU* and before *CaṄ*, the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) is shortened.
7.04.002: [The elision of] the penultimate vowel does not occur for a stem ending in *aC* that has lost its final element (*alopin*), nor for the roots *śās*, nor for those having *ṛT* as an *it*.
7.04.003: [The elision of the penultimate vowel does not occur] for the roots *bhrāj*, *bhās*, *bhāṣ*, *dīp*, *jīv*, *mīl*, and *pīḍ*, except when followed by a suffix beginning with *a* or *ra*.
7.04.004: There is elision [of the penultimate vowel] of the root *pibati*, and there is also elision of the *īT* of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).
7.04.005 The substitute *i* is applied to the root *sthā*.
7.04.006 The substitute *i* is optionally applied to the root *ghrā*.
7.04.007 The substitute *u* is applied to the vowel *ṛ* [of the roots *stambh*, *skambh*, *skumbh*, and *klambh*].
7.04.008 The suffix *chandas* is always [used].
7.04.009 The substitution of *digi* occurs for the root *day* when the *liṭ* suffix follows.
7.04.010 Guṇa is substituted for the vowel of a root ending in *ṛ*, provided it begins with a conjunct consonant.
7.04.011 [The substitution of *ṛ* occurs] for the vowel *ṛ* and for those [roots] ending in *ṝ* in the case of the suffix *ṛcch*.
7.04.012 For the roots *śṝ*, *dṝ*, and *pṝ*, a short vowel is optionally substituted [before the same suffix].
7.04.013 [The substitution of *ṛ* occurs] for a non-*aṇ* vowel before the suffix *ka*.
7.04.014 There is no substitution [of *guṇa*] before the suffix *kaP*.
7.04.015 Before the suffix *āP*, [the substitution of *guṇa* for the final vowel of the root] may optionally take place.
7.04.016 Before the suffix *aṄ*, there is the substitution of *guṇa* for the vowels *ṛ* and *ṝ* (as well as *ṛt*).
7.04.017 The augment *sthuk* is added after the root *as*.
7.04.018 The vowel *a* is substituted for the final vowel of the root *śvi*.
7.04.019 The substitute *puṃ* is applied to the root *pat*.
7.04.020 The augment *uṃ* is added after the root *vac*.
7.04.021 Guṇa substitution occurs for the root *śīṅ* before an affix marked with *sārvadhātuka*.
7.04.022 The substitute *ayaṅ* is applied [to the root *śī*] before an affix beginning with *y* that is marked with *k* or *ṅit*.

7.04.023 A short vowel is substituted [for the root vowel] of the root *ūh* when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*). 7.04.024 [A long vowel is substituted for the root vowel of *ūh*] before the suffix *et*, when that suffix occurs in the *liṅ* mood. 7.04.025 A long vowel is substituted [for the root vowel] before both non-*kṛt* suffixes and *sārvadhātuka* suffixes.
7.04.026: *Cv-AU* [are substituted] for *ca*.
7.04.027: *rīṄ* [is substituted] for *ṛT* [at the end of a verbal root]. 7.04.028: *riṄ* [is substituted] for *ṛT* before *Ś*, *sa*, *yaK*, *LīṄ*, and *k*.

7.04.029 A *guṇa* substitute is applied for the roots √*ṛ* and those beginning with a consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*) or the letter *ā*, except when followed by the suffix *yaṅ*. 7.04.030 And [the same applies] when *yaṅ* follows.
7.04.031 An *īkārādeśa* is substituted for the roots √*ghrā* and √*dhmā*.
7.04.032 Before the affixes *Cv* and *au*, [the final vowel of the preceding element is lengthened].
7.04.033 Also before the affix *KhaC*.
7.04.034 The forms *aśanāyā*, *udanāyā*, and *dhanāyā* are used in the senses of hunger, thirst, and greed, respectively.
7.04.035 Not in the Vedic meters (chandas) for [the word] *aputra*.
7.04.036 The suffixes *yus* and *yu* are applied after *duras*, *draviṇas*, *vṛṣan*, and *ṛṣan*.
7.04.037 The vowel *āT* is substituted [for the final vowel of the preceding stem] when followed by *aśva* and *agha*.
7.04.038 In the *Yajus* of the *Kāṭhaka*, [the substitution of] *deva* and *sumna* [occurs].
7.04.039 In a *Ṛk* verse, there is elision (*lopa*) of the final vowel of *kavi*, *adhvara*, and *pṛtanā*.
7.04.040 The augment *iT* is applied before the suffix *ti* when it is marked with *K* after the roots *dyati*, *syati*, *mā*, and *sthā*.
7.04.041 The substitution of *śā* for the root *śo* (to sharpen) optionally occurs before the suffix *ch*.
7.04.042 The substitution of *hi* for the root *dhā* (to place) occurs before the suffix *ch*.
7.04.043 The substitution of *hi* also occurs for the root *jahāti* (to abandon) before the suffix *Ktvī*.
7.04.044 Optionally [the substitution of *āt* for *as* occurs] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
7.04.045 [The substitution of *āt* for *as* occurs] after the verbal roots *su*, *vas*, *nī*, *dhe*, *dhā*, and *sthā*, as well as in the case of *sīy-* (the optative suffix).
7.04.046 For the final vowel of a root belonging to the *ghu* class, the substitute *dad* is applied in place of *da*.
7.04.047: After a prefix ending in *a* or *ā*, the *t* of the root *at* [is replaced by *ī*].
7.04.048: After the root *ap*, [the *bh* of the suffix *bhi* is replaced by *i*].
7.04.049: After the root *as*, the *s* of the suffix *si* is replaced by *ī* when it is an *ārdhadhātuka*.
7.04.050 There is elision of the [feminine] suffixes *tā* and *as*. 7.04.051 Also before the vowel *r*. 7.04.052 And before the *eT* sounds (*e*, *o*, *ai*, *au*).
7.04.053: For the roots *dīdhī* and *vevī*, when followed by *i* or a vowel (*ivarṇa*), [the substitution of *yaṅ* for *ya* occurs].
7.04.054: In the presence of the *saN* affix, for the roots *mī*, *mā*, *ghu*, *rabh*, *labh*, *śak*, *pat*, and *pad*, the augment *is* is added after a vowel (*aC*).
7.04.055: For the roots *āp*, *jñap*, and *ṛdh*, the augment *īT* is added [before the *saN* affix].

7.04.056 After the root *dambh*, [the penultimate vowel] becomes *i* and [the final consonant] is replaced by *t*. 7.04.057 After the root *muc* when it is intransitive, [the penultimate vowel] optionally undergoes *guṇa* substitution. 7.04.058 In this context, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

7.04.059 A short vowel [is substituted for the final of a reduplicated stem]. 7.04.060 When a consonant begins [the reduplicated syllable], the remaining [consonants] are elided. 7.04.061 [The elision applies] to the *khay* sounds (velars and palatals) preceded by *śar* (sibilants and *h*).
7.04.062 After the verbal root *ku*, when followed by the suffix *ha*, the substitution of a palatal (*cu*) occurs.
7.04.063 The substitution [of a palatal] does not occur after the root *kav* when followed by the intensive suffix *yaṅ*.
7.04.064 In the Vedic language, [the substitution of a palatal] occurs after the root *kṛṣ* when followed by the suffix *ha*.

7.04.065 The forms *dāti*, *dharti*, *darati*, *dharati*, *darṣi*, *bobhūti*, *tuṣṭu*, *teṣṭu*, *alarti*, *arṣi*, *āpaṇī*, *phaṇat*, *saṃsani*, *ṣyadat*, *kariti*, *krat*, *kaniti*, *kradat*, *bhariti*, *bhrat*, *daviti*, *dhvat*, *davidyutat*, *tariti*, *trat*, *sarīsṛpat*, *amvarīvṛjat*, *marmṛjya*, and *aganīganti*—
these also [are treated as such].
7.04.066 An *u* followed by a non-*aT* vowel [is replaced by *ū*].
7.04.067 There is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the roots *dyut* and *svap*.
7.04.068 There is vocalization of the root *vyath* in the *liṭ* [perfect] tense.
7.04.069 There is lengthening of the vowel of a root ending in /i/ or /u/ before an affix marked with the *k*-sign that begins with /iṇ/.
7.04.070: [The augment] *āT* is substituted for the initial vowel of a verbal root beginning with *aT*.
7.04.071: After that [verbal root], the augment *nuṬ* is added if the root consists of two consonants (*dvi-hal*).
7.04.072: And [the augment *nuṬ* is added] after the root *aś* (to eat) and *an* (to breathe).
7.04.073 The *a* of the root *bhū* [is replaced by *guṇa*] before the suffix *Ślu*.
7.04.074 [The substitution of *guṇa* for the *a* of the root *sū* occurs] in the Vedic usage (*nigama*) as *sasūva*.
7.04.075 There is *guṇa* substitution for the three roots beginning with *nij* before the suffix *Ślu*.

7.04.076 *iṭ* is added after the roots beginning with *bhṛ*. 7.04.077 *iṭ* is also added after the roots *ṛ*, *pī*, and *pṝ*. 7.04.078 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this [addition of *iṭ*] occurs diversely (*bahulam*).
7.04.079: Before the suffix *saN*, [the final vowel] of a verbal root ending in short *a* is elided.
7.04.080: When followed by a *pU* sound, a *yaṆ* sound, or *j*, the *u* of the root *o* is substituted [for the preceding *a*].
7.04.081: For the roots *sravati*, *śṛṇoti*, *dravati*, *pravati*, *plavati*, and *cyavati*, this substitution is optional.
7.04.082 A *guṇa* substitute occurs for [the final vowel] before an affix marked with *yaṅ* or when *luK* elision has occurred.
7.04.083 A long vowel (*dīrgha*) is substituted [for the penultimate vowel] of a root ending in a consonant other than *k*, provided it does not have *iK* as an augment.
7.04.084 [The substitution of *nīK* occurs] for the roots *vancU*, *sraṃsU*, *dhvaṃsU*, *bhraṃśU*, *kas*, *pat*, *pad*, and *skand*.
7.04.085: The augment *nuK* is added after a verbal root ending in a nasal consonant that ends in *a*.
7.04.086: [The augment *nuK* is added] also after the roots *jap*, *jabh*, *dah*, *daś*, *bhañj*, *paś*, and *sā*.
7.04.087: [The augment *nuK* is added] also after the roots *car* and *phal*.
7.04.088: [The substitution of *u* occurs] for the *aṭ* (vowel) that follows *ut*.
7.04.089: [The substitution of *u* occurs] also for the *aṭ* that follows *ti*.
7.04.090: [The substitution of *rīk* occurs] for [the final vowel of a verbal root] ending in *ṛt*, as well as for [the penultimate vowel] when *ṛt* is the penultimate letter.

7.04.091: And [the substitution of] *ruK* and *riK* occurs when there is elision (*luK*). 7.04.092: Also after [a stem ending in] *ṛT*. 7.04.093: Like *saN*, [the substitution occurs] before a light vowel when followed by *CaṄ*, provided there is no elision of a vowel (*an-AC-lope*).

7.04.094 A long vowel is substituted for a short vowel [in the reduplication] of [the roots] *smṛ*, *ṝtvar*, *prath*, *mrad*, *stṝ*, and *spaś*. 7.04.095 [The substitution of a long vowel] is optional in the case of the roots *veṣṭ* and *ceṣṭ*.
7.04.097: *ī* is substituted for the final vowel of a *gaṇa*.
8.01.001: The word *sarva* becomes *dvi* when it is a reduplicated form (*āmreḍita*).
8.01.002: That which follows it is called the *āmreḍita*.
8.01.003 And [the *kṛt* affix *ktvā*] is also [optionally replaced by *lyap*] when it follows a word with an *anudātta* accent.
8.01.004 [The *kṛt* affix *ktvā* is optionally replaced by *lyap*] after a word expressing a constant state (*nitya*) or a distributive sense (*vīpsā*).
8.01.005 [The *kṛt* affix *ktvā* is optionally replaced by *lyap*] after the verb *pari*, when it signifies exclusion (*varjana*).
8.01.006 [The particle *pra*, *sam*, *upa*, or *ud*] is optionally treated as a pragṛhya when used for the purpose of filling out a metrical foot.
8.01.007 [The particles] *upari*, *adhi*, and *adhas* are optionally treated as pragṛhya when expressing proximity.
8.01.008 [A vocative] at the beginning of a sentence is optionally treated as a pragṛhya when expressing envy, consent, anger, reproach, or threatening.
8.01.009 [The word] *eka* [is treated] like a *bahuvrīhi*. 8.01.010 And also when there is an obstruction (*ābādha*). 8.01.011 In the subsequent [rules], it is treated like a *karmadhāraya*.
8.01.012: When a word expressing a quality (*guṇavacana*) is used in the sense of "kind" (*prakāra*), [the suffix *ka* is optionally added].
8.01.013: With the words *priya* ("dear") and *sukha* ("pleasure"), when not meaning "without difficulty," [the suffix *ka* is optionally added].
8.01.014: With the words *yathāsvam* ("according to one's own") and *yathāyatham* ("as it is fitting").
8.01.015 In the cases of copulation, secrecy, boundary, honor, transgression, sacrificial vessels, and non-union, [the substitution of *o* for *au* occurs] after a word ending in *au*.
8.01.016 [The substitution occurs] after a word [ending in *au*].
8.01.017 [The substitution occurs] after a word [ending in *au*].
8.01.018 All [the elements] are unaccented when they do not stand at the beginning of a word.
8.01.019 And [all the elements] of a vocative are also unaccented.
8.01.020 For *yuṣmad* and *asmad* standing in the sixth, fourth, or second case, the substitutes *vām* and *nau* [are used].
8.01.021 In place of the dual endings *vas* and *nas*, [the suffixes] *vas* and *nas* are substituted when followed by a plural ending.

8.01.022 In place of the singular endings *te* and *me*, [the suffixes] *tva* and *ma* are substituted. 8.01.023 In place of the second case singular endings *tvā* and *mā*, [the suffixes] *tvā* and *mā* are substituted.

8.01.024 [The particle *na* is used with the particles *ca*, *vā*, *ha*, *aha*, *eva*, and *yukte*. 8.01.025 [The particle *na* is used with words having the sense of "seeing" (*paśya-artha*), provided it does not mean "looking at" (*an-ālocane*). 8.01.026 [The particle *na* is optionally used after a nominative case-form (*prathamā*) that is preceded by another word.]
8.01.027: After a verbal suffix (*tiṅ*), the particles *gotra* and so forth are used in the sense of censure or repetition.
8.01.028: A verbal suffix (*tiṅ*) follows a word that is not itself a verbal suffix (*atiṅ*).
8.01.029: This does not apply after the suffix *luṭ*.
8.01.030 When joined with the particles *yat*, *yadi*, *hanta*, *kuvid*, *ned*, *ced*, *caṇ*, *kaccit*, or *yatra*, [the Imperative is used].
8.01.031 With *naha* used in the sense of prohibition (*pratyārambha*).
8.01.032 With *satyam* used in a question.

8.01.033 Before a word beginning with *a* that is not a prātilomya (non-repetitive), [the final *i* or *u* of a preceding word is elided]. 8.01.034 Also before *hi*, [the final *i* or *u* of a preceding word is elided]. 8.01.035 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), even multiple words [may be compounded] provided they are mutually expectant (*sākāṅkṣam*).

8.01.036 [The particle *ca* is used] with the words *yāvat* and *yathā*. 8.01.037 [The particle *ca* is used] immediately after a word expressing worship (*pūjā*). 8.01.038 [The particle *ca* is used] also when it is separated from a prefix (*upasarga*).
8.01.039 The particles *tu*, *paśya*, *paśyata*, *aha*, and *aiḥ* [are compounded] when expressing honor. 8.01.040 And [the particle] *aho* [is also compounded in this sense].
8.01.041 In other cases (*śeṣe*), [the compounding] is optional (*vibhāṣā*).

8.01.042 The word *purā* [takes the indeclinable particle *ca*] when there is a desire to obtain (*parīpsā*). 8.01.043 The word *nanu* [takes the indeclinable particle *ca*] when it expresses a request for permission (*anujñāeṣaṇā*). 8.01.044 The word *kim*, when not preceded by a prefix (*anupasarga*) and not negated (*apratiṣiddham*), [takes the indeclinable particle *ca*] in a question regarding an action (*kriyāpraśne*).
8.01.045 Optionally [the substitution of *luṅ*] occurs when there is elision (*lop*).
8.01.046 The conditional (*lṛṭ*) is used for the future tense after the particles *ehi*, *manye*, and *prahāse* (jesting).
8.01.047 [The conditional is used] after *jātu* when it does not precede [another word].

8.01.048 A word ending in *kim* and a word having *cid* as its final member [form an indefinite compound]. 8.01.049 The particles *āho* and *utāho* [form an indefinite compound] when they are immediately followed by a word ending in *cid*. 8.01.050 In other cases, it is optional (*vibhāṣā*).

8.01.051 The periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*) is not used after an imperative (*loṭ*) expressing motion, unless all the other factors [of the action] are different. 8.01.052 And [the periphrastic future is also not used] after an imperative. 8.01.053 An imperative with a prefix, excluding the last person, is optionally [used].
8.01.054 *hanta* and 8.01.055 *ām* [are enclitic] when separated by one intervening word from an addressive vocative (*āmantrita*), provided it is not used in close proximity (*anantike*).
8.01.056 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), that which follows *yat*, *hi*, or *tu* [is enclitic].

8.01.057: The particle *cana* (and its variants), *cid*, *iva*, *go*, *tra*, and others, as well as words ending in *taddhita* suffixes beginning with *ām*, and those that are repeated (*āmreḍita*), do not lose their original accent when they follow [another word], except when they are connected with *agata*.
8.01.058: The same applies when they follow particles such as *ca* ("and") and others.
8.01.059: When *ca* or *vā* are used in conjunction [with another word], the first [word] retains its original accent.
8.01.060 *ha* occurs in the sense of "kṣiyā" (reproach) and "yācñā" (request);
8.01.061 *aha* occurs in the sense of "viniryoga" (assignment or application); 8.01.062 *ca* and *eva* occur when there is elision (*lopa*) of *aha*, serving as a restriction (*avadhāraṇa*).
8.01.063 Optionally, when there is elision of *ca* and the others [in the sense of "and so forth"]. 8.01.064 Also *vai*, *vāva*, and *iti* [are used] in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
8.01.065 [The word *eva* is used] after *eka* and *anya* when they are semantically connected (*samartha*).

8.01.066 A word ending in a *vṛtti* suffix is always [accented with the udātta on its final syllable]. 8.01.067 A word denoting an object of worship (*pūjita*) following a word denoting the agent of worship (*pūjana*)—provided the former is not derived from words such as *kāṣṭha* and the like—is unaccented (*anudātta*).
8.01.068 A finite verb (*tiṅ*) following a word denoting motion (*sagati*) is also [unaccented].
8.01.069 Also before the suffix *kutsana* when a case-ending (*sUP*) follows, provided it does not begin with *go-tra*.
8.01.070 A verb (*gati*) is elided before another verb (*gati*).
8.01.071 And also before a finite verb (*tiṅ*) that bears an acute accent (*udātta*).

8.01.072 An *āmantrita* [vocative] that precedes [another word] is not treated as if it were non-existent (*avidyamānavat*). 8.01.073 [The vocative] is not [treated as non-existent] when followed by another *āmantrita* that has the same referent (*samānādhikaraṇa*), provided it is a general term (*sāmānyavacana*). 8.01.074 [This applies to] a general term (*sāmānyavacana*).
The *vibhāṣita* rule applies when there is a specific statement regarding the plural number.
8.2.1: That which precedes is not established (*asiddha*).

8.2.2: The elision of *n* (*nalopa*) is treated as *asiddha* with respect to case endings (*sup*), accent (*svara*), technical names (*saṃjñā*), the augment *tuK*, and the substitution of *iD* in the context of *kṛt* suffixes.
8.02.003 Not before the suffix *mu*. 8.02.004 When a *yaṇ* substitute for an *udātta* or *svarita* vowel is itself *svarita*, the following *anudātta* vowel becomes *svarita*.
8.02.005 In the case of a single substitute (*ekādeśa*) for two vowels where one is *udātta*, the resulting single substitute is *udātta*.
8.02.006 An acute (svarita) syllable [is optionally substituted] for the first syllable of a word that begins with an unaccented (anudātta) vowel.
8.02.007 There is elision (lopa) of the *n* at the end of a nominal stem (*prātipadika*).
8.02.008 This elision does not occur before the case ending *ṅi* or the vocative (*saṃbuddhi*).

8.02.009: After a stem ending in *m*, after a verbal root (*dhātu*), and after a word ending in the suffix *mat*, the substitute *va* optionally takes the place of *matUP*, except when the stem begins with *yav* or other such words.
8.02.010: [The substitution of *va* for *matUP* occurs] after a stem ending in a *jhaL* consonant.
8.02.011: [The substitution of *va* for *matUP* occurs] when a technical name (*saṃjñā*) is being formed.

8.02.012 [The suffix *matup* is applied after the words] *āsandī*, *aṣṭhīvat*, *cakrīvat*, *kakṣīvat*, *rumaṇvat*, and *carmaṇvat*. 8.02.013 [The suffix *matup* is applied after the word] *udán* when it means "the ocean. 8.02.014 [The suffix *matup* is applied after the word] *rājan* when it means "good government" (*saurājya*).
8.02.015 In Vedic literature (chandas), the augment *i* is inserted after [a word ending in] *ī* or *r*.
8.02.016 The augment *nuṬ* is inserted after [a word ending in] *an*.
8.02.017 The augment *n* is inserted before the suffix *GHa* after [a word ending in] *ā*.
8.02.018 *ra* is substituted for the *ṛ* of the root *kṛp* [before a suffix beginning with a vowel].
8.02.019 [The substitution of *ay* for the final *a* of] a preposition [occurs] before the suffixes *at* and *atu*.
8.02.020 [The substitution of *ya* for the final *a* of] the root *gras* [occurs] before the suffix *yaṅ*.

8.02.021 The suffix *aC* is optionally [elided] (*vibhāṣā*). 8.02.022 Also [the final consonant of a verbal root ending in a consonant is elided], except for the roots *pari* and *gha*, when followed by a suffix beginning with *ṛ*. 8.02.023 There is elision (*lopa*) of a word-final consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*).
8.02.024 Before *r* and *ā*, [the substitution of] *s* for [the final consonant of a word] occurs.
8.02.025 Also before *dh*.
8.02.026 Before a *jhaL* (a non-nasal stop or sibilant), [the substitution of] a *jhaL* [occurs] for a *jhaL*.
8.02.027 [The substitution of *ru* for *u* occurs] after a short vowel, provided that the word is not *ṛc*.
8.02.028 [The substitution of *ru* for *u* occurs] when *iṭ* follows *iṭ*.
8.02.029 [The substitution of *ru* for *u* occurs] for the *s* and *k* of a *saṃyoga* (consonant cluster) at the beginning of a word, as well as at the end of a word.
8.02.030 *c* becomes *k*. 8.02.031 *h* becomes *ḍh*. 8.02.032 *gh* replaces the initial *d* of a verbal root (*dhātu*).
8.02.033 After the roots *druh*, *muh*, *ṣṇuh*, and *ṣṇih*, [the suffix *kvip* is applied].
8.02.034 For the final consonant *n* of the root *nah*, there is the substitution of *dh*.
8.02.035 For the final consonant *h* of the root *āh*, there is the substitution of *th*.
8.2.36: For the roots *vraśc*, *bhrasj*, *sṛj*, *mṛj*, *yaj*, *rāj*, *bhrāj*, and for the letters *ch* and *ś*, there is the substitution of *ṣ*.
8.2.37: In place of the non-nasal stops (*baś*) of a monosyllabic root ending in a *jhaṣ* consonant, there is the substitution of a *bhaṣ* stop before the suffixes *s* and *dhv*.
8.2.38: In place of the *d* of the root *dadh*, there is the substitution of *t* before the suffixes *tha* and *thoḥ*.
8.02.039: In word-final position, the *jaś*-sounds (j, b, g, d, d) replace the *jhaL* sounds (j, b, g, d, dh).
8.02.040: Following a *jhaṣ* sound, the sounds *t* and *th* are replaced by *dh*, except after the vowel *a*.
8.02.041: In the presence of the suffix *si*, the sounds *ṣ* and *ḍh* are replaced by *k*.
8.02.042: After the roots *rad* and *dā*, the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffixes (*kta* and *ktavatu*) is replaced by *n*; however, the preceding *d* is also replaced by *n*. 8.02.043:
The *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffixes is replaced by *n* after a root that begins with a conjunct consonant, ends in a long vowel (*ĀT*), and contains the semivowel *yaṇ*.
8.02.044: [The *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffixes is replaced by *n*] after the roots beginning with *lū*.
8.02.045 And [the substitution of *i* for the final vowel occurs] after a word ending in *o* or *it*.
8.02.046 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel occurs] after a word ending in *kṣi*, provided that the preceding vowel is long.
8.02.047 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel occurs] after a word ending in *śī*, provided that a non-consonant (*asparśa*) follows.
8.02.048 The suffix *an* [is applied] after a word ending in *anc*, except when it denotes the act of taking away (*apādāna*).
8.02.049 The suffix *an* [is applied] after the word *div*, except when it denotes the desire to win (*vijigīṣā*).
8.02.050 The suffix *an* [is applied] after the word *nirvāṇa*, except when it means "without wind" (*avāta*).
8.02.051 For the root *śuṣ*, [the suffix] *ka* is substituted. 8.02.052 For the root *pac*, [the suffix] *va* is substituted. 8.02.053 For the root *kṣā*, [the suffix] *ma* is substituted.
8.02.054 The suffix *pra* is optionally substituted for *styā* [after the prefix *ni*].
8.02.055 After a prefix that is not an *upasarga*, the suffixes *phulla*, *kṣība*, *kṛśa*, and *ullāgha* are used [in the sense of the past passive participle].
8.02.056 After the roots *nud*, *vid*, *und*, *trai*, *ghrā*, and *hrī*, the suffix *na* is used [in the sense of the past passive participle] when it does not end in *ar*.
8.02.057 [The suffix *kta* is not used after the roots] *dhyai*, *khyā*, *pṛ*, *mūrch*, and *mad*.

8.02.058 [The suffix *kta* is used after the root] *vid* to denote either possession (*bhoga*) or cognition (*pratyaya*). 8.02.059 [The suffix *kta* is used after the root *bhid* to denote] a fragment (*śakala*).
8.02.060: The word *ṛṇam* (debt) is formed by [the substitution of] *ṇa* for [the final consonant of the root] in the sense of being a debtor (*ādhamarṇye*).
8.02.061: In Vedic literature (*chandas*), the forms *nasatta*, *niṣatta*, *anutta*, *pratūrta*, *sūrta*, and *gūrta* are established as correct.
8.02.062: The augment *kU-* (any consonant except *y*) is substituted for the suffix *KviN*.
8.02.063 Optionally [the substitution of] *na* occurs for [the final letter of] the root *naś*.
8.02.064 *Na* is substituted for *m* when it follows a verbal root ending in *m*.
8.02.065 And [the substitution of *na* occurs for *m*] when it follows a verbal root ending in *m* or *v*.
8.02.066 For *sas* and *sajuṣ*, *ru* is substituted [in the nominative singular].
8.02.067 [The forms] *avayāḥ*, *śvetavāḥ*, and *uroḍāḥ* are also [irregularly formed].
8.02.068 [The form] *ahan* [is irregularly formed].
8.02.069 *ra-* [is substituted for the final vowel] when followed by a suffix other than *suP*.

8.02.070 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the substitution of *s* for the final vowel of *amnas* and *ūdhah* may optionally occur before a suffix beginning with *a*. 8.02.071 And the same applies to the word *bhuvas* when it is one of the Great Utterances (*mahā-vyāhṛti*).
8.02.072: For the words *vasu*, *sraṃsu*, *dhvaṃsu*, and *anaḍuh*, the substitution of *d* occurs [in place of the final consonant].
8.02.073: In the case of the suffix *tiP*, the substitution of *r* occurs for the word *an-as* (provided it is not *asti*).
8.02.074: In the case of the suffix *siP*, the substitution of *ru* optionally occurs for the root.

8.02.075: [A long vowel is substituted] for a short *iK* vowel that is an *upadhā* (penultimate) before the suffix *dha*. 8.02.076: [A long vowel is substituted for a short *iK* vowel that is an *upadhā*] before the suffixes *ra* and *va*. 8.02.077: [A long vowel is substituted for a short *iK* vowel that is an *upadhā*] also before a consonant (*hal*).
8.02.078 And [the substitution of *u* occurs] for the vowel following the augment *upadhā*.
8.02.079 The substitution of *u* does not occur for the vowel of roots ending in *bh*, nor for *ku*, *ru*, and *chu*.
8.02.080 For the letter *d* following the *s* of *adas* when it is not followed by *se*, the substitution of *u* occurs, and for the final *d*, the substitution of *m* occurs.
8.02.081: A long vowel (īT) is substituted for the final short *e* (eT) of a word ending in the plural number.
8.02.082: The final syllable (*ṭe*) of a sentence is protracted (*pluta*) and acute (*udātta*).
8.02.083: This [protraction] occurs in response to a greeting, provided the person addressed is not a Śūdra.

8.2.84: [The substitution of *e* for the final vowel of an interjection occurs] when it is called out from a distance (*dūrāt*). 8.2.85: [The substitution of *e* for the final vowel of an interjection occurs] when *hai* or *he* are employed [in the sense of calling out]. 8.2.86:

According to the Eastern grammarians, [the substitution of *e* for the final vowel of an interjection occurs] even for a syllable that is not final, provided it contains a heavy vowel (*guru*) and does not end in *ṛ*. This applies to each individual [interjection].
8.02.087 om [is used] in the act of taking up; 8.02.088 in the sacrificial rite (yajñakarman); 8.02.089 the Praṇava is yours.
8.02.090 [The substitution of *yaj* occurs] before the suffix *-ya*.
8.02.091 [The substitution of *yaj* occurs] for the initial consonant of the verbs *brūhi*, *preṣya*, *śrauṣaṭ*, *vauṣaṭ*, and *āvaha*.
8.02.092 [The substitution of *yaj* occurs] for the initial consonant of the word *agnīdh* when it follows the verb *pra-iṣ*, as well as for that which follows it.

8.02.093 The particle *he* is optionally [treated as pragṛhya] in response to a question. 8.02.094 It is also [optionally treated as pragṛhya] when used in reproach after having restrained someone. 8.02.095 A reduplicated word (*āmreḍita*) is [always treated as pragṛhya] when used in the sense of reviling.
8.02.096 A finite verb (*tiṅ*) joined with a non-verbal element (*aṛga*) requires [the subsequent word to be pronounced with a high pitch].
8.02.097 [The same applies] to words that are being deliberated upon. 8.02.098 However, in common speech (*bhāṣā*), the preceding word [is pronounced with a high pitch].
8.02.099 And [the first syllable of a word] in *pratiśravaṇa* (answering) [is unaccented].
8.02.100 [The first syllable of a word] at the end of a question or used in a sense of praise is unaccented (*anudātta*).
8.02.101 Also, when *cit* is employed in the sense of comparison (*upamā*), [the preceding word is unaccented].
8.02.102 And [the first syllable] of *upari* and *svit* [is acute when followed by *āsīt*].
8.02.103 In the case of a reduplicated word (*āmreḍita*), the acute accent falls on the first syllable when expressing envy, approval, anger, or contempt.
8.02.104 In the case of a finite verb (*tiṅ*) used for a request, a blessing, or a command, there is no expectation of a subsequent word (*ākāṅkṣā*).
8.02.105 The final vowel of *anantya* (the penultimate) is also lengthened when followed by a question or a narrative (*praśna* and *ākhyāna*).

8.02.106 When a vowel with the *pluta* accent follows, the *aiC* diphthongs (*e*, *o*, *ai*, *au*) are changed to *iT* (*i*, *ī*) and *uT* (*u*, *ū*) respectively, before vowels with the *iT* and *uT* accents.

8.02.107 When a vowel with the *pluta* accent follows, the *eC* diphthongs (*e*, *o*, *ai*, *au*) that are not *pragṛhya* are changed to *āT* (*ā*) for the first half and *iT* (*i*, *ī*) or *uT* (*u*, *ū*) for the second half, provided they are not separated by a distance.
8.02.108: In the *saṃhitā*, the letters *y* and *v* are substituted for those two (*au* and *aḥ*) before a vowel (*aC*).
8.03.001: In Vedic literature (*chandas*), the suffix *ru* is substituted for the possessive suffixes *matU* and *vasU* in the vocative case.
8.03.002: In this context, the preceding [vowel] may optionally be nasalized (*anunāsika*).

8.03.003 An *āT* [vowel] is always substituted [for the final vowel of a verbal root] before an affix beginning with *aṬ*. 8.03.004 An *anusvāra* is substituted for a nasal [consonant] when followed by a consonant. 8.03.005 The augment *suṬ* is added after the prefix *sam*.
8.03.006 Before a suffix beginning with *khay*, the final vowel of a masculine stem ending in *am* is substituted by *ū*.
8.03.007 Before a suffix beginning with *chav*, the final vowel of a neuter stem ending in *as* is substituted by *ī*, except for the word *praśān*.
8.03.008 In the case of *ṛc* verses, both [the preceding and following rules] apply optionally.
8.03.009 [The substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] after a long vowel before the augment *aṬ*, within the same word.
8.03.010 [The substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] for the *v* of *nṛ-* before the suffix *p*. 8.03.011 [The substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] for the *v* of *svatavas-* before the suffix *pāyu*.
8.03.012 [The substitution of *l* occurs] for *k* before a reduplicated syllable (*āmreḍita*). 8.03.013 [The substitution of *lopa* (elision) occurs] for *ḍh* before *ḍh*.
8.03.014 [The substitution of *lopa* (elision) occurs] for *r* before *r*.
8.03.015 The *visarjanīya* is substituted for *kh*, *r*, *avasa*, and *naya*.
8.03.016 [The *visarjanīya* is substituted for *r*] before a *sUP* [case-ending].
8.03.017 [The *visarjanīya* is substituted for the *r*] of *bhoḥ*, *bhagoḥ*, *aghoḥ*, when not preceded by *a*, before a vowel other than *ś*.

8.03.018 According to Śākaṭāyana, there is an optional light articulation for the vowels *v* and *u*. 8.03.019 According to Śākalya, there is elision [of the vowel]. 8.03.020 According to Gārgya, there is elision of the final *o* (*oṭ*).

8.03.021 And [the substitution of *m*] occurs for the final vowel (*u*) when followed by a word (*pada*). 8.03.022 When followed by a consonant (*haL*), this substitution occurs for all [final vowels].
8.03.023 The substitute *anusvāra* is applied in place of *m*.
8.03.024: A *n* that is not at the end of a word (*apadānta*) is replaced by *anusvāra* before a *jhaL* (consonant).
8.03.025: The *m* of the root *sam* is replaced by *anusvāra* before the suffix *Kvi*, when followed by *rāj*.
8.03.026: Before *he* followed by *m*, [the *m* of *sam*] is optionally replaced by *anusvāra*.
8.03.027: *na* is substituted for *na-par-e* (a *na* followed by *e*).
8.03.028: The augment *kuK* is added after *ṛ*, and *ṭuK* after *ṇ*, before a suffix beginning with *śaR*.
8.03.029: The augment *dhuṬ* is added after *ḍ* before *si*.

8.03.030 n-aś ca [the augment *nuṭ* is applied after a word ending in *n*] 8.03.031 ś-i tuK [the augment *tuK* is applied before the suffix *śi*] 8.03.032 ṛaM-aḥ hrasv-āt aC-i ṛaMuṬ nityam [the augment *ṛamuṬ* is invariably applied after a short vowel of the pratyāhāra *ṛam* when followed by a vowel]
8.03.033 The vowel *u* (uṅ) following *ma* optionally becomes *v*.
8.03.034 The visarga (*visarjanīya*) is replaced by *s*.
8.03.035 The visarga is replaced by *s* when followed by a consonant (*śar*).
8.03.036 Or [the substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] before a suffix beginning with *śaR*.
8.03.037 And [the substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] before a suffix beginning with *kU* when it is marked with *P*, and before a suffix beginning with *XK* when it is marked with *P*.
8.03.038 [The substitution of *s* for *visarga* occurs] before a suffix beginning with *sa*, provided that the suffix does not stand at the beginning of a word (*apadādi*).
8.03.039: The substitute *ṣ* is applied in place of the *iṇ* (the phonemes *i*, *u*, *ṛ*, *ṝ*, *lṛ*) when followed by *ṣ*.
8.03.040: The substitute *ṣ* is applied in place of the *iṇ* [root] following the words *namas* and *puras* when they signify motion.

8.03.041: The substitute *ṣ* is applied in place of the *iṇ* [root] ending in a vowel other than *a* (*it*), provided that the vowel is in the penultimate position (*upadha*) and the suffix is not a *pratyaya* (suffix).
8.03.042 The suffix *tiras* is optionally [replaced by *tiraḥ*] when followed by a word meaning "other than.

8.03.043 The words *dvi*, *tri*, and *catur* [are replaced by *dvir*, *tris*, and *catur* respectively] when they have the sense of the suffix *kṛtvas*. 8.03.044 The suffixes *is* and *us* [are applied] when there is semantic connection (*sāmarthya*).
8.03.045 In a compound, the word *nityam* always retains its original form when it does not follow *uttara*, *ada*, or *atha*.
8.03.046 A short vowel (*aT*) at the end of a word that is not an indeclinable (*an-avyaya*) retains its original form before the words *kṛ*, *kami*, *kaṃsa*, *kumbha*, *pātra*, *kuśā*, and *karṇī*.
8.03.047 The words *adhas* and *śiras* retain their original forms when followed by *pada*.

8.03.048 And [the substitution of *sa* for *sma* occurs] before words beginning with *kas*, *ka*, etc. 8.03.049 In the Vedic language (*chandas*), this substitution is optional (*vā*) before *pra* and *āmreḍita*. 8.03.050 [The substitution of *sa* for *sma* occurs] before *kaḥ*, *karat*, *karati*, *kṛdhi*, and *kṛte*, provided that [the word following *sma*] is not *aditi*.
8.03.051 The substitution of *ad* for the fifth case ending (*pañcamī*) occurs before a word meaning "over" (*parau*), when it has the sense of "above" (*adhy-arthe*).
8.03.052 The substitution of *ad* for the fifth case ending occurs diversely (*bahulam*) before the words *pāti* and *tau*.
8.03.053 The substitution of *ad* for the sixth case ending (*ṣaṣṭhī*) occurs before the words *pati*, *putra*, *pṛṣṭha*, *pāra*, *pada*, *payas*, and *poṣa*.
8.03.054 Or [the substitution of *ṣ* occurs] after *iḍā*. 8.03.055 A retroflex (*mūrdhanya*) [substitution occurs] for [the dental *s*] that is not at the end of a word.
8.03.056 For the *s* of *sah*, there is the substitution of *ṣaḍ* when it is followed by *s*.
8.03.057 Before an affix beginning with *iṇ* or *ku*.
8.03.058 Even when there is an intervention by *nuṭ*, the *visarga*, or *śar*.
8.03.059 When [the *s*] belongs to a substitute (*ādeśa*) or an affix (*pratyaya*).
8.03.060 And [the substitution of *ṣ* occurs] for the *s* of the roots *śās*, *vas*, *ghas*, and those ending in *n*.
8.03.061 [The substitution of *ṣ* occurs] for the *s* of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) only when followed by the root *stu* or a root having the marker *Ṇy*, provided that *ṣaṇ* follows.
8.03.062 And [the substitution of *ṣ* occurs] for the *s* of the roots *svid*, *svad*, and *sah*, as well as those ending in *n*.
8.03.063: Before a suffix beginning with *s*, the augment *aṬ* is inserted even when there is an intervening vowel.
8.03.064: In the case of the roots *sthā* and others, the augment *aṬ* is inserted before the suffix beginning with *s* even when there is an intervening reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

8.03.065: After a preposition (*upasarga*), the augment *aṬ* is inserted before the roots *su-nō-ti*, *su-v-ati*, *sy-ati*, *stu-ati*, *stobh-ati*, *sthā*, *sen-ay-ati*, *sedh-ati*, *sic-ati*, *sañj-ati*, and *svañj-ati*.

8.03.066 [The suffix *ka* is added after the root *sad* when followed by the prefix *a-*] except when it means "to sit down. 8.03.067 [The suffix *ka* is added after the root *stambh*] when preceded by the prefix *ava*.
8.03.068 [The suffix *ka* is added after the root *labh*] when preceded by *ava*, provided it does not mean "supporting" or "being near."
8.03.069: The augment *veT* is applied after the prefix *vi-* before the verbal root *svan*, when used in the sense of eating.

8.03.070: The augment *niṣ* is applied after the prefixes *pari*, *ni*, and *vi* before the roots *sev*, *si*, *tasi*, *say*, *siv*, *sah*, and the roots beginning with *suṬ* (the desiderative marker), as well as *stu* and *sañj*.
8.03.071: The augment *niṣ* is optionally applied after the roots beginning with *siv* even when there is an intervention by the vowel *a*.
8.03.072 After the prefixes *anu*, *vi*, *pari*, *abhi*, and *ni*, the root *syand* takes the augment *ṣ* when it does not refer to living beings.
8.03.073 After the prefix *veḥ*, the root *skand* takes the augment *ṣ*, except in the case of the *kta* suffix (*aniṣṭhā*). 8.03.074 And [the augment *ṣ* is applied] after the prefix *para*.
8.03.075 *pariskanda-* [is used] among the Eastern Bharatas.
8.03.076 After the prefixes *ni*, *niḥ*, and *vi*, [the suffix *ap* is added] to the roots *sphurati* and *sphulati*.
8.03.077 After the prefix *veḥ*, [the suffix *ap* is added] invariably to the root *skabhnoti*.

8.03.078: After a verbal root ending in the vowel *i* or *ī*, the substitute *dh* is applied in place of the *s* of the suffixes *sī*, *dhvam*, *luṅ*, and *liṭ*, except when the root ends in *ṛ*. 8.03.079: Optionally, the same substitution applies after a root ending in the augment *iṭ*.
8.03.080: In a compound, the word *aṅguli* becomes *aṅga* [when followed by another word].
8.03.081 The word *bhīru-* [is followed by] *sthānam*.
8.03.082 [The words] *agni-*, *stu-*, *stoma-*, and *soma-* [are followed by *ṣatva*].
8.03.083 [The word] *jyotis-* and *āyus-* [are followed by] *stoma-*.
8.03.084 [The suffix ṅasi becomes *āt* after *mātṛ* and *pitṛ* when followed by *svasṛ*.
8.03.085 [The suffix *āt* is substituted for the case-ending *ṅasi* after *mātṛ* and *pitṛ*, provided that the following word does not contain the vowel *a* as its penultimate letter.
8.03.086 [The suffix *āt* is substituted for the case-ending *ṅasi* after *abhi* and *niḥ* when followed by *stan*, provided that the word is not a technical grammatical term.]
8.03.087: After the prefixes *upa* and *sarga*, and after the indeclinable *prāduḥ*, the root *as* takes the augment *t* before a suffix beginning with a vowel other than *y*.
8.03.088: After the prefixes *su*, *vi*, *nis*, and *dur*, the roots *sup*, *sū*, *ti*, and *sam* take the augment *t* before a suffix beginning with a vowel other than *y*.
8.03.089: After the prefixes *ni* and *nadī*, the root *snā* takes the augment *t* when skill (*kauśala*) is expressed.
8.03.090 *pratiṣṇāta* [is used] with reference to a *sūtra*; 8.03.091 *kapiṣṭhala* [is used] as a *gotra* name;
8.03.092 *praṣṭha* [is used] in the sense of one who goes at the head.

8.03.093 *viṣṭara-* [is substituted for *vistṛta-*] after *vṛkṣa* and *āsa*. 8.03.094 [The same substitution occurs] also when a name of a *chandas* (meter) follows. 8.03.095 *sthir-* [is substituted for *sthira-*] after *go* and *yudh*.
8.03.096 After the prefixes *vi*, *ku*, *śamī*, and *pari*, the word *sthalam* [is substituted for *sthala*].

8.03.097 After *amba*, *ambaḥ*, *go*, *bhūmi*, *savya*, *apa*, *dvi*, *tri*, *kuśe*, *ku*, *śarku*, *aṛgu*, *mañji*, *puñji*, *parama*, *ibarhis*, *divi*, and *agni*, the word *staḥ* [is substituted for *stha*].
8.03.098 Also in *suṣāman* and other such forms.
8.03.099 The suffix *eT* is applied after [a word ending in] *aG* (any consonant except *y*) when it denotes a name (*saṃjñā*).
8.03.100 After a word denoting a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*), [the suffix *eT* is applied] optionally.
8.03.101 When a secondary suffix (*taddhita*) beginning with *t* or *d* follows, [the suffix *eT* is applied] after a word ending in a short vowel.
8.03.102 The substitution of *niṣ* for *nis* occurs before the verbal roots *tap* and *tad*, except when they denote repeated action (*āsevane*).
8.03.103 Before the forms *yuṣmad*, *tat*, and *tatakṣuḥ*, the word *antaḥ* takes the form *ād*.
8.03.104 According to some teachers, this [substitution] does not occur in the *Yajus* (Vedic sacrificial formulas).
8.03.105: The substitution of *u* occurs for the final vowel of the words *stuta* and *stoma* when followed by the suffix *ya*, provided they are used in Vedic literature (*chandas*).
8.03.106: [The substitution of *u* occurs] after a word ending in a compound whose prior member (*pūrvapada*) [ends in a vowel]. 8.03.107: [The substitution of *u* occurs] for the suffix *suṇ*.
8.03.108 After the roots *san* and *tan*, [the suffix] *ana* [is added].
8.03.109 Also after the root *sah* when combined with *pṛtanā* and *ṛta*.
8.03.110 [The substitution of *u* for the radical vowel does not occur] for roots ending in *r*, nor for *sṛp*, *sṛj*, *spṛś*, *spṛh*, *sav*, *na*, and so forth.
8.03.111 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel] of a word ending in *sāt* and of a word beginning with a verbal root occurs [before a suffix marked with K or Ṅ].
8.03.112 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel] of the root *sic* occurs before the suffix *yaṅ*.
8.03.113 [The substitution of *i* for the final vowel] of the root *sedhati* occurs when it means "to go."
8.03.114 And [the substitution of *s* for *ṣ* occurs] in *prati-stabdha-* and *ni-stabdha-*.
8.03.115 [The substitution of *s* for *ṣ* occurs] in *soḍhaḥ*.
8.03.116 [The substitution of *s* for *ṣ* occurs] in the roots *stanbhū*, *śvi*, and *sah* when followed by *Caṅ*.
8.03.117: After the root *su*, the augment *iṭ* is not applied before the suffixes *sya* and *saN*.
8.03.118: After the roots *sad* and *svañj*, the augment *iṭ* is not applied before the suffix *liṭ* when it follows [the prefix *ni*].
8.03.119: After the prefixes *ni*, *vi*, and *abhi*, the augment *aṬ* is optionally applied before the suffix *luṅ* (when it does not denote the agent) in Vedic usage.
8.04.001. After *ra* and *ṣa*, the *n* [of a suffix] becomes *ṇa* when followed by a homogeneous vowel (*samāna-ac*).
8.04.002. This substitution occurs even when there is an intervention (*vyavāya*) by the augment *aṭ*, a *ku*-class consonant, a *pu*-class consonant, the prefix *āṅ*, or the augment *nuṬ*.
8.04.003. In a compound name (*saṃjñā*), the *n* following a word ending in a short *a* (*ag*) becomes *ṇa* when preceded by a prior member (*pūrvapada*) that ends in *ra* or *ṣa*.
8.04.004 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *vana*, *puragā*, *miśrakā*, *sidhrakā*, *śārikā*, and *koṭarāgra*.

8.04.005 [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the words *pra*, *nir*, *antar*, *śara*, *ikṣu*, *plakṣa*, *āmra*, *kārṣya*, *khadira*, and *piyūkṣā*, even when no specific compound name (*saṃjñā*) is intended.
8.04.006 [The suffix *cha* is applied] optionally after words denoting medicinal herbs (*oṣadhi*) and trees (*vanaspati*).
8.04.007 [The suffix] *aT* is applied after [the word] *ahar-* ending in [the *taddhita* suffix] *an*.
8.04.008 [The suffix *aT* is applied] after [the word] *vāhana-* when preceded by [a prefix] ending in *āhi*.
8.04.009 [The suffix *aT* is applied after *vāhana-*] to form the word *pāna-* when it denotes a place.
8.04.010 Or [the substitution of *ṇatva* occurs] before an affix having the sense of a verbal action (*bhāva*) or an instrument (*karaṇa*).

8.04.011 And [the substitution of *ṇatva* occurs] before a nominal stem-final (*prātipadika-anta*), the particle *nuṭ*, and case-endings (*vibhakti*). 8.04.012 [The substitution of *ṇatva* occurs for the letter *n*] when it follows a single vowel (*eka-ac*) in the final member of a compound (*uttara-pada*).
8.04.013 Also before the suffix *mat*.
8.04.014 After a prefix, even when not in a compound, the substitution of *ṇa* for *na* occurs before the roots *pā*, *pe*, and *pai*. 8.04.015 Also before the roots *hi*, *nu*, *mī*, and *nā*.
8.04.016: [The substitution of] *ān* occurs before the *loṭ* suffix.

8.04.017: [The substitution of *ān* occurs] also before the following roots: *ne*, *gad*, *nad*, *pat*, *pad*, roots ending in *ghu*, *mā*, *syati*, *hanti*, *yāti*, *vāti*, *drāti*, *psāti*, *vapati*, *vahati*, *śāmyati*, *cinoti*, *degdhi*, and *ṣu*.
8.04.018: In the remaining cases, the substitution is optional (*vibhāṣā*) when the root begins with a consonant other than *k* or *kh*, and does not end in *ṣ*, provided it is not part of a *pada*.
8.04.019 [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] for the vowel of a root ending in *i*, *ī*, or *u*, *ū*, when followed by an affix marked with *ṅ* or *k*.
8.04.020 [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] for the final vowel of a root ending in *a*, when followed by an affix marked with *ṅ* or *k*.
8.04.021 Both [the *guṇa* substitution of the root-final vowel and that of the reduplication] occur when the affix marked with *ṅ* or *k* follows a root beginning with a consonant.
8.04.022: For the root *han*, when preceded by *aṭ* (the augment), [the substitution of *ghn* for *han* occurs].
8.04.023: Optionally, [the substitution of *ghn* for *han* occurs] before the suffixes *vas* and *mus*.
8.04.024: [The substitution of *ghn* for *han* occurs] before the substitute *antaḥ*.
8.04.025 And [the final vowel of] *ayana* [is long].
8.04.026 In Vedic meter, [the final vowel of a word ending in] *ṛt* is long when followed by a separation (*avagraha*).
8.04.027 Also, [the final vowel of a word ending in] *nas*, when it occurs within a verbal root (*dhātu*) or is followed by *uru* or *ṣuhyas*, [is long].
8.04.028: [The substitution of *u* for the final vowel of a verbal root occurs] after a prefix (*upasarga*) when followed by a suffix beginning with a consonant other than *an*.
8.04.029: [The substitution of *u* for the final vowel of a verbal root occurs] before a *kṛt* suffix beginning with a vowel.
8.04.030: [The substitution of *u* for the final vowel of a verbal root] before a suffix beginning with *ṇ* is optional.
8.04.031: Also after a consonant, [the substitution of a long vowel occurs] for the penultimate short *i*, *u*, or *ṛ* of a verbal root ending in a consonant.
8.04.032: [The substitution of a long vowel occurs] for the initial *i*, *u*, or *ṛ* of a root that has the augment *nuṬ*.
8.04.033: Or [the substitution of a long vowel occurs] for the initial *i*, *u*, or *ṛ* of the roots *niṃs*, *nikṣ*, and *nind*.
8.04.034 [The substitution of *ṣ* for *s*] does not occur after the verbal roots √bhā, √bhū, √pū, √kam, √gam, √pyāyī, or √vep.
8.04.035 [The substitution of *ṣ* for *s*] does not occur when the suffix is preceded by a retroflex sibilant (*ṣ*) that stands at the end of a word.
8.04.036 [The substitution of *ṣ* for *s*] does not occur for the root √naś when it ends in *ṣ*.
8.04.037 [The substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] at the end of a word.
8.04.038 [The substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] even when there is an intervening *pada*.
8.04.039 [The substitution of *u* for *v* occurs] also before the roots *kṣubh*, *nā*, and others.
8.04.040 *s* followed by *t* or *th* is replaced by *ś* or *ṣ*, respectively, when followed by *c* or *ch*.
8.04.041 *ṣ* followed by *ṭ* or *ṭh* is replaced by *ṣ* or *ṣ*, respectively, when followed by *ṭ* or *ṭh*.
8.04.042 A word-final *ṭ* is not changed to *n* when followed by *a* or *ā*.
8.04.043 A *t* or *th* is replaced by *ṣ* before a following *s*.
8.04.044 [The same substitution occurs] after a *ś*.
8.04.045 An *anunāsika* (nasalized) substitute may optionally take the place of a *yaṇ* (semivowel) when followed by an *anunāsika*.
8.04.046: After a vowel (*aC*), when followed by *ra* or *ha*, the doubling occurs.
8.04.047: Also [the doubling occurs] when followed by a consonant (*an-aC*).
8.04.048: The doubling of the word *putra* does not occur after *na*, *āt*, *ini*, or *ā* when used in an abusive sense (*ākrośe*).
8.04.049: [The substitution of] *śaR* occurs before a vowel (*aC*).
8.04.050: According to Śākaṭāyana, this applies when three or more consonants follow.
8.04.051: According to Śākalya, this applies in all cases.
8.04.052: [The substitution of] *n* occurs for the final phoneme of the names of teachers (*ācārya*) when a long vowel precedes it.
8.04.053: A *jaś*-class sound replaces a *jhal*-class sound before a *jhaś*-class sound.
8.04.054: In the case of a reduplication (*abhyāsa*), a *car*-class sound replaces a *jhal*-class sound.
8.04.055 And [anusvāra is substituted] before a consonant (*khar*).
8.04.056 Optionally [anusvāra is substituted] at the end of a word (*avasāne*).
8.04.057 For a non-*pragṛhya* vowel that is not *aṇ*, [anusvāra is substituted] when followed by a nasalized vowel (*anunāsika*).
8.04.058: An *anusvāra* becomes a homogeneous (*parasavarṇa*) sound before a semivowel (*yāṅ*).
8.04.059: [The same substitution] optionally occurs when the *anusvāra* is at the end of a word (*padāntasya*).
8.04.060: A final *t* [becomes a homogeneous sound] before *l*.
8.04.061: After the root *ud*, the *s* of the roots *sthā* and *stanbhu* is replaced by *ṣ* when followed by a suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant (any consonant except *y*).
8.04.062: After a suffix beginning with a *jhay* consonant (any consonant except *y*), the *s* of the aforementioned roots is optionally replaced by *h*.
8.04.063: After a suffix beginning with a *jhay* consonant, the *ś* of the root *śās* is replaced by *ch* when followed by a suffix marked with *aṬ*.
8.04.064: There is elision of *y* and *m* [following] a consonant (*hal*) before *y* and *m*.
8.04.065: There is elision of a *jhar* [consonant] before a homogeneous *jhar* [consonant].
8.04.066: An *anudātta* [vowel] following an *udātta* [vowel] becomes *svarita*.

8.04.067 A vowel that is followed by an udātta or svarita accent does not [become pluta] according to Gārgya, Kāśyapa, and Gālava. 8.04.068 [The substitution of] *a* for *ā* occurs [in the case of a vocative].
